children.translated_text: In the <s>Nyāyavārttikatātparyaṭīkā</s> composed by <s>Vācaspati Miśra</s>
The first session of the first chapter
<s>Nyāyavārttikatātparyaṭīkā</s>

children.text: viśvavyāpī viśvaśaktiḥ pinākī viśveśāno viśvakṛd viśvamūrttiḥ /
children.translated_text: The all-pervading, all-powerful <s>Pinākī</s> (Śiva), lord of the universe, maker of the universe, embodiment of the universe,
The knower of the universe, the destroyer of the universe, worshipped by the universe — may he fulfill our desires. //
I bow to him who is adorned with <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>vijñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), and <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty),
The treasure-house of verbal purities, <s>Akṣapāda</s> (Gautama), the protector. //
Under the pretext of explaining the treatise, having removed all objections,
The <s>Nyāyavārttikatātparyaṭīkā</s> is being composed by us. //
I desire some meritorious [result] from rescuing those who are sunk in the mire of the bondage of difficult-to-cross [ignorance],
From the uplifting of the aged cows of <s>Uddyotakara</s> (i.e., his doctrines). //

<s>NyS</s> 1.1.1: From the true knowledge of the categories — <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge), <s>prameya</s> (objects of valid knowledge), <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt), <s>prayojana</s> (purpose), <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example), <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion), <s>avayava</s> (members of syllogism), <s>tarka</s> (hypothetical reasoning), <s>nirṇaya</s> (ascertainment), <s>vāda</s> (discussion), <s>jalpa</s> (wrangling), <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavil), <s>hetvābhāsa</s> (fallacious reasons), <s>chala</s> (quibbling), <s>jāti</s> (futile rejoinders), and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (points of defeat) — there is attainment of the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>). //

children.text: atha bhagavatākṣapādena niḥśreyasahetau śāstre praṇīte, vyutpādite ca bhagavatā pakṣilasvāminā, kimaparamavaśiṣyate yadarthaṃ vārttikārambha iti śaṅkāṃ nirācikīrṣuḥ sūtrākāroktāśāstraprayojanānuvādapūrvakaṃ vārttikārambhaprayojanaṃ darśayati-yadakṣapāda iti //
children.translated_text: Now, when the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) aimed at the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>) has been composed by the venerable <s>Akṣapāda</s>, and explained by the venerable <s>Pakṣilasvāmin</s> (Vātsyāyana), what further remains for the sake of which the <s>Vārttika</s> is undertaken? — wishing to dispel this doubt, he shows the purpose of undertaking the <s>Vārttika</s> by first restating the purpose of the <s>śāstra</s> as stated by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the sūtras) — 'that which <s>Akṣapāda</s>' and so on. //

children.text:
yadyapi bhāṣyakṛtā kṛtavyutpādanametat, tathāpi dignāgaprabhṛtibhirarvācīnaiḥ kṛhetusantamasasamutthāpanenācchaditaṃ śāstraṃ na tattvanirṇayāya paryāptamiti uddyotakareṇa svanibandhoddyotena tadapanīyata iti prayojanavānārambha iti /
sūtroktaprayojanānuvādaśca prayojanavacchāstravyutpādanena svanibandhasya prayojanavattāṃ prekṣāvatpravṛttyaṅgaṃ darśayitum, vyutpādanamātrasya ca kākadantaparīkṣāgranthasādhāraṇyena prekṣāvatpravṛttyanaṅgatvāt /
atra caikaviśatiprabhedabhinnasya duḥkhasyātyantikī nivṛttiḥ śamaḥ, tasmai /
kasya? jagataḥ /
paramakārūṇiko hi bhagavān muniḥ jagadeva duḥkhapaṅkamagnāmuddidhīrṣuḥ śāstraṃ praṇītavān /
tatra yadi kaścinna pravarteta, kimāyātaṃ śāstrasya? na cānadhikṛtapuruṣavyutpādanenāsya taponidheḥ kaścidasti doṣaḥ /
tathā ca viśvāmitrāstriśaṅkuṃ yājayāmāsa, viśaṣṭhaścadhamayonijāmakṣamālāmupayeme /
tapaḥprabhāva eva hi tāddaśasteṣāṃ yata evaṃvidhāḥ pāpmāno vilīyanta iti /
children.translated_text: For it is precisely the power of their <s>tapas</s> (austerities) that was such that sins of this kind dissolved away.
And this concern does not apply to us and others of meager <s>tapas</s>.

children.text: na hi gajānāmudaryaṃ tejo vaṭakāṣṭhamaśitaṃ pacatītyasmadādīnāmapyudaryeṇa tejasā tathā bhavitavyam /
children.translated_text: For the digestive fire of elephants cooks wood from the <s>vaṭa</s> tree when eaten — [but that does not mean] the digestive fire of us and others should be the same.
The ignorance produced by sophists beginning with <s>Dignāga</s> is called the ignorance of sophists. //

Although the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> (commentator) has already provided the explanation, nevertheless, because the <s>śāstra</s> has been obscured by the false darkness of reasoning raised by later thinkers beginning with <s>Dignāga</s>, it is not sufficient for the ascertainment of truth — so <s>Uddyotakara</s>, by the light of his own composition, has removed that [darkness] — thus the undertaking is purposeful. / And the restatement of the purpose stated in the <s>sūtra</s> is to show the purposefulness of his own composition through the exposition of the <s>śāstra</s> as purposeful, serving as a condition for the engagement of discerning persons, since mere exposition, being common to treatises examining crow's teeth [i.e., trivial matters], does not serve as a condition for the engagement of discerning persons. / And here, the absolute cessation of suffering, which is divided into twenty-one kinds, is tranquility — for the sake of that. / Of whom? Of the world. / For the supremely compassionate venerable sage composed the <s>śāstra</s> wishing to rescue the world itself, sunk in the mire of suffering. / Now, if someone does not engage [with the teaching], what loss is there for the <s>śāstra</s>? And there is no fault whatsoever for this treasury of <s>tapas</s> (asceticism) in instructing persons who are not qualified. / Thus <s>Viśvāmitra</s> performed the sacrifice for <s>Triśaṅku</s>, and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> married <s>Akṣamālā</s> who was of low birth.

children.text: avigītaśiṣṭācāraparamparaprāptaḥ paramaśiṣṭena vārttikakāreṇa kṛto 'pīṣṭadevatānamaskāro na śāstre niveśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The salutation to the chosen deity, made by the <s>vārttikakāra</s> (author of the Vārttika), the supreme teacher, received through an unbroken tradition of conduct approved by the learned, has not been placed within the <s>śāstra</s>.

children.text: na khalvanyadapi maṅgalyaṃ śāstre niveśitam, prasiddhataratayā tu maṅgalyāntaravacchiṣyā avagabhiṣyantīti sarvamavadātam //
children.translated_text: Nor has any other auspicious [formula] been placed in the <s>śāstra</s>, but because it is more well-known, the disciples, having been separated from other auspicious [formulas], will understand — thus all is pure. //

children.text:
tatra saṃkṣepataḥ prathamasūtramanūdya tasya tātparyamāha--pramāṇādipadārthatattvajñānānniḥ- śreyasādhigama ityetacchāstrasyādisūtram /
tasya śāstrasya abhisaṃbandhavākyam /
ādigrahaṇena kramaprāptasyaiva prathamaṃ vyākhyānaṃ yuktam na dvitīyāderiti darśitam /
abhimataḥ saṃbandho 'bhisaṃbandhaḥ, śāstraniḥśreyasayorhetuhetumadbhāvaḥ /
tasya idaṃ sūtrāvākyamābhisaṃbandhavākyam /
pramāṇādipadārthatatvajñānādityatra hi jñāyate 'neneti jñānamiti vyutpatyā tatvajñānaṃ śāstramucyate /
pañcamyā ca tasya hetutvam /
na hi viṣaghnamantravat svarūpamātreṇa tadavivakṣitārthaṃ niḥśreyasaheturiti padārthatatvāvagamakaraṇatayā śāstramapadiśati, na tu svarūpeṇa /
tena śāstrasya niḥśreyase kartavye pramāṇāditatvāvagamo 'vāntaravyāpāra itayuktaṃ bhavati /
tathā ca pramāṇādipadārthatatvaṃ pratipadyam, pratipādakaṃ ca śāstramiti śāstrapramāṇādipadārthatatvayorjñāpyajñāpakabhāvaśca pramāṇādipadārthatatvajñānaniḥśreyasayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvalakṣaṇaśca saṃbandhaḥ sūcito bhavati /
tadidamabhigheyasaṃbandhaprayojanapratipādanārthatvaṃ prathamasūtrasya /
patpadārthatattvajñānasya ca yathā niḥśreyasādhigamaṃ pratyupayogaḥ tathāgre nivedayiṣyate /

children.translated_text: And one whose conviction in the trustworthiness (<s>āptatva</s>) of the sage is established will, from the sage's statement — being trustworthy — ascertain the purpose and the rest and then engage.
But when the trustworthiness is not established, [there is non-engagement] due to doubt about the meaning.

children.text: na khalu kṛṣyādāvapi viriścitasasyādyadhigamānāṃ pravṛttiḥ, antarāvagrahādipratibandhena phalānutpādasyāpi nyāyaprāptatvena tadabhidhānamanarthakamiti sāmpratam, viśeṣasmṛtyanapekṣasya saṃśayasyānutpādāt /
children.translated_text: Indeed, even in agriculture and other [activities], there is no engagement of those whose attainment of grain and the like is not established, since the non-production of fruit is also justifiable by intermediate obstacles such as drought and the like — so it would be pointless to state this — this is appropriate, because doubt does not arise without the recollection of a specific [differentiating feature].
But from the [authoritative] statement, the recollection of the specific [feature] arises — so it is not pointless. //

There, having briefly restated the first <s>sūtra</s>, he states its purport — 'From the true knowledge of the categories such as <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) and the rest, there is attainment of <s>niḥśreyasa</s> (the highest good)' — this is the opening <s>sūtra</s> of the <s>śāstra</s>. / Its — of the <s>śāstra</s> — correlative statement. / By the word 'opening' (<s>ādi</s>), it is shown that the explanation of what comes in due order should come first, not that of the second [sūtra] and so on. / The intended correlation (<s>abhisaṃbandha</s>) is the relation of cause and effect between the <s>śāstra</s> and <s>niḥśreyasa</s>. / This is the correlative statement of that <s>sūtra</s>. / In the phrase 'from the true knowledge of the categories such as <s>pramāṇa</s>,' by the derivation 'that by which something is known is knowledge,' the true knowledge means the <s>śāstra</s>. / And by the fifth case [ablative], its being a cause [is indicated]. / For the <s>śāstra</s> is not a cause of <s>niḥśreyasa</s> merely by its own form, like an incantation against poison; rather, it teaches the <s>śāstra</s> as the means of apprehending the reality of the categories, not by its mere form. / Therefore, the intermediate function of the <s>śāstra</s> in bringing about <s>niḥśreyasa</s> is the apprehension of the reality of the categories — thus it is proper. / And thus, the reality of the categories such as <s>pramāṇa</s> is what is to be understood, and the <s>śāstra</s> is its means of understanding — so the relation of what is to be made known and its means of making known between the <s>śāstra</s> and the reality of the categories, and the relation of cause and effect between the knowledge of the reality of the categories and <s>niḥśreyasa</s>, is indicated. / This is the purpose of the first <s>sūtra</s>: to present the subject matter, the correlation, and the purpose. / And how the knowledge of the reality of the categories is useful for the attainment of <s>niḥśreyasa</s> will be explained later.

Having thus stated the purport of the first <s>sūtra</s>, he states the purport of the opening statement of the <s>bhāṣya</s> — 'from the <s>pramāṇa</s>, the apprehension of the object' — this and so on — is the correlative statement of that [sūtra].

children.text: tasya śāstrasya niḥśreyasādhigamena saha sūtreṇa ghaṭitasya /
children.translated_text: Of that <s>śāstra</s> which has been connected with <s>niḥśreyasa</s> by the <s>sūtra</s>.

children.text: kutaścinnimittād vighaṭanaśaṅkāyām anu sūtraghaṭanāyāḥ paścāt sandhasanaṃ ghaṭanam anusandhānam, tasya vākyamanusandhānavākyamiti //
children.translated_text: When there is a suspicion of disconnection from some cause, the reconnection — the joining after the previous joining with the <s>sūtra</s> — is the correlative reconnection; the statement of that is the correlative reconnection statement. //

children.text:
evaṃ kilātra śaṅkyate -- yadaśakyānuṣṭhānopāyopadeśakaṃ tadanarthakam, yathā jvaharatakṣakacūḍārantālaṅkāropadeśakaṃ vacanam /
tādṛśaṃ ceda śāstramiti /
tathā hi prameyādīnāṃ tāvatpadārthānāṃ tattvajñānaṃ pramāṇatattvajñānādhīnam /
na hi pramāṇaṃ tattvenānavadhāritaṃ bodhakatvamātraṇa svagocarāvadhāraṇāyālaṃ tāvanmātrasya tadābhāsasādhāraṇyāt, api tu bodha katvaikārtha samavetenāvyabhicāritvena /
tadeva hi pramāṇyam /
taccāśakyāvadhāraṇam /
tadanavadhāraṇācca prameyādayo duravadhāraṇāḥ /
tathā hi vijñānasca tāvatprāmāṇyaṃ svato vā niścīyate, parato vā? na tāvat pūrvaḥ kalpaḥ /
na khalu vijñānamānātmasaṃvedanamātmānamapi gṛhṇīyāt, prāgava tatprāmāṇaṇyam /
nāpi vijñānāntaram, tadvijñānamityava gṛhṇīyāt, na punarasyāvyabhicāritvem /
jñānatvamātraṃ ca tadābhāsasādhāraṇamiti na svataḥ prāmāṇyāvadhāraṇam /
etena svasaṃvedananaye 'pi avyabhicāragrahaṇaṃ pratyuktam /
nāpi parataḥ /
paraṃ hi tadgocaraṃ vā jñānamabhyupeyeta, arthakriyānirbhāsaṃ vā jñānam, tadgocaranāntarīyakārthāntaradarśanaṃ vā /
tacca sarvaṃ svato 'navadhāritaprāmāṇyamākulaṃ sat kathaṃ pūrvaṃ pravartakaṃ jñānamanākulayet? svato vāsya prāmāṇye kimaparāddhaṃ pravatākajñānena yena tasminnapi tanna syāt /
na ca prāmāṇyaṃ jñāyate svataḥ ityāveditam /
yadā ca saṃvedanaprāmāṇyamaktena krameṇa duradhigamaṃ tadā kaiva kathendriyādīnāmavyabhicārisaṃvedanakāryavyaṅgyapramāṇabhāvānām?
tadeva dṛṣṭārthāḥ pramāṇabhṛtāṃ vyavahārā bhavantu sandehādapi yathātathā, adṛṣṭārthāstu bahuvittavyāyāyāsasādhyā vaidikā vyavahārā dattajalā/jalayaḥ prasaktāḥ /
tasmāt pramāṇādipadārthatattvajñāpanadvāreṇa na śāstraṃ niḥśreyasena saṃbadhyata iti /
seyamāśaṅkā prāmāṇyajñānopāyakathanenādivākyena bhāṣyakṛtā nirākṛtā /
tathā hi pramāṇamarthavaditi nityayoge matup /
nityatā cāvyabhicāritā /
tenārthāvyabhicārītyarthaḥ /
iyameva cārthāvyabhicāritā pramāṇasya yaddeśakālanarāvasthāntarāvisaṃvādo 'rthasvarūpaprakārayostadupadarśitayoḥ /
atra hetuḥ pravṛttisāmarthyāt samarthapravṛttijanakatvāt /
yadi punaretadarthavannābhaviṣyat, na samarthapravṛttimakariśyat, yathā pramāṇābhāsa iti vyatirekī hetuḥ /

children.translated_text: Or it is a reason combining both positive and negative concomitance.
Because for inference, being intrinsically valid, positive concomitance too is possible.

children.text: pravṛttijanakatvaṃ tu pramāṇasya na sākṣāt, kiṃ tvarthapratipattijananadvāreṇetyāha-- pramāṇato 'rthagratipattāviti /
children.translated_text: But the capacity of <s>pramāṇa</s> to generate activity is not direct; rather, it is through the medium of producing apprehension of the object — thus he says — 'from <s>pramāṇa</s>, the apprehension of the object.'
And the justification of all of this we shall present at the occasion of explaining the <s>Vārttika</s>. //

Here the following objection may be raised: that which teaches means of accomplishment that cannot be carried out is purposeless, like a statement teaching the adornment of a <s>takṣaka</s> serpent's crest with a jewel. / And this <s>śāstra</s> is of that kind. / For, to begin with, the true knowledge of the categories such as <s>prameya</s> (objects of knowledge) and the rest depends on the true knowledge of <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge). / For a <s>pramāṇa</s> whose reality has not been ascertained cannot, merely by its capacity to produce cognition, suffice for the ascertainment of its own object, since that much is common to the semblance of <s>pramāṇa</s> as well; rather, [it can do so] through its non-deviating nature, co-extensive with its capacity to produce cognition. / That alone is the validity of <s>pramāṇa</s>. / And that cannot be ascertained. / And because of the inability to ascertain it, <s>prameya</s> and the rest are difficult to ascertain. / For is the validity of a cognition ascertained intrinsically or extrinsically? / Not the first alternative. / Indeed, cognition, which is not self-aware, cannot grasp even itself, let alone its own validity. / Nor can another cognition grasp 'that is a cognition,' and certainly not its non-deviating nature. / And mere cognition-hood is common to the semblance [of cognition] — so validity is not ascertained intrinsically. / By this, the ascertainment of non-deviation is also addressed for the self-cognition theory. / Nor extrinsically. / For the external [factor] would be either a cognition having that [cognition] as its object, or a cognition manifesting successful activity, or the observation of another object necessarily connected with the object of that [cognition]. / And all of this, being confused because its validity has not been intrinsically ascertained, how could it render the prior cognition that motivates [action] unconfused? / Or if its validity is intrinsic, what offense has the motivating cognition committed that the same [intrinsic validity] should not apply to it? / And it has been stated that validity is not known intrinsically. / And when the validity of awareness is thus difficult to ascertain by the stated method, what need is there to speak of the sense organs and the like, whose validity as <s>pramāṇas</s> is to be inferred through the effect of non-deviating awareness? / Let then the transactions of those who hold <s>pramāṇas</s> be directed toward seen [empirical] purposes — they proceed even from doubt, as they may — but the Vedic transactions directed toward unseen purposes, which require the expenditure of much wealth and effort, would be undermined. / Therefore, the <s>śāstra</s> cannot be connected with <s>niḥśreyasa</s> through the means of making known the reality of the categories such as <s>pramāṇa</s>. / This objection has been refuted by the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> through the opening statement, by describing the means of knowing validity. / For <s>pramāṇa</s> possesses its object — the affix <s>matup</s> is in the sense of invariable connection. / And invariability means non-deviation. / Thus the meaning is: that which does not deviate from its object. / And this non-deviation of <s>pramāṇa</s> from its object is the non-discordance — in other conditions of place, time, person, and circumstance — of the form and manner of the object as indicated by it. / Here the reason is: from the capacity of activity — from the capacity to generate effective activity. / For if this [pramāṇa] did not possess its object, it would not have generated effective activity, just as a semblance of <s>pramāṇa</s> [does not] — this is the negative concomitant reason.

children.text:
syādetat /
bhavantu pramāṇādayaḥ padārthāḥ śakyajñānāḥ, śāstreṇa tu te nābhidhīyanta iti na niḥśreyasena saṃgatiḥ śāstrasyetvata āha--śāstrasya puruṣaśreyo 'bhidhāyakatvāt /
yadyapi śreyo duḥkhanivṛttimātyantikīṃ vakṣyati, tathāpi sopāyaiva sā atra śreyaḥśabdena vivakṣitā, tanmātrasya śāstrāviṣayatvāt /
tadayamarthaḥ /
śāstraṃ tāvadetat puruṣaśreyaḥ sahopāyenābhidhatta ityanubhavasiddha sadaśakyānuṣṭhānatayāpavaditavyam /
sā cedaśakyānuṣṭhānatāpanītā pramāṇata ityādinā saṃhitaṃ niḥśreyasena saha śāstramiti /
śāstrasyetyādi grahaṇakavākyaṃ vivṛṇoti--śāstraṃ punarityādinā upabhogāt prakṣayeṇetyantena /
pramāṇādivācakapadagrahaṇena tallakṣaṇāni ca tatparīkṣāśvopalakṣayati /
tathā ca pañcādhyāyī śāstramityaṅktamityavirodhaḥ /
pañcādhyācītyanena vyūhaḥ samūhināmucitānupūrvī /
upalakṣakapadasvarūpamāha-- padaṃ punarita /
emasmṛtisamārūḍhā varṇā ekārthapratipādanāvacchinnāḥ samūhaḥ /
evaṃ svārthasmṛtyavāntaravyāpārāṇāṃ sūtrapadānāṃ nānāpadārthaviśiṣṭaikapadārtharūpavākyārthapratyāyanakāryāvacchinnānāṃ samūho veditavyaḥ /
evaṃ ca kvacit kenacidarthenaikena sūtravākyānāmekavākyatvaṃ samūhaḥ prakaraṇam /
children.translated_text: And thus, somewhere, the collection of <s>sūtra</s>-sentences having unity of sentence-meaning through some single meaning is a section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>).
And a collection of sections through some coherence of their own meanings is a session (<s>āhnika</s>).
The same should be understood in each case.
And we shall briefly indicate these coherences of meaning among sections, sessions, and chapters in their respective places. //

It may be objected: let the categories such as <s>pramāṇa</s> be knowable, but since they are not expressed by the <s>śāstra</s>, there is no connection of the <s>śāstra</s> with <s>niḥśreyasa</s> — therefore he says: because the <s>śāstra</s> expresses what is conducive to the person's highest good. / Although he will say that the highest good is the absolute cessation of suffering, nevertheless, it is only that [cessation] together with its means that is intended here by the word 'highest good,' since the mere [cessation] alone is not within the scope of the <s>śāstra</s>. / The meaning is this: this <s>śāstra</s> expresses the person's highest good together with its means — this is established by experience and cannot be dismissed as incapable of being carried out. / And that charge of incapacity to be carried out has been removed by [the statement] 'from <s>pramāṇa</s>' — [thus] the <s>śāstra</s> is connected with <s>niḥśreyasa</s>. / He elaborates the introductory statement of the <s>śāstra</s> — 'the <s>śāstra</s> again' and so on up to 'by exhaustion through experience.' / By the use of the word denoting the categories such as <s>pramāṇa</s>, their definitions and their examination are also indicated. / And thus the five chapters constitute the <s>śāstra</s> — so there is no contradiction. / 'Five chapters' indicates the arrangement — the proper order of the aggregated [topics]. / He states the nature of the constituent word — 'the word, again.' / Letters that have mounted upon a single memory, delimited by the capacity to convey a single meaning, are a collection [i.e., a word]. / Similarly, the collection of <s>sūtra</s>-words, which have the intermediate function of occasioning the recollection of their own meanings, delimited by the function of conveying a sentence-meaning that has the form of a single meaning qualified by multiple word-meanings, should be understood.

children.text: tadevaṃ śāstrasvarūpaṃ darṃśayitvā nāntareṇa tadarthakathanaṃ puruṣaśreyo 'bhidhāyakatvamasrū sidhyitīti tadarthaṃ kathayati-- tatpadārthā iti /
nanu pramāṇādīnāṃ pratinaramānantyena durjñānatvamiti tadavasthamevānarthakyaṃ śāstrasya prasaktamityata āha -- ṣoḍaśātmānaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, since the categories such as <s>pramāṇa</s> are difficult to know due to their infinity relative to each person, the purposelessness of the <s>śāstra</s> remains just as it was — therefore he says — 'having sixteen aspects.'

children.text: ātmā svabhāvaḥ pramāṇādīnāṃ pramāṇatvādisāmānyaviśeṣa iti yāvat /
children.translated_text: The <s>ātman</s> (self/nature) is the inherent nature of <s>pramāṇa</s> and the rest — meaning their generic and specific characteristics such as being a <s>pramāṇa</s> and so forth.
This is what has been stated:

children.text: āntargaṇikabhedādānantye 'pi svasāmānyaviśeṣaiḥ saṃgṛhītā na durjñānā iti yato 'sya padārthāḥ pramāṇādayaḥ, tat tasmāt śāstraṃ puruṣaśreyo 'bhidhatte //
children.translated_text: Even though infinite due to internal sub-classifications, since they are comprehended through their own generic and specific characteristics and thus not difficult to know — since its categories are <s>pramāṇa</s> and the rest — therefore the <s>śāstra</s> (science) teaches what is beneficial for a person.

Having thus shown the nature of the <s>śāstra</s>, since the capacity to express the person's highest good cannot be established without the exposition of its meaning, he expounds the meaning for that purpose — 'those categories' and so on.

children.text:
syādetat /
pramāṇādayaḥ padārthāḥ prāmāṇikā aprāmāṇikā vā? aprāmāṇikatve kalpanāmātranirmitāḥ kathaṃ niḥśreyasāya kalpante? na ya ṣoḍaśātmānaḥ kalpanāḥ kośasyānantaprasaratvāt /
prāmāṇikatve vā pramāṇādeva tatsiddheḥ śāstrasya vaiyarthyamityata āha--pratyakṣeti /
pratyakṣānumānādhigatagrahaṇenāprāmāṇikatvaṃ niṣiddham /
ata eva vastutattvamiti /
pramāṇādayaḥ padārthā nopamānaviṣayā iti nopamānamupanyastam /
yadyapi prameyamātmādyapavargāntalakṣaṇamāgamikaṃ tathāpyāgamasyāptapraṇetṛkatayā tatrāpi mūlabhūtamanumānaṃ pratyakṣaṃ vāstīti pratyakṣānumāne eva darśite /
nanūktaṃ prāmāṇikatve śāstravaiyarthyamityata āha-- tasya viṣaya iti /
vyavaharamāṇā api pramāṇairlaukikā vainayikabuddhivirahiṇo naitān padārthān viviñcate /
aviviktāścete na niḥśreyasāya kalpanta iti anadhigatetyaṅktam /
ādhyātmikī śaktiḥ śuśrūṣādiḥ /
puruṣatyuktam /
tatra vivakṣitaṃ puruṣaviśeṣaṃ grahītuṃ saṃbhavinaḥ puruṣaprakārān darśayati--puruṣaḥ punariti /
heyaṃ darśayati--tatreti /
upādeyānāha-- itara iti /
apekṣā jijñāsā /
sā sandigdhasya tāvadasti viṣayasya /
vipratipannasya tu sākṣiṇāṃ purato jalpavitaṇḍābhyāṃ viṣyamāṇasya vigalite 'haṅkāre sandigdhasya sa/jātajijñāsasya sāpekṣasya sataḥ /
apratipannasyāpi kenacit prakāreṇa sandehamāpādya sāpekṣīkṛtasya pratipādyatā /
tadidamuktak--itare sāpekṣāḥ santaḥ pratipādyā iti /
asandigdho 'pi tattvapratipādanāya kārūṇikena sandigadhaḥ kṛtvā pratipādyata iti /
tat kiṃ sāpekṣamādhikṛtya śāstraṃ pravṛttam? tathā ca pramātaṇāṃ na pramāṇāntare pravṛttiḥ syādityata āha-- te yadeti /
kañcid viṣayaṃ jijñāsavo yedandriyādyapekṣante, tadā pratyakṣeṇa pratipādyāḥ /
evamuttaramapi yojyam /
ayamabhisandhiḥ, na dṛṣṭaprayojanopayogivastuvijñāsā ihāpekṣābhimatā, kiṃ tu niḥśreyasopayogipadārthajijñāsā /
sā cāsminneva śāstre pravṛttihetuḥ nānyatra /
tadidamuktam-- yadā punariti /
paramapuruṣārthayasadhanaṃ tu jijñāsava iti śeṣaḥ /
ihābhimataṃ śreyo nirdhārayituṃ śreyomātrapramārān āha--śreyaḥ punaḥ sukhamahitanivṛttiśca /
tatrāpyavāntaraprakārānāha--tacchreyaḥ sukhanduḥkhanivṛttiśca bhidyamānaṃ dvidhā vyavatiṣṭhate /
tadāha-- dṛṣṭādṛṣṭabhedena /
na vyāsajya kiṃ tu pratyekamityāha-- dṛṣṭaṃ sukha strakcandanavanitādibhogajanma /
adṛṣṭaṃ sukhaṃ svargādi /
evaṃ ca duḥkhanivṛttirapi śreyo dṛṣṭāmadṛṣṭaṃ ceti yojanīyaṃ cakāralopāt /
ahitanivṛtteḥ śreyasa ātyantikānātyantikatvena dṛṣṭādṛṣṭasya bhedamāha--ahitanivṛttirapīti /
abhimataṃ śreyo nirdhārayati--ātyantikīti /
punariti nirdhāraṇamavadyotayati /
ātyantikatvaṃ nirvṛtternivṛttasya punaranutpādaḥ /
sa ca kāryakāraṇatadanuṣaṅginivṛttyā lakṣyate /
na hyakāraṇaṃ kāryaṃ jāyate /
tadidamuktam-- ekaviṃśatiprabhadabhinduḥkhahānyeti /
gauṇamukhyabhedena caikaviṃśateḥ śarīradīnāṃ duḥkhatvaprakārānāha--evaviṃśatīti /
ṣaṣṭhamindriyaṃ manaḥ /
tasya viṣaya icchādveṣaprayatnāḥ /
yadyapi viṣayaḥ śarīramapi tathāpyanyathāsya duḥkhahetubhāva ityāha śarīramiti śarīrāvacchinna ātmapradeśo duḥkhāyatanamiti śarīraṃ duḥkhāyatanamuktam /
indriyaviṣayabuddhadīnāṃ duḥkhatvopacāre kāraṇamāha--indriyāṇīti /
tatrendriyāṇi tāvad gandhādiviṣayabodhanāt, viṣayā bodhyatvāt /
buddhayastu sākṣād duḥkhasādhanānīti duḥkhatvenopacaryante /
saṃkhasya duḥkhatvopacārabījamāha--sukhamiti /
sādhanapāratantyaṃ kṣayitvaṃ kāma iti duḥkhahetavaḥ sakalasukhānasaṅginaḥ, tasmāt sukhamapi duḥkhānuṣaṅgi /
uktaprakāraduḥkhahānasādhanamāha--tasya hāniriti /
saṃśayāditattvajñānapariśodhitaparamanyāyamārgaḥ khalu heyopādeyabhūtadvādaśavidhaprameyatattvaparibhāvanabhavā prasaṃkhyānena nirmṛṣṭanikhilapravṛttihetudoṣānuṣaṅgo 'pravartamāno na śarīrendriyādihetumapūrvadharmādharmapracayamātanoti /
anādi bhavaparamparopattaṃ ca dharmādharmapracayamanantamapyaniyatavipākasamayamapi prasaṃkhyānaparipākaprabhāvāt paritastattadupabhogabhāginaḥ kāyān nirmāya tatttphalopabhāgāt prakṣiṇoti /
acintyasāmarthyātiśayo hi samādhiḥ /
yathāhuratrabhavantaḥ,
ko hi yogaprabhāvādṛte agastya ica samudraṃ pibati, sa iva ca daṇḍakāraṇyaṃ sṛjati?

children.translated_text: In the <s>Yogabhāṣya</s>, 8.10.
Thus.
This absolute cessation of suffering is the highest good (<s>śreyas</s>).
This is what was stated — because the <s>śāstra</s> teaches what is beneficial for a person.

One might object: Are the categories such as <s>pramāṇa</s> and the rest established by valid means or not? If not established by valid means, being mere fabrications of imagination, how can they serve the highest good? For these sixteen categories are not mere imaginations, since the scope of imagination is unlimited.
Or, if they are established by valid means, then since their establishment comes from <s>pramāṇa</s> itself, the <s>śāstra</s> would be purposeless — therefore he says 'perception' (<s>pratyakṣa</s>).
By the statement 'apprehended through perception and inference,' the claim that they lack valid foundation is refuted.
Hence 'the reality of things' (<s>vastutattvam</s>).
Since the categories such as <s>pramāṇa</s> are not objects of analogy (<s>upamāna</s>), analogy is not presented.
Although <s>prameya</s> (the knowable), characterized from <s>ātman</s> through <s>apavarga</s> (liberation), is based on scripture, nevertheless since scripture has trustworthy authors, inference or perception which is fundamental to it also exists — therefore only perception and inference are shown.
To the objection that if established by valid means the <s>śāstra</s> would be purposeless, he says 'its subject matter.'
Even ordinary people who operate with <s>pramāṇas</s>, lacking disciplined intelligence, do not discriminate these categories.
Since undiscriminated, they do not serve the highest good — hence the word 'not [previously] ascertained.'
The inner capacity refers to the desire to learn (<s>śuśrūṣā</s>) and the like.
Regarding the person, it has been stated.
To enable grasping the intended specific type of person, he shows the possible types of persons — 'a person, moreover.'
He shows what is to be rejected — 'among these.'
He states what is to be adopted — 'the other.'
<s>Apekṣā</s> means the desire to know (<s>jijñāsā</s>).
That exists first for a doubtful subject matter.
But for one who holds a contrary position, when debated through <s>jalpa</s> (disputation) and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavil) before witnesses, once pride has dissolved, having become doubtful, having developed the desire to know, being expectant —
Even one who has not engaged at all can be made expectant by inducing doubt through some means, and then instructed.
This is what was stated — 'the others, being expectant, are to be instructed.'
Even one who is not in doubt can be made doubtful by a compassionate teacher for the purpose of teaching the truth, and then instructed.
Then is the <s>śāstra</s> undertaken only for the expectant? In that case, <s>pramāṇas</s> would not function for other <s>pramāṇas</s> — therefore he says 'they, when.'
When those desiring to know some subject matter depend on the senses and the like, then they are to be instructed through perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>).
The same should be applied to what follows.
The intended meaning is: the desire to know objects useful for seen purposes is not what is meant here by 'expectation,' but rather the desire to know the categories useful for the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>).
And that is the cause of engagement in this <s>śāstra</s> alone, not elsewhere.
This is what was stated — 'when, however.'
The supplement is: 'desiring to know the means to the supreme human goal (<s>paramapuruṣārtha</s>).'
To determine the intended good, he states the types of good in general — 'the good, moreover, is happiness and the cessation of the undesirable.'
He states the subtypes therein — 'that good, being divided into happiness and the cessation of suffering, stands as twofold.'
Therefore he says — 'by the distinction of seen and unseen.'
Not collectively but individually, he says — 'seen happiness is that born from the enjoyment of garlands, sandalwood, butter, and the like.'
Unseen happiness is heaven (<s>svarga</s>) and the like.
And similarly, the cessation of suffering as a good should also be understood as seen and unseen — the conjunction 'and' being elided.
He states the distinction of seen and unseen regarding the absolute and non-absolute cessation of the undesirable — 'the cessation of the undesirable also.'
He determines the intended good — 'the absolute.'
The word 'moreover' highlights the determination.
Absoluteness of cessation means the non-recurrence of what has ceased.
And that is characterized by the cessation of effects, causes, and their accompaniments.
For no effect arises without a cause.
This is what was stated — 'the destruction of suffering in its twenty-one forms.'
He states the modes in which the twenty-one items beginning with the body are suffering, in terms of primary and secondary senses — 'the twenty-one.'
The sixth sense-organ is <s>manas</s> (mind).
Its objects are desire (<s>icchā</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), and effort (<s>prayatna</s>).
Although the body is also an object, its being a cause of suffering is different — therefore he says 'the body': the region of the <s>ātman</s> delimited by the body is the seat of suffering, hence the body is called the seat of suffering.
He states the reason for the figurative attribution of suffering to the sense-organs, objects, cognitions, and the like — 'the sense-organs.'
Among these, the sense-organs, because they cause awareness of objects like smell and the like; the objects, because they are what is known.
But cognitions are directly the instruments of suffering — hence they are figuratively called suffering.
He states the basis for the figurative attribution of suffering to pleasure — 'pleasure.'
Dependence on means, transience, desire — these causes of suffering accompany all pleasures; therefore pleasure too is accompanied by suffering.
He states the means of eliminating suffering of the described type — 'the cessation of that.'
One who has purified the supreme path of <s>Nyāya</s> through the true knowledge of doubt and the rest, contemplating the twelve <s>prameyas</s> (knowables) that are to be rejected and adopted, through <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s> (meditative discernment), having the attachment to all causes of activity completely cleansed, no longer acting, does not accumulate the unseen merit and demerit (<s>apūrva-dharma-adharma</s>) that cause body, sense-organs, and the like.
And the accumulation of merit and demerit acquired through beginningless series of births, though infinite and though of indeterminate time of fruition, through the power of the maturation of <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s>, having fashioned bodies capable of experiencing each respective result, is exhausted through the experience of those results.
For the power of <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) is of inconceivable excellence.
As the venerable ones say:
Who indeed, other than by the power of <s>yoga</s>, drinks the ocean like <s>Agastya</s>, and creates the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest like him?

children.text:
syādetat /
kevalasya duḥkhasyātyantikī nivṛttiḥ śreyaḥ puyaṣapravṛttyaṅgam /
iyaṃ tu duḥkhavat sukhasyāpyātyantikī nivṛttiriti kathaṃ śreyaḥ, kathaṃ ca prekṣāvatpravṛttyaṅgamityata āha--puruṣā rāgādimanta iti /
yadyapi rāgādimatā puthagjanānāmetanna pravṛttyaṅgam, te hi madhuviṣasaṃpṛktamapyannaṃ madhuratayā āpātaramaṇīyaṃ viṣaviṅgattu mārayatu mā va mīmaradupayu/jmahe tāvadāpātasukham, ko hi hastagataṃ pādagataṃ karotīti vicintyopabhu/jate /
vivekinastu āyatimālocayantaḥ svargamapi kupitaphaṇiphaṇāmaṇḍalacchāyapratima ityapajahati /
tena mā bhūdetad rāgādimatāṃ pravṛttyaṅgam, vivekināṃ tu bhaviṣyati /
avivekināmapi cāpratipannavipratipannānāṃ vivekādhānopayaḥ pūrvamāveditaḥ /

children.translated_text: And here, only discernment (<s>viveka</s>) and dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) are regarded as the basis for engagement with the <s>śāstra</s>.
Engagement is of two kinds: uniform and twofold.

children.text: puruṣabhedo rāgavairāgyābhyām, prāptavyasya sarvasya sukhasya duḥkhasaṃbhedenāniṣṭapakṣanikṣepādaniṣṭapratiṣedhārthaiva pravṛttirvivekināmekarūpaiva /
children.translated_text: The distinction among persons is due to attachment (<s>rāga</s>) and dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>); since all attainable pleasure is accompanied by suffering, the engagement of the discerning, aimed solely at negating the undesirable through casting aside the unwanted aspect, is of one form alone.
But the engagement of the undiscerning is said to be of two forms.

One might object: The absolute cessation of suffering alone is the good and the basis for a person's engagement. But this [liberation] involves the absolute cessation of pleasure as well as suffering — so how is it the good, and how can it be the basis for engagement by a discerning person? Therefore he says — 'persons possessed of attachment (<s>rāga</s>) and the like.'
Although for ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjanāḥ</s>) possessed of attachment and the like this is not a basis for engagement — for they, even when food is mixed with honey and poison, thinking 'it is sweet and initially delightful, let the poison kill or not kill, let us at least enjoy the immediate pleasure; who indeed makes what is in the hand go to the foot?' — reflect thus and consume it.
But the discerning ones (<s>vivekinaḥ</s>), considering the future, reject even heaven (<s>svarga</s>) as comparable to the shade of an angry serpent's hood-jewel canopy.
Therefore, let this not be the basis for engagement of those with attachment; it will be so for the discerning.
And even for the undiscerning — those who have not engaged or who hold contrary positions — the usefulness of instilling discernment has been previously explained.

children.text:
tadanena prapañcena pramāṇato 'rthapratipattavityādivākyasya tātparyamabhidhāya tadavayavaṃ pravṛttisāmarthyāditi vivarītuṃ bhūmimāracayati--pravṛtterapīti /
dṛṣṭaṃ pravṛttisāmarthyaṃ heturiti rāgādimatpravṛttisāmarthyamupanyastam, na tu vītarāgānām/na hi tatpravṛtterniḥ- śreyasādhgimalakṣaṇaphalasaṃbandho dṛṣṭo niḥśreyasasyālaukikatvāt /
pramāṇasyārthavadanarthakatvād ityayuktam, pramāṇamanarthakamiti hi vipratiṣiddhamityata āha-- pramāṇaṃ tāvaditi /
na hyapramāṇamapramāṇamiti gṛhītaṃ pravṛttyai kalpate /
kiṃ tarhi? pramāṇamiti /
na cāpramāṇe pramāṇābhimāno vinā pramāṇādisādharmyāditi tatsādharmyaṃ pṛcchati--kiṃ punariti /
uttaram--sāmānyaparicchedakatvam /
tadvivṛṇeti--pramāṇenāpīti /
rajatavijñānamapi purovarti śuklabhāsvaraṃ saddravyaṃ paricchinatti, śuktikājñānamapi /
kevalamekasminnava viṣaye rajatasamāropāpavādābhyāṃ buddhacorvādhakabhāva iti bhāvaḥ /
tadevamubhayataḥ pravṛttiḥ samarthāt pramāṇādeva, nāpramāṇādarthavyabhicāriṇa ityāha--so 'yaṃ pramāteti /
children.translated_text: Thus, in both cases, engagement proceeds from a capable <s>pramāṇa</s> alone, not from a non-<s>pramāṇa</s> that deviates from the object — therefore he says 'this very knower (<s>pramātā</s>).'
And from this it is established that capable engagement is invariably concomitant with [the exclusion of] what is purposeless — this is the intended meaning.

children.text: tathā ca samarthā pravṛttiranarthavadvacatirekasaṃpannapramāṇasyārthavattve heturityāha--tasyāḥ samarthāyāḥ pravṛtterhetoḥ punaḥ pramāṇasyārthavattvamarthāvyabhicāritvam /
children.translated_text: And thus, capable engagement being the reason, the meaningfulness of <s>pramāṇa</s> — that is, its non-deviation from the object — is established as possessing invariable concomitance with the exclusion of the purposeless, therefore he says — 'of that capable engagement as the reason, the meaningfulness of <s>pramāṇa</s> is its non-deviation from the object.'
But incapable [engagement], even though immediately following, is not connected [with the result], due to the absence of proper application.

Having thus stated through this elaboration the purport of the statement 'the ascertainment of objects through <s>pramāṇa</s>' and the like, he prepares the ground for explaining its component 'from the capacity of engagement' — 'of engagement also.'
The capacity of engagement as a visible cause refers to the capacity for engagement of those possessed of attachment and the like, not of the dispassionate. For the connection of their engagement with the result characterized as the means to the highest good is not observed, since the highest good is supramundane.
The [objection] that <s>pramāṇa</s> would be purposeless because it deals with what is purposeful is incorrect, for saying '<s>pramāṇa</s> is purposeless' is self-contradictory — therefore he says 'a <s>pramāṇa</s>, in the first place.'
For what is apprehended as 'not a <s>pramāṇa</s>, not a <s>pramāṇa</s>' does not serve as a basis for engagement.
What then? Only what is [apprehended as] a <s>pramāṇa</s>.
And there cannot be the notion of being a <s>pramāṇa</s> regarding what is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> without similarity to <s>pramāṇa</s> and the rest — so he asks about that similarity: 'what, moreover?'
The answer: 'the capacity to determine the universal.'
He elaborates on that — 'even by a <s>pramāṇa</s>.'
Even the cognition of silver determines a present thing that is white, shining, and a real substance — as does the cognition of a shell.
The only difference is that regarding one and the same object, through the superimposition and sublation of silver, the cognitions stand in the relation of sublated and sublating — this is the meaning.

children.text:
saṃpratyādivākyamākṣeptumanuvadati-- pramāṇata iti /
ākṣipati--paraspareti /
samādhatte--neti /
ākṣepavākyaṃ vibhajate--yadi pramāṇata iti /
na tāvadarthapratipattiḥ pravṛttiheturapi tu tadviniścayaḥ /
na ca tanmātram, api tu tadarthajātīyasya śreyohetutāmasakṛdupalabhya saṃpratyupalabhyamānasyārthasya tajjātīyatayā śreyohetubhāvānumānasahito viniścayaḥ pravṛttihetuḥ /
seyaṃ śreyaḥsādhanatānumānasahitā pramāṇato 'rthapratipattirviniścatiḥ samarthapravṛttinimittamuktā /
na cārthavinaścayaḥ prāmāṇyāvadhāraṇamantareṇa, prāmāṇyāvadhāraṇaṃ ca śreyohetutānumānanimittavyāptigrahaṇaṃ ca na samarthāṃ pravṛttiṃ vinā, na ca samarthā pravṛttistābhyāṃ vivaneti parasparāśrayatā /
tadidamuktam, cadi pūrvaṃ pramāṇato 'rthapratipattiḥ rviniścitirapekṣitopayatānumānasahitā pravṛttisamārthyamantareṇa kimiti pratipadyate niścinoti apekṣitopāya eveti ca toyameveti ceti? samādhānaṃ vibhajate--tacca naivamiti /
yat tāvaduktam, pramāṇasya duravadhāraṇatvādarthaviniścayābhāvānna pravṛttisāmarthyamiti, tatra brūmaḥ--satyam, na svataḥ prāmāṇyaṃ śakyāvadhāraṇam /
paratastu dṛṣṭārtheṣvanabhyāsadaśāpanneṣu pravṛttisāmathyadiva tad gamyate /
arthapratītyadhīnā tu pravṛttirnārthāvadhāraṇādhīnā, arthasandehādapi prekṣāvatāṃ pravṛtteḥ /
no khalūpāyatāvinaścayenāpi pravartamānā na anāgataphale sandihate /
tadamī saṃdihānā api pravartamānāḥ pravṛttisamārthyāt pramāṇasya tattvaṃ viniścatya tajjātīyasyānyasyābhyāsadaśapannasya pravṛttisamārthyāt prāgeva tajjātīyatvena liṅgena prāmājhayāvadhāraṇāt arthaviniścayena pravartante /
evaṃ ca dṛṣṭārthamantrāyurvedaprāmāṇyaṃ pravṛttisāmarthyenāvadhārya tajjātīyasyāptoktasyādṛṣṭārthasya vedasya vināpi pravṛttisāmarthyaṃ prāmāṇyāvadhāraṇamāptoktatvena nivedayiṣyate /
na ca phalajñānaṃ parīkṣyate prekṣāvaddhiḥ, tasya yādṛśatādṛśasyāpīṣṭatvādiṣṭalakṣaṇatvācca phalasya tatsādhanatvaṃ te parīkṣante /
tathā hi toyajñānam, pipāsostatra pravṛttiḥ, pravṛttasya tadāptiḥ, āptasya pānam, pānena codanyopaśāntirityetāvataiva pramātā kṛtī bhavati, na punarudanyopaśamamapi parīkṣate, tasya yādṛśatādṛśasyāpīṣṭatvāditi kecit /
vayaṃ tu brūmaḥ, phalajñānamapyabhyāsadaśāpannatayā tajjātīyatvena liṅgenāvadhṛtāvyabhicārameva /
evaṃ tatpūrvaṃ tatpūrvataraṃ tatpūrvatamamiti /
na ca saṃpratitanasya phalajñānasya prāmāṇyāvadhāraṇāyedānīmeva pūrvasya phalajñānasya tajjātīyatvena pramāṇyāvadhāraṇe satyanavastheti /
vācyam /
pūrvatarasādharmyeṇa pūrvameva pūrvasyāvadhṛtaprāmāṇyatvāt /
evaṃ pūrvatamasādharmyeṇa pūrvatarasya /
evaṃ tatpūrvasādharmyeṇa pūrvatamasyetyanāditayaivātra parihāraḥ /
eteṣu ca madhye yatphalajñānaṃ svapnādyupabhogatulyatayā śaṅkitavyabhicāraṃ tadanabhyāsadaśāpannam /
ataḥ pravṛttisāmarthyaṃ tatra prāmāṇyāvadhāraṇāya vinivaśanīyamityarthapratipattipravṛttisāmarthyayoranāditvamuktam /
anumānasya tu pravṛttisāmarthyaliṅgajanmano 'nyasya vā nirastasamastavyabhicāraśaṅkasya svata eva prāmāṇyamanumeyāvyabhicāriliṅgasamutthatvāt /
na hi liṅgākāra jñānaṃ liṅgaṃ vinā, na ca liṅgaṃ liṅginaṃ vineti svata eva gṛhītāvyabhicāliṅgasamutthaṃ niṣkampamupapadyate jñānam /
pratyakṣajñānaṃ tvarthādutpadyamānamapi na gṛhītāvyabhicārāt, api tu sattāmātreṇāvasthitāt /
na ca kāraṇāntarāṇyapīndriyādīni asyārthena gṛhītāvyabhicārāṇi na cārthenāvyabhicārāṇi /
śābdaṃ tu jñānu nārthādutpadyate,
tadabhāve 'pi sati śabde bhāvāt /
nāpi liṅgasyeva śabdasyārthāvyabhicāraḥ, kiṃ tu saṅketagrahaṇamātrāt padārthapratyāyanena vākyārthamadhigamayati śabdaḥ /
tasmāt pratyakṣaśābdavijñānayorna svato 'vyabhicāragraha iti /
pravṛttisāmarthyaṃ tajjātīyatvaṃ vā liṅgamarthāvyabhicārāyānusaraṇīyam, jñānagatatajjātīyatvaliṅgagrāhiṇaśca jñānasya mānasapratyakṣasya tādṛśasyādṛṣṭavyabhicāratayā parito nirastasamastavibhramāśaṅkasya svataḥ prāmāṇyamiti nānavasthā /
aitenopamānaṃ vyākhyātam /
saṃvedanasya cārthāvarubhicāritākathanena tatkāraṇānāmindriyādīnāmapi pramāṇatvamaktaṃ veditavyam /
na hyavyabhicārivijñānajanakatvādanyadeṣāṃ prāmāṇyam /
na cārthavyabhicāriṇāmindriyādīnāṃ kathamarthāvyabhicārivijñānajanakatvamiti sāṃpratam, kāraṇasvabhāniyogaparyanuyogayoraśakyatvāt /
tasmādarthasandehādanabhyāsadaśāpannāt pramāṇatā 'rthapratipattau pravṛttisamārthyasaṃbhavāt pravṛttisamārthyajñānasya cābhyāsadaśāpannasya tajjātīyatvena prāmāṇyānumānādanabhyāsadaśāpannasya tu pravṛttisāmarthyāntarajñānena prāmāṇyānumānādanāditvānnārthapratipravṛttisāmarthyayoḥ parasparāśrayatvamastīti /
arthasyāpekṣitopāyatānumānapravṛttisāmarthyayoḥ parasparāpekṣatvamavaśiṣyate /
tatrāpyanāditāparihāraḥ /
utpannamātrakasya hi bālakasya stanaṃ dṛṣṭvā prāgbhavīyastajjātīyāpekṣitānubhavajanitaḥ saṃskāra āvirasti /
tataśca smaraṇam /
tato 'pekṣitopāyatānumānam /
tataḥ pravṛttiḥ /
tatastasyāḥ sāmarthyam /
evaṃ pūrvasmin pūrvasmin janmanītyanāditayā na bījāṅkuravat parasparāpekṣiteti /
children.translated_text: Thus in each preceding birth— through beginninglessness, there is no mutual dependence, like the seed and the sprout /
The apprehension of the object— /
The meaning is: the apprehension of the object and the apprehension of the object's capacity as a required means /
Therefore everything is well-established //

Now he restates the initial statement in order to raise an objection— 'from <s>pramāṇa</s>' /
He raises the objection— 'mutual' /
He resolves— 'no' /
He analyzes the objection statement— 'if from <s>pramāṇa</s>' /
It is not the apprehension of the object that is the cause of activity, but rather the ascertainment of it /
And it is not that alone, but rather the ascertainment accompanied by the inference of the capacity to produce well-being of the present object, based on having repeatedly observed that things of the same type produce well-being, recognizing the present object as being of that same type— that is the cause of activity /
This apprehension of the object from <s>pramāṇa</s>, accompanied by inference of its capacity to produce well-being, the ascertainment, has been stated as the ground for effective activity /
And ascertainment of the object is not possible without the determination of validity, and the determination of validity and the grasping of the concomitance that is the basis for inferring the capacity to produce well-being are not possible without effective activity, and effective activity is not possible without those two— thus there is mutual dependence /
This is what was stated: 'if first there is apprehension of the object from <s>pramāṇa</s>, the ascertainment accompanied by inference of the required means— without the capacity for activity, how does one apprehend, ascertain that it is indeed the required means, and that it is this very thing?' He analyzes the resolution— 'and that is not so' /
As to what was said, that because <s>pramāṇa</s> is difficult to determine, there is no ascertainment of the object and hence no capacity for activity— to that we say: true, the validity cannot be determined intrinsically /
But extrinsically, in the case of objects whose results have been seen and which have not reached the stage of unfamiliarity, that [validity] is understood through the capacity for activity /
Activity depends on the apprehension of the object, not on the determination of the object; for even from doubt about the object, discerning persons engage in activity /
Indeed, even one who acts based on the determination of the means does not cease to doubt about the future result /
These persons, even while doubting, engaging in activity, having ascertained the reality of <s>pramāṇa</s> through the capacity for activity, and having determined the validity of another thing of the same type that has reached the stage of familiarity through the mark of being of the same type even before the capacity for activity— they act with the ascertainment of the object /
And thus, having determined the validity of mantras and <s>Āyurveda</s> whose results are seen through the capacity for activity, the determination of the validity of the <s>Veda</s>, whose results are unseen but which is of the same type and spoken by a trustworthy person, even without the capacity for activity, will be conveyed through the property of being spoken by a trustworthy person /
And the knowledge of the result is not what discerning persons examine; for the result, being desired whatever its nature, and having the defining characteristic of being desired— they examine whether something is a means to that /
For example, the knowledge of water, the activity of a thirsty person toward it, the attainment of it by the one who has acted, the drinking of it once attained, and the quenching of thirst by drinking— with just this much the knower is satisfied, and does not further examine the quenching of thirst, since the result is desired whatever its nature— so say some /
But we say: the knowledge of the result too, having reached the stage of familiarity, has its non-deviation ascertained through the mark of being of the same type /
Thus its prior, its prior's prior, its most prior— and so on /
And there is no infinite regress in determining the validity of the present knowledge of the result by determining the validity of the prior knowledge of the result through being of the same type right now /
It should be said: /
Because the validity of the prior has already been determined through similarity to the earlier one /
Thus the validity of the earlier through similarity to the earliest /
Thus the validity of the earliest through similarity to what preceded it— the resolution here is through beginninglessness itself /
And among these, that knowledge of the result which is suspected of deviation due to its resemblance to the experience in dreams and the like— that has not reached the stage of familiarity /
Therefore, the capacity for activity must be applied for determining its validity— thus the beginninglessness of both the apprehension of the object and the capacity for activity has been stated /
But for inference, which is born from the capacity-for-activity mark or another mark whose every suspicion of deviation has been removed, validity is intrinsic, because it arises from a mark that is an unfailing indicator of the inferable /
For cognition in the form of a mark does not exist without the mark, and the mark does not exist without the thing marked— therefore cognition arisen from a mark whose non-deviation has been intrinsically grasped is established as unshakeable /
But perceptual cognition, though arising from the object, does not arise from one whose non-deviation has been grasped, but merely from one that exists /
And the other causes such as the sense organs also do not have their non-deviation from the object grasped, nor are they unfailing with respect to the object /
But verbal cognition does not arise from the object, since it exists even in the absence of that [object] when the word is present /
Nor does the word have non-deviation from the object like a mark; rather, the word conveys the sentence-meaning merely through the grasping of convention and the indication of word-meaning /
Therefore, for perceptual and verbal cognitions, there is no intrinsic grasping of non-deviation /
The capacity for activity or being of the same type must be followed as a mark of non-deviation from the object, and the cognition that grasps the mark of being of the same type in the cognition— that mental perception (<s>mānasapratyakṣa</s>), being of such a type that no deviation has been seen, having completely removed all suspicion of error on every side, has intrinsic validity— so there is no infinite regress /
By this, <s>upamāna</s> (analogy) has been explained /
And by stating the non-deviation of cognition from the object, it should be understood that the validity of the causes such as the sense organs has also been stated /
For their validity is nothing other than being the producers of non-deviating cognition /
And the objection that how can sense organs that deviate from the object produce cognition that does not deviate— that is not valid, because of the impossibility of the demand for an explanation of the intrinsic nature of causes /
Therefore, since from doubt about the object that has not reached the stage of familiarity, validity in the apprehension of the object is possible through the capacity for activity, and since the knowledge of the capacity for activity, having reached the stage of familiarity, leads to the inference of validity through being of the same type, and for what has not reached the stage of familiarity, the inference of validity is through the knowledge of another instance of the capacity for activity, and because of beginninglessness— there is no mutual dependence between the apprehension of the object and the capacity for activity /
There remains the mutual dependence between the inference of the object's capacity as a required means and the capacity for activity /
There too, the resolution is through beginninglessness /
For a newborn infant, upon seeing the breast, a latent impression arises, born from experiences of required objects of the same type in previous lives /
From that comes memory /
From that comes inference of the capacity as a required means /
From that comes activity /
From that comes the capacity of that [activity] /

children.text:
tadanenoktena krameṇa pramāṇato 'rthapratipatāvityasya śāstrānusandhānavākyatva tātparyaṃ ca samāhitam /
idānīmasyaiva tātparyāntaramāha--pramāṇapravṛtyorveti /
tatredamamāśāṅkyate munirhi pratyakṣasaṃśayādivyutpādanadvāreṇa sākṣāccānena śāstreṇānvīkṣikpā heyopādeyabhāvāvasthitadvādaśavidhaprameyavyutpādakaṃ nyāyamanumānaparanāmānaṃ niḥśreyasasiddhaye vyutpādayāṃbabhūva /
na ca nyāyataḥ pramāṇāt prameyatattvaniścayamātrānniḥśreyasādhigamaḥ /
api tvādyantavarjjaṃ daśānāṃ prameyāṇāṃ duḥkhasaṃjñābhāvanam, ātmanaśca yāthātmyabhāvanamityādibhyaḥ pravṛttibhya ātmatattvasākṣātkāravairāgyaparipākakrameṇāpūrvayordharmādharmayoranutpādenotpannayośvopabhogāt /
prakṣayeṇeti /
tathā ca niḥśreyasaṃ pratyantaraṅgatvāt pramāṇānnyāyāt pravṛttireva balīyasī, na nyāyaḥ /
tasmāt pravṛttireva vyutpādanīyā na pramāṇaṃ niḥśreyasaheturapi pravṛtterantaraṅgatvāt /
tatredabhupatiṣṭhate pramāṇato 'rthapratipattau satyā pravṛtteḥ samārthyaṃ phalenābhisaṃbandho, na tu pramāṇato 'satyārthapratipattau /
tasmādarthavat prayojanavat pramāṇamapi pravṛttivadeva /
etaduktaṃ bhavati, yathāntaraṅgatayā pravṛttirbalīyasī evaṃ mūlakāraṇatayā pramāṇamapi /
na hyapramāṇāt pravṛttiḥ phalenābhisaṃbadhyate /
tasmāt tulyamubhayamapi /
tathāpi pramāṇavyutpādanena pravṛttirapi vyutpāditā bhavatīti pramāṇasya vyutpādanamakāri śāstreṇa, na tu pravṛtteḥ /
sāmānyābhidhānaṃ ca paramanyāyaparam, tasyaiva prakṛtatvāditi /
prāmāṇyajñānopāyapratipādanaparatayānusandhānavakyatvamasya pūrvamuktam /
saṃprati paraparyanuyogamukhenāsyānusandhānavākyatvu pratipādayati-- lokavṛtteti /
yathā hi pramāṇapratipattyupāyaṃ pratyācakṣāṇaka evaṃ praṣṭāvyo jāyate, kiṃ bhavān pramāṇena pramāṇajñānopāyaṃ pratyācaṣṭe, apramāṇena veti? yadi brūyāt pramāṇeneti, sa prativaktavyaḥ, pramāṇajñānopāyamavidvān kathaṃ bhavānevamāheti? apramāṇeneti cedanujñayā vartitavyam /
atha pramāṇenāgṛhītaprāmāṇyeneti, vā/manasayorvisaṃvādaḥ /

children.translated_text: Therefore, even unwillingly, you must follow worldly practice /

children.text: anyathā nāsi laukiko na parīkṣaka ityunmattavadupekṣaṇīyaḥ syā iti /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, you are neither a person of the world nor an examiner— you would be disregarded like a madman /

children.text: tadidaṃ lokavṛttamākṣeptāraṃ bodhayitumanena bhāṣyeṇānūdyate pramāṇato 'rthapratipatau pravṛttisāmarthyāvat pramāṇa yato 'taḥ sarvaḥ pramātā pramāṇenāvagatārthavattvenārthamavadhārya pravartamānaḥ phalamupalabhata iti lokavṛttam /
children.translated_text: This worldly practice, in order to instruct the objector, is restated by this <s>bhāṣya</s>: 'Since there is capacity for activity when the object has been apprehended from <s>pramāṇa</s>, the <s>pramāṇa</s> is such that every knower, having ascertained the object through apprehending it by means of <s>pramāṇa</s> as having a real object, and acting accordingly, obtains the result'— this is the worldly practice /
That [worldly practice] is restated by the statement beginning 'from <s>pramāṇa</s>' through the device of showing the cause //

Thus, by the sequence stated, the purport that 'from <s>pramāṇa</s>, the apprehension of the object' is a statement of investigation of the <s>śāstra</s> has been settled /
Now he states another purport of this very [statement]— 'of <s>pramāṇa</s> and activity' /
Here this is anticipated: the sage, through the means of teaching perception, doubt, and the like directly by this <s>śāstra</s>, taught <s>nyāya</s>, which is also called <s>anumāna</s> (inference), as the means of determining the twelve-fold <s>prameya</s> situated in the form of what is to be abandoned and accepted, for the attainment of the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>) /
And it is not from <s>nyāya</s>, the <s>pramāṇa</s>, from the mere ascertainment of the reality of <s>prameya</s>, that the attainment of the highest good comes /
Rather, it comes from activities such as the contemplation of the ten <s>prameyas</s> excluding the first and last as suffering, and the contemplation of the true nature of the self, and the like, through the sequence of the maturation of direct realization of the self's reality and dispassion, through the non-production of the unprecedented <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, and through the exhaustion of those already produced by their being experienced /
And thus, because activity is more proximate to the highest good, activity is more powerful than <s>nyāya</s>, the <s>pramāṇa</s> /
Therefore, activity alone should be taught, not <s>pramāṇa</s>, since activity is more proximate even though <s>pramāṇa</s> is a cause of the highest good /
Here it is established that when there is true apprehension of the object from <s>pramāṇa</s>, the activity has capacity, the connection with the result— but not when the apprehension of the object from <s>pramāṇa</s> is untrue /
Therefore, <s>pramāṇa</s> is as purposeful and significant as activity itself /
This is what has been said: just as activity is more powerful because of its proximity, so too <s>pramāṇa</s> is powerful because of being the root cause /
For without <s>pramāṇa</s>, activity does not connect with the result /
Therefore both are equal /
Even so, by teaching <s>pramāṇa</s>, activity too is taught— so the <s>śāstra</s> has taught <s>pramāṇa</s>, not activity separately /
And the general statement is focused on <s>nyāya</s> as the primary subject, since that is the topic under discussion /
The purport of this as a statement of investigation through the presentation of the means of knowing validity was stated earlier /
Now he demonstrates the purport of this as a statement of investigation through the device of the opponent's challenge— 'worldly practice' /
For just as one who denies the means of knowing <s>pramāṇa</s> can be asked: 'Sir, do you deny the means of knowing <s>pramāṇa</s> by means of a <s>pramāṇa</s> or without a <s>pramāṇa</s>?' If he says 'by means of a <s>pramāṇa</s>', he should be told: 'not knowing the means of knowing <s>pramāṇa</s>, how can you say this?' If [he says] 'without a <s>pramāṇa</s>', then his admission should be accepted /
Or if [he says] 'by means of a <s>pramāṇa</s> whose validity has not been grasped'— then there is a contradiction between speech and mind /

children.text:
asyaiva bhāṣyasya tātparyāntaraṃ vaktu bhūmimāracayati--heyahāneti /
artho 'rthaśabdaḥ pramāṇato 'rthapratipattāvityatra sthitaḥ padaṃ vāyakaṃ yeṣāṃ tāni tathā /
etadvāttikagranthasyaitādṛśaṃvyākhyānam, bhāṣyagatasya tvanyathā bhaviṣyati /
upāyaḥ śāstramiti /
śāstraśabdastadarthaparaḥ, arthasyāpi śabdavacchāstraśarīratvāt /
atra ca heyahānādhigantavyapadaiḥ pramāṇaprameyayorūpādānād gobalīvardanyāyena saṃśayādiṣu nigrahasthānānteṣu śāstrapadaṃ pravartate /
tenopāyapadena saṃśayādayo nigrahasthānānto evoktā iti /
grahaṇakavākyaṃ vivṛṇeti--heyamiti /
tātparyamāha--etasmiṃśceti /
cena pramāṇapramāpramātṛprameyarūpaṃ caturvargāntaramapi sūcayati /
tatra heyādicaturvarge cāryamāṇatayārthapadasūcite pramāṇādicaturvarge ca pramāṇasya prādhānyapradarśanārthamidaṃ bhāṣyam /
yadyapi caturvargadvayatattvāvagamo niḥśreyasādhigamahetuḥ, tathāpi pramāṇameva pradhānam, tanmūlatvāditarasiddheḥ /
tadidamuktam, arthavaditi /
atiśāyane matup /
pramātrādyapekṣayā heyādyepakṣayā cātiśayena prayojanavat pramāṇam /
kasmāt? pramāṇato 'rthapratipattau satyāṃ pravṛttasya pramātustaditarapratilambhāt /
pramāyāśca tatkāryatvāt /
tadidamuktam--pravṛttisāmarthyāditi /
tadetasmāt prādhānyād vivakṣābhedena trivargadvayāt prāguddeśaḥ pramāṇasyeti /
etena yadāhureke yadi prādhānyāt prāthamyaṃ tat prameyasyaiva, athoṣāyatvāt tat saṃśayādīnām,
children.translated_text: By this, what some say — 'if primacy [determines] priority, then it should belong to <s>prameya</s> (the object of knowledge) itself; or if it is due to being a means, then it should belong to <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt) and the rest' —

children.text: teṣāṃ pramāṇopāyatvāt, kasmācca pramātrādibhyaḥ prāthamyaṃ pramāṇasyeti? tannirastaṃ bhavati, pramāṇopāyānāmapi saṃśayādīnāṃ pramāṇādhīnatvāditi /
children.translated_text: because they are means for <s>pramāṇa</s>, and why should <s>pramāṇa</s> have priority over <s>pramātṛ</s> (the knower) and the rest? — that is refuted, since even <s>saṃśaya</s> and the rest, which are means for <s>pramāṇa</s>, are themselves dependent on <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: nanvavagatam, arthapadatayā heyādicaturvargo darśita itiḥ, pramāṇādicaturvargastu kathaṃ pradarśita iti pṛcchati--kathaṃ punariti /
children.translated_text: One might object: it is understood that the group of four beginning with 'that which is to be avoided' has been shown through the word '<s>artha</s>' (object), but how has the group of four beginning with <s>pramāṇa</s> been shown? — he asks this with 'how then?'
The answer is: 'through the comprehension of <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>prameya</s>.'

He prepares the ground for stating another purport of this very <s>Bhāṣya</s> — 'that which is to be avoided, abandonment' etc.
The word '<s>artha</s>' (object/meaning) in the phrase 'from the apprehension of objects through <s>pramāṇa</s>' is established as the word-referent; those [terms] whose constituents are explanatory words are thus explained.
This is the explanation of the <s>Vārttika</s> text in this manner, but the <s>Bhāṣya</s> passage will be explained differently.
The means is the <s>śāstra</s> (science/treatise).
The word '<s>śāstra</s>' refers to that meaning, since even the object has the nature of a body of <s>śāstra</s> like a word.
Here, through the terms 'that which is to be avoided,' 'abandonment,' and 'that which is to be known,' since the forms of <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) and <s>prameya</s> (objects of knowledge) are taken up, by the maxim of the cow and the ox, the word '<s>śāstra</s>' extends to [categories] from <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt) up to <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (points of defeat).
Thus by the word 'means,' <s>saṃśaya</s> and the rest up to <s>nigrahasthāna</s> are indeed stated.
He explains the introductory sentence — 'that which is to be avoided' etc.
He states the purport — 'in this' etc.
And the particle 'ca' also indicates another group of four in the form of <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge), <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition), <s>pramātṛ</s> (knower), and <s>prameya</s> (object of knowledge).
Among these, this <s>Bhāṣya</s> is for the purpose of demonstrating the primacy of <s>pramāṇa</s> in the group of four beginning with <s>pramāṇa</s>, while the group of four beginning with 'that which is to be avoided' is indicated by the word '<s>artha</s>' as being under discussion.
Although the understanding of the true nature of both groups of four is the cause of attaining the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>), nevertheless <s>pramāṇa</s> alone is primary, since the establishment of everything else is rooted in it.
This is what has been said — '<s>arthavat</s>' (purposeful).
The suffix <s>matup</s> is in the sense of excellence.
<s>Pramāṇa</s> is exceedingly purposeful in comparison with <s>pramātṛ</s> etc. and in comparison with 'that which is to be avoided' etc.
Why? Because when there is apprehension of objects through <s>pramāṇa</s>, the knower who has engaged [in action] obtains everything else.
And because <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition) is an effect of that [<s>pramāṇa</s>].
This is what has been said — 'by the capacity of activity.'
Therefore, due to this primacy, by difference in intention, the enumeration of <s>pramāṇa</s> comes before the two groups of three.

children.text:
tadevaṃ tātparyaṃ vyākhyāyāvayavārthaṃ vyākhyātumupakramate--tadidaṃ vākyāmavayavaśa upanyasya varṇyate vyākhyāyate 'vayavaśa iti /
tatrāsyāvayaveṣu vyākhyātavyeṣu prāthamyāt pramāṇata iti vivṛṇoti--tatreti /
vibhajate-pramāṇata itīyaṃ nimittapañcamī /
nimittapañcamī cet kasmāt pramāṇāditi nābhihitamityata āha-- asyeti /
pramāṇata ityevaṃrūpasyābhidhānaṃ vacanavyāptyarthaṃ vibhaktivyāptyarthaṃ ceti /
vacanavyāptyarthamiti mṛśyāmahe, na tu vibhaktivyāptyarthamiti, pañcamīvyatirekeṇa taserabhāvādityāha----kathaṃ punariti? pariharati--labhyata iti /
vyāpteḥ prayojanaṃ pṛcchati-kiṃ siddhaṃ bhavatīti /
uttaraṃ-vacanavyāptyā saṃplavo vyavasthā ca /
tadubhayaṃ vibhajate--pramāṇeneti /
yatra dvayorbahūnāṃ vā saṃpalvaḥ pramāṇānāṃ tatraikaikasyāpyasti pratipattisādhanatvaṃ pramāṇasyeti kathayituṃ saṃplavāvasare 'pi pramāṇenetyaṅktam /
ata eva vyavasthāyāmevakāraḥ pramāṇenaiveti /
vibhaktivyāpteḥ prayojanamāhavibhaktivayāptyā hetatukaraṇabhāvaḥ /
gamyate ityanuṣajyate /
tadvibhajate-pramāṇādarthādhigatirbhavatīti hetutvaṃ gamyate /
pramāṇenārthādhigatirbhavatīti karaṇarūpo 'rtho gamyata iti saṃbandhaḥ /
kasmāt punaḥ karaṇārtho gamyata ityata āha--pramāṇeneti /
arthamarthādhigati sādhayatīti sādhakatamatvāt /
atra ca karaṇabhāvanāntarīyakasya hetubhāvasya pañcamya abhidhānaṃ pramāṇaphalayostādātmyapratiṣedhārtham, bhedādhiṣṭhānatvāddhetuphalabhāvasya, na khalu paraśureva cchideti /
pramāṇaprātipadikalabdhakaraṇatvānuvādaśca pramākārakāntarebhyo 'bhyarhitatvenāsya vyutpādyatvaṃ ca prāthamyaṃ ca yuktamiti darśayituṃ saṃplavamākṣipati--saṃplaveti /
samādhatte--neti /
ākṣepu vibhajate--syānmatiriti /
viśiṣṭo bhinno viṣayo yeṣāṃ tāni tathā /
bahuvacanamāntargaṇikabhedābhiprāyam /
arthasāmarthyasamutthaṃ hi pratyakṣamarthagocaram /
sa evārthaḥ pratyakṣagocaro yo jñānapratibhāsamātmano 'nvayavyatirekāvanukārayati /
na ca sāmānyaṃ nirastasamastārthakriyāsāmarthyamevaṃ bhavitumarhati /
svalakṣaṇaṃ tu syāta /
tadeva hi paramārthasat, arthakriyāsāmarthyalakṣaṇatvād vastunaḥ /
etadevāsya svamasādhāraṇaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ yaddeśato 'nanugamenādeśātmakasya paramāṇutvam, kālato 'nanugamena ca kṣaṇikatvam /
tasmāt svalakṣaṇaviṣayaṃ pratyakṣam /
na ca svalakṣaṇamanumānasyāpi gocaraḥ /
taddhi gṛhītapratibandhaliṅgahetukam /
pratibanṇaśca tādātmyatadutpattilakṣaṇaḥ svalakṣaṇaviṣayo 'śakyagraha iti sāmānyadharmāvāśrayate /
na ca sāmānyamekamanekadeśakālāvasthāsaṃsargi bhavitumarhati /
tadidamanādivāsanodbhūtavikalpadhiṣṭhānaṃ vikalpākārasya vā alīkasya vā bāhyatvamanumānagācaro 'bhyupeyam /
tacca bhāvābhāvasādhāraṇyācca bāhyasādṛśyacca niyatapratibhāsatvāccānyavyāvṛttiniṣṭham /
yat khalu bhāvābhāvasādhāraṇam, tadanyavyāvṛttiniṣṭhameva yathā amūrtatvam /
tad vijñānādau bhāve śaśaviṣāṇādau cābhāve sādhāraṇam /
bhāvābhāvasādhāraṇaśca vikalpagocaro 'sti ghaṭo nāsti ghaṭa iti /
yadi punarasādhāraṇo bhāvo bhaved astiśabdo na prayujyeta, punaruktatvāt /
nāstīyapi na vaktavyaṃ virodhāt, evamabhāvāsādhāraṇye 'pi vācyam /
na cālīkasya sarvasāmarthyavirahiṇaḥ paramārthasattā svalakṣaṇena sādṛśyaṃ manyate 'nyavyāvṛteḥ /
na ca gauriti niyatau buddhivyapadeśau vināścādivyāvṛttim /
tasmāt sāmānyamanyavyāvṛttirūpamabāhyaṃ bāhyabhedāgrahād bāhyatvenāvagāhyamānamanumānaṃ bāhyo pravartayati /
pāramparyeṇa ca bāhyapratibandhād bāhyaṃ prāpayat saṃvādakaṃ sad bhrāntamapi pramātrāśayavaśāt pramāṇam /

children.translated_text: Therefore, its own particular characteristic (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) is not its object.
And it has been indicated that even <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) does not have the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) as its object.

children.text: na cābhyāmanyat pramāṇamasti, pramāṇasya sato 'traivāntarbhāvāt, anantarbhāve vā pramāṇatvānupapattaḥ /
children.translated_text: And there is no other <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) besides these two, since any existing <s>pramāṇa</s> would be included within these very two; or if not included, its status as a <s>pramāṇa</s> would be untenable.

children.text: na ca sāmānyaviśeṣābhyāmanyadasti prameyāntaraṃ yatraite tat saṃploṣyete ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And there is no other <s>prameya</s> (object of knowledge) besides the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) and the particular (<s>viśeṣa</s>) into which these two could merge — this is the meaning.

Having thus explained the purport, he begins to explain the meaning of the components — 'this statement is presented by setting forth the components of the sentence and is explained component by component.'
Among these, since the components are to be explained and <s>pramāṇa</s> comes first, he explains 'from <s>pramāṇa</s>' — 'among these.'
He analyzes: 'from <s>pramāṇa</s>' — this is an ablative of cause (<s>nimittapañcamī</s>).
If it is an ablative of cause, why was it not expressed as 'from <s>pramāṇa</s>' [with a different form]?

children.text:
samādhānavākyaṃ vivṛṇoti--etacca neti /
yathā caitat tathā tatra tatra nivedayiṣyate /
viśeṣo vyavacchedakaḥ /
sa ca vakrakoṭarādirantyaśca /

children.translated_text: He gives examples of order and conflation — 'like the sense organ' etc.
Not tolerating the conflation, he says — 'because it is already known' etc.
He reconciles with 'therefore otherwise' etc.
He explains the objection — 'if' etc.

He explains the conciliatory statement — 'and this is not' etc.
How this is so will be explained in the respective places.
<s>Viśeṣa</s> (particular) means that which differentiates.
And that is [something] like a curved hollow, and is the final [differentiator].

children.text:
syādetat /
nāsti vaiyarthyamadhigatīnāmāśutaravināśitayā tadgocarādhigatyantarotpādaṃ prati pramāṇāntarasyārthavattvādityata āha--adhigataṃ cārthamadhigamayatā pramāṇeneti /
yadyapyadhigataya āśutaravināśinyaḥ,
tathāpyekatarapramāṇajanitārthādhigalibdhajanmanaḥ saṃskārādeva sthāyinastadarthasmṛtisantatisaṃbhāvād adhigamarthamadhigamayatā pramāṇena piṣṭaṃ piṣṭaṃ syāditi /
samādhivākyaṃ vivarītumanuvadati--nānyatheti /
vivṛṇoti--na brūma iti /
ayamabhisandhi, na hi pramāṇakāraṇāni prekṣāvantiḥ, yenaivamālocayeyuḥ--janitameva pramāṇamanyamenāsmāsu, vayamihodāsmaha iti /
nāpi svakāraṇabalalabdhajanmāni pramāṇāni dirśito 'yamartho 'nyatamena cāsmāsu pramāṇena, kṛtamasmābhiriti virantumarhanti /
pramātuścetanatvādayamanayoga iti cet--na, priyatamasya vastuno 'nena bhūyo bhūyaḥ pramitsitatvāt /
children.translated_text: If it is objected that because the knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>) is conscious, this connection [between desire and cognition] is inappropriate — no, because even the most beloved object is desired to be known again and again through this [<s>pramāṇa</s>].
And because even an undesired object such as the words of a wicked person, though not sought to be known, is indeed cognized through this [<s>pramāṇa</s>].

children.text: tasmānna pramātrabhisandhānāt pramāṇasya pravṛttirapravṛttirvārthe, kiṃ tu samārthyot /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the functioning or non-functioning of <s>pramāṇa</s> with respect to an object is not due to the intention of the knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>), but rather due to [its own] capacity.
Otherwise there would be the absurd consequence that the pain of fire-burning etc. would not be directly perceptible (<s>pratyakṣa</s>).

One might argue thus:
There is no purposelessness, since cognitions are subject to rapid destruction, and therefore another <s>pramāṇa</s> is purposeful for producing a subsequent cognition of the same object — to this he says: 'by a <s>pramāṇa</s> that makes known an already known object.'
Even though cognitions are subject to rapid destruction,
nevertheless, from the <s>saṃskāra</s> (mental impression) alone — which is enduring and born from the cognition of the object produced by one <s>pramāṇa</s> — the memory of that object [continues],

children.text:
cattu pramāṇaṃ pramitsādhīnapravṛtti tadyadi pramātā na vyāpārayet kimāyātaṃ pramāṇasya? na hi toyamapi pipāsunā na pīyata iti tasya pipāsopaśamanaśaktirapīti /
tasmāt pratyutpannakāraṇasāmagrījanitā buddhiḥ pramā /
tajjanakāni ca pramāṇāni samānaviṣayāṇyapi /
sa eva cānena sāmagrībhedaḥ pradarśitaḥ anyathā pratyakṣeṇetyādinā /
yadyapi sākṣātkārāsākṣātkārādirapi prakārabhedo 'sti, tathāpyasau prakṛtānupayogānnoktaḥ /
yadi ca dravyaṃ tvacā gṛhītamiti kṛtaṃ cakṣuṣā, cakṣuṣā vā gṛhītamiti kṛtaṃ tvacetyucyeta, na rūpavijñānaṃ vā sparśavijñānaṃ vopajāyeta /
children.translated_text: And if it were said that 'the substance has been grasped by the skin, so the eye is unnecessary,' or 'it has been grasped by the eye, so the skin is unnecessary,' then neither visual cognition nor tactile cognition would arise.
For that purpose, either the eye or the skin must be employed.

children.text: tathā ca saṃplavavaiyarthye 'pi vyavasthāyāṃ na vaiyarthyamityāha--viṣayāntara iti /
children.translated_text: And thus, even though there is purposelessness in conflation, there is no purposelessness in the ordered arrangement — he says this with 'in a different object-domain' etc.
He concludes the topic under discussion with 'therefore' etc.

But if <s>pramāṇa</s> depends on the desire to know for its functioning, then if the knower does not employ it, what would the <s>pramāṇa</s> achieve? Indeed, water too is not drunk by one who is not thirsty, yet that does not negate its capacity to quench thirst.
Therefore, cognition (<s>buddhi</s>) produced by the aggregate of presently existing causes is <s>pramā</s> (valid knowledge).
And <s>pramāṇas</s> are the producers of that, even when they share the same object.
And this very difference in the aggregate [of causal conditions] has been demonstrated by this.

children.text:
vibhaktyarthaṃ nirūpya prātipadikārthanirūpaṇamavatārayati--pramāṇeti /
atra cāvadhāryate 'nenetyavadhāraṇaṃ vicāra iti /
vicāraṇāya bhāvabhavitārau pṛcchati-- kiṃ punariti /
kecidāhuḥ, anadhigatārthagantṛ pramāṇamiti /
viṣayasārūpyaṃ sākārasya vijñānasyetyante /
vijñānasyaivānākārasyātmānāmaprakāśanasāmarthyamityapare /
upalabdhisādhanamiti vṛddhāḥ /
tasmād viprapitteḥ saṃśayāt praśrnaḥ /

children.translated_text: By the explanation of the question about the nature [of <s>pramāṇa</s>], the question about who possesses that nature has also been explained.
The answer is: '<s>pramāṇa</s> is the cause of apprehension (<s>upalabdhi</s>).'

And there is no unwanted consequence [of including] doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>) and error (<s>viparyāsa</s>) as causes of apprehension, because of the qualification '<s>arthavat</s>' (purposeful/veridical), since those two, due to their demonstrated deviation from the true object, are not purposeful.

children.text: no khalu vikalpayamānaṃ vastvasti, arthakriyāsu vopayujyate //
children.translated_text: Indeed, that which is merely a conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) does not [correspond to] a real thing, nor is it useful in practical activities (<s>arthakriyā</s>).

Having determined the meaning of the case ending, he introduces the determination of the meaning of the stem — '<s>pramāṇa</s>' etc.
And here, 'that by which one ascertains' — ascertainment means investigation (<s>vicāra</s>).
For the purpose of investigation, he asks about the nature and the possessor of that nature — 'what then?' etc.
Some say: '<s>pramāṇa</s> is that which apprehends a previously unknown object.'
[Others say:] 'The conformity with the object is [the nature] of cognition that has a form' — thus say the proponents of <s>sākāravāda</s>.
[Others say:] 'Of cognition itself, which is formless, the self being non-manifest' —

children.text:
syādetat /
smṛtihetorapi prāmāṇyaprasaṅgaḥ /
na hyasau nopalabdhihetuḥ /
na cārthasahakāri pramāṇamiti saṃskārasyārthasahakāritāvirahādaprāmāṇyamiti sāṃpratam, nadīpūrasya pipīlikāṇḍasaṃcaraṇasya cātītānāgatavarṣaliṅgasya, śabdasyātītānāgatagocarasyārthasahakāritāvirahiṇaścapramāṇatvaprasaṅgāt /
jñāpakatvena kāryatvena vā kathañcidarthasaṃbandhe saṃskārasyāpi tat samānamiti tasyāpi smṛtirūpopalabdhihetoḥ prāmāṇyaṃ prasaktam /
maivam, pramāṇaśabdena tasyāpāstatvāt /
pramāsādhanaṃ hi pramāṇam na ca smṛtiḥ pramā /
lokādhīnāvadhāraṇo hi śabdārthasabandhaḥ /
lokaśca saṃskāramātrajanmanaḥ smṛteranyāmupalabdhim arthāvyabhicāriṇīṃ pramāmācaṣṭe /
tasmāt taddhetuḥ pramāṇamiti na smṛtihetau prasaṅgaḥ /
anadhigatārthagantṛtvaṃ ca dhārāvāhikavijñānānāmadhigatārthagocarāṇāṃ lokaprasiddhapramāṇabhāvānāṃ pramāṇyaṃ vihantīti nādriyamahe /
na ca kālabhedenānadhigagocaratvaṃ dhārāvāhikānāmiti yuktam, paramasūkṣmāṇāṃ kālakalābhedānāṃ piśitalocanairasmādṛśairanākalanāt /
na cādyenaiva vijñānenopadarśitatvādarthasya pravartitatvāt puruṣasya prāptitvāccottateṣām, aprāmāṇyamameva vijñānānāmiti vācayam /
na hi vijñānasyārthaprāpaṇaṃ pravartanādanyat, na ca pravartanamapyarthapradarśanādanyat /
tasmādarthapradarśanamātravyāpārameva jñānaṃ pravartakaṃ prāpakaṃ ca /
pradarśana ca pūrvavaduttareṣāṃ vijñānāmabhinnamiti kathaṃ pūrvameva vijñānaṃ pramāṇa nottarāṇyapi? puruṣāpekṣayā tu prāmāṇye candratārakādivijñānasya puruṣānapekṣitasyāprāmāṇyaprasaṅgaḥ /
na cātidavīstayā tadarthasya heyatayā tadapi puruṣasyāpekṣitam, tasyopekṣaṇīyārthaviṣayatvāt /
na copekṣaṇīyam apyanupādeyatvāddheyamiti nivedayiṣyate /
upalabdhihetuṃ ca pramāṇaṃ vadatā anadhigatārthagantṛtvaṃ cārthasārūpyaṃ cātmānātmaprakāśanaśaktiśca pramāṇamiti nirastāni bhavanti /
upalabdhimātrasyatvāddheyamiti nivedayiṣyate /
upalabdhihetuṃ ca pramāṇaṃ vadatā anadhigatārthagantṛtvaṃ cārthasārūpyaṃ cātmānātmaprakāśanaśaktiśca pramāṇamiti nirastāni bhavanti /
upalabdhimātrasyārthāvyabhicāriṇa smṛteranyasya pramāśabdenābhidhānāt /
hetugrahaṇena sārūpyaśaktyoḥ phalādabhinnayorapākaraṇāt hetuhetumadbhāvasya tādātmaye 'nupapatteriti /

children.translated_text: And when there is the property of being a cause of apprehension, there is <s>pramāṇa</s>-status.
By the explanation using the future participle (<s>bhavitṛ</s>), the [present] state (<s>bhāva</s>) has been explained.
Thus, whether it is knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) or ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>), that which is a cause of apprehension is <s>pramāṇa</s>.
Its nature (<s>bhāva</s>) is its reality (<s>tattva</s>) — this is established.

One might object: there is the unwanted consequence of validity even for the cause of memory. For that [memory] is indeed a cause of apprehension. And it is not correct to say that because <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) must be a co-operative cause of the object, and because <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression) lacks such co-operative causation with the object, it is therefore not a <s>pramāṇa</s> — for there would be the unwanted consequence of <s>pramāṇa</s>-status for a river flood [as a sign] of ant-mound movement, for a sign of past and future rainfall, and for verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) whose scope extends to past and future [objects] and which lacks co-operative causation with the object.
