tadeva hi pratyakṣaṃ saṃśayasya nivartakaṃ yadananyathāsiddham, yathauṣṇyagrāhi vahneḥ /
idaṃ tu sādṛśyenāpi saṃbhavāt svayaṃ sandigdhaṃ sanna saṃśayocchedāyālamityarthaḥ /
mā bhūt pratyakṣasya viṣayaḥ, bhavati tvāgamasya /
no khalu kṣaṇikaḥ śabdo 'rthapratyāyane samarthaḥ, tasyānvayavyatirekakālānavasthāyino 'śakyasamayatvenārthapratipatteranupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: Certainly a momentary sound (<s>śabda</s>) cannot be capable of conveying meaning, because for something that does not persist through the times of positive and negative concomitance, convention cannot be established, and therefore the apprehension of meaning is impossible.

children.text: tasmād yadyapi sākṣānnityo 'ham ityāgamo nābhidhatte, tathāpi viditasaṃgaterarthapratyayaṃ kurvannātmano nityatāmākṣipannityatāviṣayo bhavati /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even though scripture does not directly state 'I am eternal,' nevertheless, by producing the apprehension of meaning through known conventions, it implies the eternality [of sound] and thus has eternality as its object.
As they say:
'It [sound] must be eternal, because perception serves another's purpose.'

Thus it will determine the eternality [of sound] — to this he says: 'This matter is not the object of perception.'
For only that perception which is established as not otherwise possible can dispel doubt, as [the perception] that apprehends heat [is established] in the case of fire.
But this, being possible also through similarity, is itself doubtful and thus cannot suffice for the resolution of doubt — this is the meaning.
Let it not be the object of perception; it is, however, the object of scripture (<s>āgama</s>).

children.text:
ityata āha---nāgamaviṣayaḥ /
yadyapi varṇavyaktayaḥ kṣaṇikāḥ, tathāpi svasvasāmānyaviśeṣagatvādyupahitā gavādivyaktaya iva gotvādyupadhānāḥ śakyasaṃketā iti na nityatāmākṣipatyāgama ityarthaḥ /
bhavatu kiṃ no bādhyata iti /
na khalu candramasaḥ parabhāge hariṇasadasadbhāvasandehaḥ śakyaḥ kadācidapyucchettumasmadādīnāmityarthaḥ /
kathaṃ na bādhyata iti /
sandigdhanityānityabhāve śabde kṛtakatvaṃ dṛṣṭamiti nānityatvena svabhāvataḥ pratibaddham /
tathā ca na buddhyādīnāmanityatvaṃ sādhayitumarhatītyarthaḥ /
sarvamiti /
kṛtakatvaprayatnanāntarīyakatvapratyayabhedabheditvādītyarthaḥ /
sarvaṃ cānumānamiti /
yadi ca pañcarūpo 'pi hetuḥ, saṃśayakāraṇaṃ sarvamevānumānamiti sarvamapramāṇaṃ syādityarthaḥ /
vaināśikāḥ prāhuḥ nityāsaṃbhavāditi /
na, bādhāparijñānāditi /
bādhāviṣayāparijñānādityarthaḥ /
svadeśe parotpattipratibandhakatvaṃ sapratidhatvam /
sautrāntikamate hi rūpaṃ sapratighamiṣyate mūrtaṃ ca, nitya eveti vā anitya eveti vā abhilāpo nopapadyeta, sthāṇureveti vā puruṣa eveti vā abhilāpaḥ /

children.translated_text: He objects — 'it will not be so.'
The meaning is: let there be no assertion.
He resolves it — 'it is contradictory.'
He states the same in one passage — 'but is it not the case that...'

To this he says — 'it is not the object of scripture.'
Even though the individual instances of phonemes are momentary, nevertheless, being endowed with their respective universal and particular properties, like individual cows endowed with cowness, they are capable of convention — therefore scripture does not imply eternality: this is the meaning.
Let it be so; why is it not refuted?
The meaning is: the doubt about the existence or non-existence of the rabbit on the far side of the moon can never be resolved by people like us.
How is it not refuted?
When sound is of doubtful eternal or non-eternal nature, 'being produced' (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) is observed — hence it is not inherently connected with non-eternality.
And thus it cannot serve to prove the non-eternality of cognition and the rest — this is the meaning.
'All' —
Meaning: producedness, being invariably preceded by effort, being differentiated by the differentiation of cognitions, and the like.
'And all inference' —
And if even a fivefold reason is a cause of doubt, then all inference whatsoever would be a cause of doubt, and thus all would be invalid as a means of knowledge — this is the meaning.
The <s>Vaināśikas</s> (Buddhist impermanence theorists) say: 'because eternality is impossible.'
No — because the scope of refutation is not fully known: this is the meaning.
Resistance (<s>sapratighatva</s>) is the capacity to obstruct the origination of another in one's own location.
In the <s>Sautrāntika</s> view, form (<s>rūpa</s>) is accepted as resistant and corporeal — and the assertion 'it is only eternal' or 'it is only non-eternal' would not be valid, just as [the assertion] 'it is only a post' or 'it is only a person' [would not be valid in doubt].

children.text:
tadevaṃ pañcarūpayorhetvorekatra samavāyābhāvaḥ uktaḥ /
yadi punarasatpratipakṣarūparahitayorekatra saṃbhavo 'ṅgīkriyate, tathā ca saṃśayahetutvamityabhiprāyeṇa śaṅkate---atha kṛtakatveti, nirākaroti---tathāpīti /
pratyekaṃ satpratipakṣatvam, militayostvasādhāraṇatvam, tādṛśaḥ anyatrādarśanādityarthaḥ /
tat kimidānīṃ satpratipakṣatayā kṛtakatvamasādhanameva śabdānityatve, tathā ca bahu vyāhataṃ bhavatītyāśayavān pṛcchati---yadā punarevaṃbhūtāviti /
uttaram---tadā tayoriti /

nanu kṛtakatvasya sādhyatvāt śrāvaṇatvasya ca siddhatvāt prathamabhāvinā nityatvānumānena siddhāṅgakenāpahṛtaviṣayaṃ caramabhāvisādhyaṅgakamanityatvānumānameva bādhyatām ityata āha---yatnaśca kriyamāṇa iti /
children.translated_text: But since producedness is what is to be proved, and audibility (<s>śrāvaṇatva</s>) is already established, the inference of non-eternality, which depends on what is to be proved as a component, should be defeated by the inference of eternality, which comes first and has an established component — to this he says: 'and effort being made.'

children.text: siddhamapi śravaṇatvamanumānasikatādyanityadharmasādhāraṇatayā savyabhicāraṃ sannityatvasya sādhanaṃ na bhavitumarhatoti /
children.translated_text: Even though audibility is established, being common to non-eternal properties such as being perceived through inference and the like, it is deviant and thus cannot serve as a proof of eternality.
But producedness has the fivefold character [of a valid reason].
And the invalidity through <s>pramāṇa</s>-refutation of [the inference of] eternality will be demonstrated — this is the meaning.

Thus the impossibility of the co-existence in one [subject] of the two forms of the fivefold reason has been stated.
But if the co-existence in one [subject] of the two that lack the counter-balancing form is accepted, and thus they become causes of doubt — with this intent he raises the objection: 'if producedness' — and refutes it: 'even so.'
Individually each has a counter-balancing reason; but combined they are uncommon — because such [a combination] is not seen elsewhere: this is the meaning.
Then is producedness, by virtue of having a counter-balancing reason, simply not a proof at all for the non-eternality of sound? In that case much would be contradicted — with this thought he asks: 'when, however, of such a nature.' The answer: 'then of those two.'

children.text:
vipratipatterityasya vyākhyānam---vipratipatteriti /
yadyapi viruddhā pratipattirjñānaṃ vipratipattiḥ, tathāpi tasyā vādiprativādigatāyā atyantaparokṣatvāt saṃśayakāraṇatvānupapatteḥ svakāryaṃ pravādaṃ lakṣayatītyarthaḥ /
atra bhāṣyakāraḥ upalabdhyavyavasthāyā anupalabdhavyavasthāyāśca pṛthak saṃśayakāraṇatvaṃ matvā samānadharmopapatterityanena gatārthatāṃ pariharannāha sma---purvaḥ samāno 'nekaścetyādi /
tadupanyasya vārttikakāro dūṣayati---tatreti /
no khalu samānānekadharmopalabdhau satyām, satyāṃ ca viśeṣasmṛtau sādhakabādhakapramāṇāsadbhāve saṃśayo bhavatītyuktam /
tasmāt nopalabdhyanupalabdhyavyavasthe pṛthak saṃśayakāraṇe iti /
viśeṣamapi dūṣayati---samāna iti /
nanu yadi nāsita bhedaḥ, tat kimidānī sarveṣāṃ jñātṛsthatvāviśeṣaṇa trayāṇāmapi saṃśayakāraṇānāṃ samānānekavipratipattīnāmabhedaḥ, tathā ca pṛthagupādānavaiyarthyamityata āha---samānānekadharmayoriti /
punaścodayati---samānadharmaḥ sarva evāyamiti /
ayamabhisandhiḥ /
asādhāraṇo hyadṛṣṭapūrvaḥ kvacidapi na saṃśayaṃ kartumutsahate, yat punarasādhāraṇavattvaṃ saṃśayahetutvenopavarṇitaṃ bhāṣyakṛtā tat samānameva, na tvasādhāraṇam /

children.translated_text: As they say:
'The uncommon property is one thing, and the possession of it is seen to be another.'
'And if that [possession] is common to all, it is accepted as a cause of doubt.'
'Therefore, the causation of doubt by the common alone is established.'

The explanation of 'due to conflicting cognition' — 'due to conflicting cognition.'
Although conflicting cognition (<s>vipratipattiḥ</s>) is [literally] contradictory knowledge, nevertheless, since it belongs to the disputant and the opponent and is thus completely beyond observation, it cannot serve as a cause of doubt — therefore it indicates its own effect, namely the assertion (<s>pravāda</s>): this is the meaning.
Here the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>, considering that the irregularity of apprehension and the regularity of non-apprehension are separately causes of doubt, and removing the superfluity of 'due to the occurrence of common properties' by [showing it is] already covered, said: 'the first, common, and multiple' etc.
Having presented that, the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> criticizes — 'therein.'
It has not been stated that when there is apprehension of common and multiple properties, and when there is recollection of the specific, doubt arises in the absence of proving and refuting <s>pramāṇas</s>.
Therefore, the irregularity and regularity of apprehension and non-apprehension are not separately causes of doubt.
He criticizes the specific point as well — 'common.'
But if there is no difference, then since all three causes of doubt — common-property, multiple-property, and conflicting-cognition — equally belong to the knower, what [is the point of] the absence of difference? And thus the separate mention would be futile — to this he says: 'of common and multiple properties.'
He objects again — 'common property is entirely this.'
The intended meaning is: an uncommon [property], one never seen before, can never produce doubt anywhere. And what the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> described as 'possessing the uncommon' being a cause of doubt is really just the common, not the uncommon.

children.text: yacca vārttikakāreṇa sarvato vyāvṛttyā asādhāraṇasya saṃśayakāraṇatvamuktam, tatrāpi tadabhāvasya sādhāraṇasya saṃśayahetutve kimāyātamasādhāraṇasya? yathāhuḥ,
children.translated_text: And what the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> stated — that the uncommon is a cause of doubt through complete exclusion from everything — even there, since the absence of the uncommon [means] the common is the cause of doubt, what role does the uncommon play? As they say:
'If doubt arises from the absence of what is excluded from everything,'
'Then what is the role of the uncommon, whose form is non-occurrence in anything else?'
Thus.

children.text: vipratipattirapi viruddhahetudvayasamutthā ekasmin saṃśayakāraṇam, viruddhahetusamavāyaścāsādhāraṇa eva /
children.translated_text: Conflicting cognition too, arising from a pair of contradictory reasons, is a cause of doubt regarding one [subject], and the co-occurrence of contradictory reasons is exclusively uncommon.

children.text: sa ca sādhāraṇe niviśate iti sūktam sarva evāyaṃ samānadharma evābhidhīyata iti /
children.translated_text: And that subsumes under the common — therefore it is well said that 'all of this is simply described as common property.'
He resolves — 'no, due to incomplete understanding of the <s>sūtra's</s> meaning.'

children.text: na vayaṃ sarvatra sādhāraṇamapajānīmahe anvayavyatirekavyabhicāravaktṛgatatvabhedamātramādriyamāṇāḥ kāraṇabhedena trividhaṃ saṃśayamācakṣmahe ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: We do not reject the common in every case; attending merely to the distinctions of positive concomitance, negative concomitance, deviation, and belonging to the speaker, we describe doubt as threefold based on the difference of causes — this is the meaning.

children.text:
vārttikakāro bhāṣyakāramatamupanyasya dūṣayati---apare punariti /
sādhakabādhakapramāṇābhāvarahitaṃ trayamapi na saṃśayakāraṇamityuktamityarthaḥ /
api caitayoḥ pṛthak saṃśayakāraṇatve 'tiprasaṅgāt niścayapūrvaṃ na pravarteta lokaḥ, tathā ca lokavirodha iti darśayati---upalabdhyanupalabdhyordvaividhyācceti /
na cāsya kvacidāśvāso niḥśaṅkatā,

na cānabhyāsadaśānne upalabdhyanupalabdhyavyavasthayāṃ saṃśaya iti vācyam, anabhyāsadaśāpanne hi dūrād vahnijñāne upalabdhyavyavasthāyā api na nāgo vā nago veti saṃśerate, kiṃ tu kiṃśukakusumanicayo vā uṣarbudho veti, tatra samānadharmopapattireva kāraṇamitarasahitā /
children.translated_text: Nor should it be said that in the state of non-familiarity, doubt arises from the irregularity of apprehension and non-apprehension. For even one in the state of non-familiarity, upon cognizing fire from a distance through the irregularity of apprehension, does not doubt 'is it a serpent or a mountain?' but rather 'is it a cluster of <s>kiṃśuka</s> flowers or a saline mound?' — there, the occurrence of common properties, combined with the other [factors], alone is the cause.
Thus it is stated that even from mere non-apprehension of an incompetent [means], there is no doubt without the observation of common properties and the like.
Having considered alternatives, he states another objection — 'and of those who.'

children.text: sāmagrībhedena bhede trevidhyaṃ saṃśayasya sāmagrīniveśikāraṇabhedena tu pañcavidhaḥ, api tvanekavidha etyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Due to the difference in the aggregate [of causes], doubt is threefold; but due to the difference in the component causes entering the aggregate, it is fivefold — or rather, manifold: this is the meaning.

The <s>Vārttikakāra</s>, having presented the <s>Bhāṣyakāra's</s> view, criticizes — 'others, however.'
The meaning is that it has been stated that all three, without being devoid of the absence of proving and refuting <s>pramāṇas</s>, are not causes of doubt.
Moreover, if these two are separately causes of doubt, there would be an undesirable over-extension — the world would not act with any prior certainty, and thus there would be conflict with common experience — he shows this: 'because of the twofold nature of apprehension and non-apprehension.'
And he would have no confidence anywhere, no freedom from suspicion.

children.text:
samānānekadharmopapatterityatra ṣaṣṭhatatpuruṣaṃ matvā ākṣipati---na samānadharmagrahaṇāditi /
bahuvrīhiṃ mattvā samādhatte---ayaṃ parihāra iti /
atheti /
kaścāsau viśeṣaśceti kiṃviśeṣaḥ anupalabdhapūrvo viśeṣo 'syetyarthaḥ /
upalabdhapūrvāyāṃ vyaktau saṃśaye tadgatā viśeṣāḥ susmūrṣitāḥ tajjātīyavyaktyantarasaṃśaye tvanyagatāste sāmānyadvāreṇopalabdhā eveti---sāmānyapratyakṣāditi /
samānyavāneva sāmānyaḥ /

children.translated_text: Just as [in the verse]: 'This common bridge of <s>dharma</s> belongs to all kings.'
The property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) that is both universal and perceptible is so called.
Having unascertained specific properties means the absence of proving and refuting <s>pramāṇas</s> — this is the meaning.

Taking 'due to the occurrence of common and multiple properties' as a genitive <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound, he objects — 'not from the apprehension of a common property.' Taking it as a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound, he resolves — 'this is the resolution.'
'Now' — 'and what is that specific [property]?' means 'what specific [property]?' — meaning 'a specific [property] not previously apprehended.'
When doubt concerns a previously apprehended individual, the specific properties belonging to it are those one desires to remember; but when doubt concerns another individual of the same class, those [properties] belonging to another are apprehended only through the universal — hence 'from the perception of the universal.'
One who possesses the universal is itself called 'universal' (<s>sāmānya</s>).

children.text:
bauddhābhimataṃ saṃśayalakṣaṇamupanyasyati---anye tviti /
nigūḍhābhiprāyo dūṣayati---tairapīti /
aviditābhiprāyaḥ śaṅkate---dharmī cediti /
dūṣaṇavādī svābhiprāyamuddhāṭayati---yadi tāvaditi /
bauddhānāṃ hi rāddhānte na rūpādidharmāśrayaḥ kaścidasti dharmī /
tataśca siddhāntavyākopaḥ /
yadi tvāha bhavatu rāddhāntavyākopo na hi śāstrāśrayo vāda iti, tatrāpi doṣāntaramāha---dharmadharmiṇośceti /
athāpyasmaddiśeti /
samānānekadharmapadavad bahuvrīhirityarthaḥ /
sāmānyaśabdastu bhavitari dṛṣṭo yathā,
sāmānyārthasamutthāne vibhāgastu samaḥ smṛtaḥ /
iti bhāvaḥ /
vyarthaṃ cābhidhānamiti /
sāmānyaviśeṣatadvadabhyupagame 'pi tadvato 'śravaṇāt sādharmyasya sāmānyasya viśeṣā iti gamyeta, na ca sāmānyasya viśeṣā iti viruddhārthamabhidhānaṃ syādityarthaḥ /
vaiśeṣikalakṣaṇe hi viśeṣāpratyakṣādityanena sādhakabādhakapramāṇābhāvo darśitaḥ /

children.translated_text: But here that [absence of pramāṇas] needs to be stated.
Therefore the Buddhist definition is deficient — he says 'apprehension' etc.
And if the Buddhist intends by 'from the observation of similarity' etc. merely the deviation of positive concomitance, then he should say 'from the observation of multiple properties.'

children.text: tadevaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇamekaṃ, trīṇi ca viśeṣalakṣaṇānīti sthitam //
children.translated_text: Thus it is established that there is one general definition of doubt, and three specific definitions.

He presents the Buddhist-accepted definition of doubt — 'others, however.'
He criticizes with a concealed intent — 'even by them.'
Not understanding the intent, [someone] objects — 'if the property-bearer.'
The critic reveals his intent — 'if, first of all.'
For in the established Buddhist doctrine, there is no property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) that is a substrate of properties like form and the rest.
And thus there would be a conflict with their established doctrine.
But if one says 'let there be a conflict with established doctrine, for debate is not based on [one's own] doctrine,' even then there is another fault, he says — 'of property and property-bearer.'
'Even in our direction' —
The meaning is that it is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound, like the term 'common-and-multiple-property.'
The word '<s>sāmānya</s>' is seen [used] in the sense of 'potential,' as in:
'But with respect to what arises from common purpose, the share is remembered as equal.'
This is the meaning.
'And the statement is futile' —
Even accepting universals, particulars, and their possessors, since the possessor is not mentioned [in the sūtra], one would understand 'the particulars of the universal' (i.e., the properties of similarity) — and [the expression] 'particulars of the universal' would be a statement of contradictory meaning: this is the meaning.
For in the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> definition, by [the phrase] 'the particular not being perceptible' etc., the absence of proving and refuting <s>pramāṇas</s> is indicated.

children.text:
tadetāni catvāri lakṣaṇāni pu/jīkṛtya vicārayati---samāneti /
yadi tāvat saṃśayasāmānyalakṣaṇe sthite trīṇi viśeṣalakṣaṇāni tataḥ saṃśayatvenopagṛhītānāṃ trayāṇāṃ parasparavyavacchedakamātraṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vaktavyam /
tataḥ samānānekadharmopapattervipratipatterityetāvanmātraṃ vaktavyam /
kṛtamatra śeṣeṇa, tanmātrādeva parasparavyavacchedasiddheḥ /
tasmāt parasparavyavacchedamanaprekṣya saṃśayakāraṇakathanaparametat sūtram /
tathā cānyānyapi saṃśayakāraṇāni santīti tānyapi vaktavyāni /
yadā khalvayamātmanaḥ śamādau saṃśete, kimahaṃ candanavanitādisannidhāne rajye virajye veti, so 'yamasyātmanaḥ sannikarṣajanmā saṃśayaḥ āntarasya śamāderviṣayasyeti samādhatte---astu tāvaditi /
yadyapi tāvanmātreṇa samānajātīyavyavacchedasiddhiḥ, tathāpi vijātīyanirṇayādivyavacchedāya sāmānyalakṣaṇamanuvartanīyam /
tathā ca pratipattigauravaṃ syāditi tallāghavāya śeṣāpekṣā yuktā /
ātmamanaḥ---sannikarṣādayastvatyantasādhāraṇā vijātīyavyavacchedāyāpi nālamiti nopattā iti bhāvaḥ /

children.translated_text: Thus, from the determination of the causes of doubt, the determination of the types of doubt follows implicitly — this has been stated.
Now, by way of qualifying the cause, the essential nature of doubt itself is being stated — thus he says — 'or, the indication of its essential nature.'

children.text: vipratipanno 'pi puruṣaḥ saṃdigdhavat pratipādya evati manvānaścodayati---saṃśayavaditi /
children.translated_text: Thinking that even a person holding a contrary opinion (<s>vipratipanna</s>) is to be instructed just like one who is in doubt, he objects — 'like doubt.'

children.text: vipratipanno na śiṣyaḥ, kiṃ tu jalpavitaṇḍābhyāṃ śiṣyato nītvā sandigdha eva pratipādya ityabhiprāyeṇa pariharati---satyamiti //23 //
children.translated_text: One holding a contrary opinion is not a student [to be taught]; rather, having brought him [to the status of] a student through <s>jalpa</s> (disputation) and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavil), he is to be instructed only as one who is in doubt — with this intention he resolves — 'true.' //23//

He examines these four definitions together — 'common' etc.
If the general definition of doubt is established, the three specific definitions should merely state what mutually distinguishes the three [types] subsumed under doubt.
Then only 'due to the occurrence of common and multiple properties' and 'due to conflicting cognition' need be stated.
The rest is unnecessary, since the mutual distinction is already accomplished by that much alone.
Therefore this <s>sūtra</s> is aimed at stating the causes of doubt without regard to mutual distinction.
And thus there are other causes of doubt as well, and they too should be stated.
When indeed a person doubts regarding his own tranquility and the like — 'do I, in the proximity of sandalwood, butter, etc., become attached or remain detached?' — this doubt, born of the contact of the self [with its objects], pertains to the internal subject of tranquility and the rest — he resolves: 'let it be so.'
Even though the distinction from things of the same class is accomplished by that much alone, nevertheless, for the purpose of distinction from determinate cognition of different classes and the like, the general definition must be carried forward.
And thus there would be complexity in understanding; therefore the need for the rest, for the sake of economy, is justified.
But the contact of self and mind and the like, being entirely common, do not suffice even for distinction from different classes — hence they are not mentioned: this is the meaning.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.24: That for the sake of which [one] engages is the purpose (<s>prayojana</s>).

children.text:
uddeśakramaprāptasya prayojanasya lakṣaṇam---yama---nam//2// atrārthaśabdo gauṇamukhyaprayojanāvarodhārthaḥ /
tatra mukhyaṃ sukhaduḥkhāpitaparihārau, gauṇaṃ tu tatsādhanam /
atra bhāṣyaṃ---yamartham ityādi /
atrādhikṛtyetyasya vyākhyānam---vyavasāya niniścityetyarthaḥ /
samādhanau ca sukhaduḥkhāptiparihārāvarthaḥ /
na ca sukhaduḥkhaprāptiparihārau svarūpeṇa pravṛtti nivṛttigocarāviti tadupāyapravṛttyaiva cetanapravṛttigocarāviti darśayati---tadāptihānopāyamanutiṣṭhatīti /
pravṛttihetutvāditi /
yadyapi sukhaduḥkhāptihāne tadupāyāśca santi, tathāpi sāmānyena jñāyamānānīcchādyupahāramukhena pravṛttihetavaḥ /
nanu sūtre 'dhikṛtyetyasti, bhāṣye ca vyavasāyeti, tat kuto na virodha ityata āha---vyavasāyo 'rthasyādhikāra ityādi /
tadetad vārttikakāro vyācaṣṭe---yamarthamadhikṛtyeti, vyavasāyeti /
pṛcchati---kasyeti sukhadaḥkhāptiparihārayorvyavasāyastatraiva pravartayet /
na cānayoḥ pravṛttiyogyatā /
na cānyaniścayo 'nyatra pravartayati, atiprasaṅgāditi bhāvaḥ /
uttaram---sukhaduḥkhasādhanānāmiti /
tataśca pratītipravṛttyoḥ saṃpratipattirityarthaḥ /
sarvavyāpitāmasya darśayati---anena prayojaneneti /
vitaṇḍāyā api prayojanamuktaṃ prathamasūtre /
codyamānasya pravarttamānasyetyarthaḥ /
śaṅkate---yadīti /
lokyate 'neneti lokaḥ pramāṇam /
tadanvitaḥ tadutpannaḥ /
na ca pramāṇamīdṛśam, anavasthāprasaṅgāditi bhāvaḥ /
nirārakaroti---atidoṣo 'yamiti /
yathā ca pramāṇasya pramāṇopapannatā na cānavasthā, tathā dvitīye nivedayiṣyate /
na ca prasiddhataratayā na prayojanaṃ lakṣaṇīyam iti yuktam, kathamasya prayuktau sādhanatvam, kva ca prayojayati, kathaṃ ca vyāpakamiti sarvasya parīkṣakapravedanīyatvāt /
athānya iti /
aprāmāṇiko laukika iti /
yathā vaṭe vaṭe vaiśravaṇaḥ
iti /
nirākaroti---tanna budhyāmaha iti /
prayojanasya prāmāṇikatvādityarthaḥ /
yadapyuktaṃ nyāyasyāṅgaṃ prayojanaṃ na bhavati, tasmāt na vaktavyamiti, tanna yuktam /
children.translated_text: And what has been said — that purpose is not a component (<s>aṅga</s>) of the <s>nyāya</s> (logical method), and therefore should not be stated — that is not proper.

children.text: yā khalu niṣprayojaneti na brūmaḥ prayojanaṃ nyāyasyāṅgamityapi, mukhyaṃ prayojanameva hi tanna syād yadṛte puruṣādanyārthamiti /
children.translated_text: Indeed, we do not say that [examination] is purposeless, nor that purpose is a component of the <s>nyāya</s>; for the primary purpose would be precisely that without which a person does not [undertake] something for another purpose.

children.text: prayojanavāṃstu nyāyo niṣprayojanāṃ tadgatāṃ cintāmaṅgī karoti, phalavatsannidhāvaphalaṃ tadaṅgamiti nyāyāt /
children.translated_text: But the <s>nyāya</s>, having purpose, makes purposeless the inquiry belonging to it — since by the principle that what is without fruit becomes a component in the proximity of what has fruit.

children.text: tasmādanaṅgamapi prayojanaṃ parīkṣāyā mūlaṃ svarga iva setikartavyatākasya yāgādyanuṣṭhānasyeti siddham //24 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, purpose, though not a component [of nyāya], is the root of inquiry — just as heaven is [the root] of the performance of sacrifice and the like with its prescribed procedures — this is established. //24//

The definition of <s>prayojana</s> (purpose), which comes next in the order of enumeration — 'that for the sake of which... purpose.' //24// Here the word '<s>artha</s>' (object/purpose) is for the purpose of encompassing both the secondary and primary purposes. Of these, the primary [purpose] is the attainment of pleasure and avoidance of pain; the secondary is the means to that. Here the <s>bhāṣya</s> — 'that for the sake of which' and so on. Here, the explanation of 'having attended to' (<s>adhikṛtya</s>) is: 'having resolved, having determined' — this is the meaning. And in the resolution, the attainment of pleasure and avoidance of pain constitute the object. And it is not the case that the attainment and avoidance of pleasure and pain are in their own form the objects of engagement and cessation; rather, it is only through engagement with their means that they are the objects of a conscious being's engagement — thus he shows — 'he follows the means for their attainment and avoidance.' 'Because of being the cause of engagement' — although the attainment and avoidance of pleasure and pain and their means exist, nevertheless, when known in general, they are causes of engagement through the offering of desire and the like. Now, the <s>sūtra</s> has 'having attended to,' while the <s>bhāṣya</s> has 'having resolved' — how is there no contradiction? — therefore he says — 'resolution is the attending to the purpose' and so on. The <s>vārttikakāra</s> explains this — 'that for the sake of which, having attended to,' 'resolution.' He asks — 'of what?' — the resolution regarding the attainment and avoidance of pleasure and pain would engage [one] only therein. And these two are not fit for engagement [in themselves]. And the determination of one thing does not cause engagement in another, because of over-extension — this is the import. The answer — 'of the means of pleasure and pain.' And thus there is agreement between cognition and engagement — this is the meaning. He shows its all-pervasiveness — 'by this purpose.' Even for <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavil), the purpose has been stated in the first <s>sūtra</s>. 'Of one being criticized while engaging' — this is the meaning. He raises a doubt — 'if.' 'That by which [things] are perceived is <s>loka</s>' (common knowledge) — i.e., <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge). 'Connected with it' means 'born from it.' And there is no such <s>pramāṇa</s>, because of the unwanted consequence of infinite regress — this is the import. He refutes — 'this is an excessive fault.' And how <s>pramāṇa</s> is validated by <s>pramāṇa</s> without infinite regress will be explained in the second [book]. And it is not proper to say that [purpose] should not be defined because of its being more well-known — since how it serves as a means in application, where it motivates, and how it is pervasive — all this needs to be communicated to the examiner. 'But another' — an unauthorized, worldly [person]. As in [the saying] 'at every banyan tree, there is <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> [i.e., wealth].' He refutes — 'we do not understand that.' Because purpose is authoritatively established — this is the meaning.

children.text: NyS_1,1.25: laukikaparīkṣadāṇāṃ yasminn arthe buddhisāmyaṃ sa dṛṣṭāntaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.25: An example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) is that regarding which there is agreement of understanding among ordinary people, examiners, and experts.

children.text:
kramaprāptaṃ dṛṣṭāntaṃ lakṣayati---lauki---ntaḥ//25// dṛṣṭānta iti lakṣyanirdeśaḥ, śeṣaṃ lakṣaṇam /
sādhyasādharmyāt taddharmabhāvitvenāryate tathā sādhyavaidharmyādataddharmabhāvitvenāryate yaḥ so 'rthastasmin /
tathā ca nātivyāptiḥ /
udāharaṇasūtrāccedṛśaviśeṣapratilambhaḥ /
lokasāmānyam kiṃ tadityata āha---naisargikamiti /
śāstrapariśīlanalabdhajanmā buddhyatiśayo vainayikaḥ /
tadrahitā laukikāḥ pratipādyā iti tāvat /
tadviparītāḥ tadubhayaṃsapannāśca parīkṣakāḥ pratipādakā iti yāvat kathābahutvācca bahuvayanam /
tadanena vādiprativādinau darśitau, tayorbuddhisāmyaṃ vyācaṣṭe---yathā yamarthamiti /
lakṣaṇaprayojanamāha---dṛṣṭāntavirodheneti /
dṛṣṭāntasya virodho viruddhatvaṃ sādhyavikalatvādi /
pratipakṣā iti pratipakṣāsādhanāni /
samādhiḥ abhūtadośāropasya pratiṣedhaḥ /
lakṣitaśca dṛṣṭānta udāharaṇalakṣaṇāya kalpate ghaṭate iti bhāṣyam /
atra vārttikakāro laukikaparīkṣakasvarūpamavivakṣitamiti manvāna āha---buddhisāmyeti /
avivakṣāyāḥ prayojanamanvayavyatirekābhyāmāha---evaṃ ceti /
pareṣā dṛṣṭāntalakṣaṇakṣepamupanyasya dūṣayati---so 'yaṃ dṛṣṭānta iti /
dṛṣṭāntasya prayojanamāha---dṛṣṭāntaḥ sārūpyavyutpattyarthaḥ /
yathā ākṣeptroktaṃ tattadakṣaramanūdya dūṣayati---asiddhasādhanārtho veti /
na khalvasiddhaḥ sādhyena sādhanasyāvinābhāvo dṛṣṭāntena sādhyate ityarthaḥ//25 //
children.translated_text: He defines <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example), which comes next in order — 'ordinary... example.' //25// '<s>Dṛṣṭānta</s>' is the indication of the definiendum; the rest is the definition. That object regarding which — because of similarity with what is to be established, one is led [to understand] through the presence of its properties, and similarly because of dissimilarity with what is to be established, one is led through the absence of its properties — in that [object]. And thus there is no over-extension. And such specific [understanding] is obtained from the <s>sūtra</s> on illustration (<s>udāharaṇa</s>). What the commonality with ordinary people is — to this he says — 'innate.' The intellectual superiority born of the cultivation of treatises (<s>śāstra</s>) is the trained (<s>vainayika</s>) [kind]. Those devoid of that are ordinary people — [they are] those to be instructed. Those who are the opposite, or who possess both, are the examiners — those who instruct. And the plural is because of the multiplicity of debaters. By this, the proponent (<s>vādin</s>) and the opponent (<s>prativādin</s>) are indicated. He explains the agreement of understanding between them — 'just as, that for the sake of which.' He states the purpose of the definition — 'by the contradiction of the example.' Contradiction of the example means its being contradictory, i.e., being deficient with respect to what is to be established, and the like. 'Opposing arguments' means means of opposing argument. 'Resolution' (<s>samādhi</s>) means the negation of the attribution of a non-existent fault. And the defined example serves for — i.e., is fit for — the definition of illustration — this is the <s>bhāṣya</s>. Here the <s>vārttikakāra</s>, considering that the specific nature of ordinary people and examiners is not intended, says — 'agreement of understanding.' He states the reason for non-intention through positive and negative concomitance — 'and thus.' Having presented the opponent's criticism of the definition of example and refuting it — 'this very example.' He states the purpose of the example — 'the example is for the purpose of understanding the similarity.' Just as he quoted the objector, he refutes each word — 'or, for establishing what is unestablished.' The meaning is: the invariable concomitance of the reason with what is to be established, which is not [yet] established, is not established by the example. //25//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.26: An established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>) is the settled acceptance regarding a doctrine, a topic, or an assumption.

children.text: atra bhāṣyakāraḥ siddhāntasāmānyalakṣaṇamapaṭhitvaiva tātparyaṃ vyācaṣṭe---atha siddhāntaḥ ityādinā /
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s>, without reciting the general definition of <s>siddhānta</s>, explains its purport — with 'now, <s>siddhānta</s>' and so on.

children.text: tatra idamitthaṃbhūtamiti vārttikakāro vyācaṣṭe---idamiti sāmānyata iti /
children.translated_text: There, 'this is of such a nature' — the <s>vārttikakāra</s> explains — 'this, in general.'

children.text: bhāṣye ca saṃsthitiritthaṃbhāvavyastheti sāmānyopakramasya abhyupagamasya pramāṇato viśeṣaparyantatāparisamāptiḥ saṃsthitirityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And in the <s>bhāṣya</s>, '<s>saṃsthiti</s>' (settled state) means: the completion and conclusion reaching the particular through [the process beginning from] the general commencement of the acceptance, by means of <s>pramāṇa</s> — this is the meaning.
The <s>vārttikakāra</s> says that the <s>sūtra</s> is for this very meaning — 'of this meaning.'

children.text:
tantrā---ntaḥ//26// sūtrārthamākṣipati---kiṃ punariti /
lakṣaṇārtha ceti /
sāmānyalakṣaṇārtham, na khalu sāmānyalakṣaṇamantareṇa śakyo vibhāga ityuktam//26 //
children.translated_text: Doctrine... conclusion. //26// He raises an objection to the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> — 'what then?' 'And for the purpose of definition' — for the purpose of a general definition; for without a general definition, the division is not possible — this has been stated. //26//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.27: [There are distinctions] because of the difference in meaning among the settled conclusions of all systems, of particular systems, of topics, and of assumptions.

children.text:
samādhatte---nānārṣamiti /
lakṣaṇārthatvaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇārthatvam /
tantryante vyutpādyante prameyāṇyaneneti tantraṃ pramāṇam /
tadevādhikaraṇam āśrayo jñāpakatvena yeṣāmarthānāṃ te tathoktāḥ /
aśāstritaḥ apramāṇika ityarthaḥ /
ābhimānikaṃ ca prāmāṇikatvam, tena siddhāntabhedināmarthānāṃ sarveṣāṃ na prāmāṇikatvaprasaṅgaḥ /
tadevaṃ bhāṣyakāreṇa vyākhyāya sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ paṭhitam /
evaṃ vyākhyānapūrvakameva vibhāgasūtraṃ paṭhati---tantrārthasaṃsthitiriti /
tantragrahanena ca sarvatantrapratitantrayorupādānam /

children.translated_text: Because both are doctrines (<s>tantra</s>).
This is what has been stated — 'but because of the difference of doctrine.'
'An acceptance whose meaning has not been determined.'

children.text: sākṣācchāstre nopātto yathā manasa indriyabhāva iti //27 //
children.translated_text: Not directly taken up in the treatise — such as the sense-organ status of the mind (<s>manas</s>). //27//

He reconciles — 'of different sages.' The property of being for the purpose of definition means being for the purpose of the general definition. '<s>Tantra</s>' (system/treatise) — that by which the <s>prameyas</s> (knowable objects) are systematically taught — that is <s>tantra</s>, i.e., <s>pramāṇa</s> (authoritative source). That itself is the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic/basis), the support of those meanings [that depend on it] as their indicator — they are so called. 'Unauthorized' means not authoritatively established — this is the meaning. And the authoritativeness is self-claimed; therefore, not all meanings that differ from the <s>siddhānta</s> have the [unwanted] consequence of being authoritative. Thus, having explained as the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> did, the general definition is recited. Having preceded [it] with such an explanation, he recites the division-<s>sūtra</s> — 'the settled state of the purpose of the doctrine.' And by the word '<s>tantra</s>' (doctrine), both <s>sarvatantra</s> (all-system) and <s>pratitantra</s> (particular-system) are included.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.28: A meaning that is not contradicted by any system and is established in a [particular] system is the <s>sarvatantrasiddhānta</s> (conclusion of all systems).

children.text:
sarva---ntaḥ //27// yadyapi ghrāṇādiṣu bhautikatvābhautikatvādayo vipratipattayaḥ, tathāpi indriyatve nāsti vipratipattiriti /
tadetad vārttikakāro vyācaṣṭe---sarveṣāmiti /

children.translated_text: Here he objects — 'not from the example.'
He resolves — 'there is a difference.'

children.text: na caivaṃ sarvatantrasiddhāntaḥ, tasya sarvaireva niścitatvāditi, anumānāgamayoriti /
children.translated_text: And the <s>sarvatantrasiddhānta</s> (conclusion of all systems) is not like this, since it is determined by all — thus, 'of inference and scripture.'

children.text: saṃbandhagrahaṇāśrayāvanumānāgamau, yatra ca saṃbandhagrahaḥ sa dṛṣṭānta ityarthaḥ //28 //
children.translated_text: Inference and scripture rest upon the apprehension of a connection, and where there is the apprehension of the connection, that is the example — this is the meaning. //28//

All... conclusion. //28// Although there are disagreements about whether the nose and the like are elemental or non-elemental, nevertheless there is no disagreement about their being sense organs. The <s>vārttikakāra</s> explains this — 'of all.'
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.29: What is established in one's own system but not established in another's system is the <s>pratitantrasiddhānta</s> (conclusion of a particular system).
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.29: What is established in one's own system but not established in another's system is the <s>pratitantrasiddhānta</s> (conclusion of a particular system).

children.text:
samā---ntaḥ //29// samānaśabda ekaparyāyaḥ /
naiyāyikānāṃ hi samānaṃ tantraṃ nyāyaśāstram, paratantraṃ ca sāṃkhyādiśāstram /
cetanā ātmanaḥ niratiśayā apariṇāmino na kenacid dharmeṇopajanāpāyadharmeṇa yujyante /
children.translated_text: The consciousness of the self (<s>ātman</s>), being unsurpassable and not subject to transformation, cannot be associated with any property that has the nature of arising and perishing.

children.text: prākṛteṣu ca dehādiṣu tatkāraṇeṣu mahadahaṅkārapañcatanmātrabhūtasūkṣmeṣu viśeṣo 'tiśaya ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And in the products of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) — the body and the like, and their causes — the subtle [principles] <s>Mahat</s> (intellect), <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), the five <s>Tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), and the gross elements — the distinguishing feature (<s>viśeṣa</s>) means excellence — this is the meaning.
The <s>vārttikakāra</s> explains this <s>sūtra</s> — 'in general.'
The restriction is: of the <s>Yogins</s> alone, of the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> alone. //29//

Same... conclusion. //29// The word '<s>samāna</s>' (same) is a synonym [for 'one's own']. For the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> (logicians), the same system is the <s>Nyāyaśāstra</s> (science of logic), and the other system is the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and other treatises.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.30: That whose establishment leads to the establishment of another topic is the <s>adhikaraṇasiddhānta</s> (topical conclusion).

children.text:
yat---ntaḥ//30// yasyārthasya sādhyasya vā hetorvā siddhau iti viṣayasaptamī, na tu nimittasaptamī, dvayorjñāyamānayornimittanaimittikabhāvāyogāt /
tena yasminnarthe jñāyamāne tadanuṣaṅgiṇo 'rthāstadantarbhāvino gamyante, so 'rthaḥ sākṣādadhikriyamāṇastadanuṣaṅgiṇāṃ cādhāraḥ tadāśrayatvāt tatsiddheḥ, sa pakṣo vā bhavatu heturvā anena rūpeṇa adhikaraṇasiddhāntaḥ /
pakṣastāvad yathā vivādādhyāsitamupalabdhimatkāraṇamutpattimattvād tastrādivaditi /
atra hi pṛthivyādigatenotpattimattena upalabdhimatpūrvakatvaṃ tadgataṃ sādhyamānaṃ svasiddhyantargatānuṣaṅgisarvajñatvādyupetameva sidhyati, nānyathehopalabdhimatpūrvakatvasya siddhiriti /
bhāṣye hetupratisandhānaṃ sidhyat anuṣaṅgyarthāntarānvitaṃ sidhyatītpudāhlatam /
tadetatsarvāvarodhārthaṃ vārttikakṛd āha---vākyārtheti /
heturīdṛśaḥ pakṣaśca vākyārtha ityarthaḥ /
pūrvo 'rtho yaḥ sākṣāddhikṛtaḥ tasya siddhāvantargata iti bhāṣyārthaḥ//30 //
children.translated_text: That... conclusion. //30// 'Upon the establishment of which meaning' — whether what is to be proved or the reason — the locative is in the sense of the object, not in the sense of cause, since when both are being cognized, the relation of cause and caused is untenable. Therefore, when a certain meaning is known, the meanings that are accessory to it and included within it are understood — and that meaning, being directly taken up as the topic, is also the basis for those accessory [meanings] because their establishment depends on it. Whether that be a thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) or a reason (<s>hetu</s>), in this form it is the <s>adhikaraṇasiddhānta</s>. As a thesis, for example: 'the cause of what is perceptible is disputed; it possesses a producer, because of being produced — like a pot and the like.' For here, the property of being preceded by a perceptible [cause], which is the <s>sādhya</s> (thing to be proved) belonging to earth and the like that are characterized by production, when being established, is established only as inclusive of omniscience and the like that are accessory [conclusions] included within its own establishment — not otherwise is the establishment of being preceded by a perceptible [cause] possible. In the <s>bhāṣya</s>, the connection with the reason is: 'what is being established is established together with the accessory incidental meanings' — this has been illustrated. The <s>vārttikakāra</s> states this for the purpose of encompassing all — 'the meaning of the sentence.' The meaning is: both such a reason and such a thesis are the meaning of the sentence. The first meaning — that which is directly taken up — 'upon its establishment, [the other] is included within' — this is the meaning of the <s>bhāṣya</s>. //30//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.31: An <s>abhyupagamasiddhānta</s> (conclusion by assumption) is the examination of the specific [implications] of what has been accepted without examination.

children.text: athābhyupagamasiddhāntasūtram---apa-ntaḥ//31// tad vārttikakāro vyācaṣṭe---aparīkṣito 'sūtrita iti, sūtritasya prāyeṇa parīkṣāsaṃbandhāt, manaso hīndritvenāsūtritasyāpi indriyatvābhyupagamaḥ pramāṇādhikaraṇo yataḥ, tasmādayamabhyupagamasiddhāntaḥ /
sūtraṃ caivaṃ cojanīyam, asūtritābhyupagamāt hetoryatastadviśeṣaparīkṣaṇaṃ kriyate, tasmād viśeṣaparīkṣaṇāt jñāyate asūtritamapyabhyupagataṃ sūtrakāreṇa /
children.translated_text: And the <s>sūtra</s> should be construed thus: because of the acceptance of what has not been formulated in a <s>sūtra</s> — which is the reason — the specific examination of it is undertaken; from that specific examination it is known that what was not formulated in a <s>sūtra</s> was nevertheless accepted by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the <s>sūtras</s>).
This acceptance of his is the <s>abhyupagamasiddhānta</s> (conclusion by assumption). //

Now, the <s>sūtra</s> on the conclusion by assumption — 'without examination... conclusion.' //31// The <s>vārttikakāra</s> explains that — 'unexamined means not formulated in a <s>sūtra</s>,' since what is formulated in a <s>sūtra</s> is generally connected with examination. For the acceptance of the sense-organ status of the mind (<s>manas</s>), though not formulated in a <s>sūtra</s>, is based on <s>pramāṇa</s> (authoritative evidence) — since the mind is an organ — therefore this is an <s>abhyupagamasiddhānta</s>.

children.text:
evaṃ svamatena sūtraṃ vyākhyāya bhāṣyakāravyākhyānaṃ dūṣayati---śāstrānabhyupagata iti /
pramāṇīkṛtena śāstreṇānanujñātaḥ pramāṇānadhīna ityarthaḥ /
pramāṇatāntrābhyupagamasaṃsthitiriti hi siddhāntasāmānyalakṣaṇam, na ca pramāṇānadhīnābhyupagamastadanvetīti nāyamīdṛśo 'bhyupagamasiddhānto bhavitumarhatīti hṛdi nidhāyāyuktāpi darśitā /
ajñaṃ pratyasadācāratvāt pramāṇikaṃ ca puruṣaṃ pratyaśakyatvāt buddhimato 'vajñānasyāyuktatvāt aśakyatvādityarthaḥ /
sarva evāyaṃ pakṣa iti /
sarvatantrapratitantrasiddhāntau tāvat sākṣādabhyupagamyamānau svamukhenaiva pakṣatayābhidhīyete /
adhikaraṇābhyupagamau ca sākṣāt anabhyupagamyamānāvapyarthādabhyupagantavyāviti arthāpattyā pakṣāvityarthaḥ /
nanu yadyupapannaḥ pramāṇatayā abhyupagamaḥ siddhāntaḥ, tarhi siddhāntabhedināmarthānāṃ prāmāṇikatvena viruddhadharmasamāliṅgitā bhāvāḥ prasajyerannityata āha---tatpratyayāt /
tasya pramāṇopapannakarmatvasya pratyayādabhimānādityarthaḥ /
pakṣa iti /
paci vyaktīkaraṇe ityasmād vyutpannam /
karmatayā vyajyamānatayā vā upādānaṃ svārthasya pakṣa iti padam /
upādīyate 'neneti vyutpattyā /
kriyāsādhana iti pradhānakriyāsādhane /
kriyāviśeṣayukta iti avāntaravyāpārayukte tena hi pradhānakriyāyāṃ kārakāṇāṃ vaicitryaṃ bhavatīti /
yaścāsau nyāyasyābhyupagama iti /
yāvadabhyupagataṃ nyāyyasya sādhanaṃ nyāya iti, tāvabhyupagataṃ bhavati prameyasādhanaṃ pramāṇamiti /
na ca dharmiṇi anabhyupagate tadāśrayo 'bhyupagato bhavati /
tasmādubhayathāpi sarvatantrasiddhāntānapahnava ityarthaḥ /
atha saṃgrahaḥ pakṣaśabdeneti, yathā daṇḍiśabdena daṇḍasaṃbandhopahitasīmānaḥ samānāsamānajātīyāḥ sarve saṃgṛhyante, tathā pakṣaśabdenāpītyarthaḥ ayaṃ tu kalpaḥ sarvatantrasiddhāntāvyāpakatvakathanenaivārthādapākṛta iti na pṛthak nirākṛtaḥ /
pakṣaśabdo hi vyajyamānatvopādhinibandhanapravṛttiḥ, na ca vyajyamānatvamasti nisargavyakte sarvatantrasiddhānta iti bhāva /
vākyārthapratipattāviti /
pīno devadatto divā na bhuṅkte iti vākyasya divābhojananiṣedho 'rthaḥ /
tasmāt tadviparītarātribhojanavidhirarthāpattirlokasiddhā /
sā ca na yathā pramāṇāntarulaṃ tathā dvitīye nivedayiṣyate /
tadanena prabandhena bhadantadignāgoditāni dūṣaṇāni nirākṛtāni//31 //
children.translated_text:
Having thus explained the <s>sūtra</s> according to his own view, he criticizes the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>'s explanation — 'not accepted by the <s>śāstra</s>' etc.
'Not accepted by the <s>śāstra</s>' means not sanctioned by the authoritative <s>śāstra</s>, i.e., not based on <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) — this is the meaning.
For the general definition of <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine) is 'a position established through acceptance based on <s>pramāṇa</s>,' and an acceptance not based on <s>pramāṇa</s> does not conform to that — therefore this cannot be such an accepted <s>siddhānta</s>. Keeping this in mind, the impropriety is also shown.
Because it is improper conduct toward the ignorant, because it is impossible to refute a person who relies on <s>pramāṇa</s>, and because contempt of the wise is improper — 'because of impossibility' is the meaning.
'This is entirely a <s>pakṣa</s>' (thesis/position) — the <s>sarvatantra</s> (universal) and <s>pratitantra</s> (school-specific) <s>siddhāntas</s>, being directly accepted, are stated as positions in their own voice.
And the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic-based) doctrines, though not directly accepted, must be accepted through implication — so they are positions by <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) — this is the meaning.
But if an acceptance supported by <s>pramāṇa</s> is a <s>siddhānta</s>, then the objects that differ from one <s>siddhānta</s> to another, being established by <s>pramāṇa</s>, would be characterized by contradictory properties — to this he says: 'because of the conviction in that.'
'Because of the conviction' means because of the belief in its being an action supported by <s>pramāṇa</s> — this is the meaning.
'<s>Pakṣa</s>' — this is derived from the root '<s>paci</s>' meaning 'to make manifest.'
<s>Pakṣa</s> is the adoption of one's own position through action or through being made manifest.
By the derivation 'that by which [something] is adopted' —
'Instrument of action' means the primary instrument of action.
'Endowed with a specific action' means endowed with a subsidiary operation, for it is through that that the diversity of causal factors in the primary action arises.
'And the acceptance of the valid [reasoning] is <s>nyāya</s>' — insofar as the accepted means of proof is called <s>nyāya</s>, to that extent it is accepted that the means of proving what is to be known is <s>pramāṇa</s>.
And when the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) is not accepted, the property depending on it cannot be accepted.
Therefore, in either case, the <s>sarvatantra-siddhānta</s> cannot be denied — this is the meaning.
Now, if the word <s>pakṣa</s> means 'collection,' then just as the word '<s>daṇḍin</s>' (one with a staff) includes all things of the same and different classes whose boundaries are delimited by the relation with a staff, so too the word '<s>pakṣa</s>' [would include everything] — this is the meaning. But this interpretation has been implicitly set aside by the very statement that it does not extend to the <s>sarvatantra-siddhānta</s>, and so is not separately refuted.
For the word <s>pakṣa</s> has its application conditioned by the qualification of 'being made manifest,' and the <s>sarvatantra-siddhānta</s>, being manifest by nature, does not have this quality of being made manifest — this is the purport.
'In the understanding of the meaning of a sentence' —
The meaning of the sentence 'fat <s>Devadatta</s> does not eat during the day' is a prohibition of eating during the day.
Therefore, the injunction of eating at night, which is the opposite of that, is <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) well-known in the world.
And that [<s>arthāpatti</s>] is not a separate <s>pramāṇa</s> — this will be explained in the second [book].
By this discussion, the objections raised by the venerable <s>Dignāga</s> have been refuted. //31//

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.32: Proposition (<s>pratijñā</s>), reason (<s>hetu</s>), example (<s>udāharaṇa</s>), application (<s>upanaya</s>), and conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>) are the members [of a syllogism] (<s>avayavas</s>).

children.text:
prati---vāḥ //32// vārttikakāraḥ sūtratātparyamāha---avayavānāmiti /
nanvavayavasāmānyalakṣaṇam antareṇāśakyo vibhāgoddeśaḥ, tadviśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ ca /
na cedaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ vibhāgaparatvādityata āha---sūtram, vibhāgaparamapyetadarthādavayavasāmānya lakṣaṇaṃ sūcayatīti sūtram /
anyaparādapi vākyāt pratīyamāno 'rtho 'pekṣita svīkriyata eveti śābdāḥ /
tatrāvayavapadādeva sāmānyalakṣaṇamavagamyate /
avayavatvenaikavākyatā darśitā /
sā ca padānāṃ parasparamasaṃpratyāyitāpekṣitasaṃbandhayogyārthapratyayena bhavati /
tasmāt tathāvidhārthapratyāyanameva pratijñādīnāmavayavasāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ siddhamiti sūtramityanena darśitaṃ vārttikakṛtā iti /
vibhāgoddeśatātparyamāha---vibhāgeti /
tryavayavagrahaṇam upalakṣaṇārtham, dvyavayavamityapi draṣṭavyam /
atra bhāṣyaṃ tatrāpratīyamāna iti /
sāmānyenāvagatadharmiṇi viśeṣaṇāgnimattvādinā sandigdhe, agnimattvāditattvāvadhāraṇaṃ pratyayaḥ /
tasyārthaḥ prayojanaṃ hānopādānopekṣabuddhayaḥ /
tasya pravarttikā utpādikā jijñāsā pratyayasādhanānusaraṇadvāreṇa pratyāsattiḥ saṃśayatattvajñānayorviśeṣagatā na tu svarūpagatā, saṃśayānantarayā jijñāsayā saṃśayasya vyavadhānāt /
śakyaṃ prameyam /
tasmin prāptiḥ śaktatā pramāṇānāṃ pramātuśca /
sā ca svarūpasahakāribhyāṃ dvedhā /
tāmimāṃ bhāṣyakāro 'nayā vacobhaṅgyā darśayati---prakātaḥ pramāṇānīti /
pratijñādivaditi /
vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntāḥ /
pratipakṣepavarṇanamiti /
yadi śabdo nityaḥ syāt, na syāt kṛtaka iti anityatvasya nityatvaṃ pratipakṣaḥ /
tasmin hetvabhāvopavarṇanaṃ na cāyamakṛtaka iti /
tadupavarṇanapratiṣedhe sati tattvajñānābhyanujñānārtham /
tattvaṃ jñāyate 'neneti tattvajñānaṃ pramāṇam /
tadabhyanujñānārthaṃ saṃśayavyudāsaḥ tarkāparanāmā /
vyudasyate hi tena pramāṇābhyanujñānadvāreṇa itikartavyatābhūtena saṃśaṃya iti /
tadetad bhāṣyajātaṃ praśnapūrvakaṃ vārttikakṛd vyācaṣṭe---kathaṃ punariti /
na punarjijñāsādayaḥ parapratipādakāḥ śabdādavagatāḥ santaḥ /
atha mā bhūvan parapratipādakāḥ, svapratipādakā eva kasmāt na bhavantītyata āha---niścitatvācceti /
sādhanādeva gamyate prāpyate, prāptaṃ ca jñāyata ityarthaḥ /
śakyaprāptiśca prāthate jñāyata ityarthaḥ /
tat kiṃ sarvathaivānaṅgaṃ jijñāsādaya ityata uktaṃ bhāṣyakatā, prakaraṇe tu jijñāsādayaḥ samarthā iti /
tadanubhāṣya vyācaṣṭe---prakaraṇe tviti /
prakaraṇaṃ kathāpravṛttiḥ /
tadutthāpakā jijñāsādayo 'vayavā aṅgan ityarthaḥ /
te ca jijñāsādaya utpannāḥ prakaraṇasyotthāpakāḥ svarūpeṇa, na punaḥ svajñānena yena śabdapratipādyāḥ santaḥ prakaraṇe 'pyaṅgaṃ bhaveyuḥ, yathā pratijñādayaḥ svajñānena svārthān pratipādayantaḥ /
tasmāt sarvathaiva vijñāsādivācakapadaprayogo 'narthaka iti bhāvaḥ /
ata eva āha---parapratipādakatvāditi /
tuśabdo jijñāsādibhyo vyavacchinatti /
tryavayamapi ityapinā dvyavayavaniṣedhaṃ samuccinoti /
upanayanigamanayoḥ ityatra pratijñāyā apīti draṣṭavyam//32 //
children.translated_text:
Proposition... members //32// The <s>Vārttikakāra</s> states the purport of the <s>sūtra</s> — 'of the members' etc.
But the general definition of a member cannot yield the classificatory enumeration without the specific definitions of the members.
Since this [<s>sūtra</s>] is directed toward classification, it is not a general definition — to this he says: 'the <s>sūtra</s>' — even though directed toward classification, this <s>sūtra</s> also indicates the general definition of a member by implication.
The <s>Śābdas</s> (grammarian-philosophers) hold that a meaning understood from a sentence, even when the sentence has another primary purpose, is accepted if it is needed.
Here, the general definition is understood from the very word '<s>avayava</s>' (member).
By [calling them] members, their syntactic unity (<s>ekavākyatā</s>) has been shown.
And that [syntactic unity] arises from the cognition of a mutually dependent, required, and fitting meaning among the words.
Therefore, precisely such communication of meaning is the established general definition of proposition and the rest as members — this has been shown by the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> with the word '<s>sūtra</s>.'
He states the purport of the classificatory enumeration — 'classification' etc.
The mention of three members is illustrative; 'two members' should also be considered.
Here the <s>Bhāṣya</s> passage is 'there, when not understood' etc.
When the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) is known in general but is in doubt regarding a specific qualification such as 'possessing fire' etc., the ascertainment of the truth of possessing fire etc. is the conviction (<s>pratyaya</s>).
Its purpose (<s>artha</s>) is the cognitions of avoidance, adoption, and indifference.
The desire to know, which is the instigator of that [conviction], is the proximity [to knowledge] through the pursuit of the means of conviction — pertaining to the specific [difference] between doubt and true knowledge, not to [their] intrinsic nature, since doubt is intervened by the desire to know that immediately follows it.
'Capable' means the object of knowledge (<s>prameya</s>).
Reach (<s>prāpti</s>) with respect to that is the capacity of <s>pramāṇas</s> and of the knower.
And that is twofold: through its own nature and through auxiliary factors.
The <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> shows this by this mode of expression — '<s>pramāṇas</s> being evident' etc.
'Like proposition etc.' etc.
Examples by dissimilarity.
'Description of the counter-thesis' etc.
If sound were eternal, it would not be produced — thus the counter-thesis to non-eternality is eternality.
The description of the absence of the reason in that [counter-thesis] is: 'and this is not unproduced.'
When such description is negated, it serves to grant [legitimacy to] true knowledge.
'That by which truth is known' — true knowledge means <s>pramāṇa</s>.
For the purpose of granting [authority to] that, the removal of doubt, which has the alternative name <s>tarka</s> (reasoning), [is employed].
For doubt is removed through it by way of granting [authority to] <s>pramāṇa</s>, as it serves the function of 'what is to be done.'
The <s>Vārttikakāra</s> explains this <s>Bhāṣya</s> passage with a question — 'but how?' etc.
But the desire to know and the rest, being understood from the words, do not demonstrate [truths] to others.
Or even if they do not demonstrate to others, why can they not be self-demonstrating? — to this he says: 'because of being ascertained' etc.
One reaches, i.e., arrives at [knowledge], only through proof, and what has been reached is known — this is the meaning.
And the reaching of what is capable [of being known] is arrived at, i.e., known — this is the meaning.
Then are the desire to know and the rest entirely non-constituent? — to this the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> has said: 'but in the context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>), the desire to know and the rest are efficacious.'
Repeating that, he explains — 'but in the context' etc.
Context means the commencement of a discussion (<s>kathā</s>).
The desire to know and the rest, which initiate that [discussion], are constituent members — this is the meaning.
And the desire to know and the rest, once arisen, initiate the context through their own nature, not through the cognition of them that would require verbal communication so that they could also be constituent members in the context — as proposition and the rest demonstrate their own meanings through the cognition of them.
Therefore, the use of words denoting the desire to know etc. is in every way purposeless — this is the purport.
Hence he says — 'because of demonstrating to others' etc.
The word '<s>tu</s>' (but) distinguishes [proposition etc.] from the desire to know and the rest.
'Even three members' — by the word '<s>api</s>' (even), he includes the negation of two members.
'Of application and conclusion' — here, 'of proposition also' should be understood. //32//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.33: The proposition (<s>pratijñā</s>) is the statement of what is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>).

children.text:
sādhya---jñā //33// parigṛhyate 'neneti parigrahaḥ /
sa ca vacanaṃ ceti parigrahavacanam /
udāharaṇam anityaḥ śabdaḥ iti /
tadākṣipya vārttikakāraḥ samādhatte---siddhatvāditi /

children.translated_text: [The mountain] possesses fire, just as it is not devoid of it — its not having fire now is not the case.

children.text: sa ca parvate 'gnimati sādhyamāne viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyayoḥ parasparasaṃbandhalakṣaṇo niyamo 'rthāt sidhyati /
children.translated_text: And when the mountain as possessing fire is being proved, the restriction that is characterized by the mutual connection of qualifier and qualified is established by implication.

children.text: na tu sākṣādayogavyavaccheda eva sādhyaḥ, liṅgasyānyāpohaviṣayatvānabhyupagamāt /
children.translated_text: But the exclusion of the absence of connection is not directly what is to be proved, since the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is not accepted as having exclusion of the other (<s>anyāpoha</s>) as its object.
Its statement — that by which it is stated — is called the proposition-sentence.

Proposition... //33// 'That by which it is encompassed' is the encompassing (<s>parigraha</s>).
And that [encompassing] and the verbal statement [together constitute] the encompassing statement.
An example is: 'sound is non-eternal.'
Raising an objection to this, the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> resolves it — 'because of being established' etc.

children.text:
atrānyayogavyavacchedaṃ vākyārthaṃ manvāno bhadantaḥ pratijñālakṣaṇamativyāptyavyāptibhyām ākṣipati---ubhayeti /
ubhayoravadhāraṇayoḥ prāptau saṃśayena kimidamavadhāryate kiṃ cedamiti prasaktāvityarthaḥ /
pratijñāvadhṛteti /
yata evakaraṇaṃ na tato 'nyatrāvadhāraṇam iti hi śābdā iti bhāvaḥ /
vyatirekitvāditi vyabhicārādityarthaḥ /
samādhatte---sarvasmin vākye iti /
saṃsargo vākyārtha ityutsargaḥ /
kvacit punaranyayogavyavacchedo 'pīti /
sāmānyaśrutau niyamaḥ iti /
yathendriyārthasannikarṣotpannamityukte jñānaṃ sukhādi ca sāmanyena prāptam /
tatra jñānagrahaṇaṃ na vidhāyakam, prāptatvāt /
ataḥ sukhādivyavacchedaphalaṃ vijñāyate /
yadi tvasmaddarśanamatikramya sarvatrāvadhāṇaṃ karoti, tato 'sya lokavirodha ityāha---sarvatra ceti /
tat kri loke na kpacidavadhāraṇam ityata āha---yatra ceti /
codayati---nanu ceti /
siddhapratipakṣaḥ sādhyaśabdasyārtha ityabhiprāyaḥ /
pariharati---na sūtrārtheti /
sarvasandeheṣvidamupatiṣṭhate vyākhyānato 'rthapratipattiriti bhāvaḥ /
codakaḥ svābhiprāyamudghāṭayati---atha punariti /
asādhyanirdeśaḥ siddhānirdeśaḥ /
tasya nivṛttiḥ sādhyaśabdādavagamyate, na tu prajñāpanīyo 'rtha ityarthaḥ /
pariharati---asādhyaṃ ceti /
bhavedetad yadi siddhamātramasādhyaṃ syāt /
api tvanupapadyamānaṃ sādhana siddhiryasya tadapyasādhyam /
tathā cāsiddhasya cākṣuṣatvādernivṛttirityarthaḥ /
punaścodayati---atha punariti /
na kṛtakatvādi siddhaṃ nāpyanupapadyamānasādhanam /
nāpi kṛtakatvādi parāṅgatvenopāttaṃ yenāprajñāpanīyaṃ syādityarthaḥ /
pariharati---naiṣa doṣa iti /
prajñāpanīyena dharmaiṇa dharmiṇo viśiṣṭasya parigrahavacanam iti sūtrārthaḥ, na punardharmamātraparigrahavacanamiti /
abhyupagamya vyavacchedaṃ śabdārthametaduktam, paramārthatastvaniyamaḥ kvacit saṃsargaḥ, kvacid vyavaccheda ityata āha---yaccedamiti /
ito 'pi nāsiddhayorhetudṛṣṭāntayoḥ prasaṅga ityāha---sādhyanirdeśa iti ca pratijñāyāmiti /
pramāṇatantra khalvabhyupagamaḥ siddhāntaḥ /
na ca cākṣuṣatvādiṣu pramāṇamūlatā, tadabhimāno 'pi bādhakādapākṛta iti /
nanu yadi sarvatantrasiddhāntātiriktānāṃ siddhāntāntarāṇāṃ sādhyatvaṃ tarhi sādhyenaiva caritārthatvād apārthakaṃ pṛthagabhidhānameteṣāmiti, ata uktam---avasthāyāmiti /
vimatyavasthāyām, sarvatantre tu vimatiraśakyetyuktam /
parihārāntaramāha---jijñāsādīti /
dhibhāgasūtreṇa prakaraṇotthānahetavo vākyāvayavatayā nirākāryatvena jijñāsādayo buddhisthīkṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: By the <s>sūtra</s> on the division of members, the desire to know and the rest have been legitimized in their mental status as initiators of the context and as sentence-members that need not be formally refuted.
Therefore, wherever the desire to know and the rest are present, that is what is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>).

children.text: na ca cākṣuṣatvādiṣu pramāṇabādhiteṣu santi ta ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And in [properties] like visual perceptibility, which are contradicted by <s>pramāṇa</s>, they are not present — this is the meaning.
He gives another resolution — 'the meaning is worthy' etc.

Here, the venerable [<s>Dignāga</s>], considering exclusion of other connection (<s>anyayogavyavaccheda</s>) as the sentence-meaning, objects to the definition of proposition through over-extension and under-extension — 'both' etc.
When both determinations are possible, the question arises through doubt as to which is being determined — this is the meaning.
'Determined by the proposition' — since the restrictive particle '<s>eva</s>' does not [indicate] determination elsewhere [than where it is placed] — for this is [the view of] the <s>Śābdas</s> — this is the purport.
'Because of being variant' means because of deviation — this is the meaning.
He resolves — 'in every sentence' etc.
The general rule is that conjunction (<s>saṃsarga</s>) is the sentence-meaning.
But sometimes exclusion of other connection also [obtains].
'Restriction in a general statement' — just as when it is said 'that which is produced from the contact of sense organs with objects,' cognition and pleasure etc. are generally obtained.
There, the mention of 'cognition' is not injunctive, since it is already obtained.
Therefore, it is understood to have the function of excluding pleasure and the like.
But if [the opponent] extends determination everywhere beyond our view, then it contradicts common usage — he says: 'and everywhere' etc.
Is there then no determination at all in the world? — to this he says: 'and where' etc.
He objects — 'but surely' etc.
The import is that '<s>sādhya</s>' (that which is to be proved) means 'having an established counter-thesis.'
He resolves — 'not the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>' etc.
In all doubts, this principle holds: 'the meaning is ascertained from the explanation' — this is the purport.
The objector reveals his own intent — 'but then' etc.
'<s>Asādhyanirdeśa</s>' means 'the statement of what is already established.'
Its negation is understood from the word '<s>sādhya</s>' (to be proved), but the meaning to be communicated is not [merely that] — this is the meaning.
He resolves — 'and the unproved' etc.
This would be so if only what is established were 'unproved.'
But that whose establishment through proof is untenable is also 'unproved' (<s>asādhya</s>).
And thus, the negation of [properties] like visual perceptibility that are unestablished [for sound] — this is the meaning.
He objects again — 'but then' etc.
[Properties] like 'being produced' are neither established [for the counter-thesis], nor have an untenable proof,
nor are they adopted by the opponent such that they would be non-communicable — this is the meaning.
He resolves — 'this is not a fault' etc.
The meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is: the encompassing statement of the qualified property-bearer by the property to be communicated — not merely the encompassing statement of the property alone.
Having accepted exclusion as the meaning of the word on the basis of concession, he says that ultimately there is no restriction — sometimes conjunction, sometimes exclusion — hence: 'that which is this' etc.
Also from this [consideration], there is no unwanted consequence regarding the unestablished reason and example — he says: 'and in the proposition as the statement of what is to be proved' etc.
An acceptance grounded in <s>pramāṇa</s> is indeed a <s>siddhānta</s>.
And there is no <s>pramāṇa</s>-basis for [properties] like visual perceptibility, and even the presumption of that is refuted by a defeater.
But if <s>siddhāntas</s> other than the <s>sarvatantra-siddhānta</s> are [all] 'to be proved,' then since '<s>sādhya</s>' alone suffices, the separate statement of these [other <s>siddhāntas</s>] is pointless — to this he says: 'in the situation' etc.
In the situation of disagreement — but in the <s>sarvatantra</s> [doctrine], disagreement is impossible, as has been stated.
He gives another resolution — 'the desire to know and the rest' etc.

children.text:
aparamapi parihāramāha---karmakaraṇayorveti /
evaṃ tāvad vyutpattyādyālocanayā sādhyaśabdasya na hetudṛṣṭāntayoḥ prasaṅgaḥ ityuktam /
saṃprati loka evātisphuṭāstisrovidhā arthānām, kṛtamatra sūkṣmānusaraṇenetyāha---sādhyāsiddhasiddhabhedāditi /
anyatarāsiddhayorhetudṛṣṭāntayoḥ prasaṅgo mā bhūditi karmatayā te upādīyanta ityuktam /
ubhayapakṣeti pakṣaśabdo vargavacanaḥ /
saṃpratipannamubhayorvargayorityarthaḥ /
parihārāntaramāha atha veti /
avayavānāmetat prakaraṇam /
teṣāṃ ca pradhānaikārthapratyāyanenaikavākyatām āpannānāmavayavabhāvaḥ /
yatpratyāyanoddeśena te pravartante tatpradhānam /

children.translated_text: And the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) is qualified by the property to be proved.

children.text: tathā ca na sākṣāt tatpratyāyanāya te vibhavantīti tadarthaṃ sādhane vyāpriyante /
children.translated_text: And thus, since they are not capable of directly conveying that [property-bearer in its qualified form], they are engaged in the proof for that purpose.

children.text: tena siṣādhayiṣitadharmaviśiṣṭo dharmī teṣāṃ pradhānaṃ viṣayaśca /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the property-bearer qualified by the property to be proved is the principal and the object of those [members of the syllogism].

children.text: pradhānaṃ ca prathamaṃ buddhau viparivartate iti sādhyaśabdena sa evocyate, na tu hetudṛṣṭāntāvapradhāne ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And since the principal first revolves in the mind, it alone is referred to by the word <s>sādhya</s> (to be proved), not the reason and example which are non-principal — this is the meaning.

He states yet another resolution — 'of action and instrument.'
Thus, first, by considering the etymology and the like, it has been stated that the word <s>sādhya</s> (to be proved) does not apply to the reason (<s>hetu</s>) and the example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>).
Now [he shows that] in common usage itself the meanings of things are exceedingly clear in three ways, and there is no need for subtle analysis — he says 'due to the distinction of to-be-proved, unestablished, and established.'
Lest the reason and the example, one or the other being unestablished, fall under [the term sādhya], they are taken up as objects (<s>karma</s>) — this has been stated.
'Of both sides' — the word <s>pakṣa</s> (side) here means 'group.' The meaning is: what is accepted by both groups.
He states another resolution — 'or else.'
This is the section on the members [of a syllogism] (<s>avayava</s>).
And of those [members], the state of being members [belongs to them] when they attain unity of sentence by serving the purpose of conveying one principal meaning.
That for the purpose of whose conveyance they function is the principal (<s>pradhāna</s>).

children.text:
tadevamaduṣṭamasmallakṣaṇamiti yadasmallakṣaṇamanena doṣeṇa bhaṅktvā bhadantena anyathā lakṣaṇaṃ praṇītam, tadeva duṣṭamityāha---na cedayamiti /
nanu yatra sādhyapadam asti bhavatu tatreṣṭagrahaṇamanarthakam, na tvasmistadastīti kathamiṣṭagrahaṇamanarthakatamityata āha---karmagrahaṇācceti /
mā bhūt sādhyapadam /

children.translated_text: But there is the word <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis/subject).

children.text: tadapi hi pacyamānaṃ vyajyamānaṃ sādhyamevāha---tacca karma, karma cepsitamiti prāptumiṣṭamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: That too, when analyzed and elucidated, means precisely '<s>sādhya</s>' (to be proved) — and that is the object (<s>karma</s>), and the object is what is desired (<s>ipsita</s>) to be achieved — meaning 'desired to be attained.'

children.text: codayati---athāpyaniṣṭeti, nanvaniṣṭaḥ pakṣa iti vipratiṣiddhamityata uktam---arthataḥ kileti /
children.translated_text:
He objects — 'even if undesired' — but since 'an undesired thesis' is self-contradictory, it is said: 'in meaning, indeed.'
The meaning is that for one engaged in establishing a real state of affairs, such [an undesired thesis] is not desired.
The meaning is: for one engaged in establishing the reality of things, such a thing is not desired.

Thus this definition of ours is faultless — and the fact that the venerable [Buddhist teacher], having broken our definition with this fault, has composed a different definition, that itself is faulty — he says 'if this is not the case.'
But where the word <s>sādhya</s> (to be proved) exists, let the inclusion of '<s>iṣṭa</s>' (desired) be redundant there; but since it does not exist in ours, how is the inclusion of '<s>iṣṭa</s>' redundant? — to this he says 'because of the inclusion of <s>karma</s> (object).'
Let there not be the word <s>sādhya</s>.
While presenting the Buddhist position, he refutes something accepted by them in the middle — 'non-auditory.'
This has been explained in [the commentary on] the first <s>sūtra</s>.
'But [sound] is inferred from cause and from modification.'

children.text:
ityevamādeḥ /
na hi vyavaṅgayaṃ vya/jakaṃ kāraṇamanuvidhīyate /
no khalu mahatī pradīpe ghaṭo mahān alpe vā alpa iti /
mahati tu kāraṇe mahān śabda iti /
children.translated_text: But when the cause is large, the sound is large.

children.text: tasmāt kāraṇato vikārāt kāryaḥ śabdaḥ, yathā mahadbhiḥ sthūlapiṇḍairārabdho 'vayavī mahāniti /
children.translated_text: Therefore sound is an effect, [produced] from cause and modification, just as a whole that is large is produced from large, gross parts.

children.text: tadanena pratyayabhedabheditvaṃ heturupalakṣito bhavati, ādiśabdena ca sataḥ śabdasya
children.translated_text: By this, 'being differentiated by the differentiation of cognitions' is indicated as a reason; and by the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), [the argument] that existing sound, upon
manifestation, has a fault —

And so forth of this kind.
For the thing manifested does not conform to its manifesting cause.
Certainly it is not the case that a pot is large when the lamp is large, or small when [the lamp] is small.
and so forth of this kind should be understood.

children.text: doṣaśca darbhedhyādivadupayuktānāmṛcāṃ niriṣṭikatvena punaranupayogaḥ, kāryatve punaranyatvena na niriṣṭikatvāmityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the fault is that <s>ṛc</s>-verses (Vedic hymns), once used — like <s>darbha</s>-grass, firewood, and the like — cannot be used again because they are exhausted; but if [sound] were an effect, being different [each time], there would be no exhaustion — this is the meaning.

children.text: yadyapyāgamo 'pi śabdānityatve 'sti yathā somaṃ rājānamasṛjata tatastreyo vedā asṛjyanta //
children.translated_text: Although there is also scripture supporting the non-eternality of sound, such as: 'He created King <s>Soma</s>; from that the three <s>Vedas</s> were created.'
Thus.

children.text: tathāpi nāsadāsīnno sadāsīdāmnāya eva khalvayamagra āsīt //
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, [there is also]: 'There was neither non-existence nor existence; this <s>āmnāya</s> (sacred tradition) alone existed in the beginning.'

children.text:
iti nityatve 'pyāgamadarśanāt aniścayādanumānasyaivātra prāmāṇyam /
tathā cānumānavirodha iti /
prasiddhivirodhaṃ tu na budhyamāhe pramāṇavirodhād bhedena /
abodhamāha---ko 'yaṃ prasiddhivirodha iti /
ekagranthenāha---prasiddhiḥ pratyakṣādīnāmiti /
acandraḥ śaśīti /

children.translated_text: If the denotation of the word <s>śaśin</s> for the moon is denied, then there is contradiction with inference that arises from the positive and negative concomitance known through common worldly usage.

If, on the other hand, the denial is of being an object of conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>), then for you [Buddhists] there is contradiction with the direct perception of self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>).

children.text: asmākaṃ tu mānasapratyakṣavirodha iti sarvathā na pramāṇādanyā prasiddhiriti /
children.translated_text: For us, however, there is contradiction with mental perception (<s>mānasa-pratyakṣa</s>) — thus in every case there is no common usage apart from <s>pramāṇa</s>.
Having thus presented the Buddhist position and refuted the examples they cited, he concludes the Buddhist position — 'for this purpose.'

Since there is scriptural testimony for eternality as well, the inconclusive nature [of scripture] means that only inference has authority here.
And thus 'contradiction with inference.'
But we do not understand 'contradiction with common usage' (<s>prasiddhivirodha</s>) as distinct from contradiction with <s>pramāṇa</s>.
He expresses the lack of understanding — 'what is this contradiction with common usage?'
He states in one passage — 'common usage is that of perception and the rest.'
'The moon without a moon' means '<s>śaśin</s> (the moon) is called so [even without an actual rabbit].'

children.text:
tadetad dūṣayati---etacceti /
vastu hi yādṛśaṃ svakāraṇādutpannaṃ tādṛśameva tat /
na tasyānyathābhāva iti na tatra doṣo niviśate /
tadviṣayāṇi padānyapi pratyekam aduṣṭānyeva /
yā punaḥ ṣauruṣeyī dṛṣṭamanyatrārthamanyatra samāropya bhrāntyā vā paravipralambhāya vā pratijñādirūpeṇa vākyakriyā, sā svavacanavirodhādiśālinī duṣṭā /
children.translated_text: But the human act of composing a statement in the form of a thesis and the like, wherein a meaning seen in one place is superimposed upon another through error or for the purpose of deceiving others — that, being characterized by self-contradiction and the like, is faulty.

children.text: taddvāreṇa puruṣo nigṛhyate, nārtho na padānīti /
children.translated_text: Through that, the person is defeated (<s>nigṛhyate</s>), not the object, not the words.

children.text: svārthāpavādaḥ svavacanavirodhaḥ kartṛdoṣo bhramo vā vipralambho vā kriyāyāmupacaryate /
children.translated_text: Self-contradiction of one's own statement is a speaker's fault; error or deception is figuratively attributed to the act [of stating].

children.text: na ca kriyāyāṃ bhramo vā vipralambho vā, tayorabhiprāyabhedatayā puruṣadharmatvāt kriyāyā vastubādhanāt puruṣābhiprāyāvagatiriti kriyādvāreṇetyuktam //
children.translated_text: And in the act [of stating] there is neither error nor deception, since those, being differences of intention, are properties of the person; [rather,] through the act, which presents the reality, the person's intention is understood — hence it is said 'through the act.'

He then criticizes this — 'this.'
For a thing, as it has arisen from its own cause, is just so.
There is no alteration of it, and thus no fault inheres in it.
The words pertaining to it are also individually faultless.

children.text:
codayati---atha pratijñāyā iti /
tadetadatiprasaṅgena dūṣayati---naitad yuktaṃ hetvādīti /
na punardūṣaṇāni nyūnatāvayavāttaradoṣākṣepabhāvodbhāvanānīti /
trairūpyasaṃpanno hetuḥ pūrṇaḥ /
sa triṣu rūpeṣvanyatamena rūpeṇa rahito nyūno 'siddho vā viruddho vā anaikāntiko vā bhavatīti so 'yaṃ nyūnatādoṣo hetoḥ /
avayavadoṣaśca pratijñādoṣaḥ svavacanavirodhādiḥ /
hetudoṣo 'siddhātvādiḥ evamudāharaṇaraṇadoṣaḥ sādhyavikalatvādiḥ /
uttaradoṣo jātiḥ prāptyaprāptisamādiḥ /
tasyākṣepa upādānaṃ svīkāra iti yāvat /
bhāvo 'pratibhādiḥ /
sa hi vādino vā prativādino vābhiprāyaḥ /
tasyodbhāvanāni dūṣaṇanīti /
na hi saṃbhave satyupacāra iti /
pratijñāgatā hi doṣā yadi tadgatatvena udbhāvyamānā na vādino nigrahamāpādayeyuḥ, tatastatra niṣprayojanatvenāsaṃbhavāt pakṣa evopacaryeran, pārayanti tu pratijñāgatāni dūṣaṇāni nigrahituṃ vādinamiti /
so 'yaṃ pratijñādoṣāṇāṃ pratijñāyāṃ saṃbhava iti /
kasmāt punarmañcasthā ityevaṃ na prayu/jate ityata uktam---laukikaprayuktavākyānvākhyānam /
na, anādirlokaprayogo niyojyaḥ paryanuyojyo vetyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text:
He objects — 'if of the thesis.'
He criticizes this by over-extension — 'this is not proper, of the reason and the rest.'
But the refutations are not [merely] deficiency-of-member, faults of the subsequent [member], or manifestations of accusation.
A reason possessing the triple character (<s>trairūpya</s>) is complete.
That [reason], lacking any one of its three forms, is deficient — being either unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>), contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), or inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) — this is the deficiency-fault of the reason.
The fault of a member is a fault of the thesis such as self-contradiction and the like.
The fault of the reason is unestablishedness and the like; similarly the fault of the example is deficiency in what is to be proved and the like.
The fault of the subsequent [response] is the [pseudo-]refutation (<s>jāti</s>) such as the equal attainment-and-non-attainment and the like.
Its 'accusation' means adoption, i.e., acceptance.
'State' refers to non-response (<s>apratibhā</s>) and the like.
For that is the intention of either the proponent or the opponent.
The manifestation of those [states] constitutes the refutations.
For when the primary meaning is possible, there is no figurative usage.
For if the faults belonging to the thesis, being presented as belonging to it, did not bring about the defeat of the proponent, then, being purposeless there, due to impossibility [in the thesis], they would be figuratively attributed to the <s>pakṣa</s> (subject) itself. But the faults belonging to the thesis are capable of defeating the proponent.
This is the possibility of thesis-faults in the thesis.
Why then is the formulation not 'one on a stage'? — to this it is said: 'it is an explanation of statements employed in common usage.'
No — the meaning is that beginningless common usage is not to be commanded or questioned.

children.text:
syādetat /
