iṣṭagrahaṇamanakṣarārūḍhamapyabhiprāyavyāptaṃ sādhyaṃ tathā syādityevamarthaṃ yathā parārthāścakṣurādaya iti /
atra hi pārārthyamātramakṣarārūḍham /
na ca tanmātramasya sādhyam, api tvātmapārārthyam /
tacca noccārayati mā bhūdananvayo hetuḥ saṃghātatvāditi /
tasmāt tadavarodhāyeṣṭagrahaṇamityāha---atheṣṭagrahaṇeneti /
pariharati---ayamapyarthaḥ sādhanādevagamyate /
pratijñāprayogādeva gamyate /
ayamabhisandhiḥ /
vacanaliṅgāḥ hi vaktrabhiprāyā bhavanti /
yatparaṃ ca vacanaṃ sa vacanārthaḥ /
tātparyaṃ cāsya kvacid vācye kvacillakṣya iti sarva evāsau vacanārthaḥ /
yastu naivaṃvidhaḥ kathamasau vacanārthaḥ? kathamasau vādyabhiprāyavyāpta ityavagantavyam? na ca kvacidapi pakṣaḥ pratijñāpadavācyaḥ, tasya vākyārthatvena lakṣyatvād eveti /
aniṣṭanivṛttiriṣṭeti /

children.translated_text: The means of proving that, even while being sought, is itself desired at that time.
In that regard, since effort would be impossible without being preceded by desire, [it is] of that [nature].
Now, doubt is investigation.

children.text: tataśca saṃśayaviṣaya iṣyamāṇo jijñāsyamānaśca sādhya eva bhavati, na sādhanādirityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And thus what is the object of doubt, being desired and being the object of inquiry, is precisely what is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>), not the means of proof and the rest — this is the meaning.

One might object: Even though the word '<s>iṣṭa</s>' (desired) does not appear in the actual words [of the definition], it pervades the intention — and thus '<s>sādhya</s>' (to be proved) would [include] that meaning — just as in 'the eye and the rest serve another's purpose.' For there only the quality of serving-another's-purpose appears in the actual words. But that alone is not what is to be proved; rather, it is the serving-of-the-self's-other's-purpose. And that [the self] is not uttered lest the reason 'because of being an aggregate' become non-concomitant. Therefore, to encompass that, the word '<s>iṣṭa</s>' is included — he says 'if by the inclusion of <s>iṣṭa</s>.'
He resolves — 'this meaning too is understood from the proof itself.'
It is understood from the very employment of the thesis.
The intended meaning is: the intentions of a speaker are known from the indications of his statement.
And the meaning of a statement is that toward which the statement is directed.
And the purport of this is sometimes in what is directly expressed, sometimes in what is implied — thus all of that is the meaning of the statement.
But what is not of this kind — how can it be the meaning of the statement? How can it be understood as pervaded by the speaker's intention? And nowhere is the <s>pakṣa</s> (subject) directly expressed by the word 'thesis' (<s>pratijñā</s>); for it is implied, being the meaning of the sentence.
The removal of the undesired is itself the desired.

children.text:
sthānāntarīyaṃ ca bhadantasya lakṣaṇam,
sādhyatvenepsitaḥ pakṣo viruddhārthānirākṛtaḥ //
children.translated_text:
And the venerable [Buddhist] teacher's definition from another work:
'The <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis) is that which is desired as what is to be proved, and which has not been refuted by a contradictory meaning.'

children.text:
iti dūṣayati---eveneti /
atrāpi hi sādhyapadādūrdhvaṃ vṛthākṣaracatuṣṭayamiti /
tathā pakṣo yaḥ sādhayitumiṣṭaḥ
ityatrāpi vasubandhulakṣaṇe viruddhārthānirākṛtagrahaṇaṃ na kartavyam /
etaduktaṃ bhavati---na kevalamasmākrametad viruddhārthānirākṛtapadamanarthakaṃ pratibhāti, samānatīrthānāmapi tathā vibhāti, yatastairnopāttamiti /
ata evaṃ vaktavyaṃ pakṣo yaḥ sādhayitumiṣṭa iti /
yadyapyatrāpi prayojyaprayojakavyāpārayoḥ sādhayitumiti samānam, tathāpi tumunā ya eva sādhayitā vādī sa evaiṣitetyuktaṃ bhavati /
na punarvādino niyoktā sādhayitā vādī caiṣiteti /
eṣitṛtvaṃ ca vādino dhruvaṃ kṛtvaitaducyate, yadā panureṣitṛtvamapi prayojake saṃcāryate, tadā svayaṅgrahaṇenāpyapratīkāra ityabhiprāyaḥ tattvabhāktayośceti /
siddhaḥ sādhyasya prayojakaḥ kartā /
sa hi sidhyantaṃ sādhyaṃ vādī tasminniyaṃ sādhanā samavetā /
yastu tasyāpi prayojakastṛtīyasthānapatito na tasmin sādhanā samavaitīti /
yaḥ kārayati sa karotyeveti kathañcidasya bhaktyā kartṛtvam, taccāyuktaṃ sati mukhye kartarītyabhiprāyaḥ /
ā/jasatvaṃ mukhyatvam /
pūvābhiprāyasthitamarthamudghāṭayati---tumunaśceti /
atroktaṃ bhāṣyakārīyābhyupagamasiddhāntanirākaraṇāvasare 'pramāṇakamarthamiti /
yastāvat śāstrāviruddho 'rthaḥ pramāṇasiddhaḥ sa śāstrīya eva śāstrābhyupetapramāṇasiddhatvāt, taṃ vyutpādayan na śāstraṃ bādhate /
yastu pramāṇīkṛtavaiśaṣikatantraḥ śabdanityatvaṃ sādhayati so 'navadheyavacanaḥ na hetvabhidhānaṃ yāvat pariṣatprativādibhyāṃ nīyate, api tu pratijñoccāraṇānantarameva nigṛhyate /
yastu vaiśeṣikatantrādhyayanamātrād vaiśeṣikatvamātmano darśayitvā śabdanityatāṃ pratijānīte nāsau pramāṇīkṛtavaiśeṣikatantra iti na nigṛhyate iti /
yaścāpramāṇako 'bhyupagama iti /

children.translated_text: What is accepted is an acceptance (<s>abhyupagama</s>).
The expression of that should be called a thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>).
Because of the inclusion of '<s>sādhya</s>' (to be proved), the inclusion of that [other term] is more economical — this is the meaning.
He who is the venerable <s>Naiyāyika</s> — having concluded the topic, he says 'therefore, devoid of...' (33)

He criticizes this — 'thus.'
For here too, after the word <s>sādhya</s>, four syllables [<s>tvena</s> + <s>ipsitaḥ</s>] are redundant.
Likewise in '<s>pakṣa</s> is what is desired to be proved' — in this definition of <s>Vasubandhu</s> too, the inclusion of 'not refuted by a contradictory meaning' need not be made.
This is what is stated: Not only does this phrase 'not refuted by a contradictory meaning' appear to us as purposeless, it appears so to those of the same school as well, since they have not adopted it.
Therefore it should simply be said: '<s>pakṣa</s> is what is desired to be proved.'
Although here too the functions of the caused-to-do and the causer are common in 'to prove,' nevertheless by the infinitive <s>tumun</s>, the very prover who is the proponent is indicated as the desirer.
But it does not mean that the director of the proponent is the prover and the proponent is the desirer.
This is said with the desirership of the proponent taken as fixed; when the desirership is extended to the instigator too, then even by the word 'own' (<s>svayam</s>) there is no remedy — this is the intention.
Regarding the literal and figurative — the established [prover] is the direct agent of what is to be proved.
For the proponent proves the <s>sādhya</s> as it is being established; this act of proving inheres in him.
But the one who is the instigator of even that [prover], being in the third position, does not have the act of proving inhering in him.
That he who causes [something] to be done also 'does' it — this gives him agency only in a figurative sense; and that is improper when there exists a primary agent — this is the intention.
Directness is primary-ness.
He reveals the meaning established in the prior intention — 'and of the infinitive <s>tumun</s>...'
Here, in the context of refuting the position accepted by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>, what has been stated as 'a matter without <s>pramāṇa</s>-support' [means]:
Whatever meaning is not contradicted by scripture and is established by <s>pramāṇa</s> is itself scriptural, since it is established by <s>pramāṇa</s> accepted by scripture; one who explains that does not contradict scripture.
But one who, having accepted the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> system as authoritative, seeks to prove the eternality of sound — his statement is not to be heeded; he is not led [by the assembly and the opponent] to the point of stating a reason, but is defeated immediately after uttering the thesis.
But one who, merely by having studied the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> system, shows himself to be a <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> and propounds the eternality of sound — he has not [thereby] accepted the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> system as authoritative, so he is not defeated.
And what is an acceptance without <s>pramāṇa</s>-support —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.34: The reason (<s>hetu</s>) is that which establishes what is to be proved through similarity with the example (<s>udāharaṇa</s>).

children.text:
avāntarasaṃgati pradarśayan pratijñāvacanasya sādhanāṅgatvamapi darśayati---hetoravasaraprāptasyeti /
pratijñānantaraṃ hetuvacanasyāvasaraḥ /
tathā hi parapratyāyanāya vacanam uccārayanti prekṣāvantaḥ /
tadeva ca pare bodhayitavyā yad bubhutsante /
tathā satyanenāpekṣitābhidhāyinā paro bodhito bhavati /
no khalvāmrān pṛṣṭaḥ kovidārānācakṣāṇaḥ praṣṭuravadheyavacano bhavati /
anavadheyavacanaśca kathaṃ pratipādako nāma? yathā ca māṭhara samidhamāhareti guruṇā preṣita eṣohamāharāmītyanuktvā tadarthaṃ tadaryaṃ yadāyaṃ dātrāya gṛhaṃ praviśati, tadāsmai kupyati guraḥ āḥ śiṣyāpasada chāndasavacara māṭhara māmavadhīrayasīti bruvāṇaḥ /
evamanityaṃ śabdaṃ bubhutsamānāyānityaḥ śabda ityanuktvā yadeva kiściducyate kṛtakatvāditi vā, yat kṛtakaṃ tadanityamiti vā, kṛtakaśca śabda iti vā tat sarvamasyānapekṣitam āpātato 'saṃbaddhābhidhānabuddhyā, tathā cānavahito na boddhumarhatīti /
yat kṛtakaṃ tat sarvamanityaṃ yathā ghaṭaḥ, kṛtakaśca śabdaḥ iti vacanamarthasāmarthyenaivāpekṣitaśabdānityatvaniścāyakamityavadhānamatreti cet---na, parasparāśrayatvaprasaṅgāt /
avadhāne hi sati ato 'rthe niścayaḥ /
tasmāccāvadhānamiti /
na ca pariṣatprativādinau pramāṇīkṛtavādinau yadetad vacanaṃ saṃbandhāya pratīkṣete, tathā ca sati na hetvādyapyapekṣetām, tadvacanādeva tadarthaniścayāt /
anityaḥ śabda iti tvapekṣita ukte kuta ityapekṣāyāṃ kṛtakatvāditi heturupa tiṣṭhate /
so 'yaṃ pañcāvayavaprayoge ca tallakṣaṇe ca pratijñānantarakāla evāvasaro hetoḥ /
tadevaṃ hetoravasaraprāptasya sāmānyalakṣaṇāpadeśadvāreṇa tadviśeṣalakṣaṇasūtram---
udā-tuḥ//34// śrutyarthābhyāmubhayalakṣaṇasūcanāt sūtrama /
atra heturiti lakṣyanirdeśaḥ /
sa ca vibhāgoddeśe vākyāvayava iti vacanarūpaḥ /
tasya sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ sādhyasādhanamiti sādhyate 'neneti vyutpattyā yadyapi pārārthyāpannaṃ kṛtakatvādikamartham āha, tathāpi tasya vacanātmakahetusāmānadhikaraṇyānupapatterviṣayi kṛtakatvādityādikaṃ vacanamupalakṣayati /
yadi ca vacanaṃ heturityucyeta tatsādhyena samabhivyāhṛtaṃ pratijñā syāt /
atha vacanamityetāvaducyeta, tadātivyāptiḥ syāt /
upacāre tu na kvacit prasaṅgaḥ /
upanayādapi sādhanaṃ na parāṅgatayā gamyate, kiṃ tu prātipadikārthapradhānatayā svaniṣṭhamiti na tatrāpi prasaṅgaḥ /
hetvābhāsāśca na sādhanamiti sādhanapadenaiva nirākṛtāḥ /
nyāyavākyāvayavatvādeva ca na śabde prasaṅgaḥ /
tadevaṃ samānāsamānajātīyavyavacchedakatvaṃ siddhaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇasya /
idaṃ cārtham /

children.translated_text: But the specific definition is what is directly stated in the <s>sūtra</s>.

children.text: heturiti yadyapi sāmānyapadam, tathāpi prakaraṇādanvayavyatirekihetuviśeṣaparaṃ draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: Although <s>hetu</s> (reason) is a general term, nevertheless, from the context, it should be understood as referring specifically to the reason characterized by positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvayavyatireki</s>).
Therefore, <s>hetu</s> is the mention of the definiendum.
And the remainder is the definition.

Showing the subsidiary connection, he also demonstrates that the proposition-statement is a component of the proof — "when the occasion for the reason has arrived" etc.
After the proposition, it is the occasion for the reason-statement.
For wise persons utter speech for the purpose of convincing others.
And the other person should be made to understand precisely what they desire to know.
This being so, the other person is informed by the one who states what is expected.
Indeed, one who is asked about mangoes but describes kovidāra trees is not heeded by the questioner.
And how can one whose words are not heeded be called an instructor? Just as when <s>Māṭhara</s> is sent by the teacher saying "bring firewood," if without saying "I will bring it," he enters the house of a wood-giver for that purpose, then the teacher becomes angry with him, saying "Ah, wretched student, follower of Vedic recitation, <s>Māṭhara</s>, you disrespect me!"
Similarly, when someone desires to know whether sound is non-eternal, if without saying "sound is non-eternal," whatever else is said — "because of being produced" or "whatever is produced is non-eternal" or "and sound is produced" — all of this, from the first impression, appears as an unconnected statement, and thus one who is not attentive is not able to understand.
If one argues: the statement "whatever is produced is non-eternal like a pot, and sound is produced" determines the non-eternality of sound, which is the expected conclusion, by the force of its meaning alone, and therefore attention is paid here — no, because there would be mutual dependence.
For attention is paid when there is certainty about this meaning,
and this certainty arises from that attention.
Moreover, the assembly and the opponent, who have accepted the speaker's authority, do not wait for this statement to establish a connection, and in that case they would not expect the reason etc. either, since certainty about the meaning would follow from that statement alone.
But when "sound is non-eternal" is stated as the expected proposition, and the expectation arises "why?", the reason presents itself — "because of being produced."
This is the occasion for the reason in the five-membered syllogism and in its definition, precisely at the time immediately after the proposition.
Thus, the <s>sūtra</s> for the specific definition of the reason, whose occasion has arrived, through the door of the general definition designation —
Example... reason //34// The <s>sūtra</s> indicates both definitions through the heard word and the meaning.
Here, "reason" (<s>hetu</s>) is the mention of the definiendum.
And in the classificatory enumeration, as a "sentence-member," it is in the form of a verbal statement.
Its general definition is <s>sādhyasādhana</s> (that which proves what is to be proved) — although by the derivation "that by which it is proved" it refers to the object to be proved such as "being produced," which serves the purpose of convincing others, nevertheless, since co-referentiality with the reason in the form of a verbal statement is untenable,

children.text:
tadetad bhāṣyakṛdṛ vyācaṣṭe---udāharaṇeneti /
sādharmyapadavyākhyānaṃ sāmānyāditi /
sādhyasādhanapadavyākhyānaṃ sādhyasya dharmasyeti /
sādhyasyeti dharmimātre buddhirmā bhūdityata uktaṃ dharmasyeti /

children.translated_text: The meaning is: of the property-bearer together with the property.
He makes this very point clearer — "connecting with what is to be proved" etc.

By "from the similarity of the example to what is to be proved," the properties of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>), thesis-membership, and both positive and negative concomitance thesis-membership have been shown.

And in <s>sādhyasādhana</s> (proving what is to be proved), by the word <s>sādhya</s> (to be proved), the qualities of having an uncontradicted domain and having no established counter-thesis are indicated, since what is contrary to these is unfit for proof.

The <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> explains this — "by the example" etc.
The explanation of the word <s>sādharmya</s> (similarity) is "from the common property" etc.
The explanation of the phrase <s>sādhyasādhana</s> is "of the property that is to be proved" etc.
"Of the to-be-proved" — lest the cognition be of the mere property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) alone, it is said "of the property" etc.

children.text: yo dharmo dhūmādi---sādhye bhavati sa tathābhūta evodāharaṇe 'pīti /
children.translated_text: The property such as smoke etc. that exists in what is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>) exists in precisely the same manner in the example as well.

children.text: udāhniyata ityudāharaṇaṃ dṛṣṭāntadharmī tasmin na punaḥ sa eva /
children.translated_text: That which is cited as an example (<s>udāharaṇa</s>) is the property-bearer of the illustration (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) — but the property in the example is not the very same individual property as in the thesis.
Why? "Because the property belongs to another" etc.

children.text: yadi tarhi nānyasya dharmo 'nyatra vartate, kathaṃ tarhi samānatā? sā hi tattvānyatvavirodhinītyata āha---kiṃ tu tattulyaḥ sa evetyucyate, yathā tāneva śalīn upayuṅkte tāneva tittirīnīti tadanena sāmānyād iti bhāṣyaṃ vyākhyātam //
children.translated_text: If a property of one thing does not exist in another, then how can there be similarity? For similarity is incompatible with both identity and difference — to this he says: "but one that is similar to that is called the same," just as one says "he eats the very same rice, hunts the very same partridges" — by this the <s>Bhāṣya</s> passage "from the common property" has been explained.
The <s>Vārttikakāra</s> explains this — "by the example" etc.

children.text:
udāharaṇagrahaṇaprayojanamāha---yadi punariti /
sādharmyamātratvaṃ hi viruddhe cāsādhāraṇe savyabhicāre cāstīti teṣāmapi vacanaṃ hetuḥ syāt /
teṣāmapi yathāsvaṃ sādhāraṇatvādityaniṣṭamityarthaḥ /
nanu tathāpi savyabhicāre 'pyudāraṇasādharmyamiti kathaṃ nivartyate ityata āha---udāharaṇeti /
viśiṣṭavidhānasya śeṣaniṣedho 'rthasiddha ityarthaḥ /
pakṣāntaramāha---avadhāraṇena veti /
sādharmyādityato viśeṣeṇa sarvasādharmyaprāptau udāharaṇasādharmyamapi prāptameveti vidhānānarthakyaṃ parisaṃkhyāyakaṃ sadavadhāraṇārthameva bhavati /
tadavadyotanāya ca evakāraḥ sādharmyameva ityatra sādhyapadaṃ yojanīyam /
tena sādhyaikadeśāsiddhimapākariṣyati /
pṛcchati---kasya punariti /
uttaram---kasyānyasyeti /
atraiva hetudvayayāha---prakṛtatvāt pratyāsatteśca /
sādhyaṃ khalvatra prakṛtaṃ pradhānam, taduddeśena avayavānāṃ pravṛtteḥ /
sādhyasādhanamiti ca padena sannidhāpitamiti tadeva dvitīyam avadhāraṇaṃ sphuṭīkaroti---atrāpi ceti /
sādhye pratisandhāya iti bhāṣyārthamāha---sādhyodāharaṇābhyāmiti /
dvāviti /
sapakṣavyāpakāvyāpakāvityarthaḥ /
anaikāntikasya ceti /

children.translated_text: The meaning is: of the common and the uncommon pseudo-reasons.
"Being contemplated in this manner" etc.
Being thoroughly reflected upon.
"Not over-extended" — the definition of pseudo-reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) is enumerative, not injunctive — this is the meaning.

He states the purpose of mentioning "example" — "but if" etc.
For mere similarity exists in the contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), the exclusive (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>), and the deviating (<s>savyabhicāra</s>) pseudo-reasons too, so the statement of those would also be a reason.
Since they too are common in their respective ways, this is undesirable — this is the meaning.
But even so, in the case of the deviating reason, there is similarity with the example — how is it excluded? — to this he says: "by the example" etc.
The meaning is: the injunction of the qualified example implicitly negates the remainder.
The thesis-

children.text:
etat kila hetulakṣaṇa bhadanto dūṣayāṃbabhūva sādhanaṃ yadi sārdhmyaṃ na vākyāṃśaḥ,
na hyarthaḥ pañcāvayavavākyasyāvayavaḥ /
yadi sādhanasādharmyayoratyantābhedo yadi vā sāmānyaviśeṣabhāvena kathañcid bhedaḥ ubhayathāpi na pañcamī, sādhanasāmānādhikaraṇyena prathamāprasaṅgāt /
atyantābhede caikatarapadāprayogāt /
vākyaṃ cet tataḥ pañcamyupapadyate /
sādhanaṃ hi vākyarūpu sādharmyādarthādutthitaṃ yataḥ /

children.translated_text: It would be the qualified of the sentence.

children.text: na hi vākyamevārthādutthitam, api tu vivakṣādyapīti /
children.translated_text: For a sentence does not arise merely from the meaning of things, but also from the desire to speak etc.
It is not the qualified. Why?
Because of being a proof, this is impossible.

The venerable <s>Dignāga</s> reportedly criticized this definition of reason: if the similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>) that is a real entity is itself called the proof, then it is not a sentence-member.
For a real entity is not a member of a five-membered sentence.
Whether there is absolute non-difference between the proof and the similarity, or whether there is some kind of difference in the relation of genus and species — in either case there is no fifth case ending (ablative), since there would be the unwanted consequence of the first case (nominative) through co-referentiality with "proof."
And in the case of absolute non-difference, one of the two words would be unused.
But if it is a sentence, then the fifth case ending is appropriate.

children.text:
arthasamutthānāmapi jñānavivakṣādīnāmaprasaṅgaḥ, asādhanatvāditi /
na tatrāpi dvidhā doṣāt sākṣād vā sādhanaṃ pāramparyeṇa vā? yadi pāramparyeṇa, vaktṛjñānaṃ tarhi sākṣāt sādharmyasamutthaṃ pāramparyeṇa ca śrotuḥ sādhyavijñānasādhanaṃ hetuḥ syāt /
atha sākṣāt sādhanam, tarhi śrotṛjñānaṃ pāramparyeṇa sādharmyasamutthaṃ sākṣāt sādhanaṃ hetuḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: Or if it is a direct proof, then the hearer's cognition, indirectly arising from the similarity and directly being the proof, would be the reason.
But in the present context, the alternative is impossible.

children.text: yadi tu pañcāvayavavākyasya prakṛtatvāt jñānādivyavacchedaḥ, tathāpyanyasaṃbhavaḥ, upanayasyāpi sādharmyasamutthātvāt /
children.translated_text: And even if cognition etc. are excluded because the five-membered sentence is the topic, still the alternative is impossible, since the application (<s>upanaya</s>) too arises from the similarity.
And if there is contradiction by the specific definition — that is not conclusive, because of the possibility of alternatives etc.

Even for cognition, desire to speak, and the rest, which arise from the meaning of things, there is no unwanted consequence of being a reason, because they are not proofs.
Is there not a fault in both ways — is it a proof directly or indirectly? If indirectly, then the speaker's cognition, directly arising from the similarity and indirectly being the means of proving the knowledge of what is to be proved to the hearer, would be the reason.
Therefore, even in that case, the qualifier with the genitive is purposeless.
One should simply say "the reason is of the similarity" — this much alone should be stated.
He presents this criticism of <s>Dignāga</s> — "from the similarity of the example" etc.
If the similarity, which is a real entity, is itself called the proof, then this criticism applies — this is the meaning.

children.text: yadi punararthātmakasya sādharmyasyārthātmakameva sādhanaṃ sāmānyamucyate, tatrāha---atha punariti /
children.translated_text: But if the common property of the similarity, which is a real entity, is itself called the proof as a real entity, then to this he says — "but then" etc.
This is what was said by the venerable <s>Dignāga</s> — "there is no fifth case ending."

children.text:
anye tvetadanyathā vyācakṣata ityāha---anye tviti /
viśeṣātiriktaṃ na sāmānyaṃ nāma kiñcidasti, tasya kalpanāmātratvād bhedasya ca vastvadhiṣṭhānatvādityabhiprāyaḥ /
doṣāntaramāha---sādhyasādhaneti /
yadā hi sādhyasādhanaṃ nāmodāharaṇasādharmyādatiriktaṃ nāsti kiṃ tu śabdamātramavaśiṣyate, tadodāharaṇasādharmyanenābhidheyatvena viśeṣaṇīyam /
tathā ca sādhyanirdeśaḥ pratijñā ityanena virodhaḥ /
anena hyavayavaḥ śabdātmakaḥ pratijñā lakṣyate /
hetvādisamudāyāpekṣayā cāvayavo bhavati /
na cābhidhānābhidheyātmakaḥ samudāyo dṛṣṭa iti /
tasmāt samudāyābhāvāt

children.translated_text: Neither of the two would be sentence-members.
This is what was stated — "not a sentence-member."

children.text: tadetallakṣaṇaṃ vyācakṣāṇairasmābhiḥ parihṛtamiti na parihārāntaraṃ prayojayatītyāha---tatra tviti /
children.translated_text: This has been resolved by us in explaining this definition — so no further resolution is needed — he says "but there" etc.

children.text: uktaṃ yathā hetupadasannidhau sādhanapadaṃ hetupade pravartate, na copanayaprasaṅgaḥ, tasya prātipadikārthamātrapradhānatvena hetubhāvāprakāśakatvāditi //
children.translated_text: It has been stated how, in the proximity of the word <s>hetu</s> (reason), the word <s>sādhana</s> (proof) applies to the word <s>hetu</s>, and there is no unwanted consequence of it applying to the application (<s>upanaya</s>), since the latter, having its primary meaning in the stem-meaning alone, does not reveal the status of being a reason.

But others explain this differently — he says "others, however" etc.
The intent is: there is no such thing as a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) apart from the particulars, since that universal is merely a conceptual construction, while difference has a real substrate.
He states another fault — <s>sādhyasādhana</s> etc.
For when the so-called <s>sādhyasādhana</s> (proving what is to be proved) is nothing over and above the similarity of the example, and only a mere word remains, then it should be qualified by the similarity of the example as its referent.
And likewise

children.text:
atra codayati---sādharmyasyeti /
sādharmyasya liṅsya kṛtakatvādihetupadavācyasya vyabhicāritvādiyogādudāharaṇaviśeṣaṇayogo na punaḥ sādhyasādhanapadavācyasya kṛtakatvādityāderhetuvacanasyetyarthaḥ /
taduktaṃ bhadantena---tatrāpi viśeṣaṇamanarthakaṃ vacane apītyarthaḥ /
tadetad dūṣayati---vacasa iti /
vacanamapi darśanabhedena ubhayathāpi bhavati, yathā mīmāṃsakānāṃ nityaṃ vacanam, vaiśaiṣikāṇāmanityamiti /
keṣāñcidamūrtaḥ śabdaḥ, keṣāñcit mūrta iti /
yathāhuḥ
vāyurāpadyate śabdatām
iti /
tathā prātisvikamapi bhedaṃ sarveṣāmeva śabdānāmitikaraṇo darśayatītyāha---dṛṣṭaśceti /
svacaritavirodhamāha---svayamiti /
anūbhyupagateti /

yadabhyupagataṃ bhadantena tasmāt ṣaṣṭyastviti tad dūṣayati---yadapīti /

children.translated_text: Because of the use of case-relational words arising from the desire to express.
The relation should be defined as being a case-factor (<s>kāraka</s>), since the relation has within it the relation of action and case-factor.

children.text: na tu ṣaṣṭhī vā hetupañcamī vā kārakavibhaktiriti /
children.translated_text: But neither the genitive nor the ablative of cause is a case-factor case-ending.

children.text: atra bhāṣyakāreṇa śuddhaṃ hetuvacanamudāhṛtam---utpattidharmakatvāditi tasya codāharaṇasādharmyasamutthatvajñāpanāyodāharaṇamapi darśitam utpattidharmakamanityaṃ dṛṣṭamiti //
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> has cited the pure statement of the reason — 'because of having the property of being produced' — and has also shown the illustration, to indicate that it arises from the similarity with the <s>sādhya</s> (thing to be proved): 'what has the property of being produced has been observed to be non-eternal.' //

Here he raises an objection — "of the similarity" etc.
Because the similarity — i.e., the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>), "being produced" etc. as denoted by the word <s>hetu</s> — has the connection of being deviating etc., it is qualified by the example; but what is denoted by the word <s>sādhyasādhana</s> — "being produced" etc. — is the reason-statement — this is the meaning.
This is what the venerable <s>Dignāga</s> stated — "the qualifier even in the reason-statement is purposeless" — this is the meaning.
He refutes this — "of the statement" etc.
The statement too, depending on the mode of viewing, is of both kinds,

children.text:
tatra bhāṣyakāreṇa śuddhaṃ hetuvacanamudāhṛtam /
tatpratijñāpadena pūrayitvā bārttikakṛd āha---udāharaṇamiti /
atra pṛcchati---kiṃ punariti /
sato vināśo vā anityatvam, tadyogo vā? taccebhayamayuktam, na hi sadasatoḥ kaścidasti saṃbandhaḥ, asamānakālatvāt /
tataścānityaḥ śabda iti samānādhikaraṇyaṃ na syāt /
api ca śabdasya bhūtvā yadabhavanam, na tadeva piṭharasya /
na hyabhavanatvaṃ nāmāsti sāmānyam, yena dṛṣṭānto na sādhyavikalaḥ syāt /
na ca sāmānyātiriktaṃ sādṛśyaṃ vastvantaraṃ dṛṣṭamiṣṭaṃ vā /
tasmāt mṛṣṭāśeyamanityatvaṃ sādhyamiti bhāvaḥ /
gūḍhadhiya uttaram---yasyānityatvamasti tadanityam /
svābhiprāyeṇa pṛcchati---atheti /
uttaravādyabhiprāyamudghāṭayati---ubhayānteti /
aparānteti vaktavye ubhayāntagrahaṇena pūrvāntaniveśanaṃ hetorutpattimattvasyātyantiṅkīṃ pratyāsattimavinābhāvopayoginīṃ darśayitumiti /
avacchedakatvaṃ copalakṣaṇatvam, na tu viśeṣaṇatvam /
taccāparāntasya bhinnakālasya saṃbaddhasyāpi virodhitayā buddhisthasya saṃbhavati /
tathā ca yaivāparāntāvacchinnasya sattā piṭharasya saivāparāntāvacchinnasya śabdasyāpi /
evaṃ sattāsamavāyo 'pi tadvidhayoḥ piṭharaśabdayoḥ samānaḥ /
viroghibhāvaḥ paścādbhāvaścābhāvamātrāt pradhvaṃsasya viśeṣaḥ /
pṛcchati---athotpattīti /
na tāvadutpannasyotpattirdhamaḥ, tadāpyutpadyata iti pratpayaprasaṅgāt /
nāpyanutpannasya asato dharmitvāyogāditi bhāvaḥ /
gūḍhadhiya uttarama---utpattiriti /
uktābhiprāyavān punaḥ pṛcchati---kā punariyamiti /
uttaram---asadviśeṣaṇasya sato 'tyantamabhāvabhāvapratiṣedhaḥ asaditi prāgabhāvamāha, viśeṣaṇatvaṃ ca prāgabhāvasya upalakṣaṇatvam /
tacca bhinnakālasyāpi buddhisathatāmātreṇoktam /
tenāsadviśeṣaṇasya sata ityetāvataiva pūrvāntaparicchinnasya sattāsaṃbandhaḥ sattā vā tadviśeṣaṇotpattirdarśitā /
paścedṛśastasya gaganavat nātyantaṃ saṃbhavaḥ, nāpi gaganakusumavadatyantābhāva iti svarūpamuktamutpattimuparlakṣayitum /

children.translated_text: And the co-reference between the suggestive term and what it suggests is through the intention of non-difference.

children.text: na caivaṃ labdhotpattini vastuni utpadyata iti pratyayaprasaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus, there is no unwanted consequence of the cognition 'it is [still] originating' with respect to a thing that has already obtained origination.

Because in common usage, the expression 'being originated' is seen applied to [a thing's] parts, which have obtained the prior-and-posterior sequence through the entry of an operation conducive to its production.

children.text: tasmāt pūrvāntāvacchinnavastusattayā tatsaṃbandhena vā tasyaiva vastuno 'parāntāvacchinnā sattā vā tatsaṃbandho vā jñāpyate iti sarvaṃ ramaṇīyam //
children.translated_text: Therefore, by the existence of the thing delimited by the prior end, or by its connection, the existence of that very thing delimited by the later end, or its connection, is indicated — thus everything is satisfactory. //

There, the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> has cited the pure statement of the reason. Having completed it with the proposition-term, the <s>vārttikakāra</s> says — 'illustration.' Here he asks — 'what then?' Is non-eternality the destruction of what exists, or connection with that [destruction]? Both are untenable, for there is no connection between the existent and the non-existent, since they are not co-temporal. And thus the co-reference 'sound is non-eternal' would not hold. Moreover, the ceasing-to-be of sound after having come to be is not the same as that of a pot. For there is no universal called 'ceasing-to-be-ness' by which the example would not lack the <s>sādhya</s>. Nor is similarity, as something distinct from a universal, seen or accepted as a separate entity. Therefore, non-eternality as what is to be proved is unclear — this is the import. The one with a hidden intention answers — 'that which has non-eternality is non-eternal.' Asking according to his own intention — 'now then.' He reveals the respondent's intention — 'bounded at both ends.' When 'bounded at the later end' should have been said, by saying 'bounded at both ends,' the inclusion of the prior end is for the purpose of showing that the reason — the property of being produced — has the closest proximity, useful for invariable concomitance. And the delimiting [function] is suggestive, not qualifying. And that is possible for the later end, which is of a different time but is present in the intellect as contradictory even though connected. And thus, the existence of a pot delimited by the later end is the same as the existence of sound delimited by the later end. Similarly, the inherence of existence too is the same for pot and sound of that kind. The hostile nature and the posteriority distinguish <s>pradhvaṃsa</s> (posterior absence) from mere absence. He asks — 'but then, origination?' — Origination is not a property of what has already originated, because of the unwanted consequence of the cognition 'it is still originating'; nor is it [a property] of what has not originated, because of the impossibility of property-bearer status for a non-entity — this is the import. The one with hidden intention answers — 'origination.' The one with the stated intention asks again — 'but what then is this [origination]?' The answer — 'the negation of the absolute absence-and-existence of an existent qualified by non-existence': by 'non-existent' he refers to prior absence (<s>prāgabhāva</s>), and the qualifying nature of prior absence is suggestive. And that is stated merely on the basis of its mental presence even though it is of a different time. Therefore, by just this much — 'of an existent qualified by non-existence' — the connection with existence, or the existence itself, of something delimited by the prior end has been shown as origination. Such a thing is not absolutely possible like space, nor absolutely non-existent like a sky-flower — thus its essential nature has been stated to suggest origination.

children.text:
nanu bhāṣyakṛd abhūtvā bhavatītyasya vākyāsyārthamutpattiṃ vakṣyati, tvaṃ punarasadviśeṣaṇasya sato 'tyantamabhāvabhāvapratiṣedha ityasya vākyasyārthamutpattim /
ataḥ kuto na virodha ityata āha---vākyārtheti /
ya
evārtho bhāṣyakāreṇa utpattiśabdārthatayābhyanujñāto 'ṅgīkṛtaḥ, sa evāsmābhirapi /
nātyantamabhāvabhāvapratiṣedha utpattiḥ, api svasadviśeṣaṇasya sataḥ sattā vā tatsaṃbandho vetyuktamityarthaḥ//34 //
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> will state origination as the meaning of the sentence 'coming to be after not having been,' while you [state] origination as the meaning of the sentence 'the negation of the absolute absence-and-existence of an existent qualified by non-existence' — how is there no contradiction? — therefore he says — 'the meaning of the sentence.' The very meaning that was accepted by the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> as the meaning of the word 'origination' is [accepted] by us too. The negation of absolute absence-and-existence is not origination; rather, the existence or connection with existence of an existent qualified by non-existence — this is what has been stated — this is the meaning. //34//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.35: Similarly, [an illustration can be given] through dissimilarity.

children.text:
sūtrāntaramavatārayati---kimetāvaditi /
tathā---t //35// atra yadi vedharmyādityucyate tataḥ sakalakesarādimatpadārthapakṣīkaraṇenāśvatvaṃ yadā viṣāṇitvena sādhyate tasyāsti pakṣavaidharmyamiti hetuḥ syādityata āha---udāharaṇena vaidharmyamiti /
vipakṣeṇetyarthaḥ /
tathāpi yadā śarīramātraṃ pakṣīkṛtya sātmakatvaṃ sādhyate prāmādimattvena, tadāsti tasyodāharaṇena vaidharmyamiti so 'pi hetuḥ syādityata āha---eveti /
na caitāvatā sapakṣe sattvaprasaṅgaḥ, sapakṣasyābhāvāt /
avadhāraṇasya ca vyāptyā pakṣasattvenopapatteriti /
tathāpi anvayavyatirekiṇo hetāranaikāntikasya vipekṣaikadeśavyāpinaḥ saṃgrahaḥ syāt /
yathā anityaḥ śabdaḥ, utpattidharmakatvād anityo mūrtatvādityata āha---vaidharmyameva codāharaṇeneti vipakṣodāharaṇenetyarthaḥ /
bhāṣyakārīyamudāharaṇaṃ nigadenopanyasyati---anityaḥ śabdaḥ /

children.translated_text: [Thus.]
What is eternal has been observed to have the property of not being produced — this is the construction.
He refutes that — 'this.'

children.text: mā bhūt prayogamātrabhedād bhedaḥ, udāharaṇabhedād bhedo bhaviṣyatītyata āha---udāharaṇamātrabhedācceti //
children.translated_text: Lest there be difference merely from the difference in formulation, [he says] there will be difference from the difference in illustration — therefore he says — 'merely from the difference in illustration.' //

He introduces another <s>sūtra</s> — 'is that all?' Similarly... //35// Here, if it is said 'through dissimilarity,' then by making all things possessing mane and the like the subject (<s>pakṣa</s>), when horse-ness is to be proved through having horns, there would be dissimilarity of the thesis from the example — so that too would be a reason — therefore he says — 'dissimilarity through the example.' The meaning is: through the dissimilar instance (<s>vipakṣa</s>). Even so, when the body alone is made the subject and the property of having a self is to be proved through having vital breath and the like, there is dissimilarity of the thesis from the example — so that too would be a reason — therefore he says — 'thus.' And even so, there is no unwanted consequence of [the reason's] presence in the similar instance, because of the absence of a similar instance. And because the determination can be supported by the presence of the thesis [itself]. Even so, there would be the inclusion of an inconclusive reason — one that pervades only a part of the dissimilar instance — that operates through both positive and negative concomitance. For example: 'sound is non-eternal, because of having the property of being produced; non-eternal because of being corporeal' — therefore he says — 'dissimilarity alone, through the example' — meaning through the dissimilar-instance illustration. He presents the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s>'s illustration by recitation — 'sound is non-eternal.'

children.text:
tadetad bhāṣyakārīyamudāharaṇaṃ dūṣayitvā svakīyamudāharaṇamāha---udāharaṇaṃ tviti /
prāṇādinā ca svakāraṇaṃ prayatnecchādyupalakṣayati---yadubhayapakṣasaṃpratipannaṃ nirātmakaṃ ghaṭādi tatsarvamaprāṇādimad dṛṣṭam iti vyatyāsena yojanā /
prāṇādikāraṇecchādikāraṇarahitaṃ yadityarthaḥ /
tatmāt nedamiti /

children.translated_text: Not devoid of desire and the like as its inherent cause.

children.text: yaścāsau icchādisamavāyikāraṇaṃ pṛthivyādivilakṣaṇo dravyāṇāṃ navamaḥ, sa ātmetyucyate ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And that which is the inherent cause in the form of desire and the like — a ninth substance distinct from earth and the like — that is called the self (<s>ātman</s>) — this is the meaning.

children.text: anvayivyatirekiṇastadvivekasya ca tantrāntaraprasiddhena nāmnā tantrāntaraprasiddhatāṃ darśayati---so 'yamavīta iti /
children.translated_text: He shows the well-knownness in other systems of the distinction between the positive-negative [reason] (<s>anvayivyatirekin</s>) and its differentiation, using a name well-known in other systems — 'this is the <s>avīta</s>.'

children.text: vividhena prakāreṇa itaḥ prāpto vītaḥ, pakṣavyāpakatve sati sapakṣavyāptyā avyāptyā ca, tasmādanyo 'vīta iti //
children.translated_text: '<s>Vīta</s>' (separated) means arrived here in various ways — i.e., pervading the thesis while being both pervading and non-pervading of the similar instance — and what is different from that is '<s>avīta</s>' (not separated). //

Having thus refuted the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s>'s illustration, he states his own illustration — 'but the illustration.' And by 'vital breath and the like' (<s>prāṇādi</s>), he suggests his own causes such as effort, desire, and the like: 'whatever is accepted by both parties as being without a self — such as pot and the like — all of that has been observed to be without vital breath and the like' — this is the construction by inversion, since the negation of the <s>sādhya</s> is what is pervaded. And by 'without vital breath and the like,' the meaning is: without a cause in the form of desire and the like. 'Therefore, this is not so.'

children.text:
gūḍhābhisandhiḥ pṛcchati---kathaṃ punariti /
gūḍhābhisandheruttaram---atha yo 'bhyanujñāta iti /
yathā vītasyārthaparicchedakatvaṃ tathaivāvītasyetyarthaḥ /
praṣṭā svābhiprāyam udghāṭayati---anvayāditi /
gṛhītāvinābhāvo hi hetuḥ sādhyena tasya paricchedakaḥ, sa ca dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇi hetusādhyadharmayordarśane satyavinābhāvo dṛṣṭo bhavati /
na ca sātmakatvaṃ kvacid dṛṣṭam, tat kathaṃ tenāvinābhāvadarśanaṃ prāṇādimattvasya, darśane vā nāvītaḥ kiṃ tu vīta evetyarthaḥ /
uttaravādī praṣṭāraṃ pṛcchati---atha prameyatvamiti /
praṣṭā āha---vyabhicārāditi /
uttaravādyāha---na tarhyanvaya iti /
sa evaikagranthenāha---yadi ceti /
tadevamuttaravādinā svābhiprāya udghāṭitaḥ /
pṛcchati---katham /
avyabhicāritvaṃ vyatirekiṇa iti /
avyabhicāramāha---yāvaditi /
atrāpi yāvannirātmakaṃ tat sarvam aprāṇādimad dṛṣṭamiti vyatyāsena yojanā, sādhyaviparyayasya vyāptatvāt /
vyāpakanivṛttau ca vyāpyaṃ nivartate, yathā vṛkṣatvanivṛttau śiṃśapātvam ārādupalabhyamānādekaśilāmayādacalapradeśādityarthaḥ /
yadi punarevamucyate nivartatāmaprāmāṇādimattvaṃ jīvaccharīrāt prāṇādimattvasya pramāṇata upalabdhermā nivartiṣṭa nairātmyam, tasmād

children.translated_text: 'Because of deviation, [the reason] is not a [valid] reason' — he raises a doubt — 'but then.'
He refutes — 'it is not proper to say thus.'

children.text: kiṃ jīvaccharīre sādhye nairātmyaniścayād vyabhicāra uta tatsandehāt? yadi niścayāt, kṛta vyabhicāreṇa, bādhitaviṣayatvenaiva hetorapākaraṇāt /
children.translated_text: Is there deviation because of the certainty of non-selfhood in the living body, or because of doubt about it? If because of certainty, then the charge of deviation is superfluous, since the reason is [already] set aside by having a sublated subject.

children.text: atha sandehāt, tathā satyanvayino 'pyahetutve sarvānumānocchedaprasaṅga ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: If because of doubt, then in that case, even for a positive-concomitant [reason], there would be non-reason-hood, resulting in the destruction of all inference — this is the meaning. //

The one with a hidden intention asks — 'but how then?' The answer to the one with hidden intention — 'now, what is accepted.' The meaning is: just as the <s>vīta</s> [reason] has the capacity to determine the object, so too does the <s>avīta</s>. The questioner reveals his own intention — 'from positive concomitance.' For a reason whose invariable concomitance has been grasped determines [the <s>sādhya</s>], and that invariable concomitance is observed when the properties of reason and <s>sādhya</s> are seen in the example-subject. But the property of having a self has not been seen anywhere; so how can the invariable concomitance of having vital breath and the like with that be observed? And if it is observed, then it is not <s>avīta</s> but rather <s>vīta</s> alone — this is the meaning. The respondent asks the questioner — 'but then, <s>prameya</s>-hood?' The questioner says — 'because of deviation.' The respondent says — 'then there is no positive concomitance.' He says in a single passage — 'and if.' Thus the respondent has revealed his own intention. He asks — 'how?' 'The non-deviation of the negative [reason].' He states the non-deviation — 'as long as.' Here too the construction is by inversion: 'as long as [something] is without a self, all of that has been observed to be without vital breath and the like' — since the negation of the <s>sādhya</s> is what is pervaded. And when the pervader is absent, the pervaded is absent — just as when tree-ness is absent, <s>śiṃśapā</s>-ness [is absent] — from a rock-platform perceptible from a distance, made of a single stone — this is the meaning. But if it is said thus: let the absence of vital breath and the like be absent from the living body because of the <s>pramāṇa</s>-based apprehension of the presence of vital breath and the like — let the non-selfhood not be absent — therefore,
He analyzes the objection-sentence — 'if.'

children.text: na tāvadayumātmā nāma pramāṇena kvacidupalabdhaḥ, yasya pratiṣedho nairātmyamavagamyeta, tadupalambhe vā kṛtamanayā kusṛṣṭyā /
children.translated_text: Now, no such [thing called] 'self' has been apprehended anywhere through <s>pramāṇa</s>, the negation of which could be understood as 'non-selfhood'; or if it were apprehended, this cunning reasoning would be unnecessary.

children.text: tasmāt kalpayitvātmānamaprāmāṇikaṃ tatpratiṣedhasya ghaṭādāvaprāṇādimattvena vyāptiṃ gṛhītvā jīvaccharīre vyāpakasyāprāṇādimattvasya nivṛttyā nairātmyasya vyāpyasya nivṛtterātmā avagantavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, having posited a self that is not based on <s>pramāṇa</s>, having grasped its negation's pervasion with the absence of vital breath and the like in pots and the like, [and then arguing that] from the absence of the pervader — the absence of vital breath and the like — in the living body, there is absence of the pervaded — non-selfhood — the self is to be understood.

children.text: evaṃ ca sati kalpanākoṣasyāparimeyatvāt yad yadeva kalpyate tattadabhāvasyadhaṭādau sulabhatvād aprāṇādimattvena vyāpterjīccharīre 'prāṇādimuttvasya vyāpakasya nivṛtterātmasadbhāvavat sakalakālpanikaḍitthādimattvaprasaṅga ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And this being so, since the scope of postulation is immeasurable, whatever is postulated — the absence of that is easily obtainable in pots and the like, and through the pervasion with the absence of vital breath and the like, from the absence of the pervader in the living body — there would be the unwanted consequence of everything [being established], such as the possession of every postulated <s>Ḍittha</s> and the like, just like the existence of a self — this is the meaning. //
He raises a doubt — 'if there is the unwanted consequence of everything having a self?' He refutes — 'no, because of the impossibility of the alternative.'

children.text:
nirākaraṇavākyaṃ vibhajate---tacca naivam /
kasmātṛ---vikalpānupapatteḥ /
vikalpayati---kimiti /
ayamarthaḥ /
prāṇādayo hicchādyanvayavyatirekānuvidhāyibhāvābhāvatayā icchādikāryāḥ, akṣaṇikatve ca vyavasthite kāryaṃ samavāyikāraṇāpekṣamitīcchādīnāṃ samavāyikāraṇena bhavitavyam, kāryatvād ghaṭādivat, śarīrendriyādīnāṃ ca samavāyikāraṇatvaniṣedhe sati yad icchādīnāṃ samavāyikāraṇaṃ pariśiṣyate, tad dravyamātmeti ca kṣetrajña iti ca jīva iti cākhyāyate /
tadasya viśeṣato 'navagatasyāpīcchādisamavāyikāraṇatayā sāmānyarūpeṇāvadhāritasya śakyaḥ prāṇādirahiteṣu ghaṭādiṣvabhāvaḥ pratipattum /
nirātmakaśabdenāpi cāyamevārtha ucyate /
anena prāṇādilakṣaṇakāryābhāvena ghaṭādau nairātmyalakṣaṇakāraṇābhāvasya vyāptiravadhāritā /
so 'yaṃ jīvaccharīre kāryasyābhāvo vyāpako nivartamānaḥ svavyāpyaṃ tatkāraṇābhāvamādāya nivartate iti siddhaṃ jīvaccharīre prāṇakāraṇam, sa cātmeti /
yadi ca ḍitthādayo 'pi tādṛśāḥ, tadā ātmano nāmāntarāṇi nārthāntarāṇi /
nāmāni ca lokatantrāṇi, na tvicchātantrāṇīti /
avadhāritaṃ kāryaṃ prāṇādyupalakṣitamicchādi yasya so 'vadhāritakāryaḥ, sa eva svabhāvo yasya sa tathoktaḥ /
etaduktaṃ bhavati /
sāmānyatastāvadicchādīnā kāryatvenānvayavyatirekiṇā hetunā samavāyikāraṇavattvamunamitam /
ubhayasiddhaśca ghaṭādāvicchādikāraṇābhāvaḥ /
ye 'pi hi nairātmyavādino buddhiṃ vā bhūtapatiṇāmabhedaṃ vā icchādikāraṇamācakṣate, te 'pi ghaṭādau na tadātiṣṭhante /
tasmādubhayasiddhanairātmyā ghaṭādayaḥ /
teṣu cecchādikāryābhāvena nairātmyaṃ vyāptam /
so 'yaṃ jīvaccharīre kāryābhāvo vyāvartamānaḥ kāraṇābhāvaṃ vyāvartayati /
na ca kāryeṇaiva kāraṇamanumīyatāṃ jīvaccharīre, kiṃ vyatirekiṇā,
ṛjumārgeṇa sidhyantaṃ ko nu vakreṇa sādhayet
children.translated_text: Who would accomplish by a crooked path what is accomplished by a straight one?
This should not be said, because only the bare cause is established by that [direct inference]— as has been stated /

children.text: pariśeṣād viśeṣasiddhiriti cet? sa eva vyatirekītyuktam //
children.translated_text: If [one says] the specific [cause] is established by the method of elimination (<s>pariśeṣa</s>)— that itself is the negative concomitance method— as has been stated //

He analyzes the refutation statement— 'and that is not so' /
Why?— 'because of the impossibility of alternatives' /
He presents the alternatives— 'what?' /
The meaning is as follows: /
<s>Prāṇa</s> (vital breath) and the like, being present and absent in conformity with the presence and absence of desire and the like, are effects of desire and the like; and when non-momentariness has been established, an effect requires an inherent cause— therefore desire and the like must have an inherent cause, because of being effects, like a pot and the like; and when the body, sense organs, and the like have been negated as the inherent cause, what remains as the inherent cause of desire and the like— that substance is called <s>ātman</s> (self), and <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field), and <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) /
Though the specific nature of this [self] has not been ascertained, its absence can be understood in pots and the like, which lack vital breath and the like, since it has been determined in its general form as the inherent cause of desire and the like /
And by the word 'selfless' (<s>nirātmaka</s>) too, this very meaning is expressed /
By this, the concomitance (<s>vyāpti</s>) between the absence of effects characterized by vital breath and the like in pots etc. and the absence of the cause characterized by selflessness has been established /
This absence of the effect, being the pervader, when it ceases [to apply] in a living body, ceases together with what it pervades, namely the absence of that cause— thus it is established that the cause of vital breath exists in a living body, and that is the self /
And if <s>Ḍittha</s> and the like are also of such nature, then they are merely other names of the self, not other entities /
And names are determined by worldly convention, not by choice /
That whose ascertained effect, indicated by vital breath and the like, is desire and the like— that is called 'one whose effect has been ascertained'; and that which has that very nature is called thus /
This is what has been stated: /
First, in general, the possession of an inherent cause by desire and the like has been inferred through the reason of being an effect, which follows positive and negative concomitance /
And the absence of the cause of desire and the like in pots etc. is accepted by both parties /
For even those who advocate selflessness (<s>nairātmyavāda</s>), who declare intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) or the transformation of the elements without distinction as the cause of desire and the like, do not maintain that in pots and the like /
Therefore, pots and the like are selfless as accepted by both parties /
And in them, selflessness is pervaded by the absence of the effects such as desire /
This absence of effects, when it ceases [to apply] in a living body, removes the absence of the cause /
And let the cause alone be inferred in the living body through the effect— why through negative concomitance?

children.text:
yadi hi pṛthivyādisamavāyikāraṇā icchādayo bhaveyuḥ, ghaṭādiṣvapi prasajyeran /
tasmād ghaṭādiṣvicchādikāryanivṛttyā dravyāṣṭakātiriktakāraṇanivṛttirvyāptā dṛṣṭetīcchādayaḥ śarīre dṛśyamānā vyāpikāṃ svanivṛttiṃ nivartayanto vyāpyadravyāṣṭakātiriktakāraṇābhāvanivṛttimukhena navamaṃ dravyaṃ sādhayanti /
na caiṣāṃ buddhireva samavāyikāraṇam, dravyasyaiva samavāyikāraṇatvaniyamād buddheścādravyatvāt /
yathā ca bhūtānāṃ pariṇatibhedo na kāraṇaṃ tathā hi tṛtīye upapādayiṣyate /
vyatirekamukhenāpi prāmādeḥ sātmakatvenānvayasiddhau na kevalavyatirekīti cet? na svābhāvavikaṃ sādhyena pratibandhamanvayavyatirekiṇi vyāsedhāmaḥ, kiṃ tu sapakṣābhāvena vidhimukhenāsya pratibandhaṃ nirākurmaḥ /

children.translated_text: And by this much alone it differs from a positive concomitant [reason] /

children.text: na ca pakṣa eva sapakṣaḥ, jijñāsitaviśeṣasya jñātaviśeṣādanyatvāt /
children.translated_text: And the subject (<s>pakṣa</s>) itself is not the similar instance (<s>sapakṣa</s>), because what is being investigated as to its specific nature is different from what is known as to its specific nature /

children.text: śarīrādiṣu ca satsu nairātmyaniṣedha evātmasadbhāvaḥ, asanniṣedhasya sadbhāvalakṣaṇatvāt /
children.translated_text: And when body and the like exist, the very negation of selflessness is the existence of the self, because the negation of non-existence has the definition of existence /

children.text: sapakṣābhāvastu nairātmyenāpyavyapadeśya iti kathaṃ nairātmyaniṣedhena vyapadiśyatām? asato 'dhikaraṇatvāyogādityuktam //
children.translated_text: But as for the absence of a similar instance— since it cannot be designated even by selflessness, how can it be designated by the negation of selflessness? Because what is non-existent cannot be a locus— as has been stated //

For if desire and the like had earth and the like as their inherent cause, they would also arise in pots and the like /
Therefore, since in pots and the like the cessation of the effects such as desire is observed to be pervaded by the cessation of a cause beyond the eight substances— desire and the like, being observed in a body, by removing their own cessation which pervades [the absence of the ninth substance], establish the ninth substance through the removal of the absence of a cause beyond the eight substances /
And intellect alone is not their inherent cause, because of the rule that only substance is an inherent cause, and because intellect is not a substance /
And how the transformation of the elements is not the cause— that will be established in the third [book] /
If [one objects] that when the positive concomitance of vital breath etc. with having a self is established, it is not a merely negative concomitance— no, we do not deny the connection of the intrinsic nature with what is to be proved in the positive-and-negative concomitant [reason]; rather, we deny its connection through the positive method by the absence of the similar instance /
By this, what has been said by the opponents:
If [the reason has] no positive concomitance with the similar instance, then it would be a positive concomitant [reason] from [its relation to] the reason /
If it is not a positive-and-negative concomitant, then [there is] neither selflessness nor having a self //
This has been refuted by the above /
And this has been clarified by us through the justification of the positive concomitant reason /
Therefore everything is well-established //

children.text:
vipakṣavyatirekamātreṇa vyatirekiṇo gamakatvaṃ matvā codayati---yadi tarhīti /
pariharati---na, hetvarthāparijñānāditi /
na vaidharmyamātreṇa gamakatvam, api tvavyabhicāriṇā /
sa cātrāvyabhicāro nāstītyarthaḥ /
nanu mā bhūd gandhavattvaṃ heturvyatireka vyabhicārād anityādivannityādapyasya vyatirekāt, tasya tu pakṣa eva kevalaṃ na tu sapakṣavipakṣau, na tasaya vyatirekavyabhicāro 'stīti sa kasmāt na heturiti codayati---yaḥ punariti /
pariharati---satyamiti/vyatirekadharmo 'vyabhicāro nāsati vyatireke saṃbhavati, asato 'dhikaraṇatvāyogādityuktatvāditi /
pratyudāharaṇāntaraṃ darśayati---eteneti /
etena vipakṣābhāvāt tato vyāvṛttyabhāvenetyarthaḥ /
codayati---yaḥ pakṣaikadeśa iti /
yadi hi pakṣaikadeśavṛttirapi vipakṣābhāvāt na vyatirekī hetuḥ, tarhi tasya pakṣaikadeśavṛtterapi sato vipakṣanivṛttirasti sa hetuḥ prasajyeta /
asti khalvasyodāharaṇavaidharmyameveti vyatirekihetulakṣaṇamityabhiprāyaḥ /
pariharati---ayamapi na hetuḥ, kasmāt? sūtrārthenāpoditatvāt /
taṃ sūtrapāṭhapūrvakaṃ darśayati---sūtrārtha iti /
atra ca yena pakṣaikadeśavṛttervyatirekyābhāsasya nirākaraṇaṃ tadavadhāraṇaṃ prathamaṃ darśitam /
children.translated_text: And here, the refutation of the pseudo-negative-concomitant that exists in only part of the subject— that determination was shown first /
Dissimilarity is [established] by the example alone, not by the counter-example, nor even by the subject /

children.text: asya tu pakṣeṇāpīti vyatirekyapi na hetuḥ, na punarvaidharmyameveti sūtrārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: But for this [pseudo-reason], even by the subject [one sees dissimilarity]— so it is not a reason even as a negative concomitant, not merely because dissimilarity [is required only from the example]— this is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> /

children.text: tathā sati savyabhicāramātrasya nivṛttiḥ syāt, na tu pakṣaikadeśavṛtterityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: If that were the case, only what is merely deviant would be excluded, not what exists in part of the subject— this is the meaning //

Thinking that the merely negative concomitant [reason] has probative force merely through its differentiation from the dissimilar instance, he objects— 'if then' /
He resolves— 'no, because of incomplete understanding of the meaning of the reason' /
Probative force does not arise from mere dissimilarity, but from non-deviation /
And that non-deviation is absent here— this is the meaning /
Now, let the property of having smell not be the reason because of deviation in the negative concomitance— just as non-eternality and the like [deviate], since it also shows negative concomitance with what is eternal— but that [property] exists only in the subject, and not in the similar or dissimilar instances, so there is no deviation in its negative concomitance— why then is it not a reason?— he objects— 'but that which' /
He resolves— 'true' /
The non-deviation that is the property of negative concomitance is not possible in the absence of negative concomitance, because what is non-existent cannot be a locus— as has been stated /
He shows another counter-example— 'by this' /
'By this' means: because of the absence of the dissimilar instance, there is no differentiation from it— this is the meaning /
He objects— 'that which exists in only part of the subject' /
For if even what exists in only part of the subject is not a negative concomitant reason because of the absence of the dissimilar instance, then since this [property] existing in part of the subject also has cessation in the dissimilar instance, it should be a reason /
Indeed, it has dissimilarity with the example— so it has the defining characteristic of a negative concomitant reason— this is the purport /
He resolves— 'this too is not a reason'— why? 'Because it has been refuted by the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>' /
That <s>sūtra</s>-passage he shows preceded by the <s>sūtra</s> reading— 'the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>' /

children.text:
saṃprati vāsubandhavaṃ hetulakṣaṇaṃ dūṣayitumupanyasyati---heturvipakṣādviśeṣa ityanye /
etad vyācaṣṭe---anye tviti /
sādharmyamātranirākaraṇa iti /
yasya kasyacit sādharmyasya nirākaraṇe /
vipakṣasādharmyanirākaraṇe tāvadiṣṭasya saṃgrahaḥ /
yadā tu sapakṣādisādharmyanirākaraṇam, tadā aniṣṭasya viruddhādeḥ saṃgrahaḥ /
upalakṣaṇaṃ caitat /
iṣṭāniṣṭasaṃgraha iti, iṣṭaparityāga ityapi draṣṭavyam /
sa cānekabheda iti /
sapakṣādapi viśeṣe sati vipakṣād viśeṣaḥ, pakṣādapi viśeṣe sati vipakṣād viśeṣaḥ, vipakṣamātrād vā viśeṣaḥ iti prakārāḥ /
tatra pūrvayoḥ prakārayoryathākramamasādhāraṇasya cāsiddhasya ca hetutvaprasaṅga iti /
tannivṛttyartha vipakṣādeva ityavadhāryate /
dvitīyamavadhāraṇamavatārayitumāha---avadhāraṇe ceti /

children.translated_text: By the determination 'from the dissimilar instance alone,' it is differentiation that has been determined, not the dissimilar instance /

children.text: sa cāyaṃ viśeṣe cāviśeṣe ca prasṛta iti vipakṣekadeśavṛtterapi pakṣasapakṣasādhāraṇasya hetutvaprasaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: And this [differentiation] extends to both what is specific and what is non-specific— so there would be the unwanted consequence that what exists in part of the dissimilar instance but is common to the subject and similar instance would also be a reason /
To avoid that, the second determination is: 'differentiation alone' [i.e., only what is exclusively differentiated] /
He concludes— 'thus indeed' //

Now he introduces the definition of reason given by <s>Vasubandhu</s> in order to refute it— 'a reason is differentiation from the dissimilar instance, say others' /
He explains this— 'but others' /
'The refutation of mere similarity' /
When any similarity whatsoever is refuted: /
In the refutation of similarity with the dissimilar instance, what is desired is included /
But when similarity with the similar instance etc. is refuted, what is undesired— the contradictory and the like— is included /
And this is illustrative: /
The meaning of 'inclusion of the desired and undesired' should be seen as also including 'exclusion of the desired' /
'And that has many varieties' /
When there is differentiation from the similar instance as well, there is differentiation from the dissimilar instance; when there is differentiation from the subject as well, there is differentiation from the dissimilar instance; or differentiation from the dissimilar instance alone— these are the varieties /
Of those, in the first two varieties respectively, the uncommon [reason] and the unestablished [reason] would absurdly be reasons /
To avoid that, it is determined that [differentiation] is from the dissimilar instance alone /
To introduce the second determination, he says— 'and in the determination' /

children.text:
tadevadavyāpakatvena dūṣayati---satyameka iti /
atra codayati---vipakṣaikadeśavṛttipratiṣedhāditi /
viśeṣa evetyavadhāraṇena vipakṣaikadeśavṛttiḥ gaurayaṃ viṣāṇitvāditi hetutvena pratiṣiddhaḥ /
tasmādetasminnavadhāraṇe satyeva vipakṣādevetyavadhāraṇīyam /
tathā ca vipakṣādeva yo viśeṣa eva sa hetuḥ /
sapakṣāttu yo viśeṣa eva sa na heturityuktaṃ bhavati /
yathā ca aśvo 'yaṃ viṣāṇitvāt iti sapakṣād viśeṣa eveti hetutvena pratiṣiddho bhavati /
yastu sapakṣaikadeśavṛttiḥ prayatnanāntarīyakatvādiḥ sa sapakṣād viśeṣa eva na bhavati, api tu sāmānyamapīti /
na tasyāhetutvamavadhāritamiti heturevāsāvityarthaḥ /
pariharati---yadyevamiti /
yadi sapakṣādapi yo viśeṣaḥ sa sapakṣaikadeśavṛttiḥ prayatnānantarīyakatvādirhetuḥ, evaṃ sati vipakṣādeveti avadhāraṇaṃ bādhitaṃ bhavati /
śaṅkate---atheti /

na vipakṣādevetyetanmātramavadhāryate yena sapakṣaikadeśavṛttiḥ prayatnāntarīyakatvādinarna hetuḥ syāt, api tu yo viśeṣa eva sa heturiti prāpte vipakṣādeveti niyamyate, tena sāvadhāraṇasya viśeṣasya vipakṣavṛtterhetutvaṃ pratiṣiddhaṃ bhavati yathā aśvo 'yaṃ viṣāṇītvāditi /
children.translated_text: It is not merely 'from the dissimilar instance alone' that is being determined— such that 'being necessarily preceded by effort' etc. existing in part of the similar instance would not be a reason— rather, when it is established that 'only what is exclusively differentiated is a reason,' the restriction 'from the dissimilar instance alone' is added; and by this, the reason-hood of something exclusively differentiated that exists in the dissimilar instance is prohibited— like 'this is a horse because of having horns' /

children.text: yaḥ punarviśeṣaścāviśeṣaśca sapakṣe hetuḥ, tasya hetutve 'pi na vipakṣādeveti bādhitaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: But that which is both differentiated and non-differentiated in the similar instance [i.e., exists in some but not all similar instances]— even if its reason-hood is [accepted], 'from the dissimilar instance alone' is not contradicted /

children.text: yadyapi caivaṃ satyapi sapakṣaikadeśavṛtterhetutvaṃ na śrutam, tathāpi vipakṣādevetyanenāvadhāraṇenāniṣiddhamityanumatameva /
children.translated_text: And even though in this case the reason-hood of what exists in part of the similar instance has not been explicitly stated, nevertheless, since it has not been prohibited by the determination 'from the dissimilar instance alone,' it is implicitly accepted /
And by this unstated meaning, the determination has purpose— this is the meaning //

He then refutes that through under-extension— 'true, one' /
Here he objects— 'because the prohibition of what exists in part of the dissimilar instance' /
By the determination 'differentiation alone,' what exists in part of the dissimilar instance— such as 'this is a cow because of having horns'— has been prohibited as a reason /
Therefore, given this determination, 'from the dissimilar instance alone' must be determined /
And thus, that which is exclusively differentiated from the dissimilar instance alone is a reason /
But what is exclusively differentiated from the similar instance— that is not a reason— this is what has been said /
And just as 'this is a horse because of having horns' is prohibited as a reason because it is exclusively differentiated from the similar instance— /
But what exists in part of the similar instance, such as 'being necessarily preceded by effort' and the like— that is not exclusively differentiated from the similar instance, but is also common /
So its being a non-reason has not been determined— therefore it is indeed a reason— this is the meaning /
He resolves— 'if so' /
If what is exclusively differentiated from the similar instance, such as 'being necessarily preceded by effort,' which exists in part of the similar instance, is a reason— then the determination 'from the dissimilar instance alone' would be contradicted /
He raises a doubt— 'now' /

children.text:
nirākaroti---evaṃ ceti /
yathā tattulyaikadeśavṛtteravihitamapi hetutvamaniṣedhānumatam, evaṃ pakṣaikadeśavṛtterapīti so 'pi hetuḥ syādityarthaḥ /
punaḥ pratyavatiṣṭhate---naiṣa doṣa iti /
pakṣadharmatve sati viśeṣa eva vipakṣādeveti niyame kutaḥ pakṣaikadeśavṛtteḥ prāptiḥ, apakṣadharmatvāt tasyetyarthaḥ /
pariharati---yo dharmaḥ pakṣasyetyaneneti /
para āha---na kartavyata iti /
dūṣayitumavadhāraṇaṃ vikalpayati---kiṃ punariti /
prathamaṃ kalpaṃ gṛhṇāti---astu tāvaditi /
etamapi dūṣayitu vikalpayati---kiṃ punarasyeti /
sāmarthya prayojanābhisaṃbandhaḥ saṃbhavajñāpanapakṣe 'jñāpananivṛttiḥ prayojanam, asaṃbhavanivṛttipakṣe tu atyantāyogavyāvṛttiḥ phalam /
yathā nīlaṃ sarojaṃ bhavatyeveti /
vikalpya dūṣayati---ubhayathāpīti /
yuktyantaramāha---na ceti /
atyantāyogo niṣiddho bhavati, na tvayoga ityarthaḥ /
śaṅkate---atheti /
viśeṣaṇasaṃgato hyevakāro 'yogaṃ vyavacchinatti /
yathā caitro dhanurdhara eveti /

children.translated_text: If the reason is the qualifier, then [it would mean:] only what is not a property of the subject /
Therefore, it is established that what exists in only part of the subject is refuted— this is the meaning /
He refutes— 'true' /
The remainder, being mostly explained in the <s>sūtra</s> on inference, is not explained here //

He refutes— 'and thus' /
Just as the reason-hood of what exists in part of the similar instance, though not explicitly prescribed, is implicitly accepted through non-prohibition— so too would what exists in part of the subject [be a reason]— and so that too would be a reason— this is the meaning /
Again [the opponent] maintains his position— 'this is not a fault' /
When there is the property of being a property of the subject, given the restriction that it must be exclusively differentiated from the dissimilar instance alone, how can what exists in part of the subject arise [as a reason], since it is not a property of the subject?— this is the meaning /
He resolves— 'because that property which belongs to the subject'— by this /
The opponent says— 'it is not required' /
To refute [this], he analyzes the determination into alternatives— 'what then?' /
He takes up the first alternative— 'let it be' /
To refute this too, he presents alternatives— 'what then of this?' /
Capacity is the connection with purpose; in the alternative of indicating possibility, the purpose is the removal of non-indication; in the alternative of removing impossibility, the result is the removal of absolute impossibility /
Like: 'a blue lotus does indeed exist' /
Having presented the alternatives, he refutes— 'in both ways also' /
He states another argument— 'and not' /
Absolute impossibility is negated, but not [mere] impossibility— this is the meaning /
He raises a doubt— 'now' /
For the particle '<s>eva</s>' (alone), being connected with the qualifier, excludes [mere] impossibility /
Just as: '<s>Caitra</s> is an archer alone' /

children.text:
heturvipakṣād viśeṣa iti ca yadā sautrāntikapakṣamiti /
yadā tvanityatvahetau lakṣye lakṣaṇaṃ vicāryate iti vipakṣaśabdārtho vācyaḥ /
nanu ca nityo vipakṣa ityata āha---na hyasatīti /
na hi nirupākhyamākhyāyata ityarthaḥ /
na cāsyāpādānatvaṃ nāpyadhikaraṇatvaṃ yena pañcamī vā saptamī vā prayujyeteti āha---na cāsatīti /
na cāsato vipakṣād vyāvṛttyabhāvena viśeṣo 'pītyāha---vipakṣāsaṃbhave ceti /
pakṣasyaiveti /
atra caivakārāstraya padāntarānapekṣatvaṃ sūcayanti /
pakṣasyaiva dharma iti hetulakṣaṇe asādhāraṇa eva hetuḥ syāt /
samāna eva siddha iti tu hetulakṣaṇe aśvasya viṣāṇitve sādhye gotvādirhetuḥ syāt /
tasmāt trayaḥ pakṣāḥ heyāḥ /
tathā ca pakṣasya dharmaḥ samāne ca siddhaḥ ityatra savyabhicāro hetuḥ syāt /
pakṣasya dharmo vipakṣe ca nāstītyatrāsādhāraṇo hetuḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: "A property of the thesis and absent in the counter-thesis" — here the reason would be uncommon.

children.text: samāne ca siddho vipakṣe ca nāstītyatra anityaḥ paramāṇuḥ kṛtakatvāditi hetuḥ syāditi trayaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Established as the same and absent in the counter-thesis" — here the reason would be, for example, "the atom is non-eternal because it is produced" — thus three [faulty positions].
He states the seventh accepted position — "of the thesis."
The rest is easily understood.

And "the reason is distinguished from the counter-thesis" — when this represents the Sautrāntika position.
But when the definition is being examined with regard to the reason for non-eternality as the definiendum, the meaning of the word vipakṣa (counter-thesis) must be stated.
But the counter-thesis is "eternal" — to this he says "for not when non-existent."
The meaning is: what is without designation cannot be designated.
And it has neither the character of a starting-point nor of a locus, so that either the ablative or the locative case could be employed — he says "and when non-existent."
And when the counter-thesis is non-existent, there is no distinction through exclusion from it — he says "and when the counter-thesis is impossible."
"Of the thesis itself" —
Here the three particles eva (only) indicate independence from other terms.
If "a property of the thesis only" were the definition of reason, only the uncommon reason would result.
But if "established as the same" were the definition of reason, then for proving that a horse has horns, cowness and the like would be a reason.
Therefore three positions are to be rejected.
And in "a property of the thesis and established as the same," the reason would be inconclusive.

children.text: atra dignāgena sapakṣe sannasan dvedhā pakṣadharmaḥ punastridhā /
children.translated_text: Here <s>Dignāga</s> [states]: the property of the thesis (pakṣadharma), being present or absent in the sapakṣa (homologue), is twofold;
And in each case, [being] present or absent in the asapakṣa (heterologue), is again twofold, [making three for each].

children.text: iti nava pakṣadharmān hetutadābhāsān darśayitvā tatra yaḥ san sajātīye dvedhā cāsaṃstadatyaye /
children.translated_text: Thus, having shown nine property-of-the-thesis [combinations] as reasons and pseudo-reasons, therein: "That which is present in the homologue and twofold in the absence of the heterologue,"
"That is the reason; its opposite is the contradictory; the other is the inconclusive."

children.text:
ityanena hetutadābhāsaviveko darśitaḥ /
tasyārthaḥ /
yaḥ pakṣadharmaḥ sa sapakṣe san asan dvedhā iti trividhaḥ, sa punarasapakṣe sadasaddvividhatvataḥ pratyekaṃ tridhā bhavatīti /
pakṣadharmaḥ sapakṣe san vipakṣe sadasaddvividhatvatastridhā /
pakṣadharmaḥ sapakṣe 'san vipakṣe sadasaddvividhatvatastridhā, pakṣadharmaḥ sapakṣe dvedhā vipakṣe sadasaddvidhatvatastridheti /

children.translated_text: Here the examples are:
Knowability, producedness, non-eternality, producedness, audibility, being-produced-by-effort,
non-eternality, being-produced-by-effort, tangibility — these nine for [proving] eternality and the like.

By this, the discrimination between reason and pseudo-reason is shown.
Its meaning:
The property of the thesis, being present or absent in the <s>sapakṣa</s>, is twofold — thus threefold. And again, in each case, being present or absent in the <s>asapakṣa</s>, it becomes threefold in each of the three — [making nine].
The property of the thesis present in the <s>sapakṣa</s>, [combined with] presence or absence or both in the <s>vipakṣa</s>, is threefold.
The property of the thesis absent in the <s>sapakṣa</s>, [combined with] presence or absence or both in the <s>vipakṣa</s>, is threefold. The property of the thesis present in both ways in the <s>sapakṣa</s>, [combined with] presence or absence or both in the <s>vipakṣa</s>, is threefold.
They illustrate the properties to be proved such as eternality and the rest in order:
Eternal, non-eternal, produced-by-effort, intermediate, triple, permanent,
Not-produced-by-effort, non-eternal, and non-eternal — these are what knowability and the rest prove.
For the properties to be proved such as eternality and the like, knowability and the rest are the nine reasons and pseudo-reasons.

children.text:
tadeteṣu hetutadābhāseṣu heturnirdhārito yena tadupanyasya vārttikakāro vyācaṣṭe---tatra ya iti /
tadetaddūṣayati---yathāśrutīti /
tatra yaḥ san sajātīye dvedhā cāsaṃstadatyaye ityetāvanmātrāt na labhyate ityarthaḥ /
codayati---nanu coktamiti uktaṃ dignāgena,
sādhyadharmo yato hetustadābhāsāśca bhūyasā /
iti /
tadetat pariharati---uktametaditi /
na punaḥ pakṣadharma evetyarthaḥ, avadhāraṇam abuddhvā śaṅkate---athāpīti /
avadhāraṇārthālābhenottaramāha---satyamarthāditi /
nanu apakṣadharmatvanivṛttyaiva pakṣavyāpakatvaṃ gamyate, na hyavyāpako bhavatyapakṣadharmatvanivṛttimānityata āha---apakṣadharmanivṛttimātratvena ceti /

children.translated_text: By the negation of complete absence, there would be mere presence, not invariable presence — this is the meaning.
He objects — "it is not obtained."
He resolves — "not of the restrictive [sense]."

children.text: hetuhetvābhāsāveva pakṣadharmau nānya iti niyamajñāpanārthamavadhāraṇamiṣṭaṃ bhavadbhirityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: the restrictive sense is intended by you to indicate that only the reason and the pseudo-reason are properties of the thesis, and nothing else.

Having presented [<s>Dignāga</s>'s] determination of the reason among these reasons and pseudo-reasons, the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> explains — "therein, that which."
He then criticizes that — "as literally read."
The meaning is: from the mere [statement] "that which, present in the homologue, and twofold in the absence of the heterologue," [the intended meaning] is not obtained.
He objects — "but it has been said" — it was said by <s>Dignāga</s>:
"Since the reason is a property of what is to be proved, and the pseudo-reasons are mostly [the opposite]."
He resolves this — "this has been said."
But this does not mean "the property of the thesis only" — this is the meaning. Not understanding the restrictive sense, he objects — "even if."
Since the restrictive meaning is not obtained, the answer — "true, from the meaning."
But if the mere absence of not-being-a-property-of-the-thesis [suffices], then pervading the thesis [follows]; for nothing that is not a non-property-of-the-thesis fails to pervade the thesis — to this he says "merely by the absence of not-being-a-property-of-the-thesis."

children.text:
śaṅkate---athobhayeti /
nirākaroti---tathāpi san sajātīya iti /
tadetat pūrvameva vyākhyātaprāyam /
dvedhā ceti sarvathā na vaktavyamīti /
san sajātīya ityasyopādāne 'nupādāne cetyarthaḥ, /
san sajātīya iti nopādātavyamiti yaduktam, tatra śaṅkate---atha manyeteti /
nirākaroti---avadhāraṇeti /
yadyavadhāraṇaṃ yujyeta avadhāraṇārtho yukta ārambhaḥ syāt, tadeva tvayuktamityarthaḥ /
ādye pada iti /
pakṣasya dharma eva ityetasmin pada ityarthaḥ /
anyapade iti /
anye pade yayoḥ pakṣadharmatvavipakṣāsattvayoste tathokte /
tatra dvevidhyaṃ nirākriyata iti /
san sajātīyeti sarvatheti /
sajātīye dvedhā ceti padopādāne cānupādāne cetyarthaḥ /
sajātīya eva dvidhetyanenaiveti hetutadābhāsayorautsargike pakṣadharmatve sthita ityarthaḥ /
śaṅkate---atha mā bhūditi sajātīya eva dvidheti nāvadhāraṇamityarthaḥ /
nirākaroti---tathāpīti /
san sajātīye dvidheti madhyamapade ityarthaḥ /
tadevaṃ sajātīye eva dvidhetyavadhāraṇaṃ dūṣitam /

children.translated_text: Now he objects regarding the second restrictive [sense] — "if, however."
He refutes — "even so."
Even so, a reason that occurs in only a part of the thesis would be entailed.

children.text: yadi ca tadatyaya eveti nāvadhāryeta tato 'naikāntiko 'pi hetuḥ syāditi doṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: And if "in the absence of the heterologue only" were not restrictive, then even an inconclusive reason would result — this is the fault.

He objects — "if both." He refutes — "even so, present in the homologue."
This has been mostly explained before.
"And twofold" — meaning it should not be stated at all.
Meaning: with and without the inclusion of "present in the homologue."
Regarding what was said that "present in the homologue" need not be included, he objects — "if one thinks." He refutes — "the restrictive [sense]."
If the restrictive sense were valid, the restrictive-sense interpretation would be justified — but that itself is invalid: this is the meaning.
"In the first term" — meaning: in the term "a property of the thesis only."
"In the other two terms" — those two whose [content is] the property-of-the-thesis-ness and the absence-in-the-counter-thesis.
Therein the twofold nature is refuted — "present in the homologue, in every case."
Meaning: with and without the inclusion of the phrase "in the homologue, twofold."
By "in the homologue only, twofold" alone — meaning: since both the reason and the pseudo-reason are established as having the general character of being a property of the thesis, [the rest is superfluous].
He objects — "if it should not be" — meaning: "in the homologue only, twofold" is not restrictive.
He refutes — "even so."
Meaning: "present in the homologue, twofold" is the middle term.

children.text:
dignāgasyaiva pradeśāntarahetulakṣaṇam---grāhyadharmaḥ pakṣadharmaḥ /
tadaṃśena tasyaiva pakṣasyāṃśena sādhyadharmasāmānyena, vyāpto heturiti /
tadetaddhetulakṣaṇamupanyasyāsmin pūrvoktaṃ doṣamatidiśati---eteneti /

children.translated_text: He makes the extension explicit — "non-pervading and the like."

children.text: yathāśrutalakṣaṇe pakṣāvyāpakasya hetutvam, tadaṃśena vyāpta ityasya vivaraṇālocanena sapakṣe sattvaṃ vipakṣācca vyāvṛttirityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the definition as literally read, what does not pervade the thesis would qualify as a reason; by the analysis of the explanation of "pervaded by a portion of that," [one obtains] presence in the homologue and exclusion from the counter-thesis — this is the meaning.
And thus the previously stated faults follow — this is the meaning.
He criticizes by the method of looking back like a lion — "absent in the counter-thesis."

The definition of reason from another passage of <s>Dignāga</s> himself: "The grāhya-dharma (property of what is to be apprehended) is the pakṣadharma (property of the thesis). That which is pervaded by a portion of that very thesis — by the universal of the property to be proved — is the reason."
Having presented this definition of reason, he extends to it the previously stated fault — "by this."

children.text:
anyeṣāṃ hetulakṣaṇaṃ dūṣayitumupanyasyati-tādṛgiti /
tadetadvyācaṣṭe-tādṛśeti /
kilakāro 'rucau /
pakṣadharma iti ca hetorabhidhānam /
tena trilakṣaṇapravibhāvitātmā heturityarthaḥ /
dūṣayati---tat tāvaditi /
śrāvaṇatvādyapīti /
tadukto 'sādhāraṇa ityarthaḥ /
yastu tādṛśavinābhāvīti vipakṣe sattāpratiṣedhāt sapakṣe sattvaṃ gamyate eva, viśeṣaniṣedhasya śeṣābhyanujñāviṣayatvāditi manyeta, taṃ pratyāha---bhavatu tāvaditi /
ekadeśābhyanujñāne 'pi viśeṣaniṣedhasyopapatterna samastāśeṣābhyanujñāne pramāṇamastītyabhiprāyaḥ /
codayati---nanūpadarśanagrahaṇāditi /
pariharati---na tallabhyata iti /

children.translated_text: For visual perceptibility [is not invariably connected with non-eternality].

children.text: vauddhānāṃ rūpatvādijāternityāyā abhāvād na cākṣuṣatvamanityatvena vinā bhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since in the Buddhist view there is no eternal universal such as "form-ness" (rūpatva) and the like, visual perceptibility cannot exist without non-eternality — this is the meaning.

children.text: yastu manyeta viśeṣaniṣadhasya śeṣamātrabhyanujñāhetutvenāgṛhyamāṇaviśeṣatvāt pakṣasattābhyanujñānam, tathā copadarśanapadena pakṣe hetoḥ sattopadarśanaṃ bhavatīti taṃ pratyupetyāha---upetya veti /
