children.translated_text: But if one thinks that the specific negation, being the cause for permitting the mere remainder, [implies] the permitting of the existence in the thesis because of the unapprehended specific [property], and that by the word "observation" the observation of the existence of the reason in the thesis is [indicated] — to that, accepting this provisionally, he says "accepting provisionally."
This is easily understood.

He presents the definition of reason by others in order to criticize it — "of such a kind."
He explains that — "of such a kind."
The particle kila expresses disapproval.
And "property of the thesis" is a designation for the reason.
Thus, the reason whose nature is manifested by the triple mark (<s>trilakṣaṇa</s>) — this is the meaning.
He criticizes — "that, first."
"Audibility and the like also" — meaning that too would be the uncommon [reason].
But if one thinks that by "not existing without such [a property]," the negation of presence in the counter-thesis implies presence in the homologue, since a specific negation permits the remainder — to that he replies: "let it be so, first."
The intent is: even though a specific negation can permit a part of the remainder, there is no pramāṇa for it permitting the entire remainder.
He objects — "but because of the inclusion of the word observation."
He resolves — "that is not obtained."

children.text:
tadevaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ dūṣayitvā tadudāharaṇaṃ dūṣayati---yattvidamiti /
etasmin hetulakṣaṇe ityarthaḥ /
prayatnanāntarīyakatvaṃ prayatnakāraṇakatvaṃ tat sākṣāt pāramparyeṇa vā? tatra prathame kalpe dūṣaṇamāha---prayatnānantarīyakatvasyeti /
dvitīyakalpamāśaṅkya dūṣayati---atheti /
prayatnagrahaṇamapārthakamityarthaḥ /
bhāvapratyayavācyaṃ vikalpya dūṣayati---yaccedamiti /
evamapyupalabdhereveti /
na hi boddharāddhānte kiścidupalabhyamānaṃ nityamasti, yenopalabdhirviśeṣyeta ityabhiprāyaḥ /
prayatnānantaramanyathā ceti /
yat tāvadupalabdhikarma tatsarvaṃ prayatnādeva puruṣavyāpādādevopalabhyate nānyathetyarthaḥ /
śaṅkate---atheti /
asmākaṃ naiyāyikānāmiti bhāvaḥ /
uttaram---tvayaiveti /
asmaddarśanaṃ cedāsthāya tvayā bauddhenocyate, tat prayatnagrahaṇenāpyanaikāntikatvaṃ tadavasthamevetyarthaḥ /
avyāpakaṃ ceti /
na hi davadahanābhighātaprasphuṭadveṇudalavibhāgajanmā ṭhātkāro 'smadādiprayatnakārya ityarthaḥ /
śaṅkate---atheti /
varṇātmakamityarthaḥ nirākaroti---tatrāpīti /
pāramparyeṇāpi prathama eva varṇaḥ prayatnānantarīyakaḥ, na dvitīyādayaḥ /
atipāramparyāśrayaṇe tvatiprasaṅgaḥ, prāyeṇa tasya tatra tatra sulabhatvāditi bhāvaḥ /
śaṅkate---atha ya iti /
viśeṣaḥ prayatnānantarīyakatvaṃ dharmiviśeṣaṇam, prayatnānantarīyakatvaṃ sāmānyaṃ ca heturityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The specific [property], namely being-invariably-preceded-by-effort, qualifies the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>); and being-invariably-preceded-by-effort as the universal, is the reason — this is the meaning.
He refutes — "even so, another."

children.text: na hi bhavatāmasmākamiva viśeṣātiriktamasti sāmānyaṃ vastu sad yo hetuḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: For you [Buddhists] do not have, as we do, a real universal that exists over and above the particular, which could serve as the reason.

children.text: na ca kalpanāropitaṃ hetuḥ samyagjñānasya bhavitumarhati, na cātyantāsataḥ kalpanāpi saṃbhavatīti bhāvaḥ //
children.translated_text: And what is superimposed by conceptual construction cannot be a reason for correct knowledge; nor is conceptual construction possible regarding what is absolutely non-existent — this is the meaning.

Having thus criticized the definition, he criticizes its example — "but this."
The meaning is: in this definition of reason.
Is "being invariably preceded by effort" (prayatna-nāntarīyakatva) being directly caused by effort, or being caused through a chain of causes? In the first case, he states the criticism — "of being invariably preceded by effort."
Assuming the second case, he criticizes — "if, then."
The word "effort" would be purposeless — this is the meaning.
Considering what the suffix meaning "state" expresses, he criticizes — "and this."
"Even so, of apprehension alone" —
For in the Buddhist established doctrine, nothing that is apprehended is eternal, by which apprehension could be qualified — this is the intent.
"And otherwise after effort" —
All that is the object of apprehension is apprehended through effort alone, i.e., through human activity alone, and not otherwise — this is the meaning.
He objects — "if, then."
The meaning is: for us <s>Naiyāyikas</s>.
The answer — "by you yourself."
If our view is adopted and you the Buddhist say this, then even with the inclusion of "effort," the inconclusiveness remains the same — this is the meaning.
"And non-pervading" —
For the cracking sound produced by the splitting of bamboo stalks bursting due to forest fire is not an effect of effort by us and the like — this is the meaning.
He objects — "if, then."
Meaning: consisting of phonemes. He refutes — "even there."
Even through a chain of causes, only the first phoneme is invariably preceded by effort, not the second and subsequent ones.
And if an excessive chain of causation is relied upon, there would be over-extension, since that is generally easy to find everywhere — this is the meaning.
He objects — "if that which."

children.text:
tadevamudāharaṇaṃ dūṣayitvā prasaṅgena pareṣāmudāharaṇavicāraṃ dūṣayati---yadapyuktamiti /
tat khalvasat sarvasāmarthyarahitaṃ tadāśritānāśritabhāvābhāvadharmavanna bhavatītyarthaḥ /
nityaṃ tu kiścid bhavatīti /
tasya dharmayogaḥ saṃbhavatyeva, na tvasyāpyaprayatnānantarīyakatvaṃ tvapratyayābhidheyaṃ hi janma, tat prayatnenada prayatnādanyena vā viśeṣaṇīyam, yasya tu janmaiva nāsti tasya tadviśeṣaṇaṃ dūrotsāritamityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: By this, [the concept of] "absence" [is also addressed].
The absence accepted by the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> too is explained.

children.text: tasyāpi hi prāgasataḥ savakāraṇena samavāya iti janma nāstīti na tadviśeṣaṇayoga ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For that too, being previously non-existent, its conjunction with its own cause through inherence — that is, origination — does not exist; therefore the qualification by that [property of being preceded by effort] does not apply — this is the meaning.
He concludes the topic under discussion — "thus." (35)

Having thus criticized the example, he criticizes incidentally the opponents' examination of the example — "and what was said."
That [non-being], being non-existent, is devoid of all capacity; therefore it cannot have properties such as the state of being dependent or not dependent upon it — this is the meaning.
"But something eternal exists" —
The possession of properties by it is indeed possible; however, it does not have the property of not-being-invariably-preceded-by-effort, for origination is to be expressed by [the suffix] denoting a state of becoming; and that [origination] must be qualified either by effort or by something other than effort; but for what has no origination at all, that qualification is far removed — this is the meaning.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.36: An example (<s>udāharaṇa</s>) is an instance that, by virtue of sharing a property with what is to be proved, possesses the property of that [which is to be proved].

children.text:
hetāvukte nāvyāpto 'sau sādhyadharmeṇa hetubhāve vyavatiṣṭhate, na ca vyāptipradarśanamudāharaṇamantareṇeti hetulakṣaṇānantaraṃ kramaprāptamudāharaṇalakṣaṇamāha---sādhya---raṇam //36// sūtramityudāharaṇasāmānyalakṣaṇamapyanena sūcitamiti darśitam /
asya tātparyamāha---asyeti, dṛṣṭānto 'rtharūpo nodāharaṇasya vacanātmakasya svarūpato lakṣaṇaṃ saṃbhavati /
tasmāt svābhidhāyakavacanopalakṣakatvena lakṣaṇatvaṃ sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ ca bhajata ityabhisandhinoktam---udāharaṇopalakṣaṇamiti /
anena ca samānajātīyebhyaḥ pratijñādibhyaḥ asamānajātīyebhyaśca pramāṇādibhya udāharaṇaṃ vyavacchinnaṃ bhavati /
sādhyena sādharmyam ityādi bhāṣyam /
tasyārthaḥ, sādhyena dharmiṇā śabdena, sādharmyaṃ dṛṣṭāntasya sthālyādeḥ, kṛtakatvaṃ hetuḥ /
kaddhyanityatvena sādhye ca śabde dṛṣṭānte ca sthālpādau samānam /
tasmāt kāraṇat prayojakāt, taddharmabhāvī tasyaiva sādhyasya śabdasya yo dharmo dharmāntaram, yena viśiṣṭaḥ śabdaḥ siṣādhayiṣito 'nityatvena, tadanityatvaṃ taddharmaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, from that cause — that which is the operative [factor] — possessing the property of that: the property of that very <s>sādhya</s>-subject sound — a different property, by which sound is qualified as desired to be established as non-eternal — that non-eternality is the property of that.
That very state is the state of having that property (<s>taddharmabhāva</s>).
'That is present in this' — hence it possesses that property: the cooking vessel and the like possess the property of non-eternality — this is the purport.
The statement whose subject-matter is indicated by such an example is the illustration. //

When the reason has been stated, it does not remain in reason-status without being pervaded by the <s>sādhya</s>-property, and the demonstration of pervasion is not possible without illustration — therefore, following the definition of reason in due order, he states the definition of illustration — '<s>sādhya</s>... illustration.' //36// By [saying] '<s>sūtra</s>,' it has been shown that even the general definition of illustration is indicated by this. He states its purport — 'of this': since the example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) has the nature of a real object, a definition based on its own form is not possible for illustration, which has the nature of a verbal statement. Therefore, with the intention that it acquires definition-status and co-reference through being the suggestive indicator of the statement that designates it — it has been said — 'it is the suggestive indicator of illustration.' And by this, illustration is distinguished from what is of the same class — proposition and the like — and from what is of a different class — <s>pramāṇa</s> and the like. The <s>bhāṣya</s>: 'similarity with what is to be proved' and so on. Its meaning: similarity of the example — the cooking vessel and the like — with the <s>sādhya</s>-bearing subject (<s>dharmin</s>) sound; the reason is the property of being produced (<s>kṛtakatva</s>). For non-eternality is common to both the <s>sādhya</s> sound and the example — the cooking vessel and the like.

children.text:
tatra vārttikakāraḥ sūtrapadaṃ vyācakṣāṇa eva phalato bhāṣyaṃ vyācaṣṭe---sādhyeti /
udāharaṇasādharmyādityasya vyākhyānaṃ sādhyasādharmyādityatrāpi yojayati---atrāpīti /
sādhyaśabdenaiva kṛtakatvaṃ sādharmyaṃ dṛṣṭāntasya, nāsādhyena vipakṣeṇākāśādinā nityena, tato hi kṛtakatvaṃ vyāvṛttamiti /
tathā ca savyabhicāro vyavacchinno bhavati /
sādharmyameveti bhāgāsiddho vyavacchinnaḥ /
yasmāt sādhyasādharmyāt saddharmabhāvī bhavati, so 'yaṃ dṛṣṭānta udāharaṇamiti,
yāvad vākyaṃ na samāpyate, tāvadardhokta eva pṛcchati---kiṃ kutaściditi /
avadhāraṇadvayayoginaḥ sādhyasādharmyād dṛṣṭānto 'vaśyameva taddharmabhāvī bhavatīti gatārthaṃ taddharmabhāvītyetaditi bhāvaḥ /
uttaram---na bhavatyapīti /
yathā nitye śabde sādhye amūrtatvādeḥ sādhyena śabdena karmaṇaḥ sādharmyāt karma na taddharmabhāvi bhavati, nityaṃ na bhavatītyarthaḥ /
sādhyenaivetyavadhāraṇenaiva etadudāharaṇaṃ pratyuktamiti /
śiṣyopādhyāyaśyaśyāmatvamaitratanayatvādayo 'traupādhikasaṃbandhā udāhāryāḥ /
hetulakṣaṇe tu sāmānyalakṣaṇāpekṣaṃ viśeṣalakṣaṇamiti nātivyāptiḥ /
atra ca sādhyasādharmyagrahaṇena sādhanavikalamanudāharaṇaṃ bhavatītyuktaṃ bhavati /
yathā nityaḥ śabdaḥ amūrtatvāt paramāṇuvaditi /
taddharmabhāvītyanena ca sādhyavikalaṃ parāstam /
yathā nityaḥ śabdo mūrtatvāt karmavaditi /
etenobhayavikalamapi parākṛtam /
yathā nityaḥ śabdaḥ amūrtatvād ghaṭavaditi /
pañcamyupādānena ca sādhyasādharmyaprayuktaṃ taddharmabhāvitvaṃ yatra vacane pradarśyate tadevodāharaṇaṃ nānyaditi darśitaṃ bhavati /
prayojakatvaṃ ca sādhyasādharmyasya hetoḥ svābhāvikaḥ saṃbandho vyāpyatvamiti yāvat /
prayojyatvaṃ ca sādhyasādharmyasya vyāpakatvameva /
tenāpradarśitānvayaviparītapradarśitānvayayoranudāharaṇatvamuktaṃ bhavatīti /

children.translated_text: For example: 'sound is non-eternal, because of being produced, like cloth.'

children.text: yo yo 'nityaḥ sa sarva utpattimān yathā ghaṭa iti /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever is non-eternal, all of that is produced — like a pot.'

children.text: samākhyānirvacanasāmarthyāt sāmānyalakṣaṇamapyanena sūcitamityāśayavatā bhāṣyakṛtā samākhyāyā niruktiḥ kṛtā /
children.translated_text: The <s>bhāṣyakāra</s>, intending to suggest the general definition also by the power of the etymological derivation of the name, has given the etymology of the name.
The <s>vārttikakāra</s> shows that — 'it is illustrated by this.' //

There, the <s>vārttikakāra</s>, while explaining the words of the <s>sūtra</s>, explains the <s>bhāṣya</s> by its result — '<s>sādhya</s>.' He connects the explanation 'from the similarity of the illustration' with 'from the similarity of the <s>sādhya</s>' as well — 'here too.' By the word '<s>sādhya</s>' itself, the similarity of the example is the property of being produced — not with the non-<s>sādhya</s>, the dissimilar instance such as space and the like, which is eternal, since the property of being produced is excluded from that. And thus the deviant [reason] is excluded. 'Similarity alone' — the partially unestablished [reason] is excluded. Because from the similarity with the <s>sādhya</s>, [the example] possesses that property, this very example is the illustration — while the sentence is not yet completed, he asks mid-way — 'is it from something?' The import is: since the two determinations [already] yield the result, the expression 'possessing that property' is redundant. The answer — 'it does not [always] possess.' Just as when the eternality of sound is the <s>sādhya</s>, [the example] action, because of its similarity with the <s>sādhya</s> sound through the [shared property of] incorporeality, does not possess that property — does not become eternal — this is the meaning. It is by the determination 'of the <s>sādhya</s> alone' that this counter-example is answered. The incidental relations of teacher and pupil, darkness and <s>Maitra</s>'s son-hood, and the like are to be cited here. But in the definition of reason, since the specific definition presupposes the general definition, there is no over-extension. And here, by the inclusion of 'similarity with the <s>sādhya</s>,' it has been stated that what lacks the proving property is not an illustration — as in: 'sound is eternal because of incorporeality, like an atom.' And by 'possessing that property,' what lacks the <s>sādhya</s> is set aside — as in: 'sound is eternal because of corporality, like action.' By this, what lacks both is also set aside — as in: 'sound is eternal because of incorporeality, like a pot.' And by using the ablative case [in 'from similarity'], it has been shown that illustration is precisely that statement in which the possession of that property, occasioned by similarity with the <s>sādhya</s>, is demonstrated — and nothing else. And the operative nature of similarity with the <s>sādhya</s> is the natural connection of the reason — namely, its being pervaded. And the operatedness of the similarity with the <s>sādhya</s> is precisely its being the pervader. Thus it has been stated that what has an undemonstrated positive concomitance and what has a contrarily demonstrated positive concomitance are not illustrations.

children.text:
codayati---nanu ceti /
pariharati---naiṣa doṣa iti /
vacanasya viśeṣaṇatvenopalakṣaṇatvenetyarthaḥ /
abhidhīyamāna iti ca abhidhānopalakṣaṇaparam, nābhidheyaparam, asāmānādhikaraṇyadoṣasya tāvadavasthyāt /
taddharmabhāvīti sūtrāvayavavyākhyānaparaṃ bhāṣyam---tasya dharma ityādi /
atra cottaramiti guḍhābhiprāyam /
tadetad bhāṣyam anubhāṣya vyācaṣṭe---tasya dharma iti /
tasya dharmastaddharma iti hi dharmasya saṃbandhitvena pṛthagvacanam /
na ca dharma eva dharmasya, nāpi dharmāntaraṃ dharmasya, kiṃ tu dharmiṇa ityarthaḥ /
anena bhāṣyakārīyāmanupapattimuktvā vārttikakāraḥ svakīyāmapyāha---dharme ca sādhya iti /
anena hetūdāharaṇopanayalakṣaṇairvyāghāta uktaḥ /
bhāṣyam---sādhyasādharmyādutpattidharmakatvāditi, tad vyācaṣṭe---tasya dharmiṇa iti /
taddharmabhāvī bhavatīti, tadanupapannam, na hi kṛtakatvāt sthālyāderanityatvaṃ bhavati, jāyate bījādivāṅkura ityata uktam---bhavati vidyate//36 //
children.translated_text: He objects — 'but is it not so?' He resolves — 'this is not a fault.' The meaning is: the verbal statement functions as a qualifier, i.e., as a suggestive indicator. And 'being denoted' is directed at the suggestive indication by the designation, not at the denoted [object], since the fault of non-co-reference remains as before. The <s>bhāṣya</s> — 'possessing that property' — explaining this portion of the <s>sūtra</s>: 'the property of that' and so on. And here the answer has a hidden intention. Having repeated this <s>bhāṣya</s>, he explains — 'the property of that.' For the separate statement 'the property of that is <s>taddharma</s>' is because of the relational nature of the property. And the property is not [the property] of a property, nor is it a different property of a property, but rather of a property-bearer — this is the meaning. Having stated this difficulty of the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s>, the <s>vārttikakāra</s> states his own [difficulty] too — 'and when the property is the <s>sādhya</s>.' By this, the conflict with the definitions of reason, illustration, application, and conclusion has been stated. The <s>bhāṣya</s>: 'from the similarity with the <s>sādhya</s>, because of having the property of being produced' — he explains — 'of that property-bearer.' 'It possesses that property' — this is untenable, for the non-eternality of a cooking vessel and the like does not come about because of the property of being produced; it arises from a seed and the like, as does a sprout — therefore he has said — 'exists, is present.' //36//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.37: Or, the opposite, through dissimilarity with that.

children.text:
vaidharmyodāharaṇasya lakṣaṇam---tadvi---tam //37// anuvṛttena pūrayitvā savyākhyānaṃ sūtraṃ paṭhati---sādhyavaidharmyādataddharmabhāvī ca dṛṣṭānta udāharaṇamiti /
sātmakatayā sādhyena jīvaccharīreṇa vaidhamyād ghaṭāderdṛṣṭāntasya sātmakatvasādharmyavirahāditi yāvat /
yasya sādhyasya jīvaccharīrasya dharmaḥ prāṇādimattvaṃ taddharmaḥ /
sa eva bhāvastaddharmabhāvaḥ /
so 'syāstīti taddharmabhāvī /
na taddharmabhāvī ataddharmabhāvī, prāṇādirahito ghaṭādiriti yāvat /
etaduktaṃ bhavati, yatra ghaṭādau sādhyadharmābhāvaprayuktaḥ sādhanadharmābhāvaḥ, sa ghaṭādirvaidharmyadṛṣṭāntaḥ /
tadviṣayaḥ śabda udāharaṇamiti /
sūtrasthaśca vāśabdaḥ samucceye veditavyaḥ, vyatirekaviṣayatvād vaidharmyodāharaṇasyeti /
atra bhāṣyakāreṇa anvayavyatirekī pūrvasatrodāhṛto 'trāpyudāhṛtaḥ /
sādhanadharmābhāvaprayuktatvaṃ ca sādhyadharmābhāvasyoktam, taccāyuktam /
anvayavyatirekiṇihetau satyapi vaidharmye sādharmyodāharaṇamevocitam, tatra tatpūrvakatvād vaidharmyapratīteḥ ṛjumārgeṇa sidhyato 'rthasya vakreṇa sādhanāyogāt /
children.translated_text: For a positive-negative reason (<s>anvayavyatirekin</s>), even when there is dissimilarity, the similarity-illustration alone is appropriate, since in that [case] the understanding of dissimilarity is achieved straightforwardly because it presupposes [the similarity], and what is achievable by a straight path should not be achieved by a crooked one.
And the pervaded-pervader relation between the two positive [properties] should be understood as reversed between their negations.

children.text: anyathā sapakṣaikadeśavartī na hetuḥ syāditi manyamāno vārtikakāra āha---udāharaṇamavītahetāviti /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, [a reason that is] present in only a part of the similar instance would not be a [valid] reason — thinking thus, the <s>vārttikakāra</s> says — 'illustration for the <s>avīta</s> reason.'
And this has been stated by us while construing the <s>sūtra</s>. //

The definition of the illustration by dissimilarity — 'that... opposite.' //37// Having completed [the <s>sūtra</s>] with what carries over, he recites the <s>sūtra</s> with explanation — 'an example that, because of dissimilarity with the <s>sādhya</s>, does not possess that property, is the illustration.' From the dissimilarity of the example — pot and the like — with the <s>sādhya</s>-subject living body — i.e., the absence of similarity with the <s>sādhya</s>-property of having a self — this is the purport. The property of that <s>sādhya</s>-subject living body — the possession of vital breath and the like — is its property. That very state is the state of having that property. 'That is present in this' — hence 'possessing that property.' Not possessing that property is 'not possessing that property' — i.e., pot and the like are devoid of vital breath and the like — this is the purport. What has been stated amounts to this: the example — pot and the like — in which the absence of the proving property is occasioned by the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>-property, is the dissimilarity-example. The statement whose subject-matter is that is the illustration. And the word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) in the <s>sūtra</s> should be understood in the sense of aggregation, since the dissimilarity-illustration pertains to the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>). Here the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> has illustrated the positive-negative reason (<s>anvayavyatirekin</s>) in the previous <s>sūtra</s> and has illustrated it here too. And it has been stated that the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>-property is occasioned by the absence of the proving property — this is improper.

children.text:
atra ācāryadeśīyāṇām anārṣasūtrapāṭhadūṣaṇaṃ nāsmākamārṣasūtrapāṭhe 'stiti pratipipādayiṣurācāryadeśīyānāṃ pāṭhamabhiprāyaṃ cāha---anye tviti /
ārṣe hi pāṭhe sāmānādhikaraṇyād dṛṣṭāntasyārtharūpasya, śabdarūpeṇodāharaṇenaikyaṃ syāt /
yadā tu dṛṣṭāntasyodāharaṇamiti pāṭhaḥ, tadā nāyaṃ doṣaḥ /
dūṣaṇaṃ cāpareṣām, yathā na dṛṣṭāntasya udāharaṇena sāmānādhikaraṇyam, evaṃ taddharmabhāvitvasyārtharūpasya, svaviṣayavacanopalakṣaṇatvena tu sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ dṛṣṭānte 'pi tulyam /
tasmādārṣamevāstviti /
ārṣe 'pi pāṭhe paroktaṃ dūṣaṇamupanyasyati---etasminnapīti /
upahāse kilakāraḥ /
ṇyantād bhavatestācchīlye ṇininā bhāvīti vyutpannam /

children.translated_text: And thus, the meaning is: having the nature of producing that property.

children.text: na ca jñāpanādanyā kriyā saṃbhavatīti gamakatvam /
children.translated_text: And no activity other than indicating is possible — hence [it means] indicative capacity.
And that is common to all the members [of the syllogism], and hence due to being common it need not be stated — this is the meaning.
He resolves this by concession alone — 'this is not so.' //

Here, intending to show that the fault attributed by those near the <s>Ācārya</s> [i.e., followers] to the non-original <s>sūtra</s>-reading does not apply to our original <s>sūtra</s>-reading, he states the reading and intention of those near the <s>Ācārya</s> — 'others, however.' For in the original reading, because of co-reference, the example — which has the nature of a real object — would become identical with illustration, which has the nature of a verbal statement. But when the reading is 'illustration of the example,' this fault does not arise. And the fault of the others — just as there is no co-reference of the example with illustration, so too there is none for the property of possessing-that-property, which has the nature of a real object; but co-reference through being the suggestive indicator of the statement about its own subject-matter is the same even for the example. Therefore, let the original [reading] stand. He presents the fault stated by others even against the original reading — 'even in this.' The particle '<s>kila</s>' expresses ridicule. '<s>Bhāvī</s>' is derived from the root '<s>bhū</s>' (to be) with the suffix '<s>ṇini</s>' in the sense of habitual action, from the causative form.

children.text:
anye tu taddharmabhāvītyetad vikalpya dūṣayantītyāha---anye tviti /
tatra prathamakalpe dūṣaṇamāhuḥ---tad yadīti /
nāyaṃ sūtrārthaḥ sarvāvayavasādhāraṇyāditi /
tasmāt na kiñcidetat taddharmaṃ bhāvayituṃ śīlamasyeti /
dvitīyakalpe dūṣaṇamāhuḥ---daṇḍinyāyastu iti /
saṃbhave vyabhicāre ca syād viśeṣaṇamarthavat,
na saṃbhavamātre ityarthaḥ /
tadidaṃ pareṣāṃ dūṣaṇaṃ daṇḍinyāyamālambya pariharati---na vaktavyamiti /
saṃbhavavyabhicārābhyāṃ samarthaṃ viśeṣaṇamityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: Not in the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> [compound].
It is to be construed only with the intention of expressing the meaning of the other word.

children.text: sā ca bahuvrīhiṇai labhyata iti kṛtamatreninetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And that is obtained [only] through the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> — hence the suffixed form [with <s>ṇini</s>] is superfluous — this is the meaning.

children.text: suhṛdbhāvena ced, ata evāha---athāvaśyamiti prayojanāntaraṃ bhāvīgrahaṇasyānvācinoti---santīti //
children.translated_text: If out of friendly concern — for precisely this reason he says — 'but if necessarily' — he traces another purpose for the inclusion of '<s>bhāvī</s>' — 'there are.' //

Others, however, analyze and criticize '<s>taddharmabhāvī</s>' through alternatives — thus he says — 'others, however.' In the first alternative, they state the fault — 'if that.' The meaning is: this cannot be the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>, because it is common to all members. Therefore, [it is] nothing at all — 'one whose habit it is to produce that property' [is vacuous]. In the second alternative, they state the fault — 'but by the rule of <s>daṇḍin</s> (one with a stick).' A qualifier is meaningful when there is [both] possibility and deviation — not in mere possibility — this is the meaning. He resolves the others' criticism by resorting to the rule of <s>daṇḍin</s> — 'need not be stated.' The meaning is: a qualifier is meaningful through [both] possibility and deviation.

children.text: atra ca vasubandhunā pratijñādayastrayo 'vayavā durvihitā akṣapādalakṣaṇenetyuktam, tad dūṣayati---tadetasminniti //
children.translated_text: And here, <s>Vasubandhu</s> has said that proposition and the other three members are poorly formulated by <s>Akṣapāda</s>'s [i.e., <s>Gautama</s>'s] definition — he refutes that — 'in this very.' //

children.text: tadevamudāharaṇalakṣaṇamupapādya pareṣāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ dūṣayitumupanyasya vyācaṣṭe---yathā siddha iti /

yathā ca sa eva sādhyo viśiṣṭaḥ pratyayabhedabheditveneti, pratyayaḥ kāraṇam, tadetat sādhyasādhanavattvaṃ dṛṣṭāntasya bauddharāddhānte 'vyāpakam, sthālyādau dṛṣṭānte kṛtakatvānityatvarūpasādhyasādhanavattvavaikalyāt /
children.translated_text: And just as that very <s>sādhya</s>, being distinguished by the differentiation of cognition[-conditions] — where 'cognition' (<s>pratyaya</s>) means cause — this very property of the example possessing both <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s> is non-pervasive in the Buddhist established doctrine, because the example — cooking vessel and the like — lacks being produced (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) and non-eternality (<s>anityatva</s>) as <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s>.

children.text: prāgabhāvo hi sthālyāḥ kṛtakatvaṃ pradhvaṃsābhāvaścānityatā rāddhānte bauddhānām /
children.translated_text: For in the established Buddhist doctrine, prior absence (<s>prāgabhāva</s>) of the cooking vessel is its being-produced, and posterior absence (<s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s>) is its non-eternality.

children.text: na caivamubhayaṃ sthālyāmasti, tasyāḥ svābhāvavirodhitvāditi dūṣayati---atra visphūrjatāpīti /
children.translated_text: And both do not [simultaneously] exist in the cooking vessel, since it is contradictory to its own existence — he criticizes thus — 'here, even <s>Visphūrjatu</s>.' //
'By this' — 'is demonstrated as non-pervasive in this, by this' — thus it is a demonstrative illustration. //
Having thus established the definition of illustration and presented the others' definition for criticism, he explains — 'as in the established.'
'The positive concomitance of the reason with the <s>sādhya</s>, and its absence in the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>' —
This too has been answered — because of non-pervasiveness, through showing the impossibility of being-produced and non-eternality in the cooking vessel.

children.text: asmadrāddhānte tu yathā tayoḥ sthālyādau saṃbhavaḥ tathoktaṃ hetulakṣaṇasūtra iti /
children.translated_text: But in our established doctrine, the way in which both [being-produced and non-eternality] are possible in the cooking vessel and the like has been stated in the <s>sūtra</s> defining the reason.
In the <s>bhāṣya</s>, 'to be known by one having the appearance of a learned person' means: to be known by an excellent learned person — this is the meaning. //37//

children.text: NyS_1,1.38: udāharaṇāpekṣaḥ tathā iti upasaṃhāraḥ na tathā iti vā sādhyasya upanayaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.38: Application (<s>upanaya</s>) is the subsumption — depending on the illustration — [stated as] 'it is so' or 'it is not so' with respect to what is to be proved.

children.text:
svapratipattau vyāptismaraṇānantaraṃ tathā cāyaṃ na tatheti vā parāmarśajñānotpādādudāharaṇavacanasya ca vyāptipratipādakatvāt parāmarśajñāne hetorupanayasyodāharaṇapūrvakatvaniyamāt /
udāharaṇānantaramupanayaṃ lakṣayati---udā---yaḥ //38// apekṣāpadaṃ bhāṣyakṛd vyācaṣṭe---udāharaṇatantra iti /
udāharaṇavaśaḥ /
vaśyata iti vaśaḥ, vaśina udāharaṇasya vaśya ityarthaḥ /
etadeva karmaṇo bhāvaṃ niṣkṛṣya vivṛṇotti---vaśaḥ, sāmarthyam /
vaśyena udāharaṇasya phalena upanayenābhisaṃbandha ityarthaḥ /
tathātvātathātvayorviṣayaṃ vibhajate---sādhyasādharmyayukta iti /
nanu hetorupasaṃhāra apanayo na sādhyasya /
tathā cānupapannaḥ sādhyasyopasaṃhāra ityata uktam---sādhyasya śabdasyotpattidharmakatvamiti /
children.translated_text: And thus the subsumption of the <s>sādhya</s> is unjustified— therefore it has been said: 'the property of sound, the <s>sādhya</s>, being produced' /
The meaning is: the <s>sādhya</s> is subsumed through the reason's possession of the concomitance established in the example, not in its own form /
Here too, the general definition is: the subsumption that is dependent on the example is the application /

children.text: tathā na tatheti sāmānyalakṣaṇāpekṣe viśeṣalakṣaṇe iti bodhyavyam //
children.translated_text: And it should be understood that 'being so' and 'not being so' are the specific definitions, which depend on the general definition //

In one's own cognition, after the recollection of the concomitance, the apprehensive cognition arises as 'and this is so' or 'this is not so'; and since the statement of the example serves to convey the concomitance, and since the application (<s>upanaya</s>), being the cause of the apprehensive cognition of the reason, is necessarily preceded by the example— /
After the example, he defines the application— 'example... which' //38// The <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> explains the word 'dependent'— 'dependent on the example' /
'Under the control of the example' /
'Control' means being controlled; the meaning is: controlled by the example which is the controller /
He extracts and elaborates the objective meaning of this— 'control means capacity' /
The meaning is: the connection of the example with the application, which is its result, by virtue of which [the application] is controlled /
He differentiates the scope of 'being so' and 'not being so'— 'possessing similarity with the <s>sādhya</s>' /
Now, the application is the subsumption of the reason, not of the <s>sādhya</s> /

children.text:
atra kecit āhuḥ hetuvacanādeva sodāharaṇāt sādhyasiddherasādhanāṅgamupanaya iti /
tannirākartumāha vārttikakāraḥ---yathā tatheti pratibimbanārtham /
tadetat praśnapūrvakaṃ vibhajate---kiṃ punariti /
tadanena vyutpannāvyutpannatayā pareṣāmaniyatapratipattisādhanatvāt svapratipattyanusāreṇa pare bodhayitavyāḥ /
vyāptismaraṇānantarotpannaliṅgaparāmarśapūrvakaśca svayamanumeyārthapratyaya iti tathaiva pare bodhyante /
tathā ca parāmarśajñānahetorupanayasya siddhamarthavattvam /
na ca yathā liṅgaparāmarśajñānānvayavyatirekānuvidhānam anumeyajñānasya, tathā dadhibhakṣaṇādyanuvidhānamapi, yenatiprasaṅgaścodyeteti /
prayojanāntaram upanayasyāha---sādhye vā saṃbhava iti /
codayati---nanu ceti /
yadyapi sādhanatayā kṛtakatvamuktam, pratijñānantaraṃ pratipattra sādhanasyaivāpekṣitatvat, tathāpi tannāsiddhaṃ tatra sādhanatvena vyavatiṣṭhata iti svasiddhimākṣipati sāmarthyāditi bhāva /
pariharati---nokta iti /
yatparaḥ śabdaḥ sa śabdārtha iti śābdāḥ /
children.translated_text: What a word primarily conveys is the meaning of that word— so say the <s>Śābdas</s> (grammarian-philosophers) /
'Being produced' and the like primarily convey proving capacity— so by their own capacity [they serve as reasons] /
But if [the reason's proving capacity is] challenged, then the example too should not be employed /

children.text: asyāpi sādhanasāmarthyādākṣepāt avyāptasya sādhanatvāyogāt tadvidhasyāpi prameyatvādeḥ śabdanityatvādau sādhanatvabhrameṇa prayogo 'siddhepi tulya iti vyāptipradarśanārthodāharaṇaprayogavaddhetoḥ siddhatvapratipādanāya upanayasyapi prayoga iti ramaṇīyam //38 //
children.translated_text: Since this [example] too would be challenged by its proving capacity; and since what is not pervading cannot have proving force; and since even [a property] like <s>prameyatva</s> (knowability) of this type could be erroneously employed as a proof for the eternality of sound despite being unestablished as a proof— therefore, just as the example is employed for the purpose of showing the concomitance, the application too is employed for the purpose of demonstrating the establishment [of the reason in the subject]— this is elegant //38//

Here some say that the application is not a component of the proof, since the <s>sādhya</s> is established from the very statement of the reason accompanied by the example /
To refute that, the <s>vārttikakāra</s> says— 'just as, so' is for the purpose of mirroring /
This he analyzes, preceded by a question— 'what then?' /
By this, since the cognition of others, being learned or unlearned, is not fixed, others must be instructed in accordance with one's own cognition /
And one's own cognition of the inferable object is preceded by the apprehensive cognition of the inferential mark arising after the recollection of the concomitance— and thus others are instructed in the same way /
And thus the purposefulness of the application, which is the cause of the apprehensive cognition of the reason, is established /
And it is not the case that just as the cognition of the inferable follows the apprehensive cognition of the mark, so too it follows the eating of yogurt and the like— so the objection of overextension cannot be raised /
He states another purpose of the application— 'or the possibility in the <s>sādhya</s>' /
He objects— 'but is it not' /
Even though 'being produced' has been stated as a proving reason, since after the proposition the hearer expects the proof alone, nevertheless it is not established that it functions as a proving reason there— so by its own capacity it challenges its own establishment— this is the purport /
He resolves— 'it has been said that not' /
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.39: The conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>) is the restatement of the proposition after the statement of the reason //

children.text:
nigamanalakṣaṇāvatāraparaṃ bhāṣyaṃ dvividhasya punariti /
sādharmyeṇa vaidharmyeṇa dvividhānāmapi hetūdāharaṇopanayānāṃ samānaṃ nigamanalakṣaṇamityarthaḥ /
hetva---nam //39// tasmāditi /
hetvapadeśāt taddhetukam anityaḥ śabda iti pratijñāyā punarvacanam /
yadyapi ca siddhanirdeśo nigamanam, sādhyanirdeśaśca pratijñā, tathāpi yasyaiva pratijñāyāṃ sādhyatvamāsīt, tasyaiva nigamane siddhatvamityavasthāvantamekamāśritya samānaviṣayatayā nigamanaṃ pratijñetyupacaryate /
tathā ca punarvacanamapyupapannam /
tadetad bhāṣyakāro vyācaṣṭe---sādharmyokta iti /
vyutpādayati---nigamyante iti /
sādharmyavaidharmyayoḥ pratijñātaḥ prabhṛti nigamanāntaṃ prayogamāha---tatreti /
atra prathamasūtravadeva yathāsvamavayaveṣu pramāṇānāṃ paramanyāyaṃ stotuṃ saṃbhavamāha---avayavasamudāye ceti /
āptopadeśasyeti /
sedava somyedamagra āsīt /
ityāderāptopadeśasya pratyakṣānumānābhyāṃ pratisandhānāt /
nanu kasmāt pratijñaivāptopadeśo na bhavati, kṛtamasyā āgamāntaraviṣayatvenetyata āha---anṛṣeśceti /
anumānaṃ hetuḥ /
syādetat /
dvitīyaṃ liṅgadarśanaṃ hetuḥ /

children.translated_text: And that is not inference /
Since the third [observation]— the observation of the mark that is the content of the application— is of such a nature, therefore he says— 'the example' /
In the example, in the example-subject /

children.text: sādhyasādhanayoḥ pratibandhaṃ saṃdṛśya samyag dṛṣṭvā liṅgasya pratīteḥ //
children.translated_text: Having seen, i.e., properly observed, the invariable connection of the <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s> [in the example], the cognition of the mark [follows] //

The <s>bhāṣya</s> introducing the definition of the conclusion is 'of the twofold, again' /
The meaning is: the definition of the conclusion is the same for both kinds of reasons, examples, and applications— by similarity and by dissimilarity /
'Reason... conclusion' //39// 'Therefore' /
After the statement of the reason, the restatement of the proposition 'sound is non-eternal' /
And although the conclusion is a statement of what has been established, and the proposition is a statement of what is to be established, nevertheless since it is the very same thing that had the status of being-to-be-proved in the proposition that has the status of being-established in the conclusion— based on the single entity occupying [successive] states, the conclusion is figuratively called 'proposition' due to having the same content /
And thus the 'restatement' is also justified /
This the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> explains— 'stated by similarity' /
He explains— 'are concluded' /
He gives the full formulation from proposition through conclusion for both similarity and dissimilarity— 'therein' /
Here, just as in the first <s>sūtra</s>, he states the possibility of praising the supreme <s>nyāya</s> of <s>pramāṇas</s> in their respective members— 'and in the collection of members' /
'Of the instruction of a trustworthy person' /
'In the beginning, dear one, this was Being alone' /
— the instruction of a trustworthy person is linked with perception and inference /
Now, why should not the proposition itself be the instruction of a trustworthy person? Since it serves the purpose of being about other scriptural [authorities]— therefore he says— 'and of one who is not a sage' /
Inference is the reason /
It might be objected: the second observation of the mark is the reason /

children.text:
etaduktaṃ bhavati---yadyapi trayāṇāmapi liṅgadarśanānāṃ sasmṛtīnāmanumānatvam, tathāpi tadekadeśe madhyame 'pi liṅgadarśane samudāyopacārādanumānavyapadeśa iti /
pratyakṣaviṣayam udāharaṇam /
kasmāt? dṛṣṭena udāharaṇe pratibandhena adṛṣṭasya sādhyadharmiṇyanumeyasya siddheḥ /
yadi punarna mūlaṃ pratyakṣamāsthīyeta, avyavasthayā nādṛṣṭaṃ sidhyediti bhāvaḥ /
nigamaprayojanaṃ pratipādayati---sarveṣāmiti /
pratijñādīnāmupanayāntānāmeko 'rthaḥ svabhāvapratibaddhaṃ liṅgaṃ vā anumeyaṃ vā, tasya pratipattiḥ, tasyāṃ sāmarthyapradarśanaṃ nigamanamiti /

children.translated_text: By this, the unity of purpose has been shown /
And the purpose is twofold /
Of those, the subordinate one is the cognition of the mark connected with its own nature /
And the supreme one is the cognition of the <s>sādhya</s> //

This is what has been stated: although all three observations of the mark together with their recollections have the nature of inference, nevertheless even in a part of that— in the middle observation of the mark— the designation 'inference' is applied by figurative extension from the whole /
The example is the domain of perception /
Why? Because through the invariable connection perceived in the example, what is unseen— the inferable in the <s>sādhya</s>-subject— is established /
For if the root perception were not relied upon, what is unseen could not be established due to lack of grounding— this is the purport /
He teaches the purpose of the conclusion— 'of all' /
The single meaning of the proposition through the application is either the mark connected with its own nature, or the inferable [object]; its cognition; the demonstration of capacity for that [cognition]— that is the conclusion /

children.text:
saṃprati vibhāge sākāṅkṣatvaṃ darśayati---itaretarābhisaṃbandha iti /
abhisaṃbandhena phalenākāṅkṣāmupalakṣayati---asatyāmiti /
pradhānaṃ hi pratijñāpadam /
taduttarakālaṃ hi sādhanākāṅkṣāyāṃ pratijñāmāśritya hetupadaṃ pravartate /
na punaḥ prathamameva hetvepekṣeti hetulakṣaṇe 'smābhirupapāditamiti /
hetupadavirahe ākāṅkṣāṃ darśayati---asati hetāviti /
udāharaṇābhāve 'pekṣāmāha---asatyudāharaṇa iti /
upanayābhāve 'pyapekṣāmāha---upanayaṃ cāntareṇeti /
nigamanābhāve 'pyapekṣāmāha---nigamanābhāve ceti /
avayavānāṃ prātisvikaṃ prayojanamuktamapi śiṣyahitatayā bhāṣyakāraḥ pratipādayati---atheti /
children.translated_text: Even though the individual purpose of each member has been stated, the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s>, for the benefit of the student, explains it [again]— 'now' /
He shows the purpose of the effort to teach the five members— 'and for this there is no' /
How then does the process begin?— he says— 'even without being established' /

children.text: vyavasthāpite tu na jāteravasara ityāha---vyavasthite hīti //
children.translated_text: But when [the matter] has been established, there is no occasion for objection— he says— 'for when established' //

Now he shows the mutual expectancy in the division— 'mutual connection' /
He indicates the expectancy through the result of the connection— 'when absent' /
For the proposition-term is the primary one /
For subsequently, when there is expectancy of the proof, the reason-term operates based on the proposition /
But it is not the case that the reason is expected first— as we have established in the definition of the reason /
He shows the expectancy when the reason-term is absent— 'when the reason is absent' /
He states the expectancy when the example is absent— 'when the example is absent' /
He states the expectancy even when the application is absent— 'and without the application' /
He states the expectancy even when the conclusion is absent— 'and when the conclusion is absent' /

children.text:
atra kecit āhuḥ nigamanamasādhanāṅgam /
katham? pratijñayā gatārthatvāditi /
tanmatam apākartuṃ vārttikakāraḥ saprayojanaṃ nigamanaṃ darśayati---pratijñāviṣayasyārthasyeti /
caturbhiḥ khalvavayavairhetostrīṇi rūpāṇi dve vā pratipādite, na tvabādhitaviṣayatvāsatpratipakṣitatve /
pañcasaṃ vā caturṣu vā rūpeṣu hetoravinābhāvaḥ parisamāpyate /
tasmādabādhitaviṣayatvāsatpratipakṣitatvarūpadvayasaṃsūcanāya nigamanam /
tadidamuktam---viparītaprasaṅgapratiṣedhārthamiti /
bādhane pratipakṣe vā sādhyaviparītaprasaṅgaḥ syāditi /
so 'yaṃ pratijñāviṣayārthasya aśeṣapramāṇamūlāvayavopapattau satyāṃ pratijñeyasyārthasya siddhatayā punarvacanena nigamanena pratiṣidhyate /
na ca pratijñāvacanādeva tatsiddhiḥ, tasya sādhyaparatvāt /
na cānyaparādapyākṣepāt siddhiḥ hetvādipadāprayogavaiyarthyaprasaṅgāt, pratijñāta eva sarvākṣepasaṃbhavāt /

children.translated_text: Therefore, the conclusion serves to demonstrate the two forms /

children.text: yathā ca trairūpyātiriktametadrūpadvayaṃ tathopapāditam asmābhiḥ prathamasūtre /
children.translated_text: And how these two forms are beyond the threefold nature [of the reason]— that has been established by us in the first <s>sūtra</s> /
And the rest will be shown in the section on pseudo-reasons /

children.text: etasmin sūtrārthe parasya pratijñāyāṃ nigamanaṃ gatārthaṃ manyamānasya avakāśo nāstīti //
children.translated_text: In this meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>, there is no room for the opponent who considers the conclusion redundant with the proposition //

Here some say the conclusion is not a component of proof, because its meaning is already obtained from the proposition /
To refute their view, the <s>vārttikakāra</s> shows the conclusion has a purpose— 'of the object that is the content of the proposition' /
By the four members, three forms of the reason— or two— have been demonstrated, but not the property of having an uncontradicted subject and of not having a valid counter-argument /
The inseparability (<s>avinābhāva</s>) of the reason is completed in the fifth form— or in four forms /
Therefore, the conclusion serves to indicate the two forms of having an uncontradicted subject and not having a valid counter-argument /
This is what was stated— 'for the purpose of negating the unwanted consequence of the opposite' /
In the case of contradiction or counter-argument, there would be the unwanted consequence of the opposite of the <s>sādhya</s> /
This [negation]— when the object of the proposition-content, having all its members grounded in <s>pramāṇa</s>, has been fully established— the established status of the proposition-object is restated by the conclusion, [thereby] negating [the opposite] /
And the establishment of that is not from the proposition-statement alone, since that [proposition] has the purpose of [stating] what is to be proved /
Nor is the establishment from implied grasping from other [members], since there would be the unwanted consequence of the pointlessness of employing the reason-terms etc., because all grasping would be possible from the proposition alone /

children.text:
yastu manyeta na hetoravinābhāvasiddhimantareṇa siddhanirdeśo nigamanaṃ bhavati, na ca pāñcarūpyaṃ vinā avinābhāvasiddhiḥ /
nigamanāttu tatsiddhau na siddhanirdeśo nigamanam, api tu tadapi sādhyanirdeśa eveti, taṃ pratyupetya taddoṣanirācikīrṣayā pareṣāṃ vākyamupakṣipyate /
pareṣāṃ vākyaṃ paṭhati---upanayanigamane tviti /
dūṣayati---idaṃ tāvaditi /
yathāśruti hi nigamanopanayayorabhedaṃ sādhayati, arthagataṃ cāviśeṣaṃ hetumāha---taccaitadālokatamasoraikyaṃ kākasya kārṣyādivadāpatitam /
śaṅkate---atha hetūpanayāviti /
upalakṣaṇa caitat, pratijñānigamane ityapi draṣṭavyam /
arthāviśeṣāditi cāviśiṣṭārthatvādityunnetavyam /
tathā ca saṃbandha iti śaṅkiturabhiprāyaḥ /
atrāpi doṣamāha---sa vipakṣeti /
punaḥ śaṅkate---athaikaprayojanatveneti /
nirākaroti---tathāpīti /
sidhyatyekaprayojanatve sādhye hetoravirodhaḥ, hetustu na pratijñārthādatiticyate ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the <s>sādhya</s> of having a single purpose is established, there is no contradiction of the reason; but the reason does not exceed the content of the proposition— this is the meaning /
That has been described /
The meaning of the reason is one thing, and the meaning of the application is another— this has been described— this is the meaning /

children.text: etenopanayanigamanaprayojanābhidhānena ye tryavayavaṃ vākyamāhuḥ, tanmatamapi parāstamityāha---pakṣadharmatveti //
children.translated_text: By this explanation of the purpose of the application and conclusion, the view of those who advocate a three-membered statement is also rejected— he says— 'the property of being a property of the subject' //

But if one thinks that the conclusion as a statement of what is established does not occur without the establishment of the inseparability of the reason, and that the inseparability is not established without the five forms— and therefore in the conclusion, since that [inseparability] has been established, it is not a statement of what is established but rather still a statement of what is to be proved— against him, having taken up the position, [the author] introduces the opponents' statement with the intention of showing its fault /
He reads the opponents' statement— 'but the application and conclusion' /
He refutes— 'this is first' /
For according to the literal reading, he establishes the non-difference of the conclusion and the application, and states the objection based on lack of distinction in meaning— 'and this is like the unity of light and darkness with the blackness of the crow, which is absurd' /
He raises a doubt— 'now, the reason and the application' /
And this is illustrative; 'the proposition and the conclusion' should also be seen [here] /
And 'because of lack of distinction in meaning' should be extended as 'because of having undistinguished meaning' /
And thus 'connection'— this is the objector's intent /
Here too he states the fault— 'that with the dissimilar instance' /
Again he raises a doubt— 'now, because of having a single purpose' /
He refutes— 'even so' /

children.text:
yacca paraiḥ upanaye dūṣaṇaṃ vikalpyābhyadhāyi tat tāvadupanyasyati---yadapi yathā tatheti /
sarvasāmānyayoge hi tadeva syāt, na tu tatheti /
anyathā śabdasya kṛtakatvāditi /
na hi yathā ghaṭaḥ kṛtakaḥ, tathā śabdo 'pi kṛtakaḥ, ghaṭaśabdayorabhedaprasaṅgādityarthaḥ /
tasmāt sāmānyapratiṣedhe viśeṣapratiṣedhe ca kṛtakatvaṃ sāmānyaṃ pariśiṣyate /
tasya ca yathātathābhāvayorabhāvāt kṛtakatvādityeva syāt /
tathā ca na hetorvyatireka upanayaḥ syādityāha---pariśeṣāditi /
tadetat pareṣāṃ dūṣaṇaṃ nirākaroti---tadapyayuktamiti /
yathā tatheti vākyamupamānaikadeśamupamānamupacārāt /
upamānamartho yasya so 'yamupamānārtha upanayaḥ /
tasya bhāvastattvaṃ tasmāt /
taccopamānaṃ na sarvathā sādhyasādhanabhāvamāśritya pravartate /
sādhye śabde sādhanasya kṛtakatvasya sthālīgatasya yaḥ sarvathābhāvaḥ sthālītvādyekārthasamavāyaḥ tamāśritya na pravartate /
tathā ca śabdasthālyoḥ abhedaprasaṅgād yathā tathetyeva na syāt /

children.translated_text: Therefore, the meaning is: by excluding the other modes residing in the pot, the justification of comparison through the commonality of mere universal of being-produced [applies] — that is the meaning of 'as-so.'

children.text: nanvevamapi kṛtakatvasāmānyamātraṃ śabde syāt, na tu yathā tathābhāvaḥ, tathā ca na hetoratireka ityuktamityata āha---kṛtakatvasāmānyaṃ tviti /
children.translated_text: But even so, there would be only the mere universal of being-produced in sound, not the 'as-so' relation; and thus it has been said that there is no negative concomitance of the reason — therefore he says — 'but the universal of being-produced' etc.

children.text: na hi jātu śāvaleyasannidhau gotvasāmānyamātraṃ bhavati, api tu viśeṣasahitam /
children.translated_text: For never in the proximity of a dog does the mere universal of cow-hood exist, but rather [it exists] accompanied by a particular.
And thus the 'as-so' relation is justified — this is the meaning. //

And the objection that was raised by opponents regarding the application (<s>upanaya</s>) through an alternative — he first presents that — 'even if, as-so' etc. / For if there were a connection with the universal in every respect, it would be just that, not 'as-so.' / Otherwise [it would be]: 'sound is produced, therefore...' / For it is not the case that just as a pot is produced, so too sound is produced, since there would be the unwanted consequence of non-difference between pot and sound — this is the meaning. / Therefore, when both the universal and the particular are negated, the universal of being-produced remains as a residue. / And since neither the 'as' nor the 'so' relation applies to that [mere universal], it would be just 'because of being produced.' / And thus there would be no application involving the negative concomitance of the reason — thus he says — 'by the method of residue' etc. / He refutes this objection of the opponents — 'that too is unjustified' etc. / The sentence 'as-so' is a partial component of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>), and by figurative extension is [itself called] comparison. / The application (<s>upanaya</s>) is that whose purpose is comparison — it is the comparison-purposed application. / Its being is its reality — therefore [it functions through comparison]. / And that comparison does not operate by relying on the relation of <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved) and <s>sādhana</s> (the means of proof) in every respect. / It does not operate by relying on the complete absence — the co-inherence with a single meaning such as pot-hood and the like — of the property of being-produced that resides in the pot, which is the means, with respect to sound, which is what is to be proved. / And thus, because of the unwanted consequence of non-difference between sound and pot, 'as-so' would indeed not apply.

children.text:
etena yat parairupanayasya dṛṣṭāntādabhinnatvaṃ varṇitam, tadapi parāstamityāha---gatārthatvāditi /
anenopamānasamānatvavarṇanena /
etadeva vibhajate---yadapyuktamiti /
vyāptipradarśanaviṣayo dṛṣṭāntaḥ dṛṣṭāvyāptikasya hetoḥ sādhyadharmiṇyupasaṃhāra upanaya iti mahān bheda ityarthaḥ /
etena nigamanaṃ pratijñāyāḥ samānābhidheyatve 'pi pratijñārthatvena pratyuktam, pratijñāyāḥ sādhyaparatvāt nigamanasya ca viparītaśaṅkānivṛttiparatvāditi /
prayojanabhedasāmānyamātravivakṣayā etenetyuktam /
atra bhāṣyakāreṇa ekasminnanvayavyatirekiṇyeva vītāvītavākye pañcāvayave udāhṛte /
tatra kadācid bhrāntiḥ syādekodāharaṇatayā dve api vākye parasparāpekṣe eveti, tannirākaraṇāyāha---te ete iti /
na punaranvayi vyatireki cetyekaṃ vākyamityarthaḥ//39 //
children.translated_text: By this, the description by opponents of the non-difference of the application from the example has also been set aside — thus he says — 'because the purpose has been fulfilled' etc. / By this description of similarity with comparison. / He further elaborates this — 'even if it is said' etc. / The example is concerned with showing pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>); the application is the subsumption of the reason, whose pervasion has been observed, under the subject of the thesis — so there is a great difference — this is the meaning. / By this, the conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>) too, though having the same denotation as the thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>), has been answered as having the nature of the thesis — since the thesis is directed toward what is to be proved, while the conclusion is directed toward removing the suspicion of the contrary. / The word 'by this' is used with the intention of [indicating] merely the commonality of difference in purpose. / Here the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> has illustrated the five members in a single positive-and-negative-concomitant statement. / There, a confusion might arise that because of being a single illustration, both the positive and negative statements are mutually dependent — to remove that he says — 'these very' etc. / The meaning is: the positive-concomitant and the negative-concomitant are not one single statement. // 39 //

<s>NyS</s> 1.1.40: <s>Tarka</s> (hypothetical reasoning) is deliberation (<s>ūha</s>) for the purpose of knowing the truth of an object whose truth has not been ascertained, [conducted] on the basis of the justification of a cause. //

children.text:
atra bhāṣyaṃ tarkalakṣaṇāvatāraparam---ata ūrdhvamiti /
uddeśakramānusāreṇa /
avitarkaḥ /
//40// tarkapravṛttikramamāha---avijñāyamānatattve 'rthe iti yadyapi saṃśayasya paścādeva jijñāsā bhavati, tathāpi jijñāsāyāḥ parastādapi saṃśayo bhavati /
sa cātra vivakṣitaḥ, tarkapravṛttyaṅgatvāt /
tarkeṇa hi prasaṅgāparanāmnā dvayoḥ pakṣayorekataraniṣedhenaikataraḥ pramāṇaviṣayatayā abhyanujñātavya iti viṣayapratyāsattyā tarkapravṛttiṃ pratyaṅgatā saṃśayasyeti /
kāraṇopapattyeti vyācaṣṭe---saṃbhavatyasmin kāraṇaṃ pramāṇamiti /
atra ca kāraṇamityasya vyākhyānaṃ pramāṇamiti /
upapattivyākhyānaṃ saṃbhavatīti /
anujñāvyākhyānam /
---evavametat, netaraditi /
etaduktaṃ bhavati, yasmin viṣaye pramāṇaṃ pravartitumudyataṃ tadviparyayāśaṅkāyāṃ na tāvat pramāṇaṃ pravartate, na yāvadaniṣṭyāpattyā viparyayāśaṅkā apanīyate /
tadapanaya eva ca svaviṣaye pramāṇasaṃbhava iti copapattiriti vyākhyāyate /
tayā pramāṇasyopapattyā itikartavyatayā pramāṇaviṣayamabhyanujānatyā viśodhite viṣaye pramāṇāmapratyūhaṃ pravartate /
children.translated_text: When the domain has been purified by that justification of the <s>pramāṇa</s> — [serving] as its requisite condition — which sanctions the object of the <s>pramāṇa</s>, the <s>pramāṇa</s> operates without obstruction.

children.text: na copapattirevāstu niścayahetuḥ kṛtaṃ pramāṇeneti vaktavyam /
children.translated_text: And it should not be said that the justification alone should be the cause of ascertainment, making the <s>pramāṇa</s> unnecessary.
Because the justification, being independent [i.e., without support], cannot by itself produce ascertainment due to the unestablished-ness of its basis.
That has been demonstrated in the first <s>sūtra</s>. //

Here the <s>bhāṣya</s> introduces the definition of <s>tarka</s> — 'from here onwards' etc. / In accordance with the order of enumeration. / Non-reasoning. / //40// He states the procedure of the operation of <s>tarka</s> — 'regarding an object whose truth is not being ascertained' etc. Although the desire to know (<s>jijñāsā</s>) arises only after doubt, nevertheless doubt also arises after the desire to know. / And that [latter doubt] is what is intended here, since it serves as a component for the operation of <s>tarka</s>. / For by <s>tarka</s>, also called <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio), through the negation of one of two alternatives, the other is to be sanctioned as the object of <s>pramāṇa</s> — thus, through the proximity of the object, doubt serves as a component for the operation of <s>tarka</s>. / He explains 'on the basis of the justification of a cause' — 'in which the cause, i.e., the <s>pramāṇa</s>, occurs.' / And here, the explanation of 'cause' is '<s>pramāṇa</s>.' / The explanation of 'justification' (<s>upapatti</s>) is 'occurs' (<s>saṃbhavati</s>). / The explanation of 'sanction' (<s>anujñā</s>) — / 'It is thus, not otherwise.' / This is what has been stated: in the subject-matter in which a <s>pramāṇa</s> is about to operate, when there is a suspicion of the contrary, the <s>pramāṇa</s> does not operate until, by the consequence of an undesired result, the suspicion of the contrary is removed. / And that removal itself — [namely,] the occurrence of the <s>pramāṇa</s> in its own domain — is explained as the 'justification.' /

children.text: svakṛtasya karmaṇa ityādinā pūrvasya kāraṇamityantena saṃsāro darśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: By 'of one's own action' and so on, up to 'its cause,' <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) has been shown.
By 'the latter' and so on, up to '<s>apavarga</s>' (liberation), <s>apavarga</s> has been shown.

children.text: tena saṃsārāpavargāvicchantau vādiprativādinau prati ātmanityatvaviṣayaṃ pramāṇaṃ pravartamānamanena tarkeṇānugṛhyata iti pramāṇaviṣayaviparyayānanujñaiva ca pramāṇaviṣayābhyanujñā, aniṣṭaprasaktyā viparyayasyaiva sākṣāt nivartanāt /
children.translated_text: Thus, with respect to the two disputants who desire [respectively] <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>apavarga</s>, the <s>pramāṇa</s> operating on the subject of the permanence of the self is assisted by this <s>tarka</s>. And the non-sanctioning of the contrary of the object of <s>pramāṇa</s> is itself the sanctioning of the object of <s>pramāṇa</s>, since the contrary is directly negated through the consequence of an undesired result.

children.text: ata evānte bhāṣyakāra upasaṃjahāra---yatra kāraṇam anupapadyamānaṃ paśyati, tat nānujānātīti //
children.translated_text: For this very reason, the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> concludes at the end — 'where he sees a cause that is unjustified, that he does not sanction.' //
He gives an illustration — 'an example' etc.

children.text:
nanu yadi tarka evametat, netaradityevamākāraḥ, kathaṃ punarayaṃ tattvajñānārtho na tu tattvajñānameveteti deśayati---kathaṃ punariti /
pariharati---anavadhāraṇāditi /
paryāyairniścayādatyantabheda uktaḥ /
bhāvitāt cintitāt, ata eva prasannāt nirmalānditi /

children.translated_text: 'By the power of the <s>pramāṇa</s>' — this removes the independence of <s>tarka</s>.

children.text: syādetat---yadi na tarkastattvaniścayasādhanamapi tu pramāṇameva, hanta bhoḥ kimarthaṃ tarhi vāde pramāṇatarkasādhanetyuktamityata āha---so 'yaṃ tarka iti /
children.translated_text: One might say: if <s>tarka</s> is not the means of establishing truth but <s>pramāṇa</s> alone is, then why is it said in [the definition of] debate (<s>vāda</s>) that '<s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s> are the means of proof'? — therefore he says — 'this <s>tarka</s>' etc.
'<s>Pramāṇas</s>' — with the intention of [referring to] particular instances.
The meaning is: [<s>tarka</s>] reconnects the <s>pramāṇas</s> that have been disrupted by the suspicion of the contrary of the object of <s>pramāṇa</s>. //

Now, if <s>tarka</s> has the form 'it is thus, not otherwise,' then how is this for the purpose of knowing the truth and not itself the knowledge of truth? — he teaches — 'how then?' / He resolves — 'because of non-determination' etc. / By synonyms, the absolute difference from ascertainment (<s>niścaya</s>) has been stated. / 'From what is contemplated' means 'from what is reflected upon'; for that very reason, 'from what is clear' means 'from what is pure.' /

children.text:
vārttikakāraḥ /
sūtratātparyamāha---asyeti /
samānajātīyāt saṃśayāderasamānajātīyāt cecchādervyavacchidyate /
yadyapi saṃśayajijñāse apyavijñātatattve 'rthe pravartete, tathāpi na kāraṇopapattita iti tayorvyavaccheda iti /
tattvaṃ vyācaṣṭe---yatheti /
samānāsamānajātīyavyavacchinnamaviparītaṃ rūpaṃ tattvamityarthaḥ /
codayati---kutaḥ punariti /
na hi sāmānyajñānavidhāyakaṃ padamatrāstītyarthaḥ /
pariharati---avijñāteti /
viśeṣaniṣedhaḥ śeṣābhyanujñāheturityarthaḥ /
vimṛśati---avijñātatattva iti samāso 'yamiti /
avadhārayati---ṣaṣṭhīvigraheṇeti /
yuktam upapannam /
tṛtīyāvigraheṇa tvunapapannamityarthaḥ /
saṃśayavādyāha---viśeṣahetvabhāvāditi /
yuktamiti pratijñāmātreṇocyate, na tvatra hetuḥ abhidhīyata iti bhāvaḥ /
yuktatve hetumāha---yuktamarthagrahaṇasāmarthyāditi /
anyaścodayati---arthagrahaṇamantareṇāpīti /
jñeyena hi jñānaṃ nirūpyate na jñātrā, tasya sādhāraṇyāditi sāmarthyamityarthaḥ /
nigūḍhābhisandhiḥ pariharati---evamapīti /
tasyābhisandhibhedamurarīkṛtya codayati---mā bhūt samāsa iti /

children.translated_text: The respondent says — 'it is so indeed' etc.

children.text: nādyāpi anena svābhiprāyo darśita iti mattvā punaścodayati---anukte 'pīti /
children.translated_text: Thinking that even now he has not revealed his own intention, [the opponent] objects again — 'even if not stated' etc.

Having prefaced with the previously stated resolution, he reveals his own intention — 'here it has been stated' etc. — 'because of the unwanted consequence of not expressing the whole' — this is the revelation of the intention.

children.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati, sāmarthyaprāptasyānabhidhāne 'tiprasaṅga iti na sāmarthyamāśritya lakṣaṇe saṃśayo nirākaraṇīya iti tannirākaraṇārthamarthagrahaṇaṃ kartavyamiti //
children.translated_text: This is what has been stated: if there is non-expression of what is obtained by capacity, there would be over-extension; therefore doubt regarding the definition should not be removed by relying on capacity; rather, the mention of 'object' (<s>artha</s>) should be made for the purpose of removing that [doubt]. //

The <s>vārttikakāra</s>: / He states the purport of the <s>sūtra</s> — 'of this' etc. / [<s>Tarka</s>] is differentiated from doubt and the like, which are of the same type, and from desire and the like, which are of a different type. / Although doubt and the desire to know also operate regarding an object whose truth has not been ascertained, nevertheless they do not [operate] on the basis of the justification of a cause — so the differentiation from them [is maintained]. / He explains 'truth' (<s>tattva</s>) — 'as' etc. / The meaning is: truth is the non-erroneous form that is differentiated from what is of the same and different types. / He objects — 'from what then?' etc. / The meaning is: there is no word here that prescribes a general [kind of] knowledge. / He resolves — 'not ascertained' etc. / The negation of the specific [i.e., 'not ascertained'] is the reason for the implicit sanction of the remainder — this is the meaning. / He deliberates — 'not-ascertained-truth — this compound' etc. / He determines — 'by the sixth-case [genitive] resolution' etc. / 'Justified' means proper. / But by the third-case [instrumental] resolution, it is not proper — this is the meaning. / The advocate of doubt says — 'because of the absence of a specific reason' etc. / 'Justified' is said by mere assertion, but no reason is stated here — this is the purport. / He gives the reason for its being justified — 'justified, because of the capacity of the word artha (object)' etc. / Another objects — 'even without the mention of artha' etc. / For cognition is determined by the object, not by the cognizer, since the cognizer is common — so 'capacity' means this — this is the meaning. / The one with a hidden intention resolves — 'even so' etc. / The one who does not accept his [hidden] intention objects — 'let there not be a compound' etc.

children.text:
atra codayati---avijñātatatva iti na vaktavyamiti /
na hi tattve jñāte tattvajñānārthitā bhavati /
tasmād gamyate avijñātatattva iti bhāvaḥ /
guḍhābhisandhiruktaṃ parihāraṃ smārayati---atra tāvaduktamiti /
aviditābhiprāyaścodaka āha---mā bhūditi /
astūhastarka ityetāvadevetyarthaḥ /
uttaravādī svābhiprāyamudghāṭayati-na buddhirdheti /
yadyapi nāsmākaṃ rāddhānte śuśrūṣādayo buddhidharmā buddhitattvasyaivābhāvāt, tathāpyātmaguṇā api sāṃkhyābhiprāyeṇa buddhiguṇā uktāḥ /
etaduktaṃ bhavati, yadyūhastarka ityetāvaducyeta, yadi vā tattvajñānārthamūhastarka ityetāvanmātram, tato vijñāte 'pi tattve ya ūhaḥ pūrvānubhūtaparicchedātmā jāyate punastattvajñānārthaṃ so 'pi tarkaḥ syāt /
tasmāt avijñātatattva iti vaktavyamityarthaḥ /
yadyapi kāraṇopapattita ityetasmādayamartho 'pi gamyata eva, tathāpi kāraṇopapatterevaivaṃrūpatvaṃ nāvijñātatattvagrahaṇamantareṇa bhavati /
tathā hi adhigataparicchedātmāpyūhaḥ kāraṇasyopapattyā saṃbhavena jāyate, kāraṇasaṃbhave kāryasya abhāvāt /

children.translated_text: But that [deliberation about what is already known] does not [concern] an object whose truth is not ascertained — so the differentiation from it [is achieved].

children.text: tathā ca sati pramāṇamapi tarkaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: And that being the case, even <s>pramāṇa</s> would be <s>tarka</s> [without this qualification].
Therefore it is said 'on the basis of the justification of a cause.'

children.text: ukte sati prayojanānusaraṇam, na tviha lāghavādaraḥ sūtrakārasyeti mantavyam //
children.translated_text: When [the term] has been stated, [the sūtrakāra] follows the purpose [of each word]; it should not be thought that the <s>sūtrakāra</s> does not value brevity here. //

Here he objects — 'not-ascertained-truth need not be stated.' / For when the truth has been known, there is no desire for knowledge of truth. / Therefore it is understood [implicitly] that [the object is one whose truth is] not ascertained — this is the purport. / The one with hidden intention reminds [him] of the previously stated resolution — 'here, to begin with, it was stated' etc. / The objector, not understanding the intention, says — 'let it not be' etc. / The meaning is: let deliberation (<s>ūha</s>) be <s>tarka</s> — just this much alone. / The respondent reveals his own intention — 'not a property of intellect' etc. / Although in our established doctrine, desire to learn (<s>śuśrūṣā</s>) and the like are not properties of intellect, since intellect as a reality does not exist [in <s>Nyāya</s>], nevertheless, qualities of the self (<s>ātman</s>) are also called properties of intellect in the sense of the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> view. / This is what has been stated: if only 'deliberation is <s>tarka</s>' — this much were said, or if only 'deliberation for the purpose of knowing truth is <s>tarka</s>' — this much alone [were said], then even the deliberation that arises regarding an object whose truth has already been ascertained, which has the nature of the apprehension of what was previously experienced, would also be <s>tarka</s>. / Therefore 'not-ascertained-truth' should be stated — this is the meaning. / Although this meaning is also understood from 'on the basis of the justification of a cause,' nevertheless, the very nature of the justification of a cause cannot be [properly understood] without the mention of 'not-ascertained-truth.' / For even deliberation whose truth has been ascertained arises through the occurrence, i.e., the possibility, of a cause, since in the absence of the possibility of a cause, the effect is absent.

children.text:
codayati---ṣaṣṭhyabhidhānamiti /
pariharati---na vibhaktivyatyayāditi /
yathānyatra kaṇabhujaḥ sūtre /
vipratipannaḥ pṛcchati---kasmāt? praṣṭaivaikagranthenāha---yadi vyatyayeneti /

children.translated_text: He resolves — 'it is not unjustified' etc.
For the purpose of making known through the specific what has been understood in general.

children.text: nityatvādayo viśeṣāḥ samavāyino vahnyādayaśca dhūmādisaṃyogina iti /
children.translated_text: The specifics are permanence and the like, which are inherent, and fire and the like, which are in conjunction through smoke and the like.
The rest is easy to understand. //

He objects — 'the expression in the sixth case [genitive]' etc. / He resolves — 'no, because of interchange of case-endings' etc. / As elsewhere in the <s>sūtra</s> of <s>Kaṇabhuj</s> (Kaṇāda). / The perplexed [interlocutor] asks — 'why?' The very questioner says in a single passage — 'if by interchange' etc.

children.text:
deśayati---ūhaḥ saṃśayanirṇayābhyāmiti /
kecit siddhāntaikadeśinaḥ anumānaṃ tarka ityāhuḥ /
anye tvanumānameva yuktyapekṣaṃ viparyaye 'niṣṭaprasaṅgāpekṣaṃ tarka iti varṇayanti /
tatra prathamaṃ codakaṃ pratyāha---yat tāvaditi /
ākṣipta ākṣiptahṛdayaḥ, na tu tarkapratyayasvarūpaṃ cetayata ityarthaḥ /
viśeṣadarśanāditi viśeṣadarśanāt niścayaḥ pramāṇena bhavati na tarkeṇa, tadanujñānamātratvāt tarkasyetyarthaḥ /
codakaṃ nirākṛtya siddhāntaikadeśinaṃ nirākaroti---eteneti /
yadi saṃśayāt pracyuto nirṇayaṃ cāprāptaḥ, tarhi tasya svarūpaṃ vaktavyamiti pṛcchati---kiṃ punariti /
uttaram---bhavediti, pramāṇaviṣayābhyanujñetyarthaḥ /
dvitīyamekadeśinaṃ nirākaroti---yairapīti /
yuktiriha pramāṇopapattiḥ /
tajjanmā ca pratyayastarka eva /
sa cānumānamiti tvayocyate /
asmābhistu tarka iti saṃjñābhedamātramityarthaḥ /
śaṅkate---atheti /

children.translated_text: He refutes — "inference" etc.
Since no reasoning beyond <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) and <s>upapatti</s> (demonstration) can be determined, the object of dependence must be stated.
For dependence cannot be determined without that upon which something depends — this is the purport.

children.text: nanu yadeva kiścit svaviṣayādhigame anumānamapekṣate saivāpekṣaṇīyā yuktiranumānasya bhaviṣyatītyata āha---svaviṣayadhigame ceti //
children.translated_text: But whatever inference depends upon for the apprehension of its own object, that very thing will be the reasoning upon which inference depends — to this he says: "and in the apprehension of its own object" etc.

He teaches — "<s>Ūha</s> (reasoning) is distinct from both doubt and determination."
Some partial adherents of the established doctrine say that inference (<s>anumāna</s>) is <s>tarka</s> (reasoning).
Others, however, describe <s>tarka</s> as inference itself that depends on reasoning, i.e., that depends on the consequence of an undesirable result in case of the contrary.
Among these, he first responds to the objector — "as for that" etc.
"Disturbed" means disturbed in mind, but not one who cognizes the true nature of the conviction produced by <s>tarka</s> — this is the meaning.
"From the perception of a distinguishing feature" — determination arises through a <s>pramāṇa</s> from the perception of a distinguishing feature, not through <s>tarka</s>, since <s>tarka</s> merely grants permission [to the <s>pramāṇa</s>] — this is the meaning.
Having refuted the objector, he refutes the partial adherent — "by this" etc.
If [<s>tarka</s>] has departed from doubt and not yet reached determination, then its own nature must be stated — he asks: "what then?" etc.
The answer — "it would be" — meaning: permission [granted] to the domain of <s>pramāṇa</s>.
He refutes the second partial adherent — "even by those" etc.
"Reasoning" (<s>yukti</s>) here means the applicability of <s>pramāṇa</s>.
And the cognition born of that is <s>tarka</s> itself.
And you call that inference.
But we [call it] <s>tarka</s> — the difference is merely one of terminology — this is the meaning.
He raises a doubt — "then" etc.

children.text:
śaṅkate---atheti /
nirākaroti---evamapīti /
yadyutpattau pratyakṣāgamāpekṣam anumānam, na vaktavyaṃ yuktyapekṣamiti, sarvasyānumānasya tathābhāvenāvyabhicāreṇa viśeṣaṇāyogāditi bhāvaḥ /
punaḥ śaṅkate---athānumānasyeti /
nirākaroti---tatrāpīti /
evamapi tarko nārthāntaraṃ sthāt /
anumānabhedasya cedṛśasya pramāṇa evāntarbhāva iti bhāvaḥ /
uktamartha pramāṇayati---bhavediti /
bhaveditipratyayo 'vadhāraṇapratyayaścetyarthaḥ /
codayati---anumānamiti /
viparyayo 'niṣṭaprasaṅgo vyatireki liṅgam /
taccāgṛhītasaṃbandhe liṅgiti na pravartata iti liṅgaliṅgisaṃbandhasmṛtyapekṣatvādaprāṇādimattvaprasaṅgāditivadanumānamevetyarthaḥ /
pariharati na tarketi /

yuktaṃ vyatirekiṇi jīvaccharīre dharmiṇi prāṇādimattvasya sādhanadharmasya darśanāt, na tu yadyutpattimān ātmā abhaviṣyat, na saṃsārāpavargāvupapatsyetāmityatrātmani dharmiṇi sādhanadharma utpattirasti yaddarśanataḥ saṃskārodbodhe sati liṅgaliṅgisaṃbandhasmṛtirbhavedityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: It is appropriate in the case of the negative concomitance (<s>vyatirekin</s>) [argument] where the property of the proof — possessing vital breath etc. — is seen in the property-bearer, namely, a living body. But in the [argument] "if the <s>ātman</s> were not born, <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>apavarga</s> would not be possible," there is no proof-property "birth" in the property-bearer, the <s>ātman</s>, the seeing of which would cause the recollection of the connection between the mark and the marked when the mental impression is awakened — this is the meaning.

children.text: na kevalaṃ prasaṅgasādhanaṃ sādhyadharmiṇyasiddham, api tvanyagatameva prasaṅgahetuḥ /
children.translated_text: Not only is the proof by reductio (<s>prasaṅga</s>) unestablished in the property-bearer of what is to be proved, but the reason for the reductio belongs to something else entirely.

children.text: na tvanumānamanyagatād dharmāt pravartate, tasmādanumānādasya sphuṭo bheda ityāha---anumānaṃ ceti /
children.translated_text: But inference does not proceed from a property belonging to something else; therefore the clear distinction of this [<s>tarka</s>] from inference — he says: "and inference" etc.
The explanation of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> is "this is that" etc. //40//

He raises a doubt — "then" etc.
He refutes — "even so" etc.
Even if inference depends on direct perception and testimony for its origination, one should not say it depends on reasoning, since the qualification would not apply because all inference is invariably of that nature — this is the purport.
He raises a doubt again — "but of inference" etc.
He refutes — "even there" etc.
Even so, <s>tarka</s> would not be something different.
If this were a variety of inference,
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.41: <s>Nirṇaya</s> (determination) is the ascertainment of a matter after deliberation upon the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) and the counter-thesis (<s>pratipakṣa</s>).
This is not merely the definition of determination in general, but of determination that has examination as its purpose.

children.text: sa ca nirṇayabhedo vimarśānantarotpannatarkasahāyapramāṇanibandhanastarkaviṣaya eveti nirṇayabhedalakṣaṇamiti nāvyāpakaṃ tatra tallakṣaṇamiti darśayituṃ bhāṣyakāro nirṇayalakṣaṇamavatārayati---etasmiśca tarkaviṣaye //
children.translated_text: And that particular type of determination — arising after deliberation, assisted by <s>tarka</s>, grounded in <s>pramāṇa</s>, and having <s>tarka</s> as its domain — is a specific type of determination. To show that this definition is not under-inclusive for that, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> introduces the definition of determination — "and in this domain of <s>tarka</s>" etc.

children.text:
vimṛ---yaḥ //42// atra pakṣapratipakṣayoḥ karmatayā na nirṇayasādhanatvamityanupapattyā sādhanopālambhau vādasūtragatau lakṣaṇīyaviti tāveva tāvad bhāṣyakṛd vibhajate---sthāpanā sādhanam, pratiṣedhaḥ sādhanasya upālambhaḥ /
lakṣaṇānibandhanaṃ saṃbandhamāha---tau sādhanopālambhāviti /
yadyapyupālambho na pratipakṣāśritaḥ, tathāpi taduddeśena pravṛttastadāśrita ityucyate /
mukhyapadopādānollaṅghanena lākṣaṇikapadopādānalabhyaṃ prayojanamāha---vyatiṣaktāviti /

children.translated_text: He states the requirement, obtainable through the force of the word "object" (<s>artha</s>), that [debate] culminates in the determination of one side — "proceeding with a continuation" etc.
And this will become clear in the <s>Vārttika</s>.
He shows precisely this mutual continuation of proof and criticism — "of one of those two" etc.

children.text: yasya sādhanasya vā upālambhasya vāvasthānam, tasya sādhanasya vā upālambhasya vā yo 'rthaḥ pakṣaḥ pratipakṣo vā tasyāvadhāraṇamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The determination of the object — whether thesis or counter-thesis — of that proof or criticism which is established, is the meaning.

Deliberation... determination //42// Here, since the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) and counter-thesis (<s>pratipakṣa</s>) cannot serve as means of determination in the objective sense [karman], the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> first classifies the proof (<s>sādhana</s>) and criticism (<s>upālambha</s>) that are to be defined in the <s>sūtras</s> on debate — "establishment is proof; refutation is the criticism of the proof."
He states the connection that is the basis of the definition — "those two, proof and criticism" etc.
Even though criticism

children.text:
atra pakṣapratipakṣaprayogād vāde saṃśayo 'stīti vādabhrāntyā codayati---nedamiti /
eka iti vādī /
pratijñātamarthaṃ hetutaḥ sthāpayati /
dvitīyasya prativādinaḥ pratiṣiddhaṃ pratiṣedhaṃ vādyuktasya hetordūṣaṇamiti yāvat /
uddharati dūṣaṇābhāsīkaroti /
dvitīyena tu prativādinā vādyuktasya hetoḥ sthāpanāhetutvaṃ pratiṣidhyate /
tasyaiva vādinaḥ prativādyuktadūṣaṇapratiṣedhahetuśca prativādinaivoddhriyate /
sa vādino vā prativādino vā heturvopālambho vā nivartate /
children.translated_text: The reason or the criticism of either the proponent or the opponent is defeated.

children.text: tasmin nivṛtte yo 'vatiṣṭhate ekaḥ, tenārthanirṇayaḥ, na dvābhyām /
children.translated_text: When that is defeated, the one that remains — by that alone the determination of the matter [occurs], not by both.
Therefore, [the expression] "by thesis and counter-thesis" is inappropriate.

children.text: na tāvat saṃśayaviṣaye nirṇaye vādiprativādinau staḥ, tayorniścitayoreva pravṛtteḥ //
children.translated_text: The proponent and opponent are not engaged in a determination whose subject is doubt, for they proceed only when they are already certain.

Here, since thesis and counter-thesis are employed in debate, one objects through confusion about debate that doubt exists [in debate] — "this is not" etc.
"One" means the proponent.
He establishes the asserted position through a reason.
Of the second, the opponent — "the refuted" means the refutation, i.e., the criticism of the reason stated by the proponent.
"Extracts" means makes manifest as a pseudo-fault.
But by the second, the opponent, the establishment of the reason stated by the proponent

children.text:
abhyupetya tu pariharati---ubhābhyāmiti /
vādinaḥ sādhanasya saṃbhavaḥ prativādina upālambhasya asaṃbhavaḥ /
evaṃ prativādinaḥ sādhanasya saṃbhavo vādina upālambhasyāsaṃbhava iti /
vimṛśyeti vimarśa kṛtveti /
anupādeyo 'pi vimarśaḥ kāryatvāt kṛtivyāpya uktaḥ /
vimṛśyetipadopādānasya prayojanamāha---so 'yamiti /
avadyotya niyamena viṣayayīkṛtyetyarthaḥ /
ekadharmisthayorityasya vyatirekamāha---yathā kriyāvaditi /
