viruddhayorityasya kālabhedena vyatirekamāha---ekadharmisthayośceti /
na nirṇayamātrasyedaṃ lakṣaṇamapi tu parīkṣāviṣayasyetyāha---na cāyaṃ nirṇaya iti /
children.translated_text: He says this is not the definition of mere determination, but of determination that has examination as its object — "and this is not determination" etc.
"Ascertainment of the matter is determination" — this much alone as a definition would apply to direct perception produced from the contact of sense organs with objects — this is the construction.
He reveals the accepted [distinction] that was held in mind — "in the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) and in debate" etc.

children.text: na hi jyotiṣṭomādīnāṃ svargādisaṃbandhanirṇaye āgamena kartavye vimarśo 'sti, nāpi vādajalpavitaṇḍāsu vimarśaḥ, niścitayoreva vādiprativādinostatra pravṛtterityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: For in the determination of the connection of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and other [rituals] with heaven etc., which is to be done through scripture (<s>āgama</s>), there is no deliberation; nor is there deliberation in debate, <s>jalpa</s> (disputation), and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavil), since the proponent and opponent proceed therein only when already certain — this is the meaning.

But he resolves by concession — "by both" etc.
The proof of the proponent has possibility; the criticism of the opponent has impossibility.
Similarly, the proof of the opponent has possibility; the criticism of the proponent has impossibility.
"After deliberation" (<s>vimṛśya</s>) means having made deliberation.
Although deliberation is not [directly] to be adopted, it is said to be encompassed by action because it is an effect.
He states the purpose of using the word "after deliberation" —

children.text:
vārttikam---saṃbandho 'rthaśca pūrvavat /
saṃbandha uddeśakrameṇa tarkānantaryalakṣaṇaḥ /
arthaśca prayojanam /
samānāsamānajātīyavyavṛttirityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: The rest has been covered through the explanation of the <s>Bhāṣya</s>.

children.text: nanu bhavatu pakṣaśabdalakṣitasya sādhanasya nirṇayaṃ prati karaṇatvam, pratipakṣalakṣitasya tu taddūṣaṇasya na sākṣātsādhakatvamityata āha---pratipakṣācceti hetutvaṃ pāramparyeṇetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Granted that the proof indicated by the word "thesis" (<s>pakṣa</s>) serves as an instrument for determination, but the criticism indicated by "counter-thesis" (<s>pratipakṣa</s>) does not directly prove — to this he says: "from the counter-thesis" etc. — meaning: its being a reason is indirect.
"By thesis and counter-thesis" —
The meaning is: by proof and criticism.

The <s>Vārttika</s> — "the connection and the purpose are as before."
The connection is characterized by immediately following <s>tarka</s> in the order of enumeration.
And the purpose (<s>artha</s>) means the goal.
The meaning is: differentiation from things of the same and different classes.

children.text:
lakṣaṇamācikṣipsurvikalpayati---kva punarayamiti /
atra pakṣapratipakṣābhyāmeveti prathamaḥ kalpaḥ, tadā hi yata evakāraḥ tato 'nyatrāvadhāraṇamiti nirṇaye niyamo bhavet /
nirṇaya eveti dvitīyaḥ kalpaḥ, tadā hi pakṣapratipakṣābhyāmityatra niyamaḥ /
vimṛśyaiveti ca tṛtīyaḥ, tadāpi nirṇaye niyamaḥ /
tatra prathamaṃ kalpamākṣipati---yadi vimṛśyeti /
tasmin vikalpe nirṇayaḥ pakṣapratipakṣavimarśātilaṅghanenānyatra na pravartata iti pratyakṣaṃ pramāṇaṃ nirṇayaphalaṃ na syāt /
na hi tatra pakṣapratipakṣau, nāpi vimarśa iti pratyakṣalakṣaṇaṃ bādhyate ityarthaḥ /
tṛtīyakalpamākṣipati---eteneti /
vyāghātenetyarthaḥ /
dvitīye kalpe dūṣaṇamāha---atha pakṣeti /
tadā nirṇayasyāniyamāt pakṣapratipakṣau ca tadabhāvaśceti tadubhayam, tadāśrayaḥ nirṇayaḥ prāptoti /
tathā cāvyāpakaṃ lakṣaṇam ityarthaḥ /
prathamaṃ kalpamālambya samādhatte---tarkaviṣaya iti /
na nirṇayamātrasyedaṃ lakṣaṇam, api tu nirṇayaviśeṣasyetyarthaḥ /
na nirṇaya iti na nirṇayamātra ityarthaḥ /
atha nirṇayasya kimiti nirṇayamātrasyetyarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: "And individually by <s>pramāṇas</s>" — meaning: by direct perception and the rest.
"And collectively by <s>pramāṇas</s>" — meaning: by proof, criticism, and resolution.

children.text: pakṣapratipakṣābhyāmeva vāde nirṇayo na tu vimarśaḥ /
children.translated_text: In debate, determination is by thesis and counter-thesis alone, not deliberation.

children.text: śāstre tu nirṇaya eva na tu tatra śāstrātiriktaṃ sādhanāntaramāśrīyata ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: But in the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise), there is only determination, and no other means of proof beyond the <s>śāstra</s> is relied upon — this is the meaning.

Wishing to indicate the definition, he considers alternatives — "where then is this" etc.
Here, the first alternative is "by thesis and counter-thesis alone" — for then, from the restrictive particle "alone," the restriction in determination would be: determination [occurs] not elsewhere [than through thesis and counter-thesis].
The second alternative is "in determination alone" — then the restriction would be in [the expression] "by thesis and counter-thesis."
And the third is "after deliberation alone" — then too the restriction would be in determination.

children.text:
pakṣapratipakṣābhyāmiti /
lakṣaṇāyāṃ hi yena yat lakṣyate tadavacchedakatayā tadapi buddhau sannidhīyate /
tataśca tena niyamo bhavati lakṣyamāṇasya, yathā gaṅgāyāṃ dhoṣa iti /
gaṅgāsaṃbandhyeva tīraṃ ghoṣeṇānvīyate, na tvakūpāratīramapīti /
codayati---artheti /
pariharati---na neti /
arthagrahaṇe kriyamāṇe kālpanikatvaṃ pratiṣidhyate, na cākalpitaṃ viruddhadharmavadityekataranirṇayaḥ /
nedaṃ pakṣapratipakṣābhyāmityādi codyabhāṣyaṃ vyācaṣṭepakṣapratipakṣābhyāmiti /
ubhābhyāmityādi parihārabhāṣyaṃ vyācaṣṭe---ubhābhyāmevetyāheti /
pṛcchati--etasminniti, prathamaṃ sādhanam, dvitīyaṃ dūṣaṇam, tṛtīyaṃ samādhānam /
uttaram---sarvatra /
kadācit prathame kadācid dvitīye kadācit tṛtīye ityarthaḥ /
avaśyaṃ tu tṛtīya ityāha---atha veti /

children.translated_text: In both alternatives, the question is: "how?"
The answer — "one, first" etc.

children.text: taṃ nivartyaṃ vādinaḥ sādhanaṃ dūṣaṇena nivartya prativādī svapakṣe sādhanaṃ bravīti /
children.translated_text: Having defeated the proof of the proponent through criticism, the opponent states the proof for his own thesis.
"The first" means the proponent.

"By thesis and counter-thesis" —
For in a definition, that by which something is defined, being a delimiter, is also present in the mind.
And from that, there is a restriction of what is being defined, just as in "the village on the Ganges."
Only a bank related to the Ganges is associated with the village, not a bank at a well or at a threshing floor.
He objects — "the object" etc.
He resolves — "no, not" etc.
In the mention of "object,"

children.text:
nirṇayo 'numānameveti kecit /
tathā hi tṛtīyaliṅgadarśanaṃ pratyakṣaphalaṃ nirṇayaḥ /
tadeva cānumānamato nirṇayo nānumānādatiricyate ityarthaḥ /
pariharati---na liṅgaliṅgiti /
yadi nirṇayamātramanumānamucyeta, tadā na tasya sarvasya liṅgaliṅgisaṃbandhasmṛtyapekṣatvamiti /
yadi tu liṅgaparāmarśo nirṇayaḥ, tasya cāsti liṅgaliṅgisaṃbandhāpekṣeti tatrāha--pramāṇaphalatvāt /
sāmānyavyāpto viśeṣaḥ sāmānyanivṛttyā nivartate, śiṃśapātvamiva vṛkṣatvanivṛttyā /
na ca phale pramitirūpe nirṇaye pramākaraṇatvaṃ phalatve nāstīti nānumānatvaṃ tadviśeṣa
ityarthaḥ /
itaścānumānāt nirṇayo bhidyate ityāha--nirṇayaḥ svaviṣaya eveti na hi nirṇayo nirṇayatvena pratipattyanubandhibhūtād viṣayādanyatra, anumānaṃ tu tatra cānyatra ca /
yadānumeyo 'gnireva heyatvādibhiḥ paricchidyate 'gnijñānenānumānena, yadā tu dhūmajñānenāgniranumīyate tadānyatra ceti gamayitavyam /
śeṣamatirohitam//41 //
children.translated_text:
Ascertainment is inference itself— so say some /
For the third observation of the mark, which is the result of perception, is ascertainment /
And that itself is inference; therefore ascertainment is not distinct from inference— this is the meaning /
He resolves— 'no, because of the mark and the mark-bearer' /
If mere ascertainment were called inference, then that entire [ascertainment] would not require the recollection of the connection between mark and mark-bearer /
But if the apprehension of the mark is ascertainment, and that does require the connection between mark and mark-bearer, then to that he says— 'because of being the result of a means of knowledge' /
A particular pervaded by a universal ceases when the universal ceases— just as <s>śiṃśapā</s>-hood [ceases] when tree-hood ceases /
And in the result, which has the form of a determinate cognition, i.e., ascertainment, the property of being a means of knowledge does not exist in [what is merely] a result— so it is not inference, [which is] a particular of that [means of knowledge]— this is the meaning /
He states another reason why ascertainment differs from inference— 'ascertainment is only of its own object' /
For ascertainment, qua ascertainment, does not extend beyond the object that is bound to cognition as its content; but inference extends to that [object] and to other [objects as well] /
When fire that is to be inferred is determined by the cognition of fire, i.e., by inference, through properties such as being avoidable— that is [inference restricted to] its own object; but when fire is inferred through the cognition of smoke, then [inference extends] to another [object] as well— this should be understood /
The rest is clear //41//
// Thus ends the first daily portion of the first chapter of the <s>Nyāyavārttikatātparyaṭīkā</s> composed by <s>Vācaspatimiśra</s> //

children.text: NyS_1,2.1: pramāṇatarkasādhanopālambhaḥ siddhāntāviruddhaḥ pañcāvayavopapannaḥ pakṣapratipakṣaparigraho vādaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 1.2.1: <s>Vāda</s> (honest debate) is the adoption of a thesis and counter-thesis, involving proof and criticism grounded in <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) and <s>tarka</s> (reasoning), not contradicting any established conclusion, and furnished with the five members //
Let the wise, free from envy, with intellects exceedingly sharp and refined,
grasp the truths of the meanings of <s>Vācaspati</s>'s words, like gods //

children.text:
uddeśakramaprāptaṃ vādalakṣaṇaparaṃ sūtram avatārayituṃ bhāṣyam---tisraḥ kathā bhavantīti /
tadayuktam, bṛhatkathādīnāṃ tisṛṣu kathāsu anantarthāvāt /
na ca sāmānyalakṣaṇābhidhānamantareṇa viśeṣalakṣaṇāvasaro 'sti, vādādayaśca kathāviśeṣā ityata āha vārttikakāraḥ---tisraḥ kathā bhavantīti /
nāyaṃ kathāmātraniyamo yena bṛhatkathādīnām
akathātvaṃ syāt, api tu yannānāpravaktṛke vicāre vasati tad vicāravastu /
vicāraviṣayā vākyasaṃdṛbdhiḥ katheti yāvat /
tasyāḥ kathāyā eṣa niyamaḥ tisra eveti /
tathā ca nānāpravaktṛkavicāraviṣayā vākyasaṃdṛbdhiḥ katheti sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ pakṣapratipakṣaparigraha

children.translated_text: — it should be seen that this too is stated by implication /

children.text: yad vastu vicāryate ityarthābhidhānamātram, na tu vicāravastvityasya vivaraṇam /
children.translated_text: 'That which is the subject of inquiry'— this is merely a statement of the meaning, not an explanation of the term 'subject matter of inquiry' /
He states the qualified persons for <s>vāda</s> and the rest— 'therein, by the teacher and the like' /
He states the reason for the immediate [placement] of the definition of <s>vāda</s>— 'therein, in the order of enumeration' //

The <s>bhāṣya</s> that introduces the <s>sūtra</s> on the definition of <s>vāda</s>, which comes next in the order of enumeration, is: 'there are three kinds of debate' /
That is inappropriate, since the <s>Bṛhatkathā</s> and the like are not included among the three kinds of debate /
And without giving the general definition, there is no occasion for the specific definition; and <s>vāda</s> and the rest are specific types of debate— therefore the <s>vārttikakāra</s> says— 'there are three kinds of debate' /
This is not a restriction on mere debate such that the <s>Bṛhatkathā</s> and the like would be excluded from being debates; rather, that which resides in an inquiry conducted by multiple speakers is the subject matter of inquiry /
The composition of statements concerning a subject matter of inquiry is debate— this is the extent /
This is the restriction on that debate: exactly three kinds /
And thus, the general definition is: a composition of statements concerning a subject matter of inquiry by multiple speakers is debate— [and this] is indicated by the <s>sūtra</s>-component 'adoption of a thesis and counter-thesis'

children.text:
sūtramiti /

children.translated_text: and the rest of the <s>bhāṣya</s> has been explained /

children.translated_text: Although in <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (destructive debate) too there is adoption of thesis and counter-thesis, nevertheless there is no proof of the counter-thesis, since it lacks establishment [of its own position] /

children.translated_text: And although in <s>jalpa</s> (sophistical debate) too there is proof of thesis and counter-thesis, nevertheless the proof and criticism are not grounded in <s>pramāṇa</s>-based members and <s>tarka</s>— so [<s>vāda</s>] is differentiated from <s>jalpa</s> and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> by the phrase 'proof and criticism grounded in <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s>' /
And how this is so will be established further on //

The <s>sūtra</s> /
It has been said that the general definition too is indicated by this [<s>sūtra</s>] /
The <s>bhāṣya</s> beginning 'situated in one locus, with [mutual awareness]' he explains preceded by a question— 'what?' /
He analyzes into 'object' and 'property'— 'object and property' /
The word 'property' (<s>dharma</s>) is in the sense of a particular /
Since that [particular] has not been ascertained, the object is said to be ascertained in general /
This is what he says— 'of the object, in general' /
Even though not contradictory, they do not give rise to inquiry in this way— this is the meaning /
He states the purport of the terms '<s>pramāṇa</s>, <s>tarka</s>, proof, and criticism'— 'of this' /
By this, its qualification

samādhatte---na brūma iti /

tathā ca tarkasyāpi sādhanopālambhahetubhāvaḥ siddho bhavatītyarthaḥ /

children.translated_text:

He resolves— 'we do not say' /
Since <s>tarka</s>, having the form of a procedural requirement, assists <s>pramāṇa</s>, the members grounded in <s>pramāṇa</s> are also grounded in <s>tarka</s> /
And thus the property of <s>tarka</s> being a cause of proof and criticism is established— this is the meaning /
He analyzes and objects— 'proof and criticism are in this' /
For establishment and criticism with respect to the opponent are intended /
And those are not through <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s>, since those [<s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s>] serve as causes of one's own cognition /
The meaning of the word 'member' means the meaning of the word 'member' /
Even though intended in both ways,

children.text:
karaṇasādhanapakṣaṃ kakṣīkṛtya tāvat samādhatte---na, anyārthatvāditi /
anyaprayojanatvādityarthaḥ /
yadā tu bhāvasādhanau tadā pṛcchati---athaitāviti /
vipratipannasya praśnaḥ /
na pratipakṣaviṣaya upālambho nāpi tatsādhanaviṣayaḥ, tayorvastunoḥ svakāraṇādutpannayoḥ sadā tadrūpatvena puruṣadharmopālambhānāspadatvādityākṣepārthaḥ /
samādhatte---evametaditi /
dharmī dharmaviśiṣṭaḥ pakṣaḥ pratipakṣo vā karma, tasya viṣayaḥ /
tasya dharmiṇo vāstavaṃ tādṛśatvamatādṛśatvaṃ vā karaṇasya tu karmaiva viṣayaḥ /

anyaviṣaye tu puruṣaste niyu/jāno 'samarthīkarotīti /
so 'yaṃ puruṣasyāparādho na karmakaraṇayoḥ /
yathā ākāśe niśātamasiṃ vyāpārayataḥ puruṣasyāparādho nākāśasya śabde samarthasya, aservā niśātasya dāruṇi samarthasya /
tasmādaupacārikaḥ sādhanasyopālambho na mukhyaḥ /

children.translated_text: The primary [criticism] is of the person alone /
But it is made manifest through the medium of speech— it is of the person /

children.text: vacana upacaryate na tu pakṣe pakṣadvāreṇānudbhāvanāditi siddham /
children.translated_text: The figurative expression is applied to the speech, not to the thesis, since it is not made manifest through the medium of the thesis— this is established /

children.text: yathāyamarthaḥ sūtrapadebhyo labhyate tathā praśnapūrvakaṃ darśayati---kathaṃ punariti //
children.translated_text: How this meaning is obtained from the words of the <s>sūtra</s>— he shows this preceded by a question— 'but how?' //

adopting the view of 'instrument-means' (<s>karaṇasādhana</s>), he first resolves— 'no, because of having a different purpose' /
The meaning is: because of having a different purpose /
But when [<s>sādhana</s> and <s>upālambha</s>] are [understood as] abstract nouns, he asks— 'now, these two' /
This is the question of one who is perplexed /
Criticism is not directed at the counter-thesis itself, nor at its proof, since those two things, having arisen from their own causes, always have that nature and are thus not suitable objects of criticism as human faults— this is the purport of the objection /
He resolves— 'this is so' /
The <s>dharmin</s> (subject), qualified by the property, is the thesis or counter-thesis— that is the object (<s>karman</s>); its content /
Whether the <s>dharmin</s> actually has or does not have that nature— that is [the concern] of the instrument /
And the instrument and object are effective only when capable, not when incapable /
But a person who employs them for a different purpose renders them incapable /
And this is the fault of the person, not of the object or the instrument /
Just as, for a person who wields a sharpened sword against space, the fault is the person's, not of space which is capable [of receiving] sound, nor of the sharp sword which is capable [of cutting] wood /
Therefore, the criticism of the proof is figurative, not primary /

children.text:
yaduktaṃ pramāṇatarkasādhanopālambhagrahaṇaṃ vādasya jalpavitaṇḍābhyāṃ viśeṣaṇārthamiti,
tatra prakāraṃ pṛcchati---atheti /
praṣṭaivāha--nanvidamapīti /
uttaram---na samānamiti /
niyamamāha--pramāṇatarkasādhanopālambha
eva vādaḥ /
evakāreṇa
children.translated_text:
As to what was said— that the phrase 'proof and criticism grounded in <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s>' serves to differentiate <s>vāda</s> from <s>jalpa</s> and <s>vitaṇḍā</s>—
he asks about the manner— 'now' /
The questioner himself says— 'but is not this too' /
The reply— 'it is not the same' /
He states the restriction— 'proof and criticism grounded in <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s> alone is <s>vāda</s>' /
By the particle '<s>eva</s>' (alone),

children.text:
chalādisādhanopālambhatvaṃ vādasya vyavacchidyate, tathā ca jalpavitaṇḍābhyāṃ vyavacchedaḥ /
etaduktaṃ bhavati, tarkānugṛhītapramāṇamūlā avayavāḥ paramārthato bhavantu mā bhūvan,
vādiprativādinostvabhiprāyo bhavatu pramāṇamūlā avayavā iti /

jalpavitaṇḍayostvapramāṇamūlatvaṃ viduṣāpi prativādinā chalādibhiḥ pratyavastheyam, ekāntaparājayād
children.translated_text: But in <s>jalpa</s> and <s>vitaṇḍā</s>, even a knowledgeable opponent must counter with <s>chala</s> (equivocation) and the like despite [the arguments] not being grounded in <s>pramāṇa</s>, because of inevitable defeat;
by one who desires victory, [thinking] 'doubt is preferable [to defeat]' /

children.text: yathā cāsya śāstre vyutpādanaṃ nāsadṛśaṃ yathā caiṣa satāmācāraḥ, tathā jalpalakṣaṇe vakṣyāmaḥ //
children.translated_text: And how the teaching of this [<s>jalpa</s>] in the <s>śāstra</s> is not improper, and how this is the conduct of the virtuous— that we shall state in the definition of <s>jalpa</s> //

the property of <s>vāda</s> having proof and criticism through <s>chala</s> (equivocation) and the like is excluded; and thus the differentiation from <s>jalpa</s> and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> [is achieved] /
This is what has been said: whether the members grounded in <s>pramāṇa</s> assisted by <s>tarka</s> are ultimately [valid] or not—
let the intention of the proponent and the opponent be that the members are grounded in <s>pramāṇa</s> /
By this much alone, there is the property of having proof and criticism grounded in <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s> in <s>vāda</s>, since as a debate of dispassionate persons it culminates in the ascertainment of truth /

children.translated_text:
The <s>bhāṣya</s> beginning 'because of the application of grounds of defeat in <s>jalpa</s>' /
That is unjustified /
Since the ground of defeat is already obtained in <s>vāda</s> too from the very mention of 'criticism'— therefore the <s>vārttikakāra</s> says— '<s>chala</s> (equivocation) and <s>jāti</s> (futile objection)' /
The intent is: in the absence of the mention of 'criticism' /
He objects— 'the entire' /
If the purpose of the mention of 'criticism' is to prescribe the ground of defeat, then there would be no difference of <s>vāda</s> from <s>jalpa</s>; and the two subsequent terms [in the <s>sūtra</s>] would be redundant— this is the meaning /
He resolves— 'not of the two latter' /
Restriction means exclusive enumeration /
By this, the <s>bhāṣya</s> 'for the purpose of permitting certain [grounds of defeat]'

children.translated_text: but when even without exposure there is no impediment to the cognition of truth,
even what has been employed should not be exposed /
And this will be established more carefully in the fifth chapter //

has been explained /
Introducing and criticizing the <s>bhāṣya</s>'s explanation of 'not contradicting the established conclusion'— 'by this not contradicting the established conclusion' /
Having criticized the <s>bhāṣya</s>'s view, he asks and explains by his own view— 'but what is this term?' /
He asks— 'why then?' /
The reply— 'by the teacher and the like' /
The exposure of inability to reply and the like is indeed not obstructive to the cognition of truth—
but the excessive [resort to such exposure], though not directly impeding the cognition of truth, causes the opponent whose intellect is confused by following its purpose to be unable to cognize the truth— thus even the excessive [resort] has the property of being a hindrance to the cognition of truth /
'One who desires truth'— this excludes the desire to win; for the desire to win is impossible [in debates] with the teacher and the like / 'Threefold is the result' /
The three results are: knowledge of truth not previously known, removal of doubt, and confirmation of what has been ascertained /
But against an adversary, it is not <s>vāda</s> but rather <s>jalpa</s> and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> /
He objects— '<s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s>' /
When proof and criticism in one subject are possible through genuine <s>pramāṇa</s> assisted by <s>tarka</s>, an object characterized by contradictory properties would arise at some point— this is the meaning /
He resolves— 'this is not a fault' /
In <s>vāda</s>, the intention of the proponent and opponent is restricted: proof and criticism are to be employed with the intention of <s>pramāṇa</s>-based cognition, not with non-<s>pramāṇa</s>-based cognition as in <s>jalpa</s> and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> /
But the object is not restricted /
And thus, in <s>vāda</s>, when <s>chala</s> and the like are employed without intention, their exposure too is possible— but [<s>chala</s>] should be exposed only insofar as its non-exposure would impede the cognition of truth;

children.text:
sādhanoktaṃ prakāraṃ dūṣaṇe 'pyatidiśati---dūṣaṇamapyevam /
pūrvasmin prayojane sthite bhāṣyakāraḥ prayojanāntaramanvācinoti---avayaveṣviti /
na hi pañcāvayavopapannatvaṃ pramāṇaṃ ca tadanugrāhakaṃ ca tarkamantareṇa bhavatīti pañcāvayavopapannatvādeva pramāṇatarkapratilambhe sādhanopālambhayorvyatiṣaṅgajñāpanāyāvaśyaṃ sādhanopālambhagrahaṇaṃ tāvat kartavyam,
anyathaikaḥ svasthānasthita eva śabdasyānityatvaṃ prati pañcāvayavopapannaṃ vākyaṃ prayuṅkte,
aparo 'pi tādṛśaḥ śabdanityatā prati tādṛśameva vākyaṃ prayuṅkte iti so 'pi vādaḥ prasajyeta /
children.translated_text:
He extends the mode stated for proof to criticism as well— 'criticism too, thus' /
With the previous purpose established, the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> traces another purpose— 'in the members' /
For without the members, which are furnished with five components, and without <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s> that assist them, there can be no [valid debate]; and since <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s> are already obtained from the very fact of being furnished with five members, the mention of 'proof and criticism' must be made to indicate their intertwining—
otherwise, one person, standing in his own position, would formulate a five-membered statement for the non-eternality of sound,
and another such person would formulate a similar statement for the eternality of sound— and that too would be [wrongly called] <s>vāda</s> /

children.text:
sādhanopālambhaviśeṣaṇāya ca pramāṇatarkagrahaṇaṃ kṛtamiti bhāvaḥ /
prayojanāntaram
anvācinoti---antareṇāpi ceti vādaḥ pañcāvayavopapanna
ityekaḥ kalpaḥ /
pramāṇatarkasādhanopālambha
iti ca dvitīya ityarthaḥ /
prayojanāntaramanvācinoti---chalajātīti /
vinigraho jalpo mā vijñāyi /
vādagatanigrahasthānarahito mā vijñāyityarthaḥ /
tadvijñāne kīdṛśo 'rtho bhavatītyata āha---chalajātinigahasthāneti /
vādagato nigraho na jalpe, jalpagataśca nigraho na vāda iti sa mā vijñāyati /
children.translated_text: The ground of defeat applicable in <s>vāda</s> does not apply in <s>jalpa</s>, and the ground of defeat applicable in <s>jalpa</s> does not apply in <s>vāda</s>— let this not be [wrongly] known /
For it is desired that the ground of defeat applicable in <s>vāda</s> also applies in <s>jalpa</s> /
This desired meaning is obtained from the additional text, because of the inclusion of <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means) and <s>tarka</s> (reasoning)
— this is the meaning. //

And the mention of '<s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s>' has been made to qualify 'proof and criticism'— this is the purport /
He traces another purpose— 'and even without' /
<s>Vāda</s> is furnished with five members— this is one interpretation /
'Proof and criticism grounded in <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s>'— this is the second— this is the meaning /
He traces another purpose— '<s>chala</s> (equivocation), <s>jāti</s> (futile objection)' /
Let <s>vinigraha</s> (censure) not be known as <s>jalpa</s> /
The meaning is: let the ground of defeat applicable in <s>vāda</s> not be known [as applicable in <s>jalpa</s>] /
What kind of meaning results from that knowledge?— to this he says— '<s>chala</s>, <s>jāti</s>, and <s>nigrahasthāna</s>' /

children.text:
tadevaṃ svābhimataṃ vādalakṣaṇaṃ vyākhyāya vāsubandhavaṃ lakṣaṇa dūṣayitumupanyasyati---apare tviti svapakṣasya siddhiḥ parapakṣasya cāsiddhiḥ,
tadarthaṃ vacanaṃ vāda ityarthaḥ /
dūṣayati---atra ceti /
prathamaṃ hetuṃ vibhajate---etāviti /
pūrvaḥ pakṣo 'yuktaḥ, pakṣa uttarastu yukta ityarthaḥ /
ekasya vā śabdasya dharmino 'nekanityānityaviśeṣaṇābhisaṃbandhinaḥ puruṣābhisandhibhedāt anekaśabdābhidhānam,
svaparaśabdābhidhānamityarthaḥ /
etadeva cintyate kiṃ tatsvīkaraṇamiti /
na
children.translated_text: Having thus explained the definition of debate (<s>vāda</s>) according to his own view, he presents <s>Vasubandhu</s>'s definition in order to criticize it — 'others, however': the establishment of one's own position and the non-establishment of the opponent's position — the statement for that purpose is debate — this is the meaning. He criticizes — 'and in this.' He analyzes the first reason — 'this much.' The first alternative (<s>pakṣa</s>) is improper; the second alternative is proper — this is the meaning. Or, for one and the same property-bearer sound, which is connected with multiple qualifications — eternal and non-eternal — due to the difference in the speaker's intention, there is designation by multiple words, meaning designation by the words 'own' and 'other' — this is the meaning. This very thing is considered — what does the word 'own' (<s>sva</s>) mean? It does not

children.text:
tāvad bhūmidhanādiṣviva svocitāsu arthakriyāsu yatheṣṭaviniyogayogyatvaṃ svatvamarjanāpāditamanityatvādinā pratijñāte śabdādau saṃbhavatītyarthaḥ /
codayati---mameti pratyayotpattikāraṇattvaṃ svatvam, akāraṇatvam
asvatvamiti /
dūṣayati---nirdiṣṭa iti /
yatheṣṭaviniyogayogyatvameva mameti pratyayakāraṇatvam, nānyat /
na caitannityatvādinā pratijñāte śabde 'sti śāstrakārasyetyarthaḥ /
api copakārakatvena vyāptaṃ satvaṃ goghaṭādiṣu tathā darśanāt, pakṣāt nivartamānamupakārakatvaṃ svatvamapi svavpāpyaṃ nivartayati vṛkṣatvamiva śiṃśapātvamityāha---yacca yasyeti /
dvitīyaṃ kalpam āśaṅkate--sādhanīyeti /
nirākaroti---aho śabdārtheti /
children.translated_text: mean the capacity for use at will in desired purposive activities, as in land and wealth and the like — that is ownership acquired through appropriation, and it is not possible in sound and the like when non-eternality and the like are proposed — this is the meaning. He objects — 'mine': the property of being the cause of the cognition 'mine' is ownership; not being such a cause is non-ownership. He criticizes — 'as stated': the capacity for use at will is itself the cause of the cognition 'mine,' and nothing else. And this is not present in sound when non-eternality and the like are proposed by the author of the treatise — this is the meaning. Moreover, ownership is pervaded by the property of being beneficial, since that is observed in cows, pots, and the like. When [ownership] is excluded from the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>), the property of being beneficial, being excluded, also makes ownership — which is its own pervaded [property] — excluded, just as [the exclusion of] tree-ness excludes <s>śiṃśapā</s>-ness — thus he says — 'and whatever belongs to whatever.' He raises the second alternative as a doubt — 'what is to be proved.' He refutes — 'alas, the meaning of the word!'

children.text:
viśeṣyapadāt anatiriktārthaṃ viśeṣaṇapadamityarthaḥ /
api cedaṃ viśeṣaṇapadaṃ viśeṣyaṃ sāmānyataḥ prasṛtaṃ viśeṣe 'vasthāpayati na vā? avasthāpayatīti cet? na sādhanīyamātrārthatā svapakṣaśabdasya, na ced viśeṣaṇaṃ vyarthamityāha---vyavacchedārthaṃ cedamiti /
nanu ca viśeṣyaśabdo viśeṣaṇayogāt
viśeṣe vartamāno 'pi sāmānyaśabda eva,
tataśca śaknoti samānamarthaṃ vaktumiti codayati---sāmānyaśabdā apīti /
pariharati---na te sāmānyaśabdā iti /
api ca sādhanīyaḥ pakṣa iti /
varuddhopadarśanena sphuṭā pratītirbhavatīti ayuktapratipādanārthaṃ yuktasyāpyupanyāsa iti /
yadi na pakṣeṇa dūṣaṇaṃ saṃbadhyate kastarhi tasya viṣaya iti śaṅkate---atha dūṣaṇasyeti /
uttaram---kasyaciditi /
uttaradoṣaḥ
jātyudbhāvanam /
ākṣipyanta ityākṣepāḥ /
ke te bhāvāḥ? apratibhāvikṣepādayaḥ /
naite svaparapakṣābhyāṃ saṃbadhyante nāpi sthāpanayeti /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: the qualifying word has no meaning beyond the qualified word. Moreover, does this qualifying word establish the qualified [term] that has spread through generality into a specific [meaning], or not? If it does, then the word 'own position' (<s>svapakṣa</s>) does not merely mean 'what is to be proved.' If it does not, the qualifier is purposeless — thus he says — 'if for the purpose of exclusion.' Now, a qualified word, even while being situated in a specific [meaning] through connection with the qualifier, is still a general word; and thus it can express the same meaning — he objects — 'even general words.' He resolves — 'they are not general words.' Moreover, 'the position that is to be proved': the presentation of the proper through the demonstration of the improper produces a clear understanding — therefore, the proper too is presented for the purpose of demonstrating what is improper. If the refutation is not connected with the thesis, what then is its domain? — he raises this doubt — 'now, of refutation.' The answer — 'of some [particular thing].' A fault of the response is the production of a pseudo-refutation (<s>jāti</s>). 'Objections' (<s>ākṣepa</s>) are what are objected to. What are these states? Non-response (<s>apratibhā</s>), evasion, and the like. These are not connected with either one's own or the opponent's position, nor with the establishment [of either].
He objects — 'true.' He resolves — 'is used.'
'There is no violation of the primary meaning of a word except when impelled by purpose and the like' —

children.text:
iti hi gāthā bhavatāmityarthaḥ /
api copacāraścet /
lakṣaṇe tato varamevaṃ kriyatāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ lāghavāyetyāha---yadi ceti /
śaṅkate---atheti /
nirākaroti---svarūpata
iti /
mukhyata ityarthaḥ /
codayati---sthāpanayāpīti /
pariharati---na doṣeti /
nanu na dūṣaṇamātraṃ saṃbadhyate, asiddhyarthamiti ca dūṣaṇamātrābhidhānam,
tat kuto viśeṣapratilambha ityata āha---sāmānyābhidhāne 'pīti /
tṛtīyaṃ kalpaṃ dūṣayitumupanyasyati---svaparaśabdāviti /
etadapi /
sūtrāntaravirodhena dūṣayati---na yukta metadapīti /
children.translated_text: — for this is your maxim — this is the meaning. Moreover, if it is a figurative usage, it would be better to formulate the definition in a way that achieves brevity — thus he says — 'and if.' He raises a doubt — 'now then.' He refutes — 'in its own nature,' meaning 'primarily.' He objects — 'even by establishment.' He resolves — 'there is no fault.' Now, not only refutation alone is connected [with the thesis], and the statement is merely of refutation alone for the purpose of non-establishment — so from what is the specific [understanding] obtained? — therefore he says — 'even in a general statement.' He presents the third alternative for criticism — 'the words own and other.' This too. He criticizes through contradiction with another <s>sūtra</s> — 'this too is not proper.'
'Those [own and other positions] are connected with the [respective] proofs and refutations' —

children.text:
iti sūtre hi niyameva svapakṣe sādhanaṃ parapakṣe dūṣaṇamuktam, tathā cottarapakṣe dūṣaṇīya
eveti uttarapakṣavādināpi dūṣaṇīyaḥ /
evaṃ pūrvapakṣo 'ti sādhanīya eveti, uttarapakṣavādino 'pi sādhanīyo na dūṣaṇīyaḥ syādityarthaḥ /
api cāyuktasya pūrvapakṣasya sādhaṇaṃ yuktasya cottarapakṣasya dūṣaṇamiti viparītaprasaṅga
ityāha---svapakṣaścottarapakṣavādinaḥ pūrvapakṣāt
ayuktapakṣāt anyaḥ yukta ityarthaḥ /
na padārthaḥ
nāvayavārthaḥ /

children.translated_text: By this — meaning through the contradiction of the statement of restriction in another <s>sūtra</s>.
[It has been] explained as that which is to be rejected.
He presents the sixth alternative for criticism — 'this is just one.'
He criticizes — 'this is proper: one [thing] has multiple qualifiers.' //

For in the <s>sūtra</s>, it is stated that proof pertains only to one's own position and refutation only to the opponent's position. Similarly, in the counter-position, what is to be refuted is to be refuted only — thus even by the holder of the counter-position, [the prior position] is to be refuted. And thus the prior position is only to be proved — so it would be provable and not refutable even by the holder of the counter-position — this is the meaning. Moreover, there would be the unwanted consequence that the prior position, being improper, is proved, and the counter-position, being proper, is refuted — thus he says — 'and one's own position of the holder of the counter-position is different from the prior position, being the proper one — [which is] other than the improper position' — this is the meaning. Not the word-meaning, not the component-meaning.

children.text:
dvitīyaṃ hetumupanyastaṃ vyākhātuṃ smārayati---samāseti /
na kevalaṃ viśeṣyāt pṛthak svārtho viśeṣaṇaṃ nāvadhāryate, api tvanyasmādapi na bhidyate ityāśayavānāha---bhedācceti /
codayati---asatyapi bheda iti /
na kevalaṃ patyurviśeṣyāt senā na bhidyate 'pi tu tato 'nyebhyo 'pi hāstikāśvīyarathapadātibhya iti /
evaṃ pānakamapi
children.translated_text: He reminds [the reader] in order to explain the second reason that has been presented — 'compound.' Not only is the qualifier's own meaning not ascertained as distinct from the qualified, but it is not distinguished from anything else either — with this intention he says — 'because of the difference.' He objects — 'even when there is no difference': not only is the army (<s>senā</s>) not distinguished from its master — the qualified — but also not from others — [viz.] the elephant corps, cavalry, chariot corps, and infantry. Similarly, a drink (<s>pānaka</s>) too —

children.text:
na kevalaṃ tadaṅgebhyo jīrakādibhyaḥ, api tvanyebhyo 'pi phalasalilādibhya iti /
pariharati---tacca neti /
uktaṃ nismṛtya śaṅkatī---atha manyase svārtha iti /
uktasmāraṇena nirākaroti---tanneti /
etenaiva ca karmadhārayabahuvrīhī
children.translated_text: — not only [is it not distinguished] from its ingredients such as cumin and the like, but also not from other [things] such as fruits, water, and the like. He resolves — 'and that is not so.' Having forgotten what was said, he raises a doubt — 'now, if you think that the own meaning [of the word].' He removes [the doubt] by reminding of what was said — 'that is not so.' And by this very [reasoning], the <s>karmadhāraya</s> (appositional) and <s>bahuvrīhi</s> (exocentric) [compounds]
— are also [refuted] — thus he says — 'by this.'

children.text: api ca svaḥ pakṣo yasya sādhayituḥ sa tathoktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, '<s>sva</s>' (own) is the position of the one who proves — and he is so called.
And thus, since the [word] pertains to the prover, he says — 'and pertaining to the prover.' //

children.text: sādhanīyārthatā tu bhaviṣyati, yathā ca samāsopapattiriti codayati---nanu ceti /
children.translated_text: but it will mean 'what is to be proved'; and thus the compound would be justified — he objects — 'but surely.'
He reminds of the fault stated in the genitive-compound alternative — 'it is not possible.'

children.text: api ca pakṣāt svapakṣabhede sūtrāntaravyāghāto 'bhede vā etasya vyāghāta
children.translated_text: Moreover, if '<s>svapakṣa</s>' (own position) is different from '<s>pakṣa</s>' (position), there is contradiction with another <s>sūtra</s>; and if it is not different, there is contradiction with this [definition]
— thus he says — 'because of contradiction.' //
Now, let it not be the case that the word '<s>sva</s>' means capacity-for-use-at-will,

children.text:
api ca vākyasamāsayoḥ samāso jyāyān lāghavādityāha---āstāṃ tāvaditi /
na hyaṃ samarthaḥ samāsa iti /
siddhyasiddhyarthamityayaṃ samāsaḥ svaparapakṣayoḥ pratyekaṃ na saṃbandhārtha ityarthāt kasyacit siddhiḥ kasyacidasiddhirityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For the purpose of establishment and non-establishment' — this compound does not relate severally to one's own and the opponent's positions; rather, it means: of something, establishment; of something, non-establishment — this is the meaning.
He resolves — 'if the compound is not [possible] because of incapacity, [then] for the purpose of establishment and non-establishment.'
'Even in the compound, then' —
The meaning is: even in the compound 'for the purpose of establishment and non-establishment of one's own and the opponent's positions.' //
Moreover, since between a sentence and a compound, the compound is preferable because of brevity — thus he says — 'let that be.' For this compound is not capable — this is the meaning.

children.text:
ekavacanabahuvacanaprasaṅgo 'pi nāstyasāmarthyāditi codyasamādhānābhyāṃ darśayati--- ekavacaneti /
anityatve 'pi samāsavidheḥ samāsa eva vigrahāt jyāyāniti codyasamādhānābhyāṃ darśayati---anitya iti /
bhavatu goravamevamapi ko doṣa ityata
āha---arthaṅgatyarthaṃ ceti /
laghunopāyenāśusiddhau gurvabhidhānamanarthakam /
yathāhuḥ,
children.translated_text: He shows through objection and resolution that there is no problem of singular vs. plural either, because of incapacity — 'singular.' He shows through objection and resolution that even though the compound-rule is non-eternal [i.e., admits exceptions], the compound alone is preferable to the analysis because of the [compound] rule — 'non-eternal.' Let there be weightiness; even so, what is the fault? — therefore he says — 'and for the purpose of understanding the meaning.' When the result can be achieved quickly by a light means, a weighty expression is purposeless. As they say:

children.text: akke cenmadhu vindeta kimarthaṃ parvataṃ vrajet /
children.translated_text: 'If one could find honey in the <s>arka</s> (swallow-wort) plant, why would one go to the mountain?'
'When the desired goal can be achieved, what wise person would exert effort?' //

children.text: iti atarthakaprayogaścānapekṣitaḥ śiṣyairiti teṣāmaśāsanāt na śāstraṃ syāt, tadidam uktam---śāstratveneti //
children.translated_text: And a purposeless usage is not sanctioned by students — since there is no teaching of them [to that effect], there would be no treatise [prescribing it]. This is what has been stated — 'as a treatise.' //

children.text:
siddhyasiddhyarthamityetadapi dūṣayati--siddhyasiddhyarthamityetadapi na yuktamiti /
tanna tāvaditi---taditi tayormadhya ityarthaḥ /
adhikāraṇapratyāyanamiti prāśnikapratyāyanamityarthaḥ /
kuto vyāhatamityata āha---ye caite iti /
co yasmādarthe,
adhikaraṇe vartate pakṣasyeti vyāhatamityarthaḥ /
codayati---nāyamiti /
siddhirjñānaṃ tasya pakṣo viṣayaḥ, āśrayāstu prāśnikā ityarthaḥ /
vikalpya dūṣayati---na yuktametaditi /
na tāvat jñānaṃ pakṣaviṣayaṃ prāśnikādhikaraṇaṃ ceti bauddharāddhānte saṃbhavati,
jñānasyānādhāratvāt
viṣayiviṣayabhāvasya cātāttvikatvāt /
tasmādanyā siddhiḥ /
tatredamupatiṣṭhate---kiṃ tarhīti /
siddhiyogāt siddhaḥ pakṣo bhavati /
pramāṇayogasya siddhiḥ /
saivārthasya tathātā /
children.translated_text: He also criticizes 'for the purpose of establishment and non-establishment' — 'this too — for the purpose of establishment and non-establishment — is not proper.' 'Not to begin with' — 'that' means 'between those two' — this is the meaning. 'Communicating to the adjudicators' means communicating to the questioners — this is the meaning. How is there contradiction? — therefore he says — 'and these.' The particle '<s>ca</s>' is in the sense of 'because.' That the position (<s>pakṣa</s>) pertains to the adjudicators — this is the contradiction — this is the meaning. He objects — 'this is not so.' Establishment (<s>siddhi</s>) is knowledge; the position is its object; the questioners are its locus — this is the meaning. He criticizes through alternatives — 'this is not proper.' Now, knowledge having the position as its object and the questioners as its locus is not possible in the Buddhist established doctrine, since knowledge has no locus and since the subject-object relation is not ultimately real. Therefore, establishment is something else. Here this presents itself — 'what then?' A position becomes established through connection with establishment. The connection with <s>pramāṇa</s> is establishment. That itself is the thatness of the object.

children.text:
tasyāstu prāśnikānāṃ pratītirbhavati /
tasmāt na prāśnikapratītiḥ pakṣasyāsiddhiriti virodhaḥ /
yasmāt so 'rthastathā bhavati tasmāt tathābhāvādadhikaraṇapratyāyanaṃ bhavatīti dvitīyaṃ kalpamāśaṅkate---athāsiddha iti /
yāvat pakṣaviṣayaṃ sādhanaṃ na prayujyate tāvadyadyadhikaraṇapratyāyanaṃ tataḥ sādhanaprayogāt prāgadhikaraṇapratyāyanamastīti vādavaiyarthaṃ sādhanadūṣaṇaprayogo 'narthakaḥ /
dūṣaṇāntaramāha---pakṣasyeti /
na prayojanamantareṇedānīntanānāmasmadādīnāṃ mukhyārthaśabdasyātikramo 'vācakapadaprayogeṇa labhyate ityarthaḥ /
yathāhuḥ,
children.translated_text: And the understanding of that by the questioners occurs. Therefore, the understanding of the questioners is not the non-establishment of the position — hence there is no contradiction. Since the object becomes thus [established], from that thatness the communication to the adjudicators occurs — he raises the second alternative as a doubt — 'now, if unestablished.' As long as the proof pertaining to the position-object is not employed, whatever communication to the adjudicators [occurs] prior to the employment of the proof — there is such communication to the adjudicators — hence the debate would be pointless, and the employment of proof and refutation would be purposeless. He states another criticism — 'of the position.' The meaning is: without a purpose, the violation of the primary meaning of the word by people like us nowadays is not obtainable through the use of a non-designative word. As they say:
'When the use of words is within our control, why would we use a non-designative one?' //

children.text:
syādetat /
mañcasthāḥ krośantīti vaktavye vināpi prayojanaṃ mañcāḥ krośantītyupacāro dṛṣṭa ityata
āha---api tu pramāṇāsaṃbhaveneti /

children.translated_text: The construction is: 'but also because of the impossibility of <s>pramāṇa</s>.'

children.text: nanvihāpi vināpi prayojanaṃ pramāṇāsaṃbhavamātreṇopacāro mañcāḥ krośantītivadbhaviṣyatītyata āda---lokaprayukteti lokaprayuktaśabdārthavat /
children.translated_text: Now, here too, even without a purpose, merely because of the impossibility of <s>pramāṇa</s>, there will be figurative usage, just like 'the platforms are shouting' — therefore he says — 'like the meaning of a word used in common parlance.'

children.text: upacāro 'pi laukiko na prayojanābhāvena śakyo 'pavadituṃ na lokaḥ paryanuyojyo yataḥ /
children.translated_text: Even figurative usage, being part of common parlance, cannot be dismissed merely because of the absence of purpose — for common usage is not to be questioned.

children.text: idānīntanastu asmadādiprayogaḥ prayojanābhāve na śakyaḥ paryanuyoktumityāśayenāha---na cedaṃ laukikamiti //
children.translated_text: But the usage of people like us nowadays — without a purpose, it cannot be justified — with this intention he says — 'and this is not common parlance.' //

One might object: when one should say 'those standing on the platform are shouting,' the figurative usage 'the platforms are shouting' is observed even without a purpose — therefore he says — 'but also because of the impossibility of <s>pramāṇa</s>.'

children.text:
apare tviti /
na dūṣaṇaviṣayatvamasiddhiryena na pakṣeṇa saṃbadhyeta,
api tvajñānam /
tacca pakṣaviṣayameveti na mukhyārthalaṅghanamityarthaḥ /
atrāpi pūrvoktaṃ prasaṅgamāha--tad yadīti /
tasmāt pakṣasyetīcchatā siddhyasiddhijñānājñāne pakṣadharmāvevābhyupagantavye /
yataḥ tayoḥ pakṣadharmatvāt etadbhavati siddhaḥ pakṣo 'siddhaśceti /
astu tarhyevamityata
āha---evaṃ satīti /
naiva draṣṭrādhāratā jñānasya viṣayatā ca bauddharāddhānte saṃbhavatīti bhāvaḥ /
śaṅkate atha mā bhūditi /
asti khalvālayajñānaṃ yadupāśritya ṣaḍapi pravṛttijñānāni jāyante /
tasmādālayapratyayo draṣṭā /
tatsthe eva siddhyasiddhī /
na pakṣasya tadviṣayatvāt tasyāpīti cet, kaḥ punarayaṃ viṣayabhāvaḥ?
children.translated_text: 'Others, however' — it is not the case that being the domain of refutation is non-establishment, such that it would not be connected with the position; rather, it is ignorance. And that pertains to the position alone — hence there is no violation of the primary meaning — this is the meaning. Here too he states the previously mentioned unwanted consequence — 'if that.' Therefore, one who desires that the position be [the domain of] establishment and non-establishment must accept that the knowledge and ignorance regarding establishment and non-establishment are properties of the position alone. Since those two are properties of the position, this obtains: the position is established and [the position is] unestablished. Let it be so — therefore he says — 'this being so.' Indeed, neither the property of being a locus for a knower nor the property of being an object is possible for knowledge in the Buddhist established doctrine — this is the import. He raises a doubt — 'now, let it not be so.' For there exists the store-consciousness (<s>ālayavijñāna</s>), dependent upon which even the six active cognitions (<s>pravṛttivijñāna</s>) arise. Therefore, the <s>ālaya</s>-cognition is the knower. Establishment and non-establishment reside precisely in it. Not in the position — since it is its object — and not in that [ālaya] either — so, what then is this relation of objecthood?

children.text:
tatkāraṇatvamiti cet? cakṣurādīnāmapi jñānakāraṇānāṃ viṣayatvaprasaṅgaḥ /
asataścākāraṇasya
aviṣayatvaprasaṅgaḥ /
jñānaprakāśyatvaṃ viṣayatvamiti cet---na, jñānenārthe prakāśājananāt tasmāt jñānasya tadasamavāyinaḥ
tadaviṣayasya ca draṣṭṛsthataiveti siddham /
nirākaroti---tathāpīti /
punaḥ śaṅkate---atha tathātathāne iti pramāṇayoga ityarthaḥ /
nirākaroti---tathāpīti /
tattvaṃ jijñāsuḥ pṛcchati---ke punarete iti /
suhṛdbhāvenottaramāha---vastudharmāviti /
yadyapi pramāṇayogāyogau prameyasya ca pramātuśca,
sādhanāsaṃbandhe kartṛtvānupapatteḥ, tathāpi prameyasya prādhānyāt tatraivābhidhānapratyayāviti prameyadharmāvucyete vyaktyavyaktī, na tu pramātṛdharmāviti /
siddhyasiddhyarthamiti arthaśabdānupapattiḥ /
kasmāt? vikalpānupapatteḥ /
vikalpamāha---arthaśabdaḥ khalviti /
iha sūtre dhananimittādivacanatārthaśabdasya na saṃbhavatīti trayamavaśiṣyata iti tredhā pravartata ityuktam /
children.translated_text: In this <s>sūtra</s>, the meanings of the word <s>artha</s> as wealth, cause, and the like are not possible — therefore three [meanings] remain, and thus it operates in three ways — this is what was said.

children.text: sādhanaṃ sādhanābhāso dūṣaṇaṃ dūṣaṇābhāsa iti caturvidhaṃ vākyam /
children.translated_text: A statement (<s>vākya</s>) is fourfold: proof (<s>sādhana</s>), pseudo-proof (<s>sādhanābhāsa</s>), refutation (<s>dūṣaṇa</s>), and pseudo-refutation (<s>dūṣaṇābhāsa</s>).
He rejects the first alternative — "that is not, first of all."
"That" means "among those, the middle" — this is the meaning.

If [one says] it is the cause of that [cognition]? Then the sense-organs too, being causes of cognition, would have the unwanted consequence of being objects.
And a non-existent [thing], being a non-cause,
would have the unwanted consequence of not being an object.
If [one says] objecthood is being illuminated by cognition — no, because cognition does not produce illumination in the object. Therefore it is established that cognition, not inhering in it [the object],
and not having it as its object, resides in the perceiver.
He refutes — "even so."
He objects again — "if the being-so-and-not-so" — meaning: the connection with <s>pramāṇa</s>.
He refutes — "even so."
Desiring to know the truth, he asks — "what then are these?"
With a friendly disposition, he answers — "properties of the real."
Although the connection and non-connection with <s>pramāṇa</s> belong both to the object of knowledge and to the knower,
since agency is impossible without connection to the means of proof, nevertheless, due to the primacy of the object of knowledge, the expressions and cognitions relate to it alone — thus they are called properties of the knowable (<s>prameya</s>), not properties of the knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>).
"For the purpose of establishment and non-establishment" — the word "purpose" (<s>artha</s>) is problematic.
Why? Because the alternative interpretations are impossible.
He states the alternatives — "the word artha, indeed."

children.text:
granthāntare yuktāyuktatvena viśeṣaṇāt caturvidhavākyasaṃgrahārtho hyuddeśe arthaśabdo vyākhyātaḥ /
na ca yuktāyuktatvaviśeṣaṇe caturvidhavākyasaṃgraho bhavati sādhanābhāsasaṃbandhinaḥ pakṣasya yuktatvābhāvāt dūṣaṇābhāsaṃbandhinaśca pratipakṣasyāyuktatvābhāvādityarthaḥ /
atha na sādhanādiyogo 'pi tu sādhyadharma eva sādhanānapekṣo yuktāyuktatvamiti śaṅkate---atha punariti /
nirākaroti---tathāpīti /
kuto vyāghāta
ityata āha---na hīti /
yadi pratyāyanaṃ siddhiḥ pratītiḥ, tathāpi sā pratyāyyā na saṃbhavati /
atha karaṇam? tathāpi karma karaṇaṃ na saṃbhavatīti vyāghāta ityarthaḥ /
dvitīyaṃ kalpamāśaṅkya nirākaroti---atha prayojana iti /
prayojanaṃ kāryam /
tanna kāraṇābhāsād
bhavitumarhati /
na hi vahniriti gṛhītaḥ khadyoto dahati pacati vetyarthaḥ /
tṛtīyaṃ kalpamāśaṅkya nirākaroti---athābhidheya
iti /
granthakāraḥ sūtrakāraḥ /
evaṃ tviti /
evaṃ sati siddhiśabdo 'siddhiśabdaśca vādaḥ syāt /
nanu dhananimittādayaḥ apyarthaśabdavācyāḥ santi,
te kasmādiha na gṛhyante ityata
children.translated_text:
In another work, since the word <s>artha</s> in the enumeration has been explained as serving to comprehend the fourfold statement through the qualification of being proper and improper —
But the fourfold comprehension of statements does not work through the qualification of proper and improper, because the thesis connected with a pseudo-proof lacks propriety, and the counter-thesis connected with a pseudo-refutation does not lack propriety — this is the meaning.
If [one says] it is not the connection with proof and the like, but rather the property of the <s>sādhya</s> itself — propriety and impropriety independent of proof — he objects: "if, however."
He refutes — "even so."
Why is there a contradiction?
— therefore he says — "for not."
If conviction is establishment and cognition, even so, that to-be-conveyed [cognition] is not possible.
If [it means] an instrument? Even so, it is contradictory that the object should be the instrument — this is the meaning.
Assuming and rejecting the second alternative — "if purpose."
Purpose means effect.
That cannot arise from a pseudo-cause.
For a firefly, apprehended as fire, neither burns nor cooks — this is the meaning.
Assuming and rejecting the third alternative — "if what is to be expressed."
The author of the treatise is the <s>sūtrakāra</s>.
"If thus" —
If so, the words "establishment" (<s>siddhi</s>) and "non-establishment" (<s>asiddhi</s>) would mean debate.
But wealth, cause, and the like are also expressible by the word <s>artha</s> — why are they not taken here? — therefore

children.text:
āha---tatra sūtre /
na cānyo 'rthaśabdasya viṣayaḥ saṃbhavati, na hi siddhirdhanaṃ vā svaparapakṣayoḥ sādhanaṃ vā nivṛttirvā saṃbhavatītyarthaḥ /
api ca vacanaviśeṣaṇapakṣe svaśātravyāghāta
ityāha---siddhyasiddhyarthaṃ vacanaṃ vāda
iti bruvāṇeneti /
naiyāyikahetudūṣaṇaṃ pūrvamidaṃ sūtram
uttaram /

children.translated_text: He concludes — "thus."
<s>Tantra</s> means <s>śāstra</s> (systematic treatise).
"And they contradict common practice."

children.text: avācakapadaprayogāt sādhanadūṣaṇābhāsavādinaśca vāditvena lokasiddhasyāvāditvāpādanāt siddhyasiddhiśabdayośca vādatvāpādanārthatvādityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Because of employing non-designating words, and because of reducing to non-debater status one who is established in the world as a debater by being a proponent of pseudo-proofs and pseudo-refutations, and because the words "establishment" and "non-establishment" serve the purpose of attributing the status of debate — this is the meaning.

He says — "in that <s>sūtra</s>."
And no other meaning of the word <s>artha</s> is possible — for neither establishment, nor wealth, nor proof of one's own or the other's position, nor cessation is possible — this is the meaning.
Moreover, in the alternative where [<s>artha</s>] qualifies the statement, there would be contradiction with one's own <s>śāstra</s>
— he says — "by one who says that a statement for the purpose of establishment and non-establishment is debate."
This <s>sūtra</s> was first a <s>Naiyāyika</s> reason-refutation;
the subsequent [one follows].

children.text:
sūtraṃ dūṣayitvā vṛttiṃ dūṣayati---yathā ceti /
svasya pakṣasyeti /
svasyātmīyasya pakṣasya /
na hi
children.translated_text:
Having criticized the <s>sūtra</s>, he criticizes the <s>vṛtti</s> (commentary) — "and as."
"Of one's own thesis" —
Of one's own, i.e., belonging to oneself, thesis.
For

children.text:
pakṣavyatirekeṇaṃ pakṣādhāraṃ sādhyaṃ jñānamanyad vā siddhiśabdābhidheyaṃ saṃbhavati, jñānasya puruṣādhāratayā anādhāratayā vā pakṣādhāratvānupapatteḥ, pakṣasya tu bhavet kenacit saṃbandhena yādṛśatādṛśenetyarthaḥ /
te sādhanadūṣaṇaiḥ ityatra pṛthagukte sādhanadūṣaṇe /
yuktāyuktatvābhyāṃ te yuktāyuktatve /
sādhanadūṣaṇairiti /
na hi karma karaṇaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ /
api ca yuktāyuktārthābhyāmabhede sādhanadūṣaṇapadamanarthakaṃ te ityanenaiva yuktāyuktatvāvamarṣiṇā gatārthatvādityāha---yuktāyuktatvaśabdābhyāṃ ceti /
atha na paryāyatā, api tu sāmānyaviśeṣabhāvaḥ
yuktāyuktatve sāmānyam, sādhanadūṣaṇe ca viśeṣa iti śaṅkate---atha manyase iti /
nirākaroti---na prathameti /
ubhayavyabhicāre viśeṣaṇāviśeṣyabhāve kāmacārādutpalairityuktam /
dvitīyaṃ kalpamāśaṅkya dūṣayati---yoga iti cediti /
na khalu yogo nāma bauddhānāṃ sādhyasādhanavṛttirdūṣyadūṣaṇavṛttirvā kaścidastītyarthaḥ /
api ca sāṃvṛto 'pi yogaḥ sādhyasādhanajñānādhīnanirūpaṇatayā nānirūpite sādhye nirūpito bhavati, nirūpaṇaṃ ca nirṇaya iti yoganirūpaṇāt prāk sādhyanirṇayāt kṛtaṃ yoganirūpaṇena sādhyanirṇayārtheneti /
yuktāyuktatvena karaṇenādhikaraṇapratyāyanamiti vyāghāta
ityāha---sādhaneneti /
bhavati jñāyate /
tṛtīyaṃ kalpamāśaṅkya nirākaroti---atha padārthasyeti /
yuktāyuktatvenādhikaraṇapratyāyanamiti yuktāyuktatvayoḥ karaṇatvaṃ darśitam tat tathātvātathātvapakṣe na saṃbhavati,
children.translated_text: That the substrate is conveyed by the instrument of propriety and impropriety has been shown as the instrumentality of propriety and impropriety — that is not possible in the alternative of being-so and not-being-so,
because of being the object [not the instrument].
This is what was stated — "those are what is to be distinguished, what is to be ascertained,

children.text: na tu vyavacchedasya paricchedasya sādhane iti //
children.translated_text: but not instruments of distinguishing or ascertaining."

apart from the thesis, no other substrate of the <s>sādhya</s> — whether cognition or anything else — that could be denoted by the word "establishment" is possible, because cognition, being located in a person or having no substrate, cannot have the thesis as its substrate; but the thesis could [have such a connection] by some relation of whatever kind — this is the meaning.
"Those, by proofs and refutations" — here proofs and refutations are mentioned separately.
By propriety and impropriety — those two are propriety and impropriety.
"By proofs and refutations" —
For it is contradictory that the object should be the instrument — this is the meaning.
Moreover, if the meanings of "proper" and "improper" are not different [from proof and refutation], the terms "proof" and "refutation" would be redundant, since the import is already conveyed by "propriety and impropriety" alone — he says: "and by the words propriety and impropriety."
If [one says] they are not synonymous, but stand in the relation of general and specific — propriety and impropriety being the general, and proof and refutation being the specific — he objects: "if you think."
He refutes — "not the first."
When there is deviation in both [directions], the relation of qualifier and qualified does not hold — hence the freedom [to choose] lotuses — it is said.
Assuming and criticizing the second alternative — "if connection."
For the Buddhists have no such thing as connection that is the relation of <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s>, or of <s>dūṣya</s> and <s>dūṣaṇa</s> — this is the meaning.
Moreover, even a conventional connection, being dependent for its determination on the knowledge of <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s>, cannot be determined before the <s>sādhya</s> is determined, and determination means ascertainment — therefore, before the determination of the connection, i.e., before the ascertainment of the <s>sādhya</s>, the determination of the connection has already served its purpose of ascertaining the <s>sādhya</s>.
That the substrate is conveyed by the instrument of propriety and impropriety is contradictory
— he says — "by proof."
"It becomes" means "it is known."
Assuming and refuting the third alternative — "if of the category."

children.text:
adhikaraṇapratyāyanamiti dūṣayati---adhikaraṇeti /
śāstrasaṃbandhaḥ prayojaneneti /
codayati---prāśnikapratyāyanāditi /
kaścit
codakaṃ pṛcchati---kiṃ kāraṇam?
tatpratyāyanāditi /
children.translated_text:
He criticizes "conveying the substrate" — "substrate."
"The connection of the <s>śāstra</s> with the purpose" —
He objects — "because of conveying to the questioner."
Someone
asks the objector — "what is the reason?"
"Because of conveying to that [questioner]."

children.text:
codakasyottaram---prativādi kileti /
siddhāntyāha---santamapyarthaṃ na pratipadyata
iti /
na khalvādhyātmikaśaktisaṃpannaḥ samāhitaḥ samagre sādhanaprayoge sati santamarthaṃ na pratipadyata iti saṃbhavatītyarthaḥ /
tathāvidhenāpi cet pratipattrā so 'rtho 'nyathā pratipannaḥ, kathamasau tathā sinnatyabhidhīyate ityāha---kathaṃ ceti /
śaṅkate---atha jigīṣutayā pratipadyamāno 'pīti /
kāmakāro 'nujñā /
nirākaroti---tathāpīti /
na pratipadyate pratipadyamāna
iti vyāhatam /
na cāyamunajñāniṣedho na pratipadyate iti vāde vītarāgakathātvena jigīṣāyā abhāvāditi bhāvaḥ /
yacca prāśnikapratyāyanāditi /
anyadīyena karaṇenānyaḥ pratipadyata iti subhāṣitam /
anyaviṣayasyeti anyāśritasyetyarthaḥ /
na cāyaṃ niyama iti /
na vāde prāśnikānāmupādānam,
daivāgatānāṃ tu na varjanamityarthaḥ /
vādasya jalpavitaṇḍābhyāmabhedam abhipretya codayati---yadā tu nāyamiti /

children.translated_text: Not accepting the meaning established in the intent, he resolves — "true."
He shows his own view — "not the threefold [classification]."
He criticizes — "not because the prohibition is by you yourselves."
He criticizes the non-acceptance of the threefold classification — "even what."

The answer to the objector — "the opponent, they say."
The proponent says — "even a real matter, he does not understand."
The meaning is: it is not possible that one who is endowed with inner capacity, concentrated, and in the presence of a complete proof, does not understand a real matter.
But if such a capable understander has understood the matter otherwise, how can it be said that he has not understood it properly? — he says — "and how."
He objects — "if, while understanding, [he acts] out of desire to win."
Free will means permission.
He refutes — "even so."
"Does not understand while understanding" — this is contradictory.
And this is not a prohibition of permission — "does not understand" — because in <s>vāda</s> (debate), being a dispassionate discourse, there is no desire to win — this is the meaning.
"And because of conveying to the questioner" —
That another understands through another's instrument — this is well said.
"Of what belongs to another" means "of what depends on another."
"And there is no such rule" —
In debate there is no inclusion of questioners;
but those who come by chance are not excluded — this is the meaning.
Intending the non-difference of debate from disputation (<s>jalpa</s>) and cavil (<s>vitaṇḍā</s>), he objects — "but when this."

children.text:
yaccoktaṃ vṛttau pakṣasiddhiviṣayam, etadapi dūṣayitumupanyasyati--yaccoktamiti /
na kāmataḥ vinā prayojanamiti /
vināpi prayojanaṃ pramāṇāsaṃbhavenāpīti yojanā /
sūtroktaṃ dūṣaṇaṃ vṛttau āha---tadarthaṃ vacanaṃ siddhyasiddhyarthamityarthaḥ /
adhikaraṇaṃ dūṣayati---adhikaraṇamiti /
na hi vāde prāśnikādhāramiti /
prāśnikā eva tāvad vāde na santi, abhyupetya
uktamiti /
śaṅkate--pratyāyanādhāratvāditi /
siddhiḥ pratyāyanaṃ tadādhārāḥ prāśnikā ityarthaḥ /
nirākaroti--neti /
śaṅkate--tasminniti /
daivamilite prāśnike satītyarthaḥ /
nirākaroti---neti /
na hi daivamilitaṃ kāraṇam, mā bhūd gardabho 'pi dhūmasya kāraṇamiti bhāvaḥ /
codayati, yadi prāśnikā na santi tadvāda iti /
tayorvādiprativādinorvādasya parīkṣā kā kasya ca tayorvādasya kva ca, asau parīkṣā prāśnikābhāve hi vādatatparīkṣātadadhikaraṇānāmajñānamityarthaḥ /
pariharati---sādhaneti /
vītarāgau hi vādiprativādināveva vādasvarūpajñānaṃ ca tatparīkṣāṃ ca kartuṃ śaknutaḥ,
tat kimatra prāśnikaiḥ? sādhanaprayogaḥ pakṣaviṣayaḥ, dūṣaṇaprayogaḥ sthāpanāviṣayaḥ iti vādasvarūpam /
sādhanadūṣaṇatadābhāsānāṃ parito jñānaṃ parīkṣā /
tadarthaṃ parīkṣārthaṃ tasmin vāde 'dhikāro vītarāgayoreva vādiprativādinoḥ /
children.translated_text: For that purpose — for the purpose of examination — in that debate, the authority belongs only to the dispassionate proponent and opponent.
This is the answer to the question "where?"

children.text: tasmāt saptamyartho 'dhikaraṇārthaḥ parābhimataḥ prāśnika iti yāvat /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the meaning of the locative — the meaning of substrate — is the questioner according to the opponent's view.
That [substrate] does not exist — for the dispassionate proponent and opponent alone [suffice] until the completion of the discourse — this is the meaning.

And what was stated in the <s>vṛtti</s> concerning the establishment of the thesis — he presents that too for criticism — "and what was said."
"Not willfully, without purpose" —
Even without purpose, [it is not possible] due to the impossibility of <s>pramāṇa</s> — this is the construal.
He states the criticism from the <s>sūtra</s> in the <s>vṛtti</s> — "the statement for that purpose, for the purpose of establishment and non-establishment" — this is the meaning.
He criticizes the substrate — "substrate."
For in debate there is no substrate in the questioners.
Questioners themselves are not present in debate at all — this is said on the assumption [of the opponent's view].
He objects — "because of being the substrate of conveying."
Establishment is conveying; the questioners are its substrate — this is the meaning.
He refutes — "no."
He objects — "when he is present."
Meaning: when a questioner is present by chance.
He refutes — "no."
For what comes together by chance is not a cause; otherwise even a donkey might be a cause of smoke — this is the meaning.
He objects — if questioners are not present, then as for that debate —
What is the examination of that debate between the two — the proponent and the opponent — and of whom is it, and where is that examination of the debate? For in the absence of questioners, there is ignorance of the debate, its examination, and its substrate — this is the meaning.
He resolves — "by proof."
For the dispassionate proponent and opponent themselves are capable of knowing the nature of debate and conducting its examination —
so what need is there for questioners? The employment of proof concerns the thesis; the employment of refutation concerns the counter-establishment — this is the nature of debate.
The thorough knowledge of proofs, refutations, and their semblances is the examination.

children.text:
yadapi vṛttau coditaṃ yadi siddhyasiddhyarthaṃ vacanaṃ vādaḥ, tataḥ prāśnikaprativādinoḥ priyāpriyavacasi rathyāvāde prasaṅga iti tadapyatinirbījamityāha---yadapīti /
na hi priyāpriyavacasaḥ sākṣāt pāramparyeṇa vā siddhyasiddhyarthatā, nāpi sādhanadūṣaṇayuktāyuktatvaviśeṣaṇasaṃbandhaḥ
tasmādevaṃvādī nottarārhaḥ /
na hyunmattāya
children.translated_text:
And what was objected in the <s>vṛtti</s> — that if a statement for the purpose of establishment and non-establishment is debate, then the pleasant and unpleasant utterances of questioners and opponents in a street-argument would be entailed — that too is utterly baseless, he says — "even what."
For pleasant and unpleasant utterances do not, either directly or indirectly, have the character of being for establishment and non-establishment, nor do they have the connection with the qualification of propriety and impropriety through proof and refutation —
therefore such an objector does not deserve an answer.
For no sane person

children.text:
kaścidanunmatta
uttaramāha, bruvāṇo vā so 'pyunmattaḥ syāt /
tadidamuktam---dattaḥ svahasta iti /
pūrvaṃ siddhyasiddhyarthamiti, aparaṃ yuktāyuktatvamiti,
ubhayorapyanena codyenāsaṃbandhāt /
yadi tvavaśyam uttaraṃ vācyam, tato varamevaṃ vaktavyamityāha---yadi tviti /
seyaṃ sūkṣmekṣikā parairiha kṛteti tadanubandhena vārttikakṛtāpi kṛteti//1 //
children.translated_text:
gives an answer to a madman; and one who does so would himself be mad.
This is what was stated — "the hand has been given" [i.e., the point is conceded].
The first [objection concerns] "for the purpose of establishment and non-establishment"; the second, "propriety and impropriety" —
both of these have no connection with this objection.
But if an answer must necessarily be given, then it is better to say it thus — he says "if, however."
This subtle examination was conducted here by the opponents, and in connection with that, by the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> as well. //1//

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.2: <s>Jalpa</s> (disputation) is [debate] as described above, accompanied by quibble (<s>chala</s>), futile objection (<s>jāti</s>), and grounds for defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>) in the [establishment and] censure of proof.
Following the order of enumeration, after the definition of <s>vāda</s> (debate), he defines <s>jalpa</s> (disputation) — "as described... disputation" //2//

children.text:
atrāpi samānajātīyābhyāṃ vādavitaṇḍābhyāmasamānajātīyebhyaḥ pramāṇādibhyo vyavacchedo jalpasya sūtrārthaḥ /
yathoktopapannapadārthaṃ vyācaṣṭe---samastamiti /
codayati---yathoktopapanna iti na yuktamiti /
nigrahasthānaniyamasya pramāṇatarkasādhanopālambhābhiprāyaniyamasya ca jalpe 'bhāvāt, bhāve vā vādajalpayorabhedaprasaṅgāt,
vādalakṣaṇasya ca jalpavyāpakatvena vyabhicāraprasaṅgād
yathoktopapanna ityetadanupapannamityarthaḥ /
pariharati---naiṣa doṣa iti /
uktamātramiha saṃbhavāt yogyatāsaṃbhavād
gṛhyate, na tvanukto 'rthalabhyo niyamaḥ /
na hyasau sūtrapadaśravaṇamātrāt pratīyate, api tu tadarthe pratīte tasyānyataḥ siddhau satyāṃ gamyata iti pramāṇatarkasādhanopālambha ityetadatidiśyata
iti uktamātropalakṣaṇaparam /
tena pramāṇatarkasādhanopālambha pañcāvayavopapannaḥ siddhāntāviruddhaḥ pakṣapratipakṣaparigraha ityetasya vādapadavarjaṃ samastasya lakṣaṇasyātideśaḥ /
niyamastvārtho na saṃbadhyata iti siddham /

children.translated_text: The meaning is: 'merely the definition' means what has been stated, not the meaning [behind it] nor the defined term.
He gives an example of this very [point] — 'as elsewhere, in the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> system.'

children.text: na niyamārthe pade ityupalakṣaṇam, na pramāṇatarkasādhanopālambhapadalabhyo 'bhiprāyaniyama
children.translated_text: 'Not in a word that has a restrictive meaning' — this is an indication; 'nor the restriction of intention obtained from the words proof-through-pramāṇa-and-tarka'
— this too should be seen [as included]. //

Here too, the purport of the <s>sūtra</s> is to differentiate <s>jalpa</s> (wrangling) from <s>vāda</s> (discussion) and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavil), which are of the same type, and from <s>pramāṇa</s> and the like, which are of a different type. / He explains the meaning of the terms as they have been stated to be justified — 'the whole' etc. / He objects — 'it is not proper to say that [it is] as stated and justified' etc. / Because in <s>jalpa</s>, the restriction to points of defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>) and the restriction to the intention of proof through <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s> are absent — or if present, there would be the unwanted consequence of non-difference between <s>vāda</s> and <s>jalpa</s>, / and because the definition of <s>vāda</s> pervades <s>jalpa</s>, there would be the unwanted consequence of deviation — / therefore 'as stated and justified' is unjustified — this is the meaning. / He resolves — 'this is no fault' etc. / Here, only what has been stated, as far as it is possible, is taken through the fitness [of applicability], not the restriction obtained from the unstated meaning. / For that [restriction] is not understood from the mere hearing of the <s>sūtra</s> words, but rather, when its meaning is understood, and when it is established from another source, it is understood — thus 'proof through <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s>' is extended, / being directed merely to indicating what has been stated. / Therefore, the extension is of the entire definition — 'proof through <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s>, endowed with the five members, not contradicted by the established doctrine, adopting thesis and counter-thesis' — except for the word <s>vāda</s> (debate). / But the restriction does not apply as a meaning — this is established.

children.text:
pakṣāntaramāha---atha veti /
yathā gobhiryukto ratho goratha iti yuktapadalopa
iti /
na hi niyamārthayoriti etadapyupalakṣaṇa pūrvavadeva /
iha vādalakṣaṇaṃ paṭhatā bhāṣyakāreṇa niyamo 'pyatidiṣṭa iti manvānaścodayati---bhāṣyam
idānīmiti /
pariharati---na setreti /
jalpalakṣaṇānukūlo yaḥ pāṭhakramaḥ, tato 'rthasvarūpamātraṃ pratīyate na tvārtho 'rtha ityarthaḥ /
yadupapannam uktamātramityarthaḥ /
atra bhāṣyakāreṇa chalādīnāṃ niṣedhārthatayā sādhanāṅgabhāvamākṣipya parapakṣavighātena svapakṣarakṣaṇādaṅgabhāva
iti darśitam /
tadetad vārttikakāra ākṣipati---chalajātinigrahasthānairiti /
tat kiṃ nigrahasthānānyapyayuktāni, ca caitacchakyamityata āha---chalaṃ tāvaditi /
chalajātyorākṣeptavyayoḥ saṃpātāyātāni nigrahasthānānītyabhiprāyaḥ /

children.translated_text: He raises the resolution stated in the <s>bhāṣya</s> as a doubt — 'being a component'
'thus if' etc.
He refutes — 'even this' etc.

He counts [a total of] one hundred and thirty-six — 'therein, pervading the <s>sādhya</s>' etc. / In this set of sixteen [possibilities for the first triad], from the distinction of properties — pervading the <s>sādhya</s>, existing in part of the <s>sādhya</s>, and [their combinations with the] property-distinctions — a pair of sixteen [each] from the distinction of unestablished-ness of the qualifier and the qualified — makes sixty-four. / Similarly, from the distinction of capable and incapable qualifier and qualified — another sixty-four. / This pair of sixty-fours makes one hundred and twenty-eight, which together with the first set of sixteen makes one hundred and thirty-six. / He gives examples of the specific properties that pervade the <s>sādhya</s> — 'therein' etc. / Through pervasion and non-pervasion of the <s>vipakṣa</s> (dissimilar instance), the first and second are common (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>); the third is a positive-and-negative-concomitant reason — a genuine reason that pervades the <s>sādhya</s> and its class. / Through pervasion and non-pervasion of the <s>vipakṣa</s>, the fourth and fifth are contradictory pseudo-reasons. / Where there is no occurrence in the <s>vipakṣa</s>, he shows — 'like a dyad' etc. / The sixth, having neither a similar nor a dissimilar instance, is uncommon (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>) — hence / he says — 'like a pot and the like' etc. / The seventh and eighth, through pervasion and non-pervasion of the <s>vipakṣa</s>, are common [pseudo-reasons]. / The ninth, occurring in part of the similar instance, is a positive-and-negative-concomitant genuine reason. / The tenth and eleventh, through pervasion and non-pervasion of the similar instance, are positive-concomitant genuine reasons.

Since <s>samavāya</s> (inherence), being without a substrate, is visually perceptible [in the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> view] — to this he says: "in the <s>Aulūkya</s> (Vaiśeṣika) position" etc.
