tadevamanantarābhyāṃ dvānavataśatābhyāṃ śatatrayaṃ caturaśītaṃ yat tadevāṣṭāviṃśakaśatābhyāṃ dvānavatena ca śatena saṃpiṇḍitaṃ dvātriṃśaduttarāṣṭaśatī vikārabhūtā bhavati /
aṣṭācatvāriśat prakṛtayaḥ paścāt niveśanīyā iti /
children.translated_text:
Similarly, [reasons with] unestablished-substrate qualifier and qualified, through unestablished-for-both and unestablished-for-one-party, [yield] one hundred and twenty-eight.
Here too, "thirty-two" should be explained as before.
Only "one party" is intended here, not the distinction between proponent and opponent.
These unestablished-substrate [reasons], as before through the divisions of qualifier and qualified in different substrata, doubtful qualifier and qualified, and incompetent qualifier and qualified — with three sets of sixty-four — [yield] two hundred and ninety-two.
Thus, the three hundred and eighty-four from the two immediately preceding [sets of] two hundred and ninety-two, combined with the one hundred and twenty-eight and the [other] two hundred and ninety-two, yield eight hundred and thirty-two as derivative forms.
The forty-eight basic forms are to be added afterwards.

children.text:
ubhayāprasiddhāśrayaviśeṣyam
udāharati---yathā agnimān deśo dhūmavattvāt /
uktaṃ hi prāg yathā na deśo 'gnimattayā sādhyo 'pi tu dhūmaviśeṣa eveti /
anyatarāsiddhāśrayodāharaṇamāha---asti cātmā icchādiguṇatvāditi /
āśrayāsiddhaviśeṣaṇādayo 'pyuhanīyāḥ /
asamarthāvyāpakāsiddhaviśeṣaṇānāmudāharaṇam /
asamarthāśca te 'vyāpakāśca, vyadhikaraṇatayā asiddhāśceti vigradaḥ /
anityaḥ śabdaḥ prayatnānantarīyakatve sati kṛtakatvāditi kṛtakatvasyaiva viśeṣyasya sāmarthyādasamarthamanityatve prayatnānantarīyakatvam,
avyāpakaṃ ca stanayitnuśabdānāmavyāpakatvāt /
vyadhikaraṇatayā asiddhaṃ ca koṣṭhavāyutālvādikriyāyāṃ eva prayatnānantarīyakatvam,
na tvādyasyāpi śabdasya, prāgeva tu śrotrasamavāyina
children.translated_text: but not of the initial sound itself, and even less of the sound that inheres in the ear.
Thus.
And "because of being contingent upon effort, given that it is produced" should be seen as an example of incompetent, non-pervading, unestablished qualifieds.

He gives an example of [a reason with] a qualified whose substrate is unestablished for both parties — "just as the place possesses fire, because of possessing smoke."
For it was said earlier that it is not the place that is to be proved as possessing fire, but rather a specific kind of smoke.
He gives an example of [a reason with] a substrate unestablished for one party — "the self exists, because of being the substrate of qualities like desire etc."
Unestablished-substrate qualifiers and the rest should also be inferred.
[This is] an example of incompetent, non-pervading, unestablished qualifiers.
They are incompetent and non-pervading, and unestablished through being in different substrata — this is the analysis.
"Sound is non-eternal, because of being produced, given that it is contingent upon effort" — by the very competence of the qualified "being produced," "being contingent upon effort" is incompetent for [proving] non-eternality,
and it is also non-pervading because it does not pervade thunder-sounds.
And it is unestablished through being in different substrata, since being contingent upon effort exists only in activities of the chest, palate, etc.,

children.text:
vaibhavena tvasiddhatāvarjamudāharati---avyāpakāsamarthaviśeṣyāṇāmudāharaṇam---anityaḥ śabdaḥ pratyayabhedabheditvenopalabhyamānatvāt /
upalabhyamānatvaṃ hi nitye 'pyastīti vyabhicārādasamartham /
kāraṇabhedabheditvameva tu viśeṣaṇaṃ samarthamavyabhicārāditi /
kevalavyadhikaraṇaviśeṣyāṇāmudāharaṇam
asti pradhānaṃ bhedānāṃ goghaṭādīnāṃ sukhaduḥkhamohātmakatvenānvayadarśanāditi /
anvayadarśanaṃ hi bhedādhikaraṇatayā na pradhānadhikaraṇamiti,
vyadhikaraṇamiti vyadhikaraṇaṃ viśeṣyam /

children.translated_text: An example of mere qualifiers-in-different-substrata — "form, taste, smell, touch, and sound"

children.text: candanaśabdādatyantaṃ vibhinnārthāḥ samudāyasamudāyyasaṃbhave sati rūpādīnāmarthānāṃ rūpādiśabdānāṃ ca tena candanaśabdena vyapadiśyamānatvāt /
children.translated_text: are completely different in meaning from the word "sandalwood" — because, given the possibility that the aggregate and its parts [refer to the same thing], the objects form etc. and the words "form" etc. are designated by that word "sandalwood."

children.text: candanasya rūpādaya iti samudāyasamudāyyasaṃbhavo rūpādiṣu vyapadeśaśca rūpādiśabdeṣviti vyadhikaraṇaṃ viśeṣaṇamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: "The form etc. of sandalwood" — the possibility of aggregate and parts is in form etc., and the designation is in the words "form" etc. — hence the qualifier is in a different substratum — this is the meaning.
By this elaboration, eight hundred and thirty-two have been shown.

But he gives examples extensively, excluding unestablishedness — an example of non-pervading, incompetent qualifieds: "sound is non-eternal, because of being perceived as differentiated by differentiation of cognition."
For "being perceived" exists even in the eternal, so it is incompetent due to deviation.
But "being differentiated by differentiation of causes" as a qualifier is competent due to non-deviation.
An example of mere qualifieds-in-different-substrata:
"<s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial nature) exists, because the various things like cows, pots, etc. are seen to be concomitant with [the <s>Pradhāna</s>] through having the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion."
For the observation of concomitance, being in the substrate of the diverse [things], is not in the substrate of <s>Pradhāna</s>,
hence it is a qualified in a different substratum.

children.text:
saṃprati dvānavataśatayugmāntaraṃ darśayitumudāharaṇamāha---anyathāsiddhodāharaṇaṃ nityaḥ śabdo 'bhyāsāt /
seyaṃ kriyābhyāvṛttiryathā śabdānityatve 'pyupapadyate tathā dvitīye darśayiṣyate /
siṃhāvalokitanyāyena vyadhikaraṇaviśeṣyaṃ sandigdhaviśeṣaṇamudāharati---sandigdhāpratiddheti /
viśeṣaṇaśabdaḥ tantreṇa viśeṣaṇe viśeṣye ca karmakaraṇasādhanatayā prayukto vartate /
tena sandigdhaṃ viśeṣaṇam aprasiddhaṃ vyadhikaraṇatayā viśeṣyaṃ yeṣāṃ teṣāmudāharaṇamityarthaḥ /
yathā sandihyamāne dhūmādibhāve 'gnimān deśo dhūmavattve sati prakāśakatvāt, dhūmavattvaṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ sandigdadham /
prakāśakatvaṃ ca viśeṣyaṃ vyadhikaraṇam /

children.translated_text: For that [luminosity] is indeed a property of fire, not of the place.
He shows an example of those with an unestablished qualifier and a doubtful qualified — "conversely" etc.
"Unestablished" should also be understood.
"The place possesses fire, because of possessing smoke, given that it is luminous."

Now, to show another pair of two hundred and ninety-two, he gives an example — an example of the otherwise-established (<s>anyathāsiddha</s>): "sound is eternal, because of repetition."
This repetition of action — how it is possible even when sound is non-eternal — will be shown in the second [book].
By the method of backward glance (<s>siṃhāvalokita</s>), he gives an example of a qualified in a different substratum with a doubtful qualifier — "doubtful and unestablished" etc.
The word "qualifier" is used in a combined manner for both qualifier and qualified, in the sense of object, instrument, and means.
Thus, those whose qualifier is doubtful and whose qualified is unestablished through being in a different substratum — their example is the meaning.
For instance, when the possession of smoke etc. is doubtful: "the place possesses fire, because of being luminous, given that it possesses smoke" — "possessing smoke" is a doubtful qualifier.
And "being luminous" is a qualified in a different substratum.

children.text:
saṃprati dvānavataśatayugmāntaraṃ darśayituṃ bhūmiracanāṃ karoti---evamiti /
ye ye sandigdhāsiddhā vyāpakāvyāpakabhedena dvātriṃśat ta
evobhayānyatarāsiddhyā catuḥṣaṣṭirbhavanti tataḥ kimityata āha--te catuḥṣaṣṭitāmāpannāḥ pūrvavadbhedena vyadhikaraṇaviśeṣaṇaviśeṣyasandigdhaviśeṣaṇaviśeṣyāsamarthaviśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhedena tāvaccatuḥṣaṣṭitrayamityekaṃ dvānavataṃ śatam /
apare cāśrayāsiddhavyadhikaraṇaviśeṣaṇaviśeṣyasandigdhaviśeṣaṇaviśeṣyāsamarthaviśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhedena dvānavataṃ śatam /
tadidaṃ
children.translated_text:
Now, to show another pair of two hundred and ninety-two, he prepares the ground — "thus" etc.
The thirty-two doubtful-unestablished [reasons], divided into pervading and non-pervading, when varied by both-party and one-party unestablishedness, become sixty-four. Then what? — to this he says: those that have attained the sixty-four, as before through the divisions of qualifier and qualified in different substrata, doubtful qualifier and qualified, and incompetent qualifier and qualified — yield one set of three sixty-fours, i.e., one [group of] two hundred and ninety-two.
Another [group of] two hundred and ninety-two [comes from] the divisions of substrate-unestablished, different-substratum qualifier and qualified, doubtful qualifier and qualified, and incompetent qualifier and qualified.
This
[yields] three hundred and eighty-four based on the doubtful-unestablished.
He states another pair of two hundred and ninety-two based on the otherwise-established (<s>anyathāsiddha</s>) — "thus the variety of the otherwise-established should be seen."

punaśca sa

children.translated_text:
For the variety of the otherwise-established too, through the divisions of qualifier and qualified in different substrata, doubtful and incompetent qualifier and qualified, yields three sets of sixty-four.
And again that very otherwise-established, through the divisions of substrate-unestablished, different-substratum qualifier and qualified, doubtful and incompetent qualifier and qualified, yields three sets of sixty-four — thus from the pair of two hundred and ninety-two, [we get] three hundred and eighty-four.
He states yet another pair of two hundred and ninety-two — "thus contradictory qualifiers and contradictory qualifieds" etc.
For the contradictory qualifier and qualified too, through the divisions of qualifier and qualified in different substrata, doubtful and incompetent qualifier and qualified, and substrate-unestablished different-substratum
qualifier and qualified, doubtful and incompetent qualifier and qualified, [yield] three hundred and eighty-four.

children.text: tadevamebhistribhiścaturaśītaiḥ śatatrayairdvipañcāśacchatottaraṃ sahasramekam, dvātriṃśaduttarayā aṣṭaśatyā sahasramekaṃ caturaśītisahitā ca navaśatī /
children.translated_text: Thus, by these three [sets of] three hundred and eighty-four, [we get] one thousand one hundred and fifty-two; together with the eight hundred and thirty-two, [that gives] one thousand nine hundred and eighty-four.

children.text: tadevaṃ prakṛtibhūtāṣṭā catvāriṃśatprakṣepeṇa saṃpiṇḍitaṃ dvātriṃśe dve sahasre bhavata iti //
children.translated_text: Thus, with the addition of the forty-eight basic forms, the total combined [number] is two thousand and thirty-two.

children.text:
tanna asatvāditi /
pañcānāṃ caturṇāṃ vā rūpāṇāṃ saṃpattiravyabhicāraḥ /
sa caikasmin viṣaye viruddhayorna saṃbhavati,
antato 'satpratipakṣasyaiva rūpasyābhāvādityarthaḥ /
pañcānāṃ hetūnāmiti /
sapakṣavyāptyavyāptibhyāmanvayī dvedhā,
children.translated_text:
This is not so, because of non-existence. The fulfillment of five or four characteristics constitutes non-deviation.
And that is not possible in a single subject for contradictory [reasons],
since at the very least the characteristic of having no established counter-thesis would be absent — this is the meaning.
"Of the five reasons" — the <s>anvayī</s> (positive concomitance) reason is twofold through pervading and non-pervading the similar instances.

children.text:
vyatirekyekaḥ, anvayavyatirekyapi sapakṣavyāptpavyāptibhyāṃ dvedheti pañca hetavaḥ /

sarūpaḥ anvayino 'nvayī,

iti /

children.translated_text: He objects — "from the definition itself" etc.
He resolves — "it is not purposeless" etc.

children.text: yatparo hi śabdastatrāsau pramāṇam, samānāsamānajātīyavyavacchedakaṃ ca lakṣaṇasūtramiti tatraiva pramāṇam na tviyattāyāmatatparatvāt /
children.translated_text: For the word is an authority regarding that to which it primarily refers, and the definition-<s>sūtra</s>, being a differentiator from things of the same and different classes, is an authority only regarding that — not regarding quantity, since it is not directed toward that.
And it [the definition] does not seek [quantity], since even when [the varieties] exist, non-definition is possible due to inapplicability — just as with other objects of knowledge. //4//

The <s>vyatirekī</s> (negative concomitance) reason is one; the <s>anvayavyatirekī</s> (both positive and negative) is also twofold through pervading and non-pervading the similar instances — thus there are five reasons.
Due to the obstruction of the five reasons by similar and dissimilar [reasons], there are five groups of five.
The similar of the <s>anvayī</s> is an <s>anvayī</s>,
of the <s>vyatirekī</s> a <s>vyatirekī</s>, of the <s>anvayavyatirekī</s> an <s>anvayavyatirekī</s>.
And the dissimilar of the <s>anvayī</s> and the rest is a <s>vyatirekī</s> and the rest; the obstruction is by that. This has been stated: in each of the <s>anvayī</s> and the rest, there are five reasons — similar and dissimilar — that obstruct, so by five groups of five there are twenty-five contradictory-non-deviating [combinations].
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.5: The inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) is the deviating (<s>savyabhicāra</s>).

children.text: tadevamarthākṣiptasāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ vibhāgaṃ darśayitvā viśeṣalakṣaṇamavatārayati bhāṣyakāraḥ, teṣāṃ hetvābhāsānāṃ madhye anai---raḥ // 5 //
children.translated_text: Having thus shown the classification with the general definition implied by the meaning, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> introduces the specific definition — among these pseudo-reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>), the inconclusive //5//

children.text:
atra cānaikāntikasavyabhicāraśabdau paryāyau puruṣabhedāpekṣayā lakṣyalakṣaṇatvenāvasthitau /
yasyānaikāntikapadārtho 'prasiddhaḥ prasiddhaśca savyabhicārapadārthaḥ, taṃ pratyanaikāntika iti lakṣyatirdeśaḥ, savyabhicāra iti lakṣaṇam /
yasya tu savyabhicārapadārtho 'prasiddhaḥ prasiddhaścānaikāntikapadārthastaṃ prati savyabhicāra iti lakṣyanirdeśaḥ, anaikāntika
iti lakṣaṇam /
tatra savyabhicāra iti lakṣaṇapadaṃ kakṣīkṛtyāha bhāṣyakāraḥ vyabhicāra
ekatrāvyavasthitiḥ /
etaduktaṃ bhavati /
savyabhicārapadaṃ nirvacanasāmarthyāt lakṣaṇapadamiti /
anaikāntikapadalakṣaṇapakṣe bhāṣyakāroktam anityatvamapyeko 'nta ityādi /
tad vārttikakāraḥ paryudāsābhiprāyeṇa vyācaṣṭe---ekasminnante niyata aikāntika iti /
na heturaikāntiko yena tadanyatvena hetvābhāsamātrasaṃgrahādekajātīyatvena hetvābhāsānāṃ vibhāgasūtravirodhaḥ syāt,
kiṃ tvekasminnante yo niyataḥ sa aikāntikaḥ,
tadviparyayādanaikāntiko 'niyato 'nityatve ca nityatve cānvayena ca vyatirekeṇa cobhayapakṣagāmīti yāvat /
na caivaṃbhūtā viruddhādayo hetvābhāsā ityabhiprāyaḥ /
tadevam anaikāntikaḥ savyabhicāraḥ iti sthite pṛcchati---kaḥ punariti /

children.translated_text: The answer — "that which is of the same class as what is to be proved" etc.

children.text: avagata eṣa vyabhicāra iti, anaikāntikapadavācyatāsya kathamityata āha--anyatra sarvo 'yamiti /
children.translated_text: "This deviation is understood" — how then does it come to be denoted by the word <s>anaikāntika</s>? To this he says: "all of this elsewhere" etc.
But since the category of <s>prameya</s> (objects of knowledge) is all-pervading, there is no end or exclusion from it — therefore
It is said: "except for <s>prameya</s> (the object of knowledge)."

Here the words <s>anaikāntika</s> (inconclusive) and <s>savyabhicāra</s> (deviating) are synonyms, but depending on different persons, they are established as definiendum and definition.
For one to whom the meaning of the word <s>anaikāntika</s> is unknown but the meaning of <s>savyabhicāra</s> is known, "<s>anaikāntika</s>" is the indication of the definiendum and "<s>savyabhicāra</s>" is the definition.
But for one to whom the meaning of <s>savyabhicāra</s> is unknown but the meaning of <s>anaikāntika</s> is known, "<s>savyabhicāra</s>" is the indication of the definiendum and "<s>anaikāntika</s>" is the definition.
Among these, taking <s>savyabhicāra</s> as the definition-word, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> says: "<s>vyabhicāra</s> (deviation) is non-fixedness in one place."
What has been stated is this: the word <s>savyabhicāra</s>, by the force of its etymological derivation, is a definition-word.
In the alternative where <s>anaikāntika</s> is the definition-word, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> has said: "non-eternality too is one conclusion" etc.
The <s>Vārttikakāra</s> explains this with the intent of exclusion (<s>paryudāsa</s>) — "that which is fixed in one conclusion is <s>aikāntika</s> (conclusive)."
The reason is not [simply] <s>aikāntika</s> [in the sense that its non-being] would, by being the opposite, merely include pseudo-reasons in general under a single class and thus contradict the classification-<s>sūtra</s>.
Rather, that which is fixed in one conclusion is <s>aikāntika</s>,
and its opposite, the <s>anaikāntika</s>, is unfixed, going to both sides — towards both non-eternality and eternality, through both positive and negative concomitance.
And the pseudo-reasons such as the contradictory etc. are not of this nature — this is the intent.
Thus, with "<s>anaikāntika</s> is <s>savyabhicāra</s>" established, he asks — "what then?"

children.text:
atra bauddhaiḥ yad vikalpya dūṣaṇamuktam, tadupanyasyati--anaikāntika
iti /
kiṃ punarayamiti /
aikāntiko hetuḥ /
tato 'nyaḥ sarva eva hetvābhāsa ityarthaḥ /
dvitīyaṃ kalpaṃ dūṣayati---atha prasajyeti /
tathāpi hetorabhāvo 'naikāntikaḥ /
na cāsau savyabhicāraḥ /
bhāvadharmau hi vyabhicārāvyabhicārau nābhāve sarvopākhyāvirahiṇi yujyete ityarthaḥ /
tadetat śākyadūṣaṇaṃ nirākaroti---nāyaṃ paryudāsapakṣa iti /
paryudāsapakṣastāvadasmākamabhimata upapannataraśca,
kevalamayaṃ prasajyapratiṣedhavallabhastamāsthāya sarvaṃ dūṣayatīti tamevāṅgīkṛtya sarvatra brūma
children.translated_text: Here, the criticism stated by the Buddhists through alternatives is presented — 'inconclusive.' 'What then is this?' — a conclusive (<s>aikāntika</s>) reason. Everything other than that is a pseudo-reason (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) — this is the meaning. He criticizes the second alternative — 'now, by implicative negation (<s>prasajya</s>).' Even so, the absence of the reason is what is inconclusive. And that is not [the same as] the deviant. For deviation and non-deviation are positive properties and are not appropriate in an absence, which is devoid of all designations — this is the meaning. He refutes this Buddhist criticism — 'this is not the <s>paryudāsa</s> (exclusion) view.' The <s>paryudāsa</s> view is indeed our accepted one and is more tenable. But this [Buddhist], being fond of the <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s> (simple negation) [interpretation], criticizes everything by resorting to it; so we accept that very [interpretation] and speak [accordingly] everywhere —

children.text: na punarabrāhmaṇādāvapi vārtikakārasya prasajyapratiṣedho 'bhimataḥ, kiṃ tu paryudāsa
children.translated_text: But even in [expressions like] 'non-Brahmin' and the like, the <s>vārttikakāra</s>'s view is not <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s> (simple negation), but rather <s>paryudāsa</s> (exclusion)
alone.
But even there, the statement of <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s> is by way of concession.

children.text: na hi prasajyapratiṣedho 'pi tucchaḥ, api tu kasyacid vastuno 'bhāvena viśiṣṭaṃ kiñcideva vastvityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: For even <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s> is not vacuous; rather, it [refers to] some real entity qualified by the absence of some [other] entity — this is the meaning. //
this is the resolution of one who has this intention.

children.text:
atra bhāṣyam---nidarśanaṃ nityaḥ śabdo 'sparśatvāt iti /
vaidharmye dṛṣṭāntam āha---sparśavāniti /
anityaḥ
children.translated_text: Here the <s>bhāṣya</s> — 'an illustration: sound is eternal, because of being intangible.' He states the example for dissimilarity — 'tangible': non-eternal,

children.text:

children.translated_text: Here the <s>vārttikakāra</s> extracts the essential nature of intangibility as a reason, preceded by a question — 'what then is that intangibility?' — meaning being different from [what is tangible like] sound. Or [it is] existence qualified by inherence, or inherence qualified by existence — through positive and negative concomitance — this is the meaning. And the use of the word in the sentence-meaning, like the word '<s>aśrotriya</s>' (non-Vedic-scholar), [functions in the same way] — thus he says — 'sentence-meaning.' He objects regarding the alternative that defines it as '<s>anaikāntika</s>' (inconclusive) — 'extension.' If somewhere in a treatise-passage the inconclusive has been described, then being extended from that passage to this [context], its form being known, it would define the deviant here. But it has not been mentioned anywhere in any treatise-passage — this is the meaning. He resolves — 'this is not so.' The meaning is: it has been stated as something well-known in common knowledge. Thinking that the inconclusive is restricted at both ends by positive concomitance alone, he raises a doubt — 'because of non-pervasiveness.' He resolves — 'no.' 'By exclusion' — sometimes the positive concomitance is restricted at both ends; sometimes the negative concomitance is — this is the meaning. He presents the view of some — 'others, however.' He criticizes — 'but by them.' Deviation in the example does not constitute deviation in the definition, because they are different. Examiners do not rely on the example, but on the definition — this is the meaning. //5//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.6: Having accepted an established doctrine (<s>siddhānta</s>), [a reason] that contradicts it is the contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>).

children.translated_text: Established... contradictory. //6// He asks — 'what is [the meaning] of this <s>sūtra</s>?' For a reason, being non-conscious, does not accept an established doctrine; and the conscious person who accepts it is not characterized by any of the definitions of reason — so it is not a pseudo-reason. And the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) is not the established doctrine — so what contradicts it would not be contradictory — this is the import. The answer — 'that which contradicts an accepted meaning is contradictory: the person's acceptance is figuratively attributed to the reason through the reason.' And the word <s>siddhānta</s> is used merely with the intention of [indicating] what is the object of acceptance, not with the intention that <s>siddhānta</s> itself is meant here. Therefore, even the thesis, being an object of acceptance — the pseudo-reason that contradicts it is included. And it has been stated that what contradicts a specific [conclusion] is not a pseudo-reason. For the specific [conclusion] is not an object of acceptance — it is not within the scope of the proposition-statement; rather, it is an accessory entailment of the establishment of the proposition's meaning — so it is not within the scope of acceptance — this is the import. He states the result of this kind of <s>sūtra</s>-explanation — 'and thus.' The meaning is: without such an explanation, [the category] of the contradictory [reason] that has not been stated [explicitly]. 'Or is contradicted by what is accepted' — meaning: by its own nature or by its reason-hood. By this, the <s>bhāṣya</s> 'that obstructs it' and so on has been explained. He objects — 'but if so.' If the contradictory is defined as that which subverts reason-hood, then the deviant and the like would also be contradictory, since their reason-hood too is subverted. Or if [reason-hood is] not subverted, they would not be pseudo-reasons — this is the import. He resolves — 'true, there is indeed one.' Even though they are equal in this kind of contradictoriness, it is five-fold through the intention of distinguishing internal subdivisions. Just as <s>pramāṇa</s> and the rest, though equal in being <s>prameya</s> (knowable), are sixteen-fold through the intention of distinguishing internal subdivisions of <s>pramāṇa</s>, <s>prameya</s>, and the rest. Or just as a specific kind of grass is called '<s>tṛṇolapa</s>' (a kind of weed) because of its uncommon [nature] even though it is a kind of grass,
so too a specific kind of the contradictory —
this very [pseudo-reason] — inconclusive and the like — though a species of contradictory, is denoted by the terms contradictory-inconclusive and the like
— this is the meaning. //

children.translated_text: Here the <s>bhāṣya</s> example — 'as in: this is a transformation (<s>vikāra</s>).' <s>Mahat</s> (intellect), <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), the five <s>Tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), the eleven sense organs, the subtle elements, and the gross elements are the transformation. Its manifestation (<s>vyakti</s>) is the transformation characterized by <s>dharma</s> (property), <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (mark), and <s>avasthā</s> (state) — therefore it departs [from its original state]. Here the reason is 'because of the negation of eternality.' Its explanation — 'a transformation cannot be established as eternal.' Even when it has departed [from manifestation], the transformation exists, because of the negation of destruction. This reason — 'because of the negation of eternality' — contradicts his own <s>siddhānta</s>: 'even when departed, the transformation exists, because of the negation of destruction.' He analyzes this very [point] through a question — with 'how?' and so on. Since contradiction has two supports, having said 'it contradicts the <s>siddhānta</s>' with the intention of focusing on the <s>siddhānta</s>, the expression 'it obstructs the <s>siddhānta</s>' has been used — this is the meaning. He explains this <s>bhāṣya</s> — 'example.' Now, one who says that the reason 'because of the negation of eternality' contradicts the <s>siddhānta</s> of the negation of destruction is producing a scriptural contradiction. And thus, the reason that is temporally displaced (<s>kālātyayāpadiṣṭa</s>) is a pseudo-reason, not the contradictory — therefore he says — 'these two sentences mutually subvert each other's meaning.' For a reason that is subverted by a stronger <s>pramāṇa</s> becomes temporally displaced — just as the reason 'liquor should be drunk by a Brahmin because of being a liquid substance, like milk' —

children.translated_text: He states another explanation — 'or, the contradiction between proposition and reason.' 'This transformation departs from manifestation' — this is the proposition; it is contradicted by the reason 'because of the negation of eternality.' [The proposition means:] it departs only from manifestation, but does not perish — this indeed is the meaning of the proposition, as explained by 'even when departed it exists, because of the negation of destruction.' And thus, by [the proposition] 'it departs from manifestation,' the eternality of the transformation has been proposed; [and this] is contradicted by the reason 'because of the negation of eternality.' 'By one's own <s>siddhānta</s>' means by one's own thesis — this is the meaning. And here the <s>bhāṣya</s> is easy [to understand]. Here the <s>vārttikakāra</s> objects — 'but surely, contradiction with the proposition.' The contradiction of proposition and reason is [called] 'proposition-contradiction' — this is the meaning. He resolves — 'this is not a fault.' Having intended that the contradiction pertains to the proposition, the inclusion of proposition-contradiction among the points of defeat [is justified]; having intended that the same contradiction pertains to the reason, it is included among the pseudo-reasons. But when the reason is established for both parties, then the reason has the capacity to contradict the proposition. He concludes — 'therefore.' [This is] an example of the reason's contradiction. Contradiction-hood is the capacity to contradict. The property of sound being produced, being ascertained by <s>pramāṇa</s>, subverts the proposition of eternality — this is the meaning. Incidentally, he gives an example of contradiction between proposition and thesis that constitutes a point of defeat beyond the pseudo-reasons — 'of proposition-contradiction.' And this contradiction will be demonstrated in the third book. The example of contradiction between proposition and reason of equal strength, when the reason is unestablished for one party, is secondary — 'there is not a single entity.' For the property of being produced, though unestablished for one party, is capable of proof, and thus contradicts the proposition-meaning. But [the expression] 'because of the use of the word <s>bhāva</s> (entity) for an aggregate' contradicts the proposition-meaning when established for both parties — by just this much there is a difference — this is the meaning. //6//

children.text: vyutpattinimittamātraṃ caitat prakaraṇasamapadasya, pravṛttinimittaṃ tu satpratipakṣatvam, anyathānaikāntikasyāpi prakaraṇasamatvaprasaṅgāditi /
children.translated_text: And this is merely the etymological basis for the word <s>prakaraṇasama</s>; the ground for its application, however, is having a genuine counter-argument (<s>satpratipakṣatva</s>) — since otherwise the inconclusive too would have the unwanted consequence of being counterbalanced.
'Designation' (<s>prajñāpana</s>) — by the derivation 'that by which [something] is designated' — the illustration has been stated. //

From which... counterbalanced. //7// The <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> states the meaning of the word <s>prakaraṇa</s> (topic) — 'the two bases of investigation.' Investigation means doubt. These two are its objects — undetermined, unascertained — since only such [undetermined things] are designated by the words 'thesis' and 'counter-thesis.' By the derivation '<s>prakaroti</s>' — 'it is employed/taken up as the <s>sādhya</s>' — [one gets] <s>prakaraṇa</s> (topic). He explains the word '<s>cintā</s>' (investigation) — 'the investigation of that topic, starting from doubt and up to determination, is the examination, reflection, desire to know.' That [investigation] is indeed undertaken due to the non-apprehension of the reality. For one who apprehends either the eternal properties invariably concomitant with eternality, or the non-eternal properties invariably concomitant with non-eternality — that [person] does not desire to know about that which is [thus already] in doubt. This very non-apprehension of eternal properties or non-apprehension of non-eternal properties, being adduced by the debater with varied intentions for the purpose of determination, is a pseudo-reason called counterbalanced. Why? Because of being common to both theses: just as in the eternality-thesis there is non-apprehension of non-eternal properties, so too in the non-eternality-thesis there is non-apprehension of eternal properties. This [property], with the intention merely of non-apprehension of reality, is common to both theses —

Since the <s>sūtrakāra</s> has said "<s>prakaraṇasama</s>" (equal to the subject),
the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> shows the meaning, preceded by a question — "why?"
He teaches the causality through the negative concomitance of the non-apprehension of the true nature — "since."
"Therefore" means "of the non-apprehension of the true nature" — this is the meaning.
He objects — "but is not this."
For the <s>prakaraṇa</s> (subject) consists of the thesis and counter-thesis.
And both are what is to be proved.
And what is equal to them is equal to what is to be proved (<s>sādhyasama</s>).
And thus, the <s>prakaraṇasama</s> should not be listed separately from the pseudo-reason called <s>sādhyasama</s> (equal to what is to be proved) — this is the meaning.
He resolves — "not undistinguished."

children.text:
paramatamanubhāṣyātiprasaṅgāpādanena dūṣayati---ye tu saṃśayahetutvāditi /
codayati---samūha iti /
yasmin sati bhavatyeva tat kāraṇam, samūhe sati ca bhavatyeva naikaikasmin, tattmāt naikaikaṃ kāraṇamiti bhāvaḥ /
pariharati---samūhaḥ kāraṇamitīti /
na hyakāraṇānāṃ samūhaḥ kāraṇaṃ bhavitumarhati, atiprasaṅgāt /

children.translated_text: And without knowing the distinctiveness of the individual components, one cannot know the distinctiveness of the aggregate.
Therefore, the individual components themselves, possessing mutual co-presence, are the cause.
And thus, the causality of perception with respect to doubt is justified.

children.text: na ca yasmin sati bhavatyeva tat kāraṇam, api tu yasmin satyeva na tvasatīti lakṣaṇabhaṅgabhaṅge vakṣyāma iti //
children.translated_text: And it is not the case that whatever is present when [the effect] invariably occurs is the cause; rather, [the cause is] that only when present, and not when absent [the effect occurs] — we shall explain this in the section on the refutation of the [faulty] definition.

Having restated the opponent's view, he criticizes by showing an undesirable over-extension — "but those who, because of being a cause of doubt."
He objects — "aggregate."
Whatever is such that when it is present [the effect] invariably occurs is the cause; and when the aggregate is present [the effect] invariably occurs, not when each individual [component is present] — therefore no individual [component] is the cause: this is the meaning.
He resolves — "the aggregate is the cause" —
For the aggregate of non-causes cannot be a cause, because of over-extension.

children.text:
nanūbhayadharmānupalabdhirubhayapakṣasādhāraṇīti savyabhicāra evetyata āha---ubhayadharmānupalabdhāviti /
nobhayadharmānupalabdhiratra hetuḥ, api tu ekadharmānupalabdhiḥ /
na cāsau sādhāraṇī,
kiṃ tu tatpratipakṣetyarthaḥ /
ubhayaviśeṣānupalabdheḥ prakaraṇasamatvena abhidhānāśakyatvāt prakaraṇasamasyodāharaṇāntaraṃ dūṣayati---śarīrādanyatvaṃ tviti /
pareṣāṃ kilodāharaṇaṃ nitya
children.translated_text:
But the non-apprehension of the properties of both [sides] is common to both theses and thus is inconclusive — to this he says: "when the properties of both sides are not apprehended."
The non-apprehension of both properties is not the reason here, but rather the non-apprehension of one property.
And that is not common [to both theses],
but belongs to the counter-thesis — this is the meaning.
The non-apprehension of the distinguishing features of both [leads to] the conclusion of

children.text:
ātmā śarīrādanyatvād
ākāśavaditi /
tatra śarīrādanyatvam upalabhamāno yadā tattvaṃ nityatvamātmanaḥ pratyeti, na hi tadā jijñāsituṃ nityatvaṃ pravartate /
yadā tu tattvaṃ nityattvaṃ nopalabhate śarīrādanyatvamupalabhamāno 'pi tadā pravartate /
tasmādanvayavyatirekābhyāṃ tattvānupalabdhireva prakaraṇacintāpravartikā na śarīrādanyatvam /
tasmāt naitat prakaraṇasamasyodāharaṇam /
api tu tattvānupalabdhireva /
itaścaitanna prakaraṇasamasyodāharaṇamityāha---śarīrādanyatvaṃ cānaikāntikam /

children.translated_text: He concludes — "and thus this is not the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>"
nor the subject of the <s>sūtra</s>.
Similarly, other examples of the counter-balancing reason should be worked out. //7//

"The <s>ātman</s> (self) is different from the body,
like <s>ākāśa</s> (space)." Here, when one apprehends the difference from the body and thereby cognizes the true nature, namely the eternality of the <s>ātman</s>, one does not then proceed to inquire about eternality.
But when one does not apprehend the true nature, namely eternality, even while apprehending the difference from the body, then one proceeds [to inquire].
Therefore
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.8: What is undistinguished from what is to be proved, because of being [itself] what is to be proved, is <s>sādhyasama</s> (equal to what is to be proved).

children.text:
sādhyā---maḥ // 7// atra sādhyasama
iti lakṣyanirdeśaḥ /
sādhyāviśiṣṭa iti lakṣaṇam /
tadanena svarūpāsiddhaikadeśāsiddhāśrayāsiddhānyathāsiddhānāṃ saṃgrahaḥ, teṣāmasiddhatvena sādhyāviśiṣṭatvāt /
atra cāsiddhaḥ sādhyasama iti vaktavye sādhyāviśiṣṭagrahaṇamanyatarāsiddhasyāpi siddheḥ prāgahetutvajñāpanārtham /
anyathātyantāsiddha
eva sādhyasamo nānyatarāsiddhaḥ tasya kadācit siddheriti bhrāntiḥ syāt /
sādhyāviśiṣṭena tu so 'pi saṃgṛhīta iti /
nanvevaṃ sādhyāviśiṣṭatvenānyatarāsiddha
eva syāt netare, neṣāmasiddhatvena sādhyāviśeṣābhāvādityata
uktaṃ sūtrakṛtā sādhyatvāditi /
yadi hi sādhyaṃ nāsiddhaṃ bhavet sādhyatvādeva cyaveta, na khalu siddhaṃ sādhyate /
tasmāt sādhyatvādasiddhatā /
sā ca kasyacit sarvadā, kādācitkī kaściditi sarveṣāmaviśiṣṭatvamiti nāvyāptiḥ /

children.translated_text: Nor is there over-extension due to the over-applicability of "being what is to be proved" —
because the specific definition depends on the general definition of pseudo-reasons — this is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>.
"Because of needing to be proved" in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> is not an explanation of "because of being what is to be proved,"
but rather is aimed at [showing] the unestablishedness of what has the nature of motion.

<s>Sādhyasama</s> //7// Here, "<s>sādhyasama</s>" is the designation of the definiendum.
"Undistinguished from what is to be proved" (<s>sādhyāviśiṣṭa</s>) is the definition.
By this, the following are comprehended: unestablished in itself (<s>svarūpāsiddha</s>), partially unestablished (<s>ekadeśāsiddha</s>), unestablished as to substrate (<s>āśrayāsiddha</s>), and otherwise established (<s>anyathāsiddha</s>) — because all of these, being unestablished, are undistinguished from what is to be proved.
And here, where one should say "unestablished is <s>sādhyasama</s>," instead "undistinguished from the <s>sādhya</s>" is used —

children.text:
atra vārttikakāraḥ sūtrārthaṃ vyācaṣṭe---sādhyenāviśiṣṭo ya iti /
sādhyena vyabhicāro mā bhūdityata
āha---sādhanadharma iti hetvābhāsasāmānyalakṣaṇayoge sati etallakṣaṇamiti na vyabhicāra iti bhāvaḥ /
atra bhāṣyakāreṇa svarūpāsiddhāśrayāsiddhānyathāsiddhānāṃ sādhāraṇamudāharaṇamuktam---dravyaṃ chāyā gatimattvāditi /
tadvibhajate vārttikakāraḥ
dravyaṃ chāyeti /
atra svarūpāsiddhatāṃ tāvadāha---yathaiveti /
āśrayāsiddhatāmavatārayituṃ gatimattaṃ chāyāyāḥ pañcāvayavena vākyena sādhyati---gatimattvamiti /
āśrayāsiddhatāmāha---nāśrayāsiddhatvāditi /
satyā eva chāyāyā deśāntare darśanād yo 'syā gatimattvamanubhinoti taṃ pratyāśrayāsiddhaṃ deśāntare darśanam,
tadāśrayasyāsiddhatvāt /
tadidamuktam---sati dravyābhāva iti, sati sattva ityarthaḥ, na tāvat chāyā sāmānyaviśeṣasamavāyāntarbhūtā tasyā nityatābhāvāt /
nāpi karma, saṃyogavibhāgāsamavāyikāraṇatvābhāvāt /
na guṇo dravyāsamavāyāt /
na manodikkālaguṇaḥ,
tadguṇānāmapratyakṣatvāt /
nāpyātmaguṇo bāhyendriyapratyakṣatvāt /
nāpi nabhonabhasvatoḥ,
tadguṇānāmacākṣuṣatvāt /
nāpi tejasaḥ,
tadvirodhitvāt tatsahacaritaguṇāntarānupalabdheśca /
ata eva na pṛthivīpāthasorapi /
api ca tadguṇaścākṣuṣo nālokamantareṇa śakyagrahaḥ /
chāyā tu tamantareṇa gṛhyate,
children.translated_text:
Here the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> explains the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> — "that which is undistinguished from the <s>sādhya</s>."
Lest there be deviation from the <s>sādhya</s>,
he says — "a property of the <s>sādhana</s>" — meaning that when conjoined with the general definition of pseudo-reasons, this definition [applies], so there is no deviation.
Here the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> shows unestablishedness in its own form, unestablishedness of substrate, and otherwise-establishedness with the examples

children.text:
tasmiṃstu sati na gṛhyate iti durghaṭam /
nāpi dravyam, taddhi pṛthivyādīnāmamanyatamad bhaved anyad
vā daśamam /
na
children.translated_text:
"But when that is present, it is not apprehended" — this is difficult to reconcile.
Nor is it a substance, for that would be either one of the [nine substances] such as earth and the like, or a tenth [substance] other [than those].
Not

children.text: tadguṇānāmanupalabdadheḥ, nāpyanyad rūpavaditi yujyate, tasyādravyasya pratyakṣatvānupapatteḥ,
children.translated_text: because its qualities are not apprehended; nor is it correct [to say] "it possesses form," because of the impossibility of that non-substance being perceptible.
Because of being intangible, being non-aqueous, and the absence of being a multi-substance [composite].

children.text: tasmād bhābhāva eva chāyā na tu satīti siddham //
children.translated_text: Therefore, shadow is merely the absence of light, not a positive entity — this is established.
the former,

children.text:
yastu manyate mā bhūt
chāyā satī, bhavatu bhābhāvaḥ tathāpi nāśrayāsiddhatā deśāntaradarśanasya bhābhāvāśrayatvādeveti taṃ pratyabhyupetyānyathāsiddhatayā sādhyasamatvamāpādayati---abhyupetyeti /
svābhāviko hi saṃbandho hetoḥ sādhyena sahānumānāṅgaṃ naupādhika iti vivecitamanumānalakṣaṇe /
tadayamanyathāsiddha aupādhikasaṃbandho bhavati hetvābhāsaḥ /
seyaṃ hetorasiddhirdvidhā svarūpato hetutvena ca /
svarūpato 'pi dvedhā, svata āśrayāsiddhyā ca /
na caitāvatā savyabhicārādīnāmapi hetutvāsiddherasiddha evāntarbhāvaḥ savyabhicāratvādiviśeṣaṇena teṣāmato bhedāt /
anyathāsiddhasya tu tadviśeṣaṇatvāyogino hetutvāsiddhimātreṇa sādhyasame 'ntarbhāva
iti sarvamavadātam /
saṃkalayati---so 'yamiti /
ta ete 'siddhabhedā udāharaṇabhedeṣvapi draṣṭavyāḥ, yathā nityaḥ śabdaḥ
cākṣuṣatvāditi svayamasiddhaḥ /
tanubhuvanādīnāṃ na kartā īśvaro 'śarīratvādityāśrayāsiddhaḥ /

children.translated_text: "He is dark-complexioned because he is the son of <s>Maitra</s>, like the observed son of <s>Maitra</s>, <s>Stoma</s>" — this is otherwise-established,
because the difference in complexion is dependent on the difference in the transformation of food and drink — hence the otherwise-establishedness.
"This too, because of being unestablished" — in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, by the word "also"
the unestablishedness of the substrate, namely shadow, through its [non-]existence is indicated.

But if one thinks: let shadow not be a positive entity, let it be the absence of light — even so, there is no unestablishedness of substrate, precisely because the observation elsewhere [of the reason] has its substrate in the absence of light — to that, accepting provisionally, he shows that it is <s>sādhyasama</s> through otherwise-establishedness — "accepting provisionally."
For the natural relation of the reason with the <s>sādhya</s> is a component of inference,

children.text:
atra bhadantena idaṃ sādhyasamalakṣaṇamudāharaṇāntaraṃ kalpayitvā dūṣitam /
idaṃ kilāsyodāharaṇam,
nityaḥ
children.translated_text:
Here the venerable [Buddhist teacher], having devised a different example for this definition of <s>sādhyasama</s>, has criticized [it].
This, they say, is his example: "eternal"

children.text:
śabdo 'sparśatvād buddhivaditi /
tadetat tridhāpyasiddhaṃ na bhavatīti dūṣayitvā bhadantena śaṅkitam, atha sādhyenāviśiṣṭo dṛṣṭānto yasmin sa sādhyāviśiṣṭo hetvābhāsa iti buddherdṛṣṭāntasya nityatvenāsiddhatvāt
children.translated_text:
"sound is intangible, like cognition."
Having criticized this as not being unestablished in any of the three ways, the venerable [teacher] then objected: if the illustration in which the <s>sādhya</s> is undistinguished is [what makes it] a <s>sādhyāviśiṣṭa</s> pseudo-reason — then because cognition, the illustration, is unestablished as eternal —

children.text:
ityāśaṅkya bahuvrīhyabhāvena dūṣitam /
tadetat sarvamanabhyupagamena vārttikakāro dūṣayati---nityaḥ śabda iti /
yadyetat nodāharaṇaṃ kimudāharaṇaṃ ko vā sūtrārtha ityata āha---yathā tvasmābhiriti /
ayaṃ bhadantokto doṣa ityarthaḥ /
kasmādityata āha---bhadantena sūtrārtho na vijñātaḥ, na hi savyabhicāro 'nena lakṣyate yena savyabhicāramasparśavattvamasyodāharaṇaṃ syāt, kiṃ tu sādhyasamaḥ /
nāpi vyadhikaraṇabahuvrīhidūṣaṇenākṣarārtho jñātaḥ /
nāpi buddhivaditi dṛṣṭāntābhāsameva hetvābhāsaṃ kurvatā hetvābhāsadṛṣṭāntābhāsau jñātau bhadantenetyarthaḥ
// 8 //
children.translated_text:
this objection was raised and criticized through the absence of a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> [compound interpretation].
The <s>Vārttikakāra</s> criticizes all of this through non-acceptance — "sound is eternal."
If this is not the example, what is the example, and what is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>? — to this he says: "as, however, by us."
This is the fault stated by the venerable one — this is the meaning.
Why? — to this he says —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.9: <s>Kālātīta</s> (time-lapsed) is that which is presented after the time [has passed].

children.text:
kālā---taḥ // 9 // atra kālātīta iti lakṣyanirdeśaḥ,
kālātyayāpadiṣṭa iti lakṣaṇam /
hetorapadeśasya hi sādhyasandehaviśiṣṭaḥ kālaḥ /
yathāhuḥ---
children.translated_text:
<s>Kālātīta</s> //9// Here "<s>kālātīta</s>" (time-lapsed) is the designation of the definiendum,
and "presented after the time has passed" (<s>kālātyayāpadiṣṭa</s>) is the definition.
For the time for the presentation of a reason is characterized by the doubt regarding what is to be proved.
As they say —

children.text:
nānupalabdhe na nirṇīte nyāyaḥ pravartate,
api tu sandigdhe iti /
pare 'pyāhuḥ
children.translated_text:
"Reasoning (<s>nyāya</s>) does not operate regarding what is not apprehended, nor regarding what is determined,
but only regarding what is doubtful."
Others too say —
"Because the reason is stated when [the matter] is doubtful."

children.text:
iti /
yatra ca pratkṣānumānāgamavirodhaḥ,
anuṣṇo 'gnirdravyatvāditi ca aśrāvaṇaḥ śabdo guṇatvāditi ca, śuci naraśiraḥkapālaṃ prāṇyaṅgatvāditi ca, sa sarvaḥ pramāṇato viparītanirṇayena sandehaviśiṣṭaṃ kālamatipatatīti so 'yaṃ kālasyātyayenāpadiśyamānaḥ kālātīta
iti /
tathā codāhṛtaṃ
children.translated_text:
And where there is contradiction with perception, inference, or scripture —
such as "fire is not hot, because it is a substance," or "sound is non-auditory, because it is a quality," or "a human skull is pure, because it is a body part" — all of these, through the determination of the contrary by <s>pramāṇa</s>, have passed beyond the time characterized by doubt — and thus this [reason] is presented after the time has elapsed,
And what contradicts perception and scripture is a semblance of reasoning (<s>nyāyābhāsa</s>).

children.text:
ityatra vārttikakṛtā bādhāvinābhāvayoḥ sahāsaṃbhava iti cātra bauddhānāmākṣepo 'smābhiḥ samāhitaḥ /
evaṃ vyavasthite bhāṣyakāraḥ sūtraṃ svaparamataśliṣṭaṃ vyācaṣṭe---kālātyayena saṃśayakālātyayena yukto yasya hetorapadiśyamānasyāthaiṅkadeśaḥ /
dharmaviśiṣṭo hi dharmī hetorapadiśyamānasyārthaḥ /
sar hyati hetunā, tasyaikadeśaḥ sādhyadharmaḥ /
sa hi dharmiṇi balabalā pramāṇena tadviparotadharmanirṇayaṃ kurvatā saṃśayakālamatipātitaḥ /
sa tādṛśo hetuḥ kālātyayāpadiṣṭaḥ kālātīta
iti svamatenāsyārthaḥ /
atra ca pūrvamevodāhṛtamiti paunaruktyāt
nodāhṛtam /
children.translated_text: In this [context], the <s>vārttikakāra</s>'s [objection that] the impossibility of non-deviation and sublation coexisting, and the Buddhists' objection to that — these have been resolved by us. / Having thus established [the matter], the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> explains the <s>sūtra</s> as fitting both his own and others' views — 'connected with the lapse of the time of doubt: that part of the meaning of the reason being indicated, which is qualified by a property — for the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) qualified by a property is the meaning of the reason being indicated. / For [the subject] is pervaded by the reason; and a part of that [subject] is the <s>sādhya</s>-property. / For that [sādhya-property] has had its time of doubt passed over by a more powerful <s>pramāṇa</s> that determines a property contrary to it in the subject. / Such a reason, indicated after the lapse of time, is called <s>kālātīta</s> (mistimed)' — this is the meaning according to his own view. / And here, an illustration was already given earlier, so it is not given again to avoid repetition.

children.text:
paramate ca kālātyayena yukto yasya hetorartharūpa ekadeśo hetuviśeṣaṇamiti yāvat, sa kālātyayāpadiṣṭa
iti yojanā /
paramatenaiva nidarśanamāha---nidarśanamiti /
nityatvaṃ cātrāvasthānamātramabhimatamiti,
na
children.translated_text: And according to the other view, the construction is: 'connected with the lapse of time — a part of the meaning-form of the reason, as a qualifier of the reason — is called <s>kālātīta</s> (indicated after the lapse of time).' / He gives an illustration according to the other view itself — 'illustration' etc. / And here, permanence is understood as mere stability, so
there is no deviation with respect to pots and the like, which are manifested by conjunction with light.

children.text: tadetat pañcāvayavaṃ vākyamupanyasya saṃyogavyaṅgyatvasya hetorekadeśasya viśeṣaṇasya saṃyogasya vyaktikālātyayena hetvābhāsatāmāha---ayamaheturiti /
children.translated_text: Having presented this five-membered statement, he states that because of the lapse of time for the manifestation of conjunction — which is the qualifier of the partial [aspect of the] reason, namely being manifested by conjunction — the [reason] becomes a pseudo-reason — 'this is a non-reason' etc.

children.text: sa punarayamasiddhaviśeṣaṇatayā hetvābhāsaḥ sādhyasama eveti na pṛgvācya
children.translated_text: And this, being a pseudo-reason through having an unestablished qualifier, is indeed a <s>sādhyasama</s> (on par with what is to be proved) — so it need not be stated separately.

children.text: iti sthūlatayā eṣa doṣo bhāṣyakāreṇa nodbhāvitaḥ //
children.translated_text: Because of this crudeness, this fault has not been brought out by the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s>. //

children.text:
yat punaḥ bhadantena kālātītasaya vyākhyānaṃ kṛtaṃ pratijñānantaraṃ hi hetoḥ kālaḥ /
tamatītya hetuḥ paścādapadiśyamānaḥ kālātīto bhavati /
tad yathā, anityaḥ śabdaḥ
ghaṭādivadityukte kasmādityanuyukto hetuṃ brūte kṛtakatvāditi sa kālātīta
iti /
taccaivaṃ tena dūṣitam---kiṃ nirākāṅkṣe vādini eṣa prativādinaḥ praśnaḥ,
āho sākāṅkṣe? yadi nirākāṅkṣe tadā nyūnamevāsya nigrahasthānam, na hetvābhāsastasyāprayogāt /
prayukto hi hetustadābhāso vā syāt
nāprayuktaḥ /
atha sākāṅkṣa eva vādini prativādinaḥ praśnaḥ, tathāpi paścādapyasau hetuḥ prayukto hetureva, na hyasau tadā na svasādhyāvinābhūtaḥ,
apakṣadharmo veti /
tasmāt na kālatīto nāmāsti hetvābhāsa
children.translated_text: Now, the explanation of <s>kālātīta</s> given by the Venerable [Dignāga] is: the time for the reason comes immediately after the thesis; having passed over that [time], a reason indicated afterwards becomes <s>kālātīta</s>. / For example, when 'sound is impermanent, like a pot and the like' has been said, and upon being asked 'why?', one states the reason 'because of being produced' — that is <s>kālātīta</s>. / And that has been refuted by him [Uddyotakara] thus: is this question of the respondent [addressed] to the proponent who is without expectation, or to one with expectation? / If to one without expectation, then 'deficiency' itself is the point of defeat for him, not a pseudo-reason, since [the reason] was not employed. / For a reason that has been employed may be a [valid] reason or its semblance, / not one that has not been employed. / But if the respondent's question is [addressed] to the proponent who indeed has expectation, even then, the reason employed afterwards is still a [valid] reason; for it is not the case that it then lacks inseparability with its <s>sādhya</s>, / or is not a property of the thesis.

children.translated_text: 'saṃbhava—lam' // 13 // When the possible meaning — a specific Brahmin — has the [property of] being the subject of excellence in learning and conduct, the universal <s>brahminhood</s>, which transcends the excellence in learning and conduct, [exists] in a <s>vrātya</s> (degraded) Brahmin; through the application of that over-generalization of <s>brahminhood</s>, the negation through the supposition of a non-existent meaning — / that is <s>sāmānyacchala</s>. / 'Ah, this Brahmin is indeed not excellent in learning and conduct!' — for this laudatory statement, when one acknowledges that 'it is possible that a Brahmin has excellence in learning and conduct,' then this statement too is meant for praise, not that excellence in learning and conduct is intended from his <s>brahminhood</s> as a reason. / There, the opponent, attributing to this [statement] an intention to state a reason, refutes the statement — and that is this <s>sāmānyacchala</s>. / 'Restatement of the subject' — / the meaning is: the restatement of <s>brahminhood</s> as the subject of [excellence in] learning and conduct. / Of whom? Of the person for whom the reason is not intended. / The <s>vārttikakāra</s> explains this — 'of the universal' etc. / The meaning is: the universal whose intended meaning has been understood. / The rest is easy to understand. // 13 //

children.translated_text: An already established
figurative usage should be employed, not a novel one without purpose.
And this is an established figurative usage — "the platforms are shouting" — this is the meaning.

Among these too, the primary [usage] is the natural (<s>autsargika</s>) one, and through some exception to that, the secondary (<s>bhākta</s>) one arises.
This is what the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> states — the natural property of the expressive word is its use according to its meaning.
Is that the only [kind]? No, he says — the alternative is twofoldness.
What is the second? To this he says — through an exception to the general rule from some [particular circumstance], the use elsewhere of what has been seen elsewhere.
Thus, with the established twofold classification of properties, in the statement (<s>nirdeśa</s>), i.e., the sentence — by the derivation "that by which something is indicated."
In the case of the intention to use the secondary meaning, in "the platforms are shouting," there is a negation through the real existence of the [primary] meaning.
He states that very real existence of meaning — "the people standing on the platforms are shouting, but the platforms are not shouting."
But in the view of the <s>Vārttikakāra</s>, it should be explained as a negation of the very real existence of meaning.
Now, if what is seen in one place is used in another, then everything would be used everywhere — to this he says: "figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>) has a conveyed meaning, an arrived-at meaning."
"By a basis such as co-occurrence" — the use elsewhere of what has been seen elsewhere occurs only through a connection.
So there is no over-extension — this is the meaning.
"Not arbitrarily" — not through deception — this is the meaning.
But if there is justification even through the secondary meaning,
then nothing said by a sophistical speaker would be faulty,
since everything can somehow be justified through the secondary meaning — to this he says: "of the primary" etc.
Where it would suffice to say "of the secondary," the mention of "primary" is for the sake of obtaining an established example.

Hence
In the subordinate [part], the postulation of a different meaning.

children.text:
iti mañcā ityetadapradhānamanūdyatayā bhāktam /
na tu krośantīti
children.translated_text:
Thus "platforms" — being subordinate, as merely cited — is secondary.
But "are shouting"
does not [allow] another meaning of the word in the predicate
according to the rule.

children.text: tadiha vidhīyamānaṃ krośanameva vastu pratiṣidhyate, naiva mañcāḥ krośantīti chalavākyena /
children.translated_text: Therefore, here it is the predicate — the shouting itself, the real object — that is negated [by the equivocator], saying "the platforms are not indeed shouting."

children.text: navakambalo devadatta iti vākye tu devadattamanūdya navatvaviśiṣṭaḥ kambalo vidhīyate /
children.translated_text: But in the sentence "<s>Devadatta</s> with the new blanket," <s>Devadatta</s> is merely cited, and the blanket qualified by newness is predicated.

children.text: tatra na vidheyasya vastunaḥ kambalasya sadbhāvaḥ pratiṣidhyate, kiṃ tu tadekadeśasyānekatāyā iti mahān bheda iti siddhāntaḥ // 16 //
children.translated_text: There, the real existence of the predicated object — the blanket — is not negated; rather, only the multiplicity of a part of it [is negated]. Hence the great difference — this is the established doctrine. //16//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.17: Or, if there is no distinction, then from partial similarity there would be the consequence of everything being a single equivocation.
By saying "om" (yes), as a real thing, there would be the absurd consequence of the destruction of all distinctions.
The <s>Bhāṣya</s> and <s>Vārttika</s> have clear meaning. //17//
Or... consequence //17// From partial similarity, in the absence of triplicity [of equivocation types], even the duality that is accepted would be absurdly absent.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.18: <s>Jāti</s> (futile rejoinder) is a counter-argument based on similarity or dissimilarity.

children.text:
uddeśakramānurodhena jātilakṣaṇakramamāha bhāṣyakāraḥ---ataḥ chalalakṣaṇād--ūrdhvam /
sādha--tiḥ // 18 // pratīpamavasthānaṃ pratyavasthānam, tathā sati chalasya samyagdūṣaṇasya ca jātitvaprasaṅgaḥ /
ata uktam---sādharmyavaidharmyābhyāmiti /
na ca cchale sādharmyavaidharmye staḥ /

prayukte hetau tadābhāse vā yaḥ prasaṅgo jāyate sa jātiriti /
jalpe hi vedaprāmāṇyaṃ vidvāṃsaṃ prati kuhetunā yadā nāstikairadhikṣipyate, saduttaraṃ cāsya yadā sahasā na pratibhāti tadeśvarāṇāṃ janādhārāṇāṃ mā bhūd vedāprāmāṇyabuddhiriti jātyāpi pratyavastheyam /
anyatheśvaracaritānuvarttinīnāṃ prajānāṃ viplavo bhavediti /
kvacit punarabuddhipūrvameva hetau hetvābhāse vā jātiprayogaḥ saṃbhavati /
jāyamāno 'rthaḥ iti jātipadavyutpattinimitataṃ darśitam /
tadetad vārttikakāro vyācaṣṭe---sādharmyeṇeti /
yathā pakṣe sati pratipakṣaḥ,
evaṃ sthāpanāyāṃ satyāṃ pratyavasthānamiti /
sūtrārthastu yathāśruti, na punarudāharaṇasādharmyeṇa yathābhāṣyaṃ bodhyavyaḥ /
yadyevam, bhāṣyaṃ tarhi kathamityata
āha---udāharaṇārthamiti /
evaṃ vaidharmyeṇa vetyetadapi /

children.translated_text: [Should be taken] literally, not as in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>.
That is for the purpose of example — this is the meaning.
With a statement of the merits of this explanation, he elaborates with a question — "for what purpose is this?" //18//

Following the order of enumeration, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> states the order of the definition of <s>jāti</s> — "after this, from the definition of equivocation" etc.
Similarity... <s>jāti</s> //18// Counter-standing (<s>pratyavasthāna</s>) means standing in opposition. If so, [verbal] equivocation and genuine refutation would also absurdly be <s>jāti</s>.
Hence it is said: "through similarity and dissimilarity."
And in equivocation there is no similarity or dissimilarity.
Nor is genuine refutation based on mere similarity or dissimilarity, but on [proper] demonstration.
When a reason or a pseudo-reason has been stated, the consequence (<s>prasaṅga</s>) that arises — that is <s>jāti</s>.
For in <s>jalpa</s> (disputation), when the authoritativeness of the <s>Vedas</s> is attacked by <s>Nāstikas</s> (deniers) with a fallacious reason against a learned person, and when a correct answer does not immediately occur to him, then lest the lords who are the refuge of the people develop the notion that the <s>Vedas</s> are not authoritative, one should counter-argue even with a <s>jāti</s>.
Otherwise, there would be a disruption of the people who follow the conduct of the lords.
But sometimes the use of <s>jāti</s> with respect to a reason or a pseudo-reason may occur even unintentionally.
The etymological basis of the word <s>jāti</s> has been shown — "the meaning that is born" (<s>jāyamāna</s>).
The <s>Vārttikakāra</s> explains this — "by similarity" etc.
Just as there is a counter-thesis when there is a thesis,
so there is a counter-argument when there is an establishment.
But the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> should be taken literally, not understood through the similarity of the example as in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>.
If so, then how is the <s>Bhāṣya</s> [to be understood]? To this he says: "for the purpose of example" etc.
Similarly, "by dissimilarity" — this too.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.19: <s>Nigrahasthāna</s> (point of defeat) is erroneous understanding (<s>vipratipattiḥ</s>) and failure to understand (<s>apratipattiḥ</s>).

children.text:
vipra---nam // 19 // sūkṣmaviṣayā pratipattirviparītā /

children.translated_text:
Erroneous... defeat //19// Erroneous understanding is an understanding regarding a subtle matter that is contrary [to the truth].
And [failure to understand] regarding a gross matter is blameworthy — how is it a point of defeat? To this he says: "one who understands erroneously" etc.
He states failure to understand — "in the subject of the undertaking" etc. For the sake of brevity, instead of saying "<s>vipratipatti</s> and <s>apratipatti</s>," why is there no compound? To this he says: "because of not compounding" etc.
Beyond <s>vipratipatti</s> and <s>apratipatti</s>, there are also additional points of defeat in <s>jalpa</s> (disputation) involving reason and example, and those too are included through the extended text — this is the meaning.
The <s>Bhāṣya</s> passage "in the subject of the undertaking, non-undertaking" etc. — he explains: "failure to understand the answer for oneself and for others" etc.
Non-undertaking in the subject of the undertaking occurs in two ways:
either one fails to understand the opponent's proof, i.e., the reason for contradiction, that is to be refuted;
or [one fails to understand one's own answer].
This is the failure to understand the answer for the other — the word "answer" also indicates proof.
Failure to understand one's own answer means: having understood the opponent's proof and reason for refutation, one fails to understand one's own answer to refute it — this is the meaning.
He objects — when one has oneself employed a proof that is actually competent, how

children.text:
apratipattirvipratipattirveti draṣṭavyam /
pariharati---tadāpīti /
samarthasādhanajñānaṃ sādhanapratipattirna sādhanamātrajñānamityarthaḥ
// 19 //
children.translated_text:
should failure to understand or erroneous understanding be viewed?
He resolves — "even then" etc.
Knowledge of a competent proof is understanding of the proof, not mere knowledge of the proof — this is the meaning. //19//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.20: The multiplicity of <s>jāti</s> (futile rejoinders) and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (points of defeat) is from their varieties.

uktaḥ /
tadvi---tvam // 20// nānā kalpa iti svarūpataḥ,

children.translated_text: "Diverse" — in terms of their types.
"According to definition" means according to their own nature — this is the meaning.

To introduce another <s>sūtra</s>, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> says — "what then?" etc.
Although the example also has varieties through similarity and dissimilarity, nevertheless non-difference has been stated with the intent of non-difference of definition.
Their varieties... multiplicity //20// "Having various alternatives" — in terms of their own nature,

children.translated_text: Therefore

children.text: yaḥ pramāṇādisūtreṇoddeśaḥ, tatparikaro dvitīyaṃ sūtram, dvābhyāmuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: the enumeration by the <s>sūtra</s> on <s>pramāṇa</s> and the rest — its expansion is the second <s>sūtra</s>; and by the two, the enumeration [is complete].
The rest is easy to understand. //20//

The <s>Vārttikakāra</s> summarizes the meaning of the chapter — "the thesis of the treatise" etc.
The thesis of the treatise (<s>tantra</s>), the <s>śāstra</s>, is the <s>sūtra</s>: "from the true knowledge of <s>pramāṇa</s> and the rest, the attainment of the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>)."
For true knowledge is through the <s>śāstra</s> alone.
<s>Saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth) consists of suffering, birth, activity, faults, and false knowledge.
And its cessation is through understanding: through the successive removal [of each], there is the absence of what follows — hence <s>apavarga</s> (liberation).
// Thus ends the second lesson of the first chapter of the <s>Nyāyavārttikatātparyaṭīkā</s> composed by <s>Vācaspatimiśra</s>. //
// The first chapter is complete. //
Oṃ
In the <s>Nyāyavārttikatātparyaṭīkā</s>,
the second chapter.
Hereafter, the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> raises the doubt to be refuted by the <s>Bhāṣya</s> beginning with "the examination of <s>pramāṇa</s> and the rest" — "and this is of three kinds" etc.

deśayati /
nanu coktamiti /
śāstragatā tviyaṃ parīkṣā, sā ca na vimarśapūrvetyārthakramābhāvānnoddeśakramo bādhanīya ityarthaḥ /
pariharati satyaṃ na nirṇaye niyama iti /
na nirṇayaḥ sarvaḥ saṃśayapūrvaṃ,
vicāraḥ sarva eva saṃśayapūrvaḥ, śāstravādayoścāsti vicāra iti tenāpi saṃśayapūrveṇa bhavitavyam /
śiṣṭayośca vādiprativādinoḥ śāstre vimarśābhāvo na śiṣyamāṇayoḥ, tasmādasti śāsre 'pi vimarśapūrvo vicāraiti siddham /
saṃśītiriti saṃśayasya niruktam /
(182/2) nāvadhārayatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
(181/4) "The statement of examination for those that have a place and those that have an order" — thus it is proper that <s>pramāṇa</s> itself is examined.
Has <s>pramāṇa</s> not already been examined here first?
No, rather, it is doubt itself that is examined — he says.
"Passing over those" — he states the meaning of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> [regarding] the source of this difference in order.
"Because of being a component of examination" — for <s>pramāṇa</s> was defined first following the order of enumeration, but in the definition, doubt has no use.
But all examination has deliberation as its instrument, so at the stage of examination, by the order of meaning, doubt necessarily comes first.
Just as in "he offers the <s>agnihotra</s>" and "he cooks the rice-gruel," the cooking of rice-gruel precedes the <s>agnihotra</s>, since it is an instrument of the <s>agnihotra</s>.
And what is examined here is the definition of doubt, not doubt itself, so there is no infinite regress either.
He teaches.
"But it has been said" etc.
But this examination is within the <s>śāstra</s>, and that is not preceded by deliberation — so due to the absence of the order of meaning, the order of enumeration should not be overridden — this is the meaning.
He resolves — "true, there is no restriction in determination" etc.
Not every determination is preceded by doubt,
but every inquiry (<s>vicāra</s>) is preceded by doubt, and there is inquiry in both <s>śāstra</s> and debate, so that too must be preceded by doubt.
And the absence of deliberation for the proponent and opponent in the <s>śāstra</s> is [only] when they are already accomplished, not when they are being taught; therefore, even in the <s>śāstra</s>, inquiry is preceded by deliberation — this is established.
"<s>Saṃśīti</s>" is the etymology of <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt).
(182/2) The meaning is: one does not determine.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.1: Doubt does not arise from the ascertainment of common properties of many things, nor from the ascertainment of a property of one of them.

vyavacchedātmakatvāditi /

children.translated_text: A determination does not produce non-determination, because the effect conforms to its cause — this is the meaning.
"Not from the ascertainment of common properties alone" — this refers only figuratively to the causes stated in the definition of doubt.
"Because of residing in a single [substrate]" etc.
For the height and girth of a post are not the same as those of a person — this is the meaning. //1//

Just as the meaning of the definition has been previously determined, so the initial objection is without basis — to this he says.
"Its [meaning should be taken] literally" etc.
For the matter to be established through examination is directly understood from the definition-words themselves through explanation — this is the meaning.
"Common to these two" — he shows direct perception.
For one who directly perceives a post and a person does not doubt regarding any common property of these two — this is the meaning.
"Because of being of the nature of determination" etc.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.2: And [doubt arises] from conflicting judgments and uncertain determination.
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.3: And because of agreement [about the object] in [cases of] disagreement //
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.4: And because what is called 'instability' is [itself] stable in its own nature //
'And because of agreement in disagreement'— the meaning is: disagreement does not exist due to contradiction with its own nature // 2-4 //
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.5: Likewise perpetual doubt, because of the continued occurrence of those properties //

'Likewise perpetual doubt'— not seeing a differentiating [factor] from the causes of doubt such as the apprehension of common properties by means of other terms from 'that'— this is the prima facie view // 5 //

children.text: NyS_2,1.6: yathoktādhyavasāyādeva tadviśeṣāpekṣāt saṃśaye nāsaṃśayo nātyantasaṃśayo vā //

He states the established conclusion— 'the reply to this' / (183/13) 'As stated— or' (<s>sūtra</s> 6) //

ityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: As to what was said: 'in disagreement' /
Disagreement is with respect to the object; agreement is with respect to the intrinsic nature /
The same should be seen regarding instability too // 6 //

If the apprehension of common properties and the like were stated as the cause of doubt without qualification, then since it does not produce [doubt] later, it should not produce it earlier either— hence non-doubt; or since it produced [doubt] earlier, it should produce it later too— hence perpetual doubt. But it is not without qualification as the cause of doubt— so neither non-doubt nor perpetual doubt— this is the meaning /
'By this'— by the use of the same term /
For the word '<s>samāna</s>' is a synonym of 'similar'— as was explained earlier /
As to what was also said: 'because of the absence of similarity, ascertainment and doubt have a cause-effect [relation]' /
The meaning is: the non-determination of the specific [factor] is common to both /
But what the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> called 'similarity' should not be understood as such /
For if the production of cause and effect is similarity, that is both over-extensive and non-extensive /
Because even eternal things can be causes /
Therefore, the word 'similarity' does not denote similarity /
Rather, it pertains to the positive and negative concomitance of the properties of cause and effect— he says /
'Because of the existence of the cause'— this has been answered by the very non-determination, because truth is not apprehended /
Because even when two [reasons] with established counter-theses are combined, since they are not seen elsewhere, they are subsumed under the uncommon [reason] alone;
but when intended individually, they are different pseudo-reasons— this is the purport /
'And doubt does not arise from instability' /
(185/2) It is not a separate cause but rather an accessory to the apprehension of common properties and the like— this is the meaning /
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.7: Wherever there is doubt, in that very way there is the progression of successive [debates] //
'What is the purport of this <s>sūtra</s>?'— this is the question about the purport /

children.translated_text:
For by the logical sequence, the order of enumeration has been overridden in the examination of doubt; but in the case of <s>pramāṇa</s> and the like, since there is no cause for overriding, in accordance with the order of enumeration, the <s>pramāṇas</s> are examined before <s>prameya</s> and the rest; and among those, first the examination of the general definition of <s>pramāṇa</s>, since the specific definitions presuppose that /
The general definition is: <s>pramāṇa</s> is the means of apprehension; and that means-of-apprehension-hood belongs to perception and the like alone— hence 'of perception and the like' was said /
This the <s>vārttikakāra</s> states /
'Now at this point'— /
(186/1) He asks what is to be examined /
'What then of these?'— /
All debaters must accept means of knowledge in order to establish their own doctrines,
since without those, the establishment of their doctrines is impossible /
But one who does not even have his own position— he is neither a person of the world nor an examiner, and should be disregarded like a madman /
Therefore, since it is established for all living beings, the <s>pramāṇa</s> in general should not be examined— this is the purport /
The answer: 'first, possibility' /
'Examination is not without doubt'— so he states the seed of doubt /
'Of the existent and non-existent' /
He states the prima facie view /
'Having dispelled doubt' /
Here the intent of the prima facie objector, the <s>Mādhyamika</s>, is as follows: /
Although for me, who holds the doctrine that nothing can withstand examination, there is no means of knowledge that withstands examination, nevertheless, even the <s>pramāṇas</s> established in common usage, when examined by those very <s>pramāṇas</s>, do not withstand examination; and this is the fault of the <s>pramāṇas</s> that dissolve through self-contradiction, not my fault /
For cognition is the <s>pramāṇa</s>, and by its connection [with the object] there is the <s>prameya</s>, and that is the object /
Now if the <s>pramāṇa</s> arises first from the object, the <s>prameya</s>, then before the <s>pramāṇa</s> there is no such object— hence the contradiction with the <s>sūtra</s> 'from the contact of sense organs [with objects]' etc. // 8-9 //
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.10: If [the means of knowledge] are established later, there is no establishment of the <s>prameya</s> (object of knowledge) from the <s>pramāṇas</s> // 10 //
Now if the <s>prameya</s> is first and the <s>pramāṇa</s> later— to that he says: /
'Later' /

children.text: yadyapi svarūpaṃ na pramāṇādhīnaṃ, tathāpi tasya prameyatvaṃ tadadhīnaṃ, tadapi cetpramāṇātpūrvaṃ na pramāṇayoganibandhanaṃ syādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Although the intrinsic nature [of the object] does not depend on the <s>pramāṇa</s>, nevertheless its <s>prameya</s>-hood (status as object of knowledge) depends on it; and if that [<s>prameya</s>-hood] is prior to the <s>pramāṇa</s>, it would not be grounded in connection with the <s>pramāṇa</s>— this is the meaning /
This is what was stated: 'the designation <s>prameya</s>' // 10 //
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.11: If [they are] established simultaneously, because of being restricted to individual objects, there would be no sequential functioning of cognitions //

children.translated_text:
In simultaneity, there is contradiction with observation,
and contradiction with the <s>sūtra</s> /
The formulation is: perception and the like should not be treated as <s>pramāṇas</s>, because they do not convey objects in any of the three times /
Whatever is such that it is not treated as a <s>pramāṇa</s>— like the horns of a hare— and this is such; therefore, it is so /
Having thus stated the prima facie view, he states the established conclusion /
'Here the resolution' /
The meaning of the <s>bhāṣya</s> 'because of being a cause of apprehension' and so on is: the exposure of the non-establishment of the reason 'because of not conveying objects in all three times' /
The <s>vārttikakāra</s> himself states the refutation of this inference /
'The invalidity of perception and the like' /
(187/2) An inference that has attained its own existence can indeed bring about the invalidity of perception and other <s>pramāṇas</s>;
but not one that has not attained its own existence, since by contradiction with its own thesis, its very self-existence is impossible— so how can it bring about their invalidity?— this is the purport /
If the <s>pramāṇas</s> do not establish objects, then even [the designation] 'perception and the like' would not exist /
The meaning is: those [<s>pramāṇas</s>] are not established by <s>pramāṇa</s> [to be non-existent] and yet called 'perception and the like' /
And it is not the case that their object-establishing capacity, their being within the scope of the words 'perception' and the like that denote general and particular [properties]— he says: /
'And how otherwise?' /
Moreover, in the denial of validity, there is no non-existence of the <s>pramāṇas</s> perception and the like /
For by 'the boy without a water-pot,' the boy is not denied— what then?— his property of connection with a water-pot [is denied]; and therefore, the non-existence of the <s>pramāṇas</s>, which is the intent of the prima facie objector, would not follow— he says: /
'Because of the denial of the property' /
He raises a doubt /
'But because of the non-independence of the entity' /
He refutes /
'Even so' /
'Being denied' (188/3)— where merely this much is to be said, 'being enjoined' is for the purpose of illustration /
'By this, the meaning of the suffix'— /
The meaning of the word '<s>prāmāṇya</s>' (validity)— this is the meaning /
And the reason, as literally stated, is in a different substrate— he says: /
'And this reason' /
The <s>bhāṣya</s> beginning 'as to what was also said' he explains /
'As to what was said: by <s>pramāṇa</s>' /
'The possibility of perception and the like is negated' /
The meaning is: in the absence of perception and the like, there is [merely] a statement of causal factors /
He says that [the opponent] merely announces the impossibility of perception and the like, which is already established /
'Now if impossibility is [merely] announced' /
For there is no cessation of what is non-existent— the meaning is: a non-existent pot is not destroyed by a hammer-blow // 11 //
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.12: Because of the non-establishment in the three times, the denial is unjustified //

children.translated_text: What is to be demonstrated? // 12 //

He teaches /
'Because of the non-establishment in the three times, the denial is unjustified'— by this very statement /
He resolves /
'This is not a fault' /
Your statement contradicts your own acceptance, but for us this is neither a statement [we make] nor contradicted by [our] acceptance— this is the meaning /
'And there is no reasoning for the denial of the substrates' /
(190/1) Inference is not capable of denying the substrate, because the reason would have an unestablished locus— this is the meaning /
Moreover, for one who challenges <s>pramāṇa</s> in general, the two statements 'perception and the like are invalid' and 'perception and the like are valid' have a distinction and non-distinction of meaning that does not withstand examination— he says: /
'The invalidity of perception and the like' /
'It should be stated just thus' /
Because of the economy of not using the negative particle /
'That, in [the presence of] similarity or [not]' /
When it is said 'the pot does not exist' with the intention of expressing its incapacity even when the pot exists, one understands: it is not capable of fetching water /
'The denial of what is accepted in other systems' /
In other systems, whatever kind of <s>pramāṇa</s> is accepted, its acceptance occurs /
Just as 'the <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial nature) does not exist'— the nature of the world-cause as consisting of pleasure, pain, and delusion, i.e., the <s>pradhāna</s>-hood, is denied;
but not the world-cause [itself], since another kind of it is accepted /
'How?'— this challenges the <s>pramāṇa</s> /
'Of what?'— this challenges what is to be demonstrated /
'And what?'— this challenges the demonstrator /
He analyzes the challenge to what is to be demonstrated: /
'One who has not understood' /
He analyzes the challenge to the demonstrator: /
'And one who has understood' /
Where (191/1) is what is to be demonstrated?
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.13: And because of the denial of all <s>pramāṇas</s>, the denial is unjustified //
