children.translated_text: "Of the collection of phonemes" etc.

children.text: varṇasyaikasya vāstavatvāt kadācidvikāra upapadyate buddhiḥ samāhāramātrasya tu tatsamudāyasya na vikārasambhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because a single phoneme has real existence, the notion of modification is sometimes possible; but for a mere aggregate — i.e., the collection of those [phonemes] — modification is impossible.
Therefore, even one who does not wish to must speak of the teaching as substitution with respect to that [collection].

children.text: sa varaṃ kḷptatvādekasminnapyastu varṇa iti ityarthaḥ // 40 //
children.translated_text: Let that [substitution], being well-established, exist even in a single phoneme — this is the meaning. //40//

Thus, having refuted the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> view that sound is manifested as embedded in form and the like, that same <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, if he stands firm [saying] that because of the scriptural teaching of the relation of <s>prakṛti</s> (original) and <s>vikāra</s> (modification) among phonemes, like clay and gold, the phonemes are permanent as undergoing modification — then the examination is begun: "sound is of two kinds" etc. The teaching of modification does not apply to mere <s>dhvani</s> (articulated sound) — it cannot establish its permanent-as-modifiable nature; it could only establish this for the phonemic (<s>varṇa</s>) [level], if there were no doubt. But there is doubt even there. For some declare "<s>iko yaṇ aci</s>" and the like as teaching of modification. Others, however, [declare it] as teaching of substitution (<s>ādeśa</s>). Because of the divergent interpretations of commentators, there is doubt. Therefore, without examination, one cannot determine — this is the meaning. In this examination, [the conclusion] is determined as: the teaching is one of substitution. "Substitution" etc. Indeed, the constituent particles belonging to the gold-class, abandoning one configuration and adopting another configuration, are modified as a bracelet or as a <s>vardhamāna</s> [ornament] — for there is a continuity (<s>anugama</s>) of gold-class particles in all of them. But we do not observe a continuity of <s>i</s>-kāra or of any particle constituting it in <s>ya</s>-kāra. Therefore, from the absence of modification, we determine this to be substitution. He shows another proof for the absence of modification: "of those having different causes" etc. For if <s>ya</s>-kāra were a modification of <s>i</s>-kāra, those about to employ <s>ya</s>-kāra would first take up <s>i</s>-kāra, adopting the open (<s>vivṛta</s>) articulatory effort that is its cause. But those who are about to employ <s>ya</s>-kāra, needing it independently, adopt the slightly-closed (<s>īṣatspṛṣṭa</s>) articulatory effort. Therefore, we conclude that <s>ya</s>-kāra is not a modification of <s>i</s>-kāra. He states another proof: "and in the case of non-modification" etc. He states the non-difference of the two reasons — the one that produces and the one that indicates: "in both" etc. He states yet another proof: "being employed" etc. Just as milk, depending on time and ripening, is seen to become curd — it is not the case that <s>i</s>-kāra becomes <s>ya</s>-kāra in such a [gradual] manner — this is the meaning. If it is not a modification, then how is the grammatical description "<s>iko yaṇ aci</s>" [to be understood]? To this he says: "and in the case of non-modification" etc. When there is occasion for employing <s>ik</s> [vowels] in <s>saṃhitā</s> (euphonic combination), [the rule] prescribes the employment of <s>yaṇ</s> [semivowels] — the <s>sūtra</s> does not [mean] that <s>yaṇ</s> is a modification of <s>ik</s> — this is the meaning. Now, granted it is not a modification, but <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation) is something different [from modification], and from that the phonemes will be eternal — to this he says: "and this much" etc. "Whether <s>pariṇāma</s>" — prima facie it means a cause-effect relation, and ultimately [it is the same]. Milk or its particles never transform into the form of curd — for particles do not have the nature of composites. Therefore, only the cause-effect relation is real. And that does not exist among phonemes, since <s>yaṇ</s> is produced independently of <s>ik</s>. Therefore, when there is occasion for employing <s>ik</s> in <s>saṃhitā</s>, the employment of <s>yaṇ</s> is the grammatical description — this is the meaning. And for another reason this is a teaching of substitution — he says:
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.41: Because of the increase of the original, from the increase of the modification.
And for this reason too, there is no relation of original and modification [among phonemes] —
"Increase of the original" etc.

children.text: mahadbhiḥ khalu tūlapiṇḍairārabdhaḥ sthūlaḥ piṇḍo 'lpaiścārabdho mahānalpa iti dṛṣṭaṃ tadvadihāpi dīrghekāravikārasya yakārasyekāravikārādbhavitavyaṃ viśeṣeṇa, na cāsti viśeṣaḥ tasmānna prakṛtivikārabhāva
children.translated_text: Indeed, a large ball made from many cotton tufts is large, and one made from few is small — this is observed. Likewise here too, if <s>ya</s>-kāra were a modification of the long <s>ī</s>-kāra, it should be especially [different] from the modification of [the short] <s>i</s>-kāra; but no such difference exists. Therefore, there is no relation of original and modification —
this is the meaning. //41//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.42: The observation of less, equal, or more [is] not a valid reason for [denying] modifications.

children.text:
asyākṣepasūtram---
nyūna--tuḥ ( sū. 41 ) // alpena hi nyagrodhavījenārabdho nyagrodhatarurmahān tato 'timahatā vā nārikelabījenārabdho nārikelataruralpaḥ nārikelabījaireva parasparāpekṣamāṇasamairārabdhaḥ sama iti /
asya pratyācayānasūtram /
dvividhasyāpi hetoriti /
yadi ca nyūnasamādhikopalabdheriti sādhanaṃ tadā dvividhasya hetorabhāvād
children.translated_text: And if "because of the observation of less, equal, or more" is [presented as] a proof, then because of the absence of a twofold cause,
and because a mere counter-example is not probative,
and because a counter-counter-example is possible — this is the refutation. //42//

The objection-<s>sūtra</s> to this —
"Less... reason" (sū. 42[=41]) // For a great <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan) tree produced from a small <s>nyagrodha</s> seed is large; one produced from an even larger coconut seed — the coconut tree — is small; and one produced from <s>nyagrodha</s> seeds that are equal relative to each other is equal. The reply-<s>sūtra</s>: "of a twofold cause" etc.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.43: Not [so], because of the variation of modifications among those of unequal origins.

children.text:
yadi ca nyūnasamādhikopalabdherityanenānaikāntikodbhāvanaṃ prakṛtyanuvidhānasya kriyate tadā dūṣaṇapakṣe nātulyaprakṛtīnāṃ vikāravikalpāditi dūṣaṇam /
anaikāntikadoṣasyāsambandhatvaṃ nāma nyūnasamādhikatve tu prakṛtyanuvidhānaṃ vikāparāṇāmapracyutam /
tathā hyatulyāyāḥ prakṛterivakārā vikalpyante prakṛtibhedamanuvidhīyante, na jātu nyagrodhabījād
nārikelapādapo bhavati bhavati ca nyagrodhabījānnyagrodhapādapa
iti /
etaduktaṃ bhavati prakṛtibhedānuvidhānaṃ vikārabhedānāṃ brūmopa na pūnastadvivṛddhihrāsābhyāṃ tadvivṛddhihrāsau yenānaikāntikatvamudbhāvyeta tasmādanaikāntikodbhāvanamasaṃbaddhāmityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: What is being said is this: we assert the proportionality of modification-differences to origin-differences, not the proportionality of increase and decrease [of modification] to [increase and decrease of] that [origin] — for inconclusiveness could be raised [only against the latter]. Therefore, the disclosure of inconclusiveness is irrelevant — this is the meaning.
"But <s>ya</s>-kāra does not follow <s>i</s>-kāra" — this is the <s>Bhāṣya</s>.
Its meaning is: but [<s>ya</s>-kāra] does not follow the difference of <s>i</s>-kāra.
Therefore, the case of less, equal, or more is an illustration only for the modification of substances, not [for phonemes]. //43//

And if by "because of the observation of less, equal, or more" the disclosure of inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntika</s>) against the proportionality of original to modification is intended, then on the refutation side, the refutation is "not [so], because of the variation of modifications among those of unequal origins." The fault of inconclusiveness is [merely] irrelevance. But in the case of the less, equal, or more, the proportionality of modifications to their originals is not abandoned. For modifications of unequal originals are differentiated — they follow the difference of origin. Never does a coconut tree arise from a <s>nyagrodha</s> seed, but a <s>nyagrodha</s> tree does arise from a <s>nyagrodha</s> seed.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.44: As in the case of inequality in substance-modification, so the alternative of phoneme-modification [should be considered].

children.text:
asyākṣepasūtram--- dravyavikāra iti /
( 308 / 1 ) na prakṛtibhedamavaśyamanuvidhīyante vikārāḥ dravyatvena tulyatve 'pi prakṛtīnāṃ vikāravaiṣamyaṃ tathā ca dīrghahrasvābhyāṃ vaiṣamye vikāravaiṣamyaṃ bhaviṣyati prakṛtisāmyaiva vikāravaiṣamyam iti bhāvaḥ // 44 //
children.translated_text:
The objection-<s>sūtra</s> to this — "substance-modification" etc.
(308/1) Modifications do not necessarily follow the difference of their originals. Even though the originals are equal in being substances, there is inequality of modifications. Likewise, [even] with inequality in being long or short [vowels], there will be inequality of modifications — the purport is that the very equality of the original [leads to] inequality of modification. //44//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.45: No, because of the impossibility of the properties of modification.

children.text:
tatra pratyākhyānasūtram /
na vikāradharmeti /
yadyapi prakṛterdravyatvamabhedastathā 'pi vikārabhede prakṛtibheda evopayujyate na punaḥ prakṛterabhedaḥ
tadvikārāṇāṃ tu yadabhinnaṃ rūpaṃ dravyatvaṃ tatra tasyopayoga iti sthite parihāro 'nvaya
(syākṣepasūtraṃ dravyevikāra iti/) grahaṇaṃ parihāra uktaḥ // 45 //
children.translated_text: The reply-<s>sūtra</s> to that: "not, because of the properties of modification" etc. Although the original shares the [general property of] substance-hood, still, for difference of modification, only difference of origin is operative — not the non-difference of the original. But the common form of modifications that is undifferentiated — namely substance-hood — that [non-difference] is operative there. This being established, the refutation — the statement "substance-modification" is the objection-<s>sūtra</s>; the refutation has been stated. //45//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.46: Because those that have undergone modification do not return [to their original state].
And for this reason too, phoneme-modifications do not exist — he says:
"Modification" etc.

children.text: no khalu kṣīravikāro dadhi punaḥ kṣīraṃ dṛṣṭamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Indeed, milk that has been modified into curd is never again observed [to become] milk — this is the meaning.
"Because of the absence of inference" — this indicates the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s> [for such return]. //46//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.47: Because of the return of gold and the like, [this is] not a valid reason.
The objection to this is the <s>sūtra</s> "of gold and the like."
On the proving side, the refutation is: because of deviation. //47//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.48: Not [so], because of the non-departure of gold-nature from the modifications of that [gold].

children.text:
dūṣaṇapakṣe doṣamāha /
suvarṇodāharaṇopapattiśceti /
tathā hi /
ye suvarṇajātīya avayavā rucakatvamāpannāsta eva pūrvavyūhaparityāgena vardhamānatāmāpannāḥ punā rucakatvamāpadyante tadavayavānāṃ tatra pratyabhijñāyamānatvāta /
na tvihekāro yakārānugata ikārayakārānugato vā 'nyaḥ kaściddharmī dṛśyate ya ittvaṃ parityajya yattvamāpadyate varṇatvaṃ tvanugatamapi na dharmi,
children.translated_text: But here, neither <s>i</s>-kāra pervaded by <s>ya</s>-kāra, nor <s>ya</s>-kāra pervaded by <s>i</s>-kāra, nor any other property-bearer is observed that abandons <s>i</s>-hood and assumes <s>ya</s>-hood. And phoneme-hood (<s>varṇatva</s>), though common [to both], is not a property-bearer,
but merely a property.

children.text: na ca nivartamāna īkāro yakārasya dharmo bhavitumarhati dharmadharmiṇoḥ samānakālatvādityarthaḥ // 48 //
children.translated_text: And <s>ī</s>-kāra that is ceasing cannot be a property of <s>ya</s>-kāra, because property and property-bearer are simultaneous — this is the meaning. //48//

On the refutation side, he states the fault:
"And the gold-example is justified" etc.
For those particles belonging to the gold-class that have assumed the form of a bracelet — those very same [particles], abandoning the previous configuration, having assumed the form of a <s>vardhamāna</s> [ornament], again assume the form of a bracelet, because their particles are recognized therein.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.49: If [phonemes are] eternal, there is no modification; and if non-eternal, [there is] no stable persistence.

children.text:
nanu dadhyatreti prayoge kadekārasyotpadya nirodhaḥ /
tathā dadhi atreti prayoge kadā yakārasyotpadya nirodha ityata āha /
tadetadavagṛhya saṃdhāna iti /
avagraho 'saṃhitā dadhi atretyuccārya dadhyatretyuccāryate dadhyatreti vā saṃdhāya dadhi atretyavagṛhyataityarthaḥ /
// 49 //
children.translated_text: Now, in the usage "<s>dadhy atra</s>" (curd here), when is the cessation of <s>i</s>-kāra after its production? Likewise, in the usage "<s>dadhi atra</s>," when is the cessation of <s>ya</s>-kāra after its production? To this he says: "having apprehended this, euphonic combination" etc. <s>Avagraha</s> (disjunction) is non-<s>saṃhitā</s> (non-euphonic combination) — having pronounced "<s>dadhi atra</s>," one pronounces "<s>dadhyatra</s>"; or having combined euphonically as "<s>dadhyatra</s>," one disjunctively pronounces "<s>dadhi atra</s>" — this is the meaning. //49//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.50: Because of the suprasensory nature of eternal [entities], and because of the alternative of their properties, the denial of phoneme-modifications is not [established].

children.text:
jātivādī pratyavatiṣṭhate /
nityapakṣe tāvaditi /
yathā hi satyapi nityatve ke cidatīndriyāḥ yathā paramāṇvākāśādayaḥ ke cidaindriyakāḥ yathā gotvādayaḥ evaṃ satyapi nityatve paramāṇvākāśādayo na prakṛtivikārabhūtāḥ
varṇāstu prakṛtivikārabhāvamāpatsyante /
nityā apatyirthaḥ /
seyaṃ vikalpasamā jātirityāha /
virodhāditi /
na khalvaindriyakatvānaindriyakatvābhyāmasmi kaścinnityatvasya virodhaḥ /
prakṛtivikārabhāvena tvasti, na hi saṃbhavati kāryaṃ ca nityaṃ cetyarthaḥ /
// 50 //
children.translated_text: The proponent of universals (<s>jātivādin</s>) resists. 'In the eternality thesis, first' — just as even when eternality obtains, some [things] are supersensory, like atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>), space (<s>ākāśa</s>), and the like, while some are sensory, like <s>gotva</s> (cow-hood) and the like — so too, even when eternality obtains, atoms, space, and the like are not in the relation of material cause and modification, but letters (<s>varṇa</s>) would come to stand in the relation of material cause and modification. 'Eternal' means 'despite being eternal.' This is a futile rejoinder of the type called 'equivocal with alternatives' (<s>vikalpasamā</s>) — he says. 'Because of contradiction' — for indeed, there is no contradiction of eternality by virtue of being sensory or supersensory. But through the relation of material cause and modification there is [contradiction], for it is impossible that something be both an effect and eternal — this is the meaning. //50//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.51: And even in the case of non-persistence, the apprehension of the modification of that [letter would follow], just as the apprehension of the letter [itself].

children.text:
anityapakṣe jātivādyāha /
anavasthāyitve ceti /
yathā satyapyanavasthāyitve varṇā indriyeṇa sambadhya svaviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ janayanti evaṃ vikāramapi kariṣyantītyarthaḥ /
seyaṃ sādharmyasamā jātirityāha /
asaṃbandhāditi /

katipayakṣaṇāvasthānena varṇānāṃ kṣaṇikānāmapi svaviṣayajñānahetubhāvo yujyate avagṛhya ciraṃ sthitvā yadā saṃdhīyate saṃdhāya vā cariṃ sthitvā yadā vigṛhyate tadā varṇānāmanityānāṃ na tāvantaṃ kālamavasthānamastīti nopalabdhihetutvena vikārakṛtatvaṃ varṇānāṃ tulyam /
children.translated_text: By persisting for a few moments, even momentary letters can serve as causes of the cognition pertaining to their own objects; but when [letters] are combined — having been apprehended and having persisted for a long time — [and] when, after being combined, they persist for a long time and then are separated, then the non-eternal letters do not persist for that length of time — therefore the letter-apprehension is not equal [in force] to the production of modification by virtue of being a cause of apprehension.
Therefore, because of the absence of connection, the apprehension of letters is incapable of establishing the modification of letters — this is the meaning.

children.text: mābhūdrarṇopalabdhirvarṃṇavikāreṇa sākṣātsaṃbaddhā odaśavirodhitayā tu tannivṛttyā pāriśeṣyādvikāraṃ sādhayiṣyatītyata āha /
children.translated_text: Lest one say: granted, the apprehension of letters is not directly connected with the modification of letters, yet through the force of contradiction, by the elimination of that [eternality], it will establish modification by the method of residual elimination — to this he says:
'Nor does the apprehension of letters [establish modification].' //51//

In the non-eternality thesis, the proponent of universals says: 'and even in the case of non-persistence' — just as even when non-persistence obtains, letters produce cognition pertaining to their own object by coming into contact with the sense-organ, so too they would produce modification — this is the meaning. This is a futile rejoinder of the type called 'equal in similarity' (<s>sādharmyasamā</s>) — he says. 'Because of the absence of connection' —

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.52: Because of the absence of eternality when [letters] have the property of undergoing modification, and because of the impossibility of modification at a different time, there is no refutation.

children.text:
tadevaṃ jātyuttaramutthitameva māritaṃ kṛtvā bhāṣyakāro 'traivārthe sūtraṃ paṭhati /
vikāradharmitva iti /
vārtikam upalabhyamānasya cekārasya yatvānupapatteriti /
( 309 / 17 ) avagṛhya ciraṃ sthitvā saṃdhāya yadā yatvaṃ tadopalabhyamānatekārasya nāstītyarthaḥ // 52 //
children.translated_text: Thus, having treated the futile rejoinder (<s>jāti</s>) as dead even as it arose, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> recites the <s>sūtra</s> on this very topic. 'When there is the property of undergoing modification' — the <s>Vārttika</s>: 'and of the apprehended <s>e</s>-letter, because of the impossibility of <s>ya</s>-hood.' (309/17) When, having been apprehended and having persisted for a long time, [the letters] are combined, at that time the <s>ya</s>-hood of the apprehended <s>e</s>-letter does not exist — this is the meaning. //52//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.53: Because of the non-restriction of the material cause of the modifications of letters.

children.text:
itaśca varṇavikārānupapattiḥ /
prakṛtyaniyamāditi /
kṣīrajātīyasya dadhijātīyo vikāro na punaḥ kadā cidapi dadhijātīyasya kṣīrajātīyā vikārā upalabhyante /
iha tu yathekārajātīyasya yakārajātīyo vikāro dadhyatreti dṛśyate evaṃ yakārajātīyasyāpi vikāra ikārajātīyo dṛśyate yathā vyatheḥsati prasāraṇe yakārasyekāra
children.translated_text: But here, just as the modification of the <s>e</s>-letter-class is of the <s>ya</s>-letter-class — as in <s>dadhyatra</s> — so too the modification of the <s>ya</s>-letter-class is observed to be of the <s>i</s>-letter-class, as in [the grammatical rule] '<s>vyatheḥ</s>, when there is <s>prasāraṇa</s>, the <s>ya</s>-letter becomes an <s>i</s>-letter'
— thus.
Therefore, because of non-restriction, there is no relation of material cause and modification
— this is the meaning. //53//

And for another reason the modification of letters is untenable: 'because of the non-restriction of the material cause.' The modification of what belongs to the milk-class is of the curd-class; but never are modifications of the curd-class observed to [revert to] the milk-class.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.54: From restriction within non-restriction, there is no non-restriction.
Here the quibbler (<s>cchalavādin</s>) resists.
'From restriction within non-restriction' (sūtra 54). //54//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.55: Because of the contradiction between restriction and non-restriction, and because of restriction within non-restriction, there is no refutation.

children.text:
tadetasya vākchalatvamāpādayati /
niyamāniyamavirodhāditi /
niyamāniyamasāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ virudhyate na tvādhārādheyabhāva ityarthaḥ
// 55 //
children.translated_text: He demonstrates that this is verbal quibbling (<s>vākchala</s>). 'Because of the contradiction between restriction and non-restriction' — the co-residence (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) of restriction and non-restriction is contradictory, but not the container-contained relation — this is the meaning. //55//

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.56: But because of the tenability of modification through the acquisition of a different quality, obliteration, diminution, augmentation, residue, and fusion, [there are] modifications of letters.

children.text:
tadevaṃ prakṛtivikārabhāvaṃ nirākṛtya vikāravacanavyaktiṃ śabdānāmādeśapakṣe samarthayati /
na ceyaṃ varṇavikāropapattiriti /
ekasyāprayoge anyasya prayogo vikāra
iti sāmānyalakṣaṇam /
tasya viśeṣānāha /
sa bhidyata iti /
upamardde nāmeti /
yathā 'sterbhūriti /
leśaḥ sta ityatrāsterakāralope sakāramātrasya leśasyaikadeśasya vyavasthāpanam /

children.translated_text: 'Fusion (<s>śleṣa</s>)' —
an augment (<s>āgama</s>) of the base or of the suffix.

children.text: atrāpi kevalasyāprayoge viśiṣṭasya prayoga ityetāvatā vikārasāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ lakṣaṇīyam /
children.translated_text: Here too, the general definition of modification should be understood as just this much: when the mere [letter] is not used, the qualified [form] is used.
By this, the <s>Vārttika</s> too is explained. //56//

Having thus refuted the relation of material cause and modification, he justifies the term 'modification' in the sense of substitution (<s>ādeśa</s>) of words. 'And this tenability of letter-modification' — the general definition is: the non-use of one [letter] and the use of another is modification. He states its specific types. 'It is divided' — 'in obliteration (<s>upamarda</s>), namely' — as in <s>aster bhūḥ</s> [where a letter is obliterated]. 'Residue (<s>leśa</s>)' — in <s>sta</s>, when the <s>ra</s>-letter of <s>aster</s> is elided, only the residual portion (<s>leśa</s>), the <s>sa</s>-letter alone, is established.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.57: Those [letters], ending in an inflectional affix, are a word (<s>pada</s>).

children.text: tadevamuktena krameṇa varṇānāmanityatāṃ pratipādya śabdaprāmāṇyopayogi padaṃ nirūpayati /
children.translated_text: Having thus demonstrated the non-eternality of letters in the stated manner, he now determines the word (<s>pada</s>), which is useful for establishing the validity of verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>).
Those... word (sūtra 57). //

children.text:
evaṃ kila ke citpaśyanti na varṇāḥ pratipādayantyarthān
te hi pratyekaṃ vā anvayadhiyamādadhīran nāgadantā iva śikyālambanaṃ militā vā grāvāṇa
iva piṭharadhāraṇam /
tatra na tāvatpūrvaḥ kalpaḥ /
pratyekamarthapratyayānutpādāt /
varṇāntaroccāraṇānarthakyācca /
nāpi saṃhatāḥ ekavaktṛprayoge kramaniyamena saṃghātānupapatteḥ /
anekakartṛkaprayoge 'pi satyapi yaugapadye arthapratyayānutpādanāt /
nāpi kramavatpūrvavarṇānubhavabhāvitasaṃskārasahito 'ntyavarṇapratyayo 'rthapratyayaheturiti sāṃpratam /
bhāvanāparanāmnaḥ saṃskārasya svotpādakānubhavaviṣayasmṛtijananādanyatra sāmarthyādarśanāt /
na hi gavānubhavajanitaḥ saṃskāraḥ karoti smṛtiṃ turaṅgame /
api ceyamantyavarṇaśrutiḥ svārthasaṃketasmṛtyapekṣā vārthapratyayamādadhīta anapekṣā vā, tadapekṣatve tatkāle antyavarṇaśrutiruparatā kṣaṇikatveneti kayā saṅketasmṛtirapekṣyate antyavarṇaśrutisamaye ca saṃketasmṛtiranāgateti kimantyavarṇapratyayo 'pekṣeta /
saṃketasmṛtyanapekṣatve agṛhītasaṃketasyāpi prathamaśrāviṇor 'thapratyayaprasaṅgaḥ /
na hi ciradhyastasyānapekṣitasmṛteḥ saṃketagrahasyāsti kaścidupayoga iti /
na ca bhāvanākhyasaṃskārasahito 'ntyavarṇaḥ pratyāyako 'rthasya /
nāpyanya eva kaścitpūrvavarṇānubhavajanitaḥ saṃskāraḥ prokṣaṇādibhiriva vrīhyāderantyavarṇapratyayasahakārīti yuktam /
anekādṛṣṭakalpanāprasaṅgāt /
sa eva tāvadadṛṣṭacaraḥ kalpanīyastasya cānekatvamiti so 'yaṃ varṇebhyor 'thapratyayo bhavannanupapadyamānastadatiriktaṃ sphoṭānubhavamāyatate /
asti hi bhinnaṣvepi varṇeṣu vākyamidamekaṃ padamiti cā sarvajanīno 'nubhavaḥ /
na cāsau bhinnavarṇālambano bhavitumarhati ekasya nānātvavirodhāt /
tasmādvarṇātiriktaṃ padaṃ vākyaṃ vā'lambate /
tacce pratyekameva dhvanayo 'bhivyañjayanti kevalaṃ pūrve dhvanayaḥ svarūpamābhāsayante caramastu vyaktam /
na ceyamarthe vidhā saṃbhavinī pratyakṣajñānaniyatatvāt
vyaktavyaktāvabhāsitāyāḥ pade pratyakṣe upapattiḥ
arthasya tu padagamyasyāpratyakṣasya mānāntareṇa grahaṇamastīti agrahaṇaṃ vā na tu sphuṭāsphuṭatvābhyāṃ yogaḥ /
api ca yasminnanuvartamāne yadvyāvartate tattasmādbhidyate yathā suvarṇākyaveṣvanuvartamāneṣu kaṭakamukuṭādayaḥ /
anuvartamāneṣu tu varṇeṣu vyāvartante padabhedāstasmātte 'pi varṇebhyo bhinnā iti tānpratyāha /
te vibhaktyantāḥ padam /
ta eva varṇā eva padaṃ na tu tadatiriktaṃ sphoṭākhyamityarthaḥ /
idamatrākūtam /
na tāvadvarṇātiriktaḥ padātmā kaścidupalabhyate pratyakṣeṇa, padamiti tu vyapadeśastāneva varṇān bahūnapyekasmṛtisamārohitayā vā ekārthadhīhetutayā vā abhinnakārakāvasthāvattayā vālambate bhāktaḥ /
na caivamanyonyasaṃśrayaḥ
nartte padāvadhāraṇāpadarthādhigamo na cārthādhigamantareṇa padāvadhāraṇamiti /
ekasmṛtibuddhisamārohiṇāṃ varṇānāmasatyarthavattayā 'vabodhe sujñānatvāt tanmātrasya ca svārthena saṃketagrahasyāpi sukaratvāt taduttarakālatvācca padamiti kārakaśabdapravṛtteḥ /
itarathā sarveṣu kārakaśabdeṣu durvāramitaretarāśrayatvaṃ kāryopahitamaryādatvātkārakāṇāṃ tadanupātitvācca tacchabdānāṃ, tasmādvyapadeśamātrānurodhena naikaikavarṇamātrāvabhāsinīṣu śrotrajāsu buddhiṣu tadāhitavāsanālabdhajanmāyāṃ cānu bhūtavarṇasaṃkalanātmikāyāṃ smatibuddhāvaprathamāno varṇavibhāgopamardena na śakyaḥ padātmā pratyakṣa
iti vaktuṃ, nāpi nirbhāgasya sphuṭāsphuṭatve vā bhāgaviparyāsova vā yujyate, no khalu sarvathā 'dṛśyamāno nāma sphuṭaḥ nāpi samāropaviṣayaḥ /
na hi sāmānyātmanā 'pyagṛhītā śuktī rajatatvasamāropaviṣayaḥ /
na ca nirbhāgepadātmani gṛhīte kiṃ cidasyāgṛhītamavaśiṣyate yadagrahaṇādavyaktatvaṃ vā samāropo vā bhavet /
na ca tadeva tadaiva tena gṛhītamagṛhītaṃ ca saṃbhavati /
tasmānna pratyakṣasya tadābhāsasya vā gocaraḥ padātmā /

children.translated_text: Thus indeed, some hold this view: phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>) do not convey meanings — / for they would either individually produce the cognition of meaning, like elephant-tusks [individually] supporting a swing, or collectively, like grinding stones supporting a mortar. / Of these, the first alternative is not [acceptable] — / because individually, no cognition of meaning arises; / and because the utterance of additional phonemes would be purposeless. / Nor do they [convey meaning] collectively — because in the usage of a single speaker, a combination is impossible due to the fixed sequential order [of phonemes]; / and even in the usage of multiple speakers, even when there is simultaneity, no cognition of meaning is produced. / Nor is it proper [to say] that the cognition of the last phoneme, together with the residual impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) produced by the experience of prior phonemes, is the cause of the cognition of meaning — / because the impression, also called <s>bhāvanā</s> (disposional force), has no capacity other than generating the recollection of the object of the experience that produced it. / For an impression generated by the experience of a cow does not produce a recollection of a horse. / Moreover, does this hearing of the last phoneme produce the cognition of meaning with dependence on the recollection of the convention [connecting word and meaning], or without such dependence? If with such dependence, then at that time, the hearing of the last phoneme has ceased because of being momentary — so by what [cognition] is the convention-recollection required? And at the time of hearing the last phoneme, the convention-recollection has not yet arisen — so what would the last-phoneme-cognition wait for? / If without dependence on convention-recollection, then even for one who has not grasped the convention, being a first-time hearer, the consequence of cognition of meaning would follow. / For when the convention-grasp has been long-established and its recollection is not required, there is no use for it. / And the last phoneme together with the impression called <s>bhāvanā</s> is not the conveyor of meaning. / Nor is it proper [to say] that some other impression generated by the experience of prior phonemes, like sprinkling (<s>prokṣaṇa</s>) and the like [which prepare] rice-grain, cooperates with the last-phoneme-cognition — / because of the consequence of postulating multiple unseen [entities]. / That very [unseen entity] must be postulated as operating invisibly, and it would be multiple — so this cognition of meaning from phonemes, being unjustifiable, extends to the experience of <s>sphoṭa</s> (the holistic word-entity) beyond those [phonemes]. / For even in phonemes that are distinct, there is a universal experience 'this sentence is one, this word [is one].' / And that [experience] cannot have distinct phonemes as its object, because of the contradiction of plurality with unity. / Therefore, it takes as its object a <s>pada</s> (word) or <s>vākya</s> (sentence) that is distinct from the phonemes. / And that [<s>sphoṭa</s>] is manifested by the individual sounds (<s>dhvani</s>) — the prior sounds merely make its form dimly appear, while the final one [manifests it] clearly. / And this mode [of appearance] with respect to the meaning is not possible [as an alternative to <s>sphoṭa</s>], because the clear-unclear appearance is restricted to perceptual cognition — / [such] appearance in the word, which is perceptual, is justified; / but the meaning, which is cognized through the word and is not perceptible, is either grasped or not grasped by another <s>pramāṇa</s>, but is not amenable to the distinction of clear and unclear [appearance]. / Moreover, that which varies when something persists is different from it — just as when gold persists, bracelets, crowns, and the like [vary]. / But when phonemes persist, word-distinctions vary — therefore those [words] too are different from the phonemes. To them he replies: / 'Those [phonemes] ending in inflection are a word (<s>pada</s>).' / Those very phonemes alone are a word, not something beyond them called <s>sphoṭa</s> — this is the meaning. / The intention here is as follows: / To begin with, no word-entity beyond the phonemes is apprehended by perception; the designation 'word' figuratively takes as its object those very phonemes, either as being superimposed upon a single recollection though they are many, or as being the cause of a single cognition of meaning, or as being in an undifferentiated state of grammatical case (<s>kāraka</s>). / And there is no mutual dependence here — / [the objection being:] without the determination of a word there is no apprehension of word-meaning, and without the apprehension of meaning there is no determination of a word. / [The answer:] Because phonemes that are superimposed upon a single recollection-cognition are easily known even without meaning-content, and because the grasping of the convention of that [set of phonemes] alone with its own meaning is also easy, and because the application of the <s>kāraka</s>-word 'word' occurs after that [convention-grasp]. / Otherwise, in all <s>kāraka</s>-words, the unavoidable mutual dependence [would arise], because the <s>kārakas</s> have their scope delimited by effects, and the words for them follow upon those [delimited scopes]. Therefore, merely following the designation, the word-entity cannot be said to be perceptible — [for it is] not manifested in the auditory cognitions that each reveal only a single phoneme, nor in the recollection-cognition born of the impressions deposited by them, which has the nature of combining the previously experienced phonemes, being unable to withstand the dissolution of phoneme-distinctions — / nor are clear and unclear [appearances] justified for what is partless, nor is there a transposition of parts; / for what is in no way visible is not called 'clear,' nor is it the object of superimposition. / For even a shell not grasped even in its generic form is not the object of the superimposition of silver-hood. / And when the partless word-entity has been grasped, nothing of it remains ungrasped, the non-grasping of which could give rise to unclearness or superimposition. / And it is not possible that the same thing at the same time is both grasped and ungrasped. / Therefore, the word-entity is not the object of perception or of something that appears as perception. / Nor of inference born from the mark of cognition-of-meaning, because of the consequence of mutual dependence. / To begin with, the word-entity does not produce cognition of meaning merely by its existence — lest it always do so, being eternal. / Therefore, [it does so] through its own cognition. / And that cognition of it [arises] from the cognition of meaning — and thus, when there is cognition of meaning, there is cognition of the word, and when there is cognition of the word, there is cognition of meaning — so the mutual dependence is evident. / And this meaning-cognition cannot fail to arise from the phonemes — for they, having been previously experienced individually and being endowed with a sequential order based on [prior] experience, being superimposed upon a single cognition, are capable of producing meaning-cognition. / And there is no lack of distinction among phonemes in [different] orders — unordered, sequentially ordered, and reversely ordered — / because recollection follows the arrangement of prior experience, / and because distinction is justified from the distinction of that arrangement. / Even when the phonemes are non-different [in themselves], the difference of words in [sequences like] 'hi,' 'ne,' etc. will be justified even without postulating <s>sphoṭa</s> — / because word-difference follows upon difference of sequence; and the capacity to produce meaning-cognition belongs not to mere phonemes, but to phonemes as qualified by [specific] sequential order, addition, omission, and the like. / Each such qualification, even when the phonemes are the same, being different [from other qualifications], establishes word-difference. / Therefore, when the arising of meaning-cognition from observed phonemes following an observed pattern is justified, one ought not to postulate an unseen <s>sphoṭa</s>-entity by denying the observed phoneme-distinctions — this is established. / 'Those [phonemes] ending in inflection are a word' — / 'Modified as observed' — this is the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. / Modified by the occurrence of a different quality (<s>guṇa</s>) and the like — 'as observed' means 'as [established] by <s>pramāṇa</s>' — not in the sense of a modification of the base form (<s>prakṛti</s>), since that is contradicted by <s>pramāṇa</s> — this is the meaning. / The <s>Vārttika</s>: 'then the cognition of meaning would not obtain' — / This is the stated intention of the <s>sphoṭa</s>-proponent. / The reply: / 'From the cognition of the last phoneme' — / The cognition of phonemes is phoneme-cognition; the last such phoneme-cognition is the last-phoneme-cognition — [that is,] the recollection that encompasses all the phonemes. / And that, requiring the individual experiences of the prior phonemes, becomes the final [cognition]. / If so, then even for those who have not grasped the convention, that [recollection] would exist — and then the consequence of meaning-cognition for them would follow — therefore he says: / 'Requiring the reconnection-cognition of prior phonemes' — / 'Prior' refers to the time of convention-grasping; the phonemes occurring at that time are 'prior'; their 'reconnection' (<s>pratisandhāna</s>) is [the recognition]: 'these are just as many, of just such kinds, as the [phonemes] whose convention was grasped' — that very [recognition] is the cognition; with dependence on that. / And that [reconnection-cognition] does not exist for those who have not grasped the convention — so even though the last-phoneme-cognition exists [for them], it is not a conveyor of meaning — this is the meaning. / A word (<s>śabda</s>) is named because the form of what is to be expressed (<s>abhidheya</s>) is distinguished by connection with a different action — and 'another word' (<s>antaraśabda</s>) is a word denoting a specific [kind], because of the reason of connection with a specific action — this is the meaning. / What is said amounts to this: / That whose expressed [content] does not terminate without connection with a specific action is a <s>nāman</s> (noun); the meaning of a verb (<s>ākhyāta</s>), although in some cases it too is connected with an action, as in 'he offers while approaching' (<s>abhikrāmaṃ juhoti</s>), 'he goes after eating' (<s>bhuktvā vrajati</s>), and the like — nevertheless, 'he offers,' 'he goes,' and the like do not fail to terminate without the connection of an action; but even when co-uttered with those [verb-actions], they are connected. / But the meaning of a noun does not terminate without the meaning of the principal action-word that comes before or after. / For this very reason they say: 'where no other action-word is heard, there the verbal root <s>as</s> (to be) with the suffix <s>bhavantī</s> should be supplied.' / And in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [texts], forms like <s>abhikrāmam</s>, <s>bhoktum</s>, <s>bhakti</s>, and the like, requiring a co-ordinate and the like, not terminating without a specific action, are included under the designation <s>nāman</s>. / He gives an example of this: / 'Such as <s>brāhmaṇa</s>' — / He explains its meaning: 'an aggregate of action and <s>kāraka</s> (action-factor), qualified by the number of <s>kārakas</s>.' / For here, by the action-word, the being (<s>bhāva</s>) of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, namely <s>brāhmaṇatva</s> (Brāhmaṇa-hood), is expressed — since the word <s>bhāva</s> has the sense of action. / And the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who will be [the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>] is the <s>kāraka</s>. / The aggregate of those two — <s>brāhmaṇatva</s> and the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — qualified by the number of one of the <s>kāraka</s>, namely the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who will be, is understood from this noun-word <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — this is the meaning. / He states the definition of the verb (<s>ākhyāta</s>): / 'That which expresses the connection of action with time, having action as its principal [element], is an <s>ākhyāta</s>.' The connection of action with time is [its] being-in-sequence-of-before-and-after. / Because of [its] connection with time, the expression of that is possible. / By this [definition], he distinguishes [the verb] from noun-words like <s>pāka</s> (cooking) and the like. / Even so, in <s>bhuktvā</s> (having eaten), <s>bhoktum</s> (to eat), and the like, the [objection of inclusion under] noun would follow — / for there too, there is the cognition of a collection of moments of action delimited by a temporal boundary — otherwise, the connection with the object (<s>karman</s>) in <s>odanam</s> (rice) would not [be obtained]. / Therefore it is said 'having action as principal.' / For from the verb, the action is understood as self-sufficient, not as dependent on something else. / But in <s>bhoktum</s> and the like, the action is understood [only as] not terminating without another action. / But in <s>vrajati</s> (he goes) and the like, it is not so — this is the principality of action. / By this, <s>pacati</s> (he cooks), <s>paceta</s> (he would cook), <s>pacyate</s> (it is cooked), <s>sthīyate</s> (one stands), and the like — all are included under <s>ākhyāta</s>. / There is no [unwanted] inclusion under noun anywhere. Even <s>asti</s> (exists) and the like, which resemble both nouns and verbs — even there, [the root] <s>as</s> in the sense of <s>san</s> (being) operates with respect to an established form, not with the sense of before-and-after-action — this should be understood. / 'Since every word is pervaded by noun-hood' — / (311/6) The 'majority' is meant in the sense of 'pervasion.' / For generally in a sentence there are many noun-words, while the verb is only one in one sentence — since difference of verb [entails] difference of sentence. / He raises an objection regarding the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic): 'meaning is not cognized from a word' — / For a word expresses either a particular or a universal. Among these, he first refutes the expression of a particular: / 'Particular' — / 'Non-stability' means non-ascertainment. / Adopting [the alternative of] expression of a universal, he says: 'Not of a word' — / He refutes: 'Not of a universal' — / For elders utter sentences for the purpose of practical activity (<s>vyavahāra</s>), not out of addiction [to speech]. / And there is no practical activity accomplished by a universal; rather, all practical activity is accomplished by a particular. / And a word is not the expresser of that [particular] — only the sentence is the expresser of sentence-meaning — so there is no occasion for investigating word-meaning — this is the import of the objection. / He resolves: 'Not when there is a universal as object' — / To begin with, there is no sentence beyond words — this has been stated below. / And it is not proper that the string of phonemes itself, without the intermediate operation of conveying word-meanings, produces awareness of sentence-meaning — / for if [it did] without requiring convention-grasp, it would produce sentence-meaning-awareness even for a first-time hearer who does not know the convention. / Since, when convention-grasp is required, the impossibility of grasping the convention of the sentence with the sentence-meaning — because of [their] infinity and non-deviation — / even unwillingly, the convention of words with their own meanings must be accepted. / Therefore, the universal is the meaning of words, and how those [words], having the intermediate operation of conveying that [universal meaning], convey sentence-meaning — that has been demonstrated by us more thoroughly in the <s>Tattvabindu</s>. / This cognition of the universal from the word — whether 'cow' or 'horse' — extending to all cows or all horses, is restricted by the hearing of a specific [word like] 'white' or 'black' — this is the meaning. / He asks: 'But how is this [possible]?' — / [Forms like] 'stands,' 'goes,' and the like too ought not to function as words with respect to a particular, because of the impossibility of grasping the relation [between them and particulars]. / Therefore, these too are expressers of universals — this is the purport. / The reply: 'This [cognition] is not indeed' — / Thus, from the determination of the universal-expressing nature of the word, and from the [fact that] the cognition from the word [encompasses] both universal-form (<s>ākṛti</s>) and individual (<s>vyakti</s>), and from the disagreement of [different] theorists, doubt arises: / Is the meaning [of a word] all three [universal, form, individual], or [only] one of them? / Thus, having first ascertained the expressing nature [of words] from the cognition of the universal, the transition to another investigation has been shown. / Now, the suspicion that the word's expressing nature arises from the cognition of [only] two [of the three] does not even exist — therefore the transition to the further investigation is justified — he says: 'Let it be so' — / He affirms what is established by the cognition [of both]: 'both action and its means' — / The meaning is: '[the word] <s>bhavitā</s> (will be) <s>gauḥ</s> (a cow).' // 57 //
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.58: In the presence of individual (<s>vyakti</s>), configuration (<s>ākṛti</s>), and universal (<s>jāti</s>), doubt [arises] because of figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>). //

tatrānyatamārthamāha vārttikakāraḥ /
kiṃ vyaktiriti /
( 312 / 9) // 58 //
children.translated_text:
The <s>Bhāṣya</s> [reads]: "Is any one of these the word-referent, or is it all of them?" Therein, the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> states the thesis favoring one of them:
"Is it the individual?" —
(312/9) //58//

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.59: Because words like <s>yā</s> ("which"), collection (<s>samūha</s>), abandonment (<s>tyāga</s>), acceptance (<s>parigraha</s>), number (<s>saṃkhyā</s>), increase (<s>vṛddhi</s>), diminution (<s>apacaya</s>), color (<s>varṇa</s>), compound (<s>samāsa</s>), and affix (<s>anubandha</s>) apply figuratively to the individual, the individual [is the word-referent]. //

children.text:
atra yāśabdādiprayogasāmarthyādvyaktireva padārtha ityeke manyante /
syādetat /
vyaktivadākṛtirapi bhidyataityākṛterapyabhidhāyakaṃ kasmānna bhavatītyata
āha /
ākṛterapīti /
gotvaṃ ca jātirupādhirmaviṣyati tena nātiprasaṅgaḥ /
na copādherabhidhānam /
anabhihitasyāpi tacchabdenopahitāvacchedakatvadarśanāt /
yathā gārgikayā ślāghataityatra ślāghopādhivihito vuñ na ślāghāmāheti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Here, some think that by virtue of the applicability of words like <s>yā</s> and the like, the individual alone is the word-referent.
Objection: just as the individual is differentiated, so too is configuration (<s>ākṛti</s>) — so why should the word not denote configuration as well?
To this he says: "Of configuration too" —
<s>Gotva</s> (cow-hood) is a universal, and would be a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>); therefore there is no over-extension.
And there is no denotation of the limiting condition [itself];
for even when unexpressed, the limiting condition is seen to serve as a delimiting factor for what is denoted by that word.
Just as in "he boasts because of the <s>Gārgī</s>" — here the affix <s>vuñ</s>, conditioned by "boasting" (<s>ślāghā</s>), does not denote "boasting" — this is the import.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.60: Not so, because of the non-fixity of that. //

He refutes this proponent of the restriction of denotation to individuals:
"Not by this" —

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.61: Because of association, location, purpose, activity, measure, containment, proximity, connection, means, and dominion, there is figurative usage of the terms <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, couch, mat, king, <s>saktu</s> (barley-flour), sandal, <s>Gaṅgā</s>, cart, food, and person [respectively] even where the [primary referent] is absent. //

children.text:
nāpratīta upādhirupahitāvacchedāya prabhavati /
na ca gārgikayetyatropādhirvuñābhihito 'pi na pratīyate ślāghata iti padāntareṇa tasyābhidhānāt /
yatra tu ślāghata iti na prayujyate na tatra vuñobhāvābhidhāyinaḥ sādhutvamasti /
seyaṃ vyadhikaraṇe 'nupādhau gatiḥ /
samānādhikaraṇe tu paśvādāvupādhau pratyayāntaśabdavācyatvameva /
yathā dṛtihariḥ śveti /
atra hi dṛtiharirityetāvataiva paśau labdhe tadviśeṣaniyamārtha śveti prayujyate /
na ca prayogādevopādhergamyamānatvādanabhidhānaṃ sāṃpratam /
tadupādhyanabhidhāyinastatra prayoganiyamasya paryanuyojyatvāt /
ananuyojyatve anāderlokaprayogasya sarveṣāmeva śabdānāmanabhidhāyakatvaprasaṅgaḥ /
prayoganiyamādeva hi tebhyo 'pyartho 'vagamyate /
athāpratipādakasya prayoganiyamo nopapadyata iti yatra prayogastatpratipādakatvamityabhyupeyate tadupādhāvapi samānam /
tathā ca smarati bhagavānkātyāyanaḥ
tadantavācyaḥ samānaśabdo 'yamiti /

children.translated_text: "The same-syntactic-locus word" means: the word in the same syntactic locus — the limiting condition is to be expressed by the suffix-word —
— this is the meaning.
Therefore, in restricting [the word-referent] to the individual, the universal (<s>jāti</s>), being uncognized [from the word itself], is incapable [of serving as a delimiter].

children.text: na ca gośabdādanyadasyāḥ pratyāyakamastīti sā 'pi tena pratyāyanīyeti siddhaṃ na vyaktimātraṃ padārtha iti // 60 //
children.translated_text: And since there is no other means of making it known apart from the word "<s>go</s>" (cow), it too must be made known by that [word] — thus it is established that the individual alone is not the word-referent. //60//

A limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>) that is not cognized cannot serve to delimit what is denoted.
And in "he boasts because of the <s>Gārgī</s>," the limiting condition, though denoted by the affix <s>vuñ</s>, is not cognized [from it], since it is denoted by the separate word "boasts" (<s>ślāghate</s>).
But where "boasts" is not used, the affix <s>vuñ</s> does not have the status of a valid expression denoting the limiting condition.
This is the procedure when the limiting condition is in a different syntactic locus.
But when the limiting condition is in the same syntactic locus, as in the case of "animal" (<s>paśu</s>) and the like, the denotation is by the word that forms the suffix of the expression.
As in "<s>dṛtihariḥ śva</s>" ("a tawny [thing that is] a leather-bag — [it is] a dog").
For here, when the animal is obtained by "<s>dṛtihariḥ</s>" alone, the word "<s>śva</s>" (dog) is used for the purpose of restricting that particular [referent].
And it is not correct [to say] that because the limiting condition is understood from usage alone, it is not denoted [by the word];
for the restriction of usage to [a particular] limiting-condition-denotation is subject to challenge.
If it is not subject to challenge, then since worldly usage is beginningless, all words whatsoever would be non-denotative.
For it is from the restriction of usage that meaning is understood from them too.
Now, if it is accepted that "where there is usage, there is denotation" — because the restriction of usage is inexplicable for what does not denote — the same applies to the limiting condition [denoted by the word].
And thus the venerable <s>Kātyāyana</s> states:
"The word in the same syntactic locus — that is to be expressed by the suffix-word" —

children.text:
kaṭārtheṣu vīraṇeṣu vyūhyamāneṣviti bhāṣyam /
kaṭaṃ karotīti nirvartyasya kaṭasya karmatvamanupapannaṃ kārakādhikārīyatvāt karmasaṃjñāyāḥ,

children.translated_text: and because <s>kāraka</s>-status belongs to what is the occasion for action,
and because what is not yet accomplished cannot have the status of an occasion prior to the action.

children.text: tasmāttādarthyanimittādeva kaṭaśabdaḥ kaṭārtheṣu vīraṇeṣu vyūhyamāneṣu vartate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is by reason of purpose (<s>tādarthya</s>) alone that the word "mat" applies to the <s>vīraṇa</s> grasses being arranged for the purpose of [making] a mat.

children.text: vīraṇānāṃ ca vā racyamānānāmasti kaṭakriyāpūrvabhāvitvena nimittabhāva iti // 61 //
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, the <s>vīraṇa</s> grasses being woven do have the status of occasion for the mat-making action, by virtue of being prior to the mat. //61//

The <s>Bhāṣya</s> [reads]: "when <s>vīraṇa</s> grasses are being arranged for the purpose of [making] a mat."
[Objection:] In "he makes a mat," the object-status (<s>karmatva</s>) of the mat-being-produced is inappropriate, because the technical term "object" (<s>karman</s>) belongs to the section on <s>kārakas</s> (case-relations),

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.62: Configuration (<s>ākṛti</s>) [is the word-referent], because of the dependence on that [for the establishment of the universal], and because the establishment of existence (<s>sattva</s>) is [thereby] accomplished. //

children.text:
yadi na jātyā vinā vyaktiniyama iti jātirabhidheyā hanta bhoḥ sā 'pyākṛtyā niyantavpayetyākṛtirevābhidhīyatāmityāha /
yadi tarhīti /
( 314 / 9 ) etadapi dūṣayati /
atrāpi tadevopasthitaṃ na tadanavasthānāditi /
saṃsthānenāpi vyajyamānāṃ jātirekārthasamavāyādvyajyate ca vyavasthāpyate ca /

children.translated_text: while that [universal], persisting through the varying individuals and configurations, is grasped by a non-differentiating cognition.

children.text: tādṛśī ca vyaktisaṃsthānābhidhānānapekṣeṇāpi padena śakyā bodhayituṃ, saṃsthānaṃ tu vyaktivadbhinnamānantyavyabhicārābhyāmaśakyasaṃketagrahaṇaṃ jātyabhidhānamapekṣya na śakyaṃ padenabodhayitumiti na saṃsthānāparanāmākṛtiḥ padārtha ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And such [a universal] can be communicated by a word without depending on the denotation of individual and configuration; but configuration, being differentiated like the individual, being infinite, and being subject to deviation, is incapable of having its convention grasped [directly], and depending on the denotation of the universal, cannot be communicated by a word [alone] — therefore configuration, which is another name for <s>ākṛti</s>, is not the word-referent — this is the meaning.

children.text: nāpi jātidvāreṇa vyaktivadākṛtiḥ padārtho jātyā sahāsambandhādityāha /
children.translated_text: Nor is configuration a word-referent through the mediation of the universal, as the individual is, because of the absence of connection with the universal — thus he says:
"And that which has connection with the universal." //62//

If the individual cannot be restricted without the universal, and the universal must be denoted, well then, since the universal too must be restricted by configuration, let configuration alone be denoted — thus he says:
"If, then" —
(314/9) He refutes this too:
"Here too the same [objection] arises — not so, because of the non-fixity of that."
The universal, though manifested by configuration too, is manifested and established through inherence in a single meaning [i.e., a single real],

children.text: NyS_2,2.63: vyaktyākṛtiyukte 'py aprasaṃgāt prokṣaṇādīnāṃ mṛdgavake jātiḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.63: Even when individual and configuration are present, because of the non-applicability of sprinkling (<s>prokṣaṇa</s>) and the like to a clay cow, the universal (<s>jāti</s>) [alone is the word-referent]. //

children.text:
astu tarhi jātireva padārthaḥ tatra hi sukaraḥ saṃketagrahaḥ vyabhicārābhāvāditi /
vyaktyākṛtyostu vyabhicāraḥ jātyabhidhāyino vyaktāvākṛtau caupacārikaḥ prayogo bhaviṣyatītyabhiprāyeṇāha /
astu tarhīti /
śeṣamasyātirohitārtham /
ekamanekatra varttata iti pratijānānopava nānuyoktavyaḥ /
ubhayena vyāghātāditi /
( 318 / 13 ) yadyekamanekatra vartamānaṃ prativyakti sarvātmanā vartata iti kiṃ tvanekamanekatra vartata iti prāptam /

children.translated_text: And thus there is a contradiction in the very ground of the inquiry.

children.text: athaikamanekatra vartamānaṃ prativyaktyekadeśena varttate tathā 'pi naikamanekatra vartate kiṃ tvanekamanekatreti ekadeśānāmanekatvāditi /
children.translated_text: But if the single [universal] existing in many [loci] exists in each individual only partially, even so it is not one existing in many, but rather many in many — because the parts are many.
This contradiction from both [alternatives] has been stated in the debate on the composite whole (<s>avayavin</s>). //63//

Let the universal alone be the word-referent, for therein the grasping of convention is easy, because of the absence of deviation.
But for individual and configuration there is deviation; the usage of a word denoting the universal with respect to the individual and configuration will be figurative — with this intent he says:
"Let it be so, then" —
The rest of this has a self-evident meaning.
One who claims that a single [thing] exists in many [loci] should not himself be questioned —
"because of contradiction by both" —
(318/13) If the single [universal] existing in many [loci] exists in each individual in its entirety, then it follows that it is not one but many existing in many.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.64: Not configuration, because the manifestation of the universal depends on the individual and configuration. //
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.65: Individual, configuration, and universal — [all three] together are the word-referent. //
Having thus refuted the restriction of denotation to any one [of the three], he states the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion) of unrestricted denotation:
"Individual, configuration... referent" (sūtra 65) //

children.translated_text:
The purport here is as follows:
Immediately after the utterance of the word 'cow,' in one whose conventional connection is known, a cognition arises in a single [cognitive act] that is illuminated by the individual (<s>vyakti</s>), the form (<s>ākṛti</s>), and the universal (<s>jāti</s>) — but not as in 'the settlement is on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>' or 'the cow is a <s>Vāhīka</s> [barbarian],' where, after the cognition of <s>Gaṅgā</s>-hood or cow-hood, the meaning of the sentence — because of the impossibility of relation with that [literal meaning], or because of the inseparability [of the primary meaning from the secondary], or because of the association with a quality that is indicated [by the secondary meaning] — the bank or the <s>Vāhīka</s> person is understood; cognition here is not like that.
Due to the abundance of usage and extreme habituation, even though there is a sequence of cognitions, it is not noticed because of the extreme rapidity.
If [one objects]: 'like the penetration of a hundred lotus petals caused by an extremely swift arrow' —
No, because in the absence of a defeating cognition (<s>bādhaka</s>), when the strong appearance of non-difference in cognition [exists], there is no justification for making it otherwise.
And if that were so, non-difference would not subsist anywhere, and then difference too would not exist, because difference depends on non-difference as its substrate.
Moreover, there is no cognition of form that is devoid of the form-possessor; and form is the universal of a substance. Therefore, because of being characterized by form, the substance is the form-possessor.
And one cannot cognize that by which something is characterized without cognizing that [which is so characterized].
Just as there is no apprehension of a cognition without an object,
therefore, the apprehension of the universal is a part of the apprehension of the substance — it is not possible independently, without the apprehension of the substance.
Therefore, because of being within the scope of a single apprehension, between the universal and the universal-possessor, there is no relation of indicated and indicator. And that apprehension, arising immediately after verbal cognition, is verbal [in nature].
Nor should one say: even when within the scope of a single apprehension, of the universal and the individual, it is the universal alone that is denoted, not the individual —
because, when there is the rule that both are objects of a single cognition, the postulation that both are denoted [by the word] is justified, while the postulation of [only] one being denoted is unjustified.
For the capacity of causes is only in the effect, not in what is not an effect;
and the effect is the experience (<s>anubhava</s>), and that is single — therefore no postulation of difference in capacity [is warranted].
Through that [effect] as a medium, the word is said to be capable regarding the action too; and the medium of the effect is one — therefore, even when the objects are different, the capacity is one alone.
Moreover, for words whose operation depends on human convention, there is no capacity whatsoever that is within the scope of a <s>pramāṇa</s>, that could be either one or many.
By this, [the view that] in the case of a conventional word whose denotation of the universal has been exhausted, a capacity for [denoting] the individual should be postulated, is also rejected.
What others say — that the word, when not engaged elsewhere, has the capacity for that very meaning — that too is rejected.
For that meaning, being either cognized or uncognized, would convey the individual.
If uncognized, it would convey the individual always, because its cause is eternal.
If cognized, the objection of self-dependence is difficult to answer — for it has been said that there is no cognition of the individual distinct from the cognition of the universal.
Therefore, the <s>sūtra</s> of the sage <s>Gautama</s> is correct: 'individuals, forms, and universals are the objects of words.'
Now he raises the proponent of <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion as word-meaning): 'but individuals, forms, and universals are not the objects of words — so say some.'
(321/3) 'Now, because of occurring in substances and the like' —
But between cow-hood and horse-hood, there is no substrate-supersubstrate relation — this is the import.
Even the word '<s>sat</s>' (being), though denoting only what possesses a universal, is not [a valid counter-example]:
Why? Because of not being independent —
The universal-possessors are pots, cloths, and the like; and they are not cognized from the word '<s>sat</s>' independently — as they are from the words 'pot' and the like; rather, from the word '<s>sat</s>,' the cognition wavers among pots and the like. But the word '<s>sat</s>,' dependent on words like 'pot,' becomes the cause of the determination of pots and the like.
Therefore, because of being dependent on words like 'pot,' it is not a denoting word for the universal-possessor — this is the meaning.
'Or alternatively' —
Whatever operates dependently upon something, that does not denote that [thing] — just as the words '<s>Gaṅgā</s>,' 'cow,' and the like [do not denote] the bank, the <s>Vāhīka</s> person, and the like.
Similarly, universal-words (<s>jātiśabda</s>) with respect to the universal-possessor.
Therefore, they are not denoting words of the universal-possessor; for they operate with respect to the universal-possessor only by depending on the universal — such is the kind of dependence — this is the meaning.
'Why then does it not operate with respect to the universal-possessor independently of the universal?' — therefore he says:
'And it has been stated here' —
(321/3) 'Let the cognition of the universal-possessor be merely figurative then' — therefore he says: 'and of the possessor' —
Just as the quality characterized as sovereignty belongs to the master, and being present also in the servant who shares the master's splendor, the word 'master' is applied there — not so is the connection of the quality of universals with the individual — this is the meaning.
Moreover, a word operating in one domain first produces a cognition of that other [primary meaning], and then operates in the other [secondary domain] — as the word 'cow' first produces cognition in a cow and then operates [figuratively] for a <s>Vāhīka</s> person.
But here, the universal-word does not operate with respect to the universal-possessor by transgressing the universal; and figurative usage cannot be simultaneous — he says:
'Because of the absence of sequential operation, and because of the impossibility of simultaneity.'
He refutes the [theory of] coloring by a quality (<s>guṇoparāga</s>):
'And because of the unwanted consequence of producing erroneous cognition' —
Just as through the coloring by a quality, the cognition 'the crystal is blue' [arises] — similarly, all verbal cognition, in the absence of a defeating cognition, would be erroneous — this is the meaning.
He refutes the [theory of] denoting a single particular (<s>ekasvalakṣaṇa</s>):
'Because of being uncommon' —
'And because of the impossibility of convention' should also be considered.
Having thus raised and refuted the proponent of <s>anyāpoha</s>, he [states his own view]:
'Here, by us' —
The three — individuals, forms, and universals — are our word-meanings.
But the relation of subordinate and principal applies only somewhere for some [word]. In the denotation of the universal-possessing individual, both kinds of non-independence are not possible for words.
It is not possible that, in producing the cognition of the individual, words first require the cognition of the universal for that purpose —
because, since both are necessarily objects of a single cognition, a temporal sequence is impossible.
Nor is there independence [of universal-words] in the sense of requiring a specific word for the determination [of the individual], because of the wavering of cognition from universal-words without a specific word [to narrow it down].
Because the cognition from a universal-word does not waver regarding its own domain:
for its domain is merely the individual-possessing-a-universal, and there is no wavering of cognition here.
The restriction to a specific individual is the domain [of the specific word], and the wavering of cognition there is no fault.
For from a distance, only the substance — having height and bulk — is the object of direct perception, not whether it is a post or a person.
And the wavering of cognition here does not inflict any damage on direct perception.
Nor, in this view, is the universal-word subordinate to the words for individual and form, such that it would be figurative.
Nor is co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) untenable, because of the impossibility of non-co-referentiality for the words 'universal' and 'individual' that denote one and the same object.
Therefore, everything is clear.

children.translated_text: And then [there would be] a contradiction in [using the phrase] 'word for substance'
— this is the meaning.
This has been answered: because the words '<s>sat</s>' and 'substance' have the same object.

children.text: viśeṣamātraṃ viṣayaḥ sadādiśabdasya na punarniyato 'yameva nānya iti bhāvaḥ //
children.translated_text: The object of words like '<s>sat</s>' and the like is mere particular — but not a fixed 'this one alone and no other' — this is the import. //

Having thus stated the non-applicability of the faults stated by the opponent in the non-exclusivist view (<s>anekāntavāda</s>), refuting the opponent's refutation-statement, he states the absence of faults:
'These are not faults' —
'The word for <s>sattā</s> (being)' — the analysis is either 'the word of <s>sattā</s>' or 'the word that has the form of <s>sattā</s>.' In the first interpretation, [the objection is] 'the word for <s>sattā</s> is not a denoting word for <s>sattā</s>' — this is contradictory.
In the second interpretation, [the objection is] 'it is not a denoting word for <s>sattā</s>' — this is contradictory by the use of the genitive '<s>sattāyāḥ</s>' (of <s>sattā</s>), [for] by this very word [the genitive] you are denoting <s>sattā</s>, and yet you say that the word for <s>sattā</s> is not its denoting word — hence the contradiction. 'The word for <s>sattā</s>' should be understood as an implied reference: '<s>sattā</s> is not its denotation.'
He raises the doubt: 'according to your intent' —
He refutes: 'no' —
If you apprehend [our] intent, the acknowledgment is dependent on the apprehension of meaning — [if] you state the acknowledgment, then accordingly you should not deny it — this is the import.
Anticipating 'I proceed to deny, but I do not acknowledge,' he says: 'but if this' —
(322/4) He refutes: 'that too, no' —
Of what is not of that nature — a post, which is a non-person — [the property of] being thus (<s>tathābhāva</s>), namely the superimposed property of personhood and the like [projected] by persons who are of that nature — he who has that [superimposed property] is called 'thus' (<s>tatha</s>); the principal meaning of that [word] is the person; the cognition of that form — this is the meaning.
'Of <s>sattā</s>, as denoting the principal instrument' —
The principal instrument is the substance that is to be the possessor by way of manifestation; the word '<s>sat</s>' denotes that. But the word '<s>mat</s>' (possessing) denotes the substance-as-subordinate relation — therefore there is no co-referentiality of that [<s>mat</s>-word] with the substance-denoting word — this is the meaning.
'The non-establishment of co-referentiality of the words "<s>sat</s>" and "substance"' —
The establishment [means] cognition; what some have said — that in your view this would not occur — that too is answered by this establishment of co-referentiality.
'Having been explained, by virtue of being refutable' —
'A speech-propriety devised by oneself' — he says.
(323/3)
'The word for universal (<s>jātiśabda</s>)' — in words like '<s>sat</s>' and the like, he negates the speech-propriety devised by oneself; and there, for us, [the opponent's argument] amounts to proving what is already established — this is the meaning.
The word '<s>sat</s>' is a universal-word; its being a denoting word of difference is not accepted by him — stating this, he shows:
'If then' —
The resolution is easy.
'Even so, it is neither positively concomitant nor negatively concomitant' —
'Whatever things are infinite are not denoted by a universal-word' — there is no example [for this],
because all differences are included [in the universal].
Nor can one say 'what is denoted by a universal-word does not have infinity — like cow-hood and the like' — because, in your view, the universal itself becomes as unreal as a sky-lotus — this is the import.
He raises the doubt: 'but even so' —
Even if so, a positively concomitant example is observed — this is the import.
He refutes: 'this too, no' —
Because of the contradiction in employing a qualifier (<s>viśeṣaṇa</s>):
For there is no real thing that is 'being' (<s>sat</s>) apart from difference, from which the qualifier could be differentiated — this is the import.
'Because of non-acceptance of the status of a reason' —
(324/5) The word is not a mark (<s>liṅga</s>) in making meaning known, such that it could be vitiated by deviation.
Nor is a mere cause-of-cognition vitiated by deviation — for even the eyes and the like, being deviating insofar as they are present [when perceiving] blue and the like as well as yellow and the like, would [then] be non-causes-of-cognition.
But the grasping of convention, even when there is deviation among differences — among [entities] each embraced by a single universal — is easy to accomplish — this is the import.
'Because of the denial of being a denoting word of difference' —
When being a denoting word of difference is denied, being a denoting word of substance is [also] denied, since substance is a kind of difference.
