tadyathā kiṃnaratvanirvarttanīyaṃ karma strīpuṃsabhogyaṃ strīpuṃsayoranyatarakarmapratibandhe phalaṃ na dadātīti /
yāni prāṇyantarāṇi snehaviṣayā bhrātrādayastasya karmaṇo bhāgīnīti /
karmaphalānāmannādyāśvagrāmādīnāṃ bhāgitvātkarmabhāgīnītyucyante teṣāṃ prāṇipanāṃ karmabhirabhāgyādiśabdavācyaiḥ pratibandhāditi /
tasya vā karmaṇaḥ sahakāridharmādharmalakṣaṇaṃ nimittaṃ nāstīti /
ayamarthaḥ /
dṛṣṭānāṃ sevādikarmaṇāṃ vyabhicārādgrāmādilābhe 'dṛṣṭaṃ kāraṇaṃ kalpanīyam /
yathāhuḥ/ ... taccaiva tatra kāraṇaṃ śabdaśceti ...
dṛṣṭaṃ sevādica kāraṇam /
śabdaśceti viṣayiṇā tadviṣayamadṛṣṭamupalakṣayati /
te ca grāmādayastasmādadṛṣṭādupajāyamānā antarā vighnanāśāya devatānamaskārādijanitamapi dharmamapekṣante, tasmāt prārabhavīyena dharmeṇa svaphalanirvarttanāya dharmāntaraṃ sahakāryapekṣyate,
sahakāriṇāṃ ca vaicitryātpratibandhāpagamahetorapi sahakāritvāvirodhaḥ /
tena karmaṇaḥ sahakārinimittābhāvātpratibaddhamadṛṣṭaṃ phalaṃ na janayatītyarthaḥ /
tasya vā karmaṇaḥ sahakāriṇaḥ kāraṇasya garīyasā karmāntareṇa pratibandhātphalasyānārambhaḥ /
evaṃ svakarmaṇāṃ sahakārinimittābhāvapratibandhāvutkvā samānopabhogasattvāntarakarmaṇāmapi sahakārinimittābhāvapratibandhau darśayati /

children.translated_text: 'And of the <s>karmas</s> of other beings' —
When it is said 'because of possessing form and the like,' there would be inconclusiveness through atoms — therefore he says:
'When graspable by external sense organs' —

children.text: indriyagrāhyatve satītyetāvataiva siddhe indriyagrāhyarāśerbāhyakaraṇagrāhyaṃ rāśyantaramityetāvanmātravivakṣayā bāhyakaraṇagrāhyatve satītyuktam // 58-60 //
children.translated_text: When 'graspable by sense organs' alone would suffice, the specification 'graspable by external sense organs' is said with the intention of separating only the class graspable by external sense organs from the class graspable by sense organs [in general]. // 58-60 //

When the mind is being investigated, what connection does the investigation of the cause of the origination of the body have? — to this he says: / 'Of the mind, indeed' — / (438/10) The mind too is examined through the investigation of the substrate (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>) — so there is no lack of connection with the investigation of the cause of the origination of the body. / Examination is comprehensive investigation — and that is both of the intrinsic nature and of relations; the body is a relatum of the mind because of being the substrate of the mind — / therefore, the examination of the mind is also the examination of the body — this is the meaning. / 'At the time of origination' — / (439/1) 'Simultaneously' means 'as if simultaneous' — / The meaning is: immediately after origination. / 'Who says it does not give?' — / If the [causal] aggregate is complete, then it will certainly give [the result] immediately after origination — this is the meaning. / 'The ripening <s>karma</s>-residue (<s>karmāśaya</s>)' — / The meaning is: causing [the being] to experience its own fruit. / 'Whatever other beings are co-experiencers of that <s>karma</s>' — / For example, a <s>karma</s> that is to produce the state of a <s>kinnara</s> (celestial musician) is to be enjoyed by both man and woman; when one of the man or woman has an obstruction of <s>karma</s>, it does not give the fruit. / 'Whatever other beings are objects of affection — brothers and the like — are sharers in that <s>karma</s>' — / They are called 'sharers in <s>karma</s>' because they share in the fruits of <s>karma</s> such as food, horses, villages, and the like; because of the obstruction of those beings' <s>karmas</s>, described by words like 'unfortunate' and the like. / 'Or that <s>karma</s> does not have a cooperating condition in the form of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>' — / The meaning is as follows: / Since visible <s>karmas</s> such as service and the like deviate [from producing their results] in [obtaining] villages and the like, an unseen [force] (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) must be postulated as the cause. / As they say: '... that alone is the cause there, and [so says] scripture...' / The seen [cause] is service and the like. / 'And scripture' — by what has objects, the unseen, which is its object, is indicated. / And those villages and the like, arising from that unseen [force], also require <s>dharma</s> generated by worship of deities and the like for the removal of intermediate obstacles; therefore, by the <s>dharma</s> that is to fructify, another <s>dharma</s> is required as a cooperator for the accomplishment of its own fruit; / and because of the diversity of cooperators, there is no contradiction in [a single cause of] obstruction-removal also being a cooperator. / Therefore, since that <s>karma</s> [lacks] its cooperating condition, the obstructed <s>adṛṣṭa</s> does not generate its fruit — this is the meaning. / Or, the non-commencement of the fruit is because of the obstruction by a more powerful <s>karma</s> of the cooperating cause of that <s>karma</s>. / Having thus stated the absence of cooperating conditions and obstruction regarding one's own <s>karmas</s>, he shows the same regarding the <s>karmas</s> of other beings who are co-experiencers:
<s>NyS</s> 3.2.61: Just as the material cause of form [is taken] from the elements, so is the material cause of that [body]. //
<s>NyS</s> 3.2.62: Not [so], because of being equal to what is to be proved. //

The raising of the inconclusiveness of the reason 'because of the incapacity for human-purpose-activity' — through the example of sand and the like being equal to what is to be proved — has also been answered.
Because sand and the like too are in some way causes of human purpose, their creation too is preceded by human qualities (<s>puruṣaguṇa</s>)
— it has been said. // 62 //
<s>NyS</s> 3.2.63: Not [so], because the mother and father are the causes of origination. //

children.text:
mā bhūdvā puruṣaguṇapūrvakatvaṃ sikatādisargasya, tathā 'pi śarīrasyotpattyādi paribhāvayantaḥ sikatādibhyo vaiṣamyaṃ vīkṣamāṇāstadvilakṣaṇkārakaṇatvameva pratiṣadyāmahe tathā ca sidhyati puruṣaguṇanimittatetyāha /
viṣamaścāyamupanyāsa iti /
(440/16) nanu mātāpitarau na sākṣāt śarīrotpattau kāraṇamityata āha mātāpitṛśabdena lohitaretasī iti /

children.translated_text: 'What is to be experienced' — the agent-suffix (<s>kṛtya</s>) is [used] on the model of <s>bhavya</s>, <s>geya</s>, and the like. // 63 //

Even if the creation of sand and the like is not preceded by human qualities, still, those who contemplate the origination and the like of the body, observing the dissimilarity from sand and the like, deny the very dissimilar-cause-hood — and thus, the precedence of human qualities is established — he says: / 'And this is an unequal presentation' — / (440/16) Now, the mother and father are not directly the cause of the body's origination — to this he says: 'by the word mother-father, [what is meant is] the blood and semen' —
<s>NyS</s> 3.2.64: Similarly of food [as the cause of the body]. //
Here too there is dissimilarity — he says:
'Similarly of food' (<s>sūtra</s> 64) //
He completes [the statement] with the recitation of the prior <s>sūtra</s>:
'Because of being a cause of origination' — this is what is in question.

The <s>kalala</s> (embryonic jelly), <s>rakaṇḍa</s>, <s>māṃsapeśī</s> (lump of flesh), and the like are the stages of transformation of the blood and semen, which are the producers of the body. // 64 //
<s>NyS</s> 3.2.65: And because of non-restriction when there is conjunction. //
'prāptau--t' (<s>sūtra</s> 65) //

children.text: tasmād dṛṣṭasya vyabhicārādasti tadadṛṣṭaṃ yataḥ śarīrasarga ityarthaḥ // 65 //
children.translated_text: therefore, because of the deviation of the visible [cause], there is an unseen [force] (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) from which the creation of the body [arises] — this is the meaning. // 65 //

The conjunction of the husband and wife is the 'arrival' (<s>prāpti</s>); the non-restriction of that [conjunction] with respect to the origination of the body [means that not every conjunction produces a body],
<s>NyS</s> 3.2.66: Like the cause of the origination of the body, <s>karma</s> is the cause of the origination of the conjunction [of self and body]. //

children.text:
pārśvasthaḥ śaṅkate /
sarvātmabhiriti /
nanu yadīyenādṛṣṭena yaccharīramupāttaṃ tattasyaiva bhogāyatanaṃ nāniyama ityata āha /
na ca puruṣagata iti /
ātmamanaḥsannikarṣajau hi dharmādharmau, sannikarṣaśca manasaḥ sarvātmabhiḥ sādhāraṇa iti sarveṣāmeva dharmādharmau,
na punaḥ kaspaya cidevāsādhāraṇāvityarthaḥ /
asyottaraṃ śarīreti /
uktenaivābhiprāyeṇa śaṅkate tatsthatā ekapuruṣasthatā kuta iti cet /
uttaramān svasaṃyogeti /
punaḥ pṛcchati saṃyoge kṛto niyama iti /
(442/1) yathaivaikenātmanā manaḥsaṃyuktamevamātmāntarairapi /
evaṃ yathaikena manasā saṃyuktaṃ evamanontaraipīti nātmamanaḥsannikarṣe 'sti viśeṣa ityarthaḥ /
uttaraṃ na manoniyamahetutvāditi /
adṛṣṭa (niyama) nibandhano hi manoniyamaḥ
manoniyamanibandhanaścādṛṣṭaniyamaḥ /
anāditvācca bījāṅkuravadanyonyāśrayo na kṣatimāvahatītyarthaḥ
// 66 //
children.translated_text: A bystander raises a doubt: / 'Of all selves' — / Now, if the body taken up by [a particular person's] <s>adṛṣṭa</s> is the abode of experience for that very [person], there is no non-restriction — to this he says: / 'And not residing in a person' — / For <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> arise from the conjunction of the self with the mind, and the conjunction with the mind is common to all selves — so <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> belong to all alike, / not exclusively to any one [self] — this is the meaning. / The answer to this: 'The body' — / With the very same intent, he raises a doubt: 'if [one asks:] whence the restriction to one person?' — / The answer: 'from its own conjunction' — / He asks again: 'the restriction has been made regarding the conjunction' — / (442/1) Just as the mind is conjoined with one self, so too with other selves; / and just as it is conjoined with one mind, so too with other minds — so there is no distinction in the self-mind conjunction — this is the meaning. / The answer: 'not, because of being the cause of the restriction of the mind' — / For the restriction of the mind is grounded in <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen force); / and the restriction of <s>adṛṣṭa</s> is grounded in the restriction of the mind. / And because of beginninglessness, the mutual dependence, like that of seed and sprout, does not lead to harm — this is the meaning. // 66 //
<s>NyS</s> 3.2.67: By this, the [objection regarding] non-restriction has been answered. //

children.text:
tadevamātmaguṇanibandhane śarīrasarge vyāvasthā darśitā /
ye tu menire na karmanibandhanaḥ śarīrasargo 'pi tu prakṛtyādinibandhanaḥ /
prakṛtayo hi svayameva dharmādharmarūpanimittānapekṣāḥ sattvaraja stamastayā pravṛttiśīlāḥ sva sva vikāramārabhante, pratibandhāpagamamātre tu dharmādharmāvapekṣante tadyathā kṛṣavilaḥ kedārādāṃ pūrṇātkedārāntaramapūrṇamāpiplāvayiṣuraṣāṃ setumātraṃ kedāramāplāvayanti /
evamāplāvayanti prakṛtayo 'pi vikārāniti /
yathāhuḥ 'nimittamaprayojakaṃ prakṛtīnāmāvaraṇabhedastu tataḥ kṣetrikavaditi /
tān pratayāha /
etenāniyamaḥ pratyuktaḥ (sū. 67) /
etena karmasāpekṣāṇāṃ bhūtānāṃ śarīrasarge aniyamābhidhānena tannirapekṣāṇāṃ vyatirekamukhenāniyamaḥ pratyuktaḥ /
niyamo vyāptiḥ sādhāraṇavigrahavattvaṃ sarvātmanām /
aniyamastvavyāptiḥ kasya cidātmana kiṃ ciccharīraṃ kasyacit kiṃciditi /
prakṛtinibandhane hi śarīrasarge tasyā ekatvāt sarvātmasādhāraṇyācca na śarīrāṇāmastyasādhāraṇye hetuḥ /
bhūtagrahaṇaṃ tu prakṛtyupalakṣaṇārthaṃ na kevalamakarmanimitte śarīrasarge sādhāraṇavigrahavattvaṃ doṣaḥ
api tu mokṣo 'pi na syāditi darśayituṃ svapakṣe mokṣamupapādayati /
children.translated_text: but also liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) would not be [possible] — to show this, he justifies liberation in his own position:
'And it is justified' —

children.text: sāṃkhyapakṣe tu na mokṣaḥ syāditi darśayati /
children.translated_text: He shows that in the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> position, liberation would not be [possible]:
'When [the elements are] independent of <s>karma</s>' — // 67 //

Thus, the fixed arrangement in the creation of the body grounded in the qualities of the self has been shown. / But those who thought that the creation of the body is not grounded in <s>karma</s>, but rather grounded in <s>Prakṛti</s> and the like — / for the <s>Prakṛtis</s>, by their own nature, without depending on causes in the form of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, being inclined to activity through the three <s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — initiate their respective modifications; but they depend on <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> merely for the removal of obstruction. Just as the farmer, wishing to flood another unfilled field from a field full of water, merely breaches the embankment and floods the fields — / so too the <s>Prakṛtis</s> flood [the world with their] modifications. / As they say: 'The cause is not the motive force of the <s>Prakṛtis</s>; rather, the breaking of the barrier [is what matters] — like a farmer.' / To them he says: / 'By this, the non-restriction has been answered' (<s>sūtra</s> 67). / By this — the statement of non-restriction when the elements create the body depending on <s>karma</s> — by way of negative concomitance when they do not depend on <s>karma</s>, the non-restriction has been answered. / 'Restriction' means 'pervasion' — all selves having a body of the common type. / 'Non-restriction' means 'non-pervasion' — some self having some body and another self having another body. / For when the creation of the body is grounded in <s>Prakṛti</s>, since <s>Prakṛti</s> is one and common to all selves, there is no reason for the non-commonality of bodies. / The mention of 'elements' (<s>bhūta</s>) is for the purpose of indicating <s>Prakṛti</s> — not only is the common-body-hood a defect in the creation of bodies not caused by <s>karma</s>,
<s>NyS</s> 3.2.68: If [it is said that] that [body-creation] is caused by <s>adṛṣṭa</s>, [we reply:] because of the consequence of recurrence and termination. //

children.text:
śaṅkate /
tadadṛṣṭakāritamiti cediti upabhogvaśabdādyadarśanaṃ prakṛtipuruṣabhedādarśanaṃ vā 'dṛṣṭamucyate /
tatkāritamityarthaḥ /
nirākaroti etasminniti /
(443/4) yathā prāgadarśanamevaṃ nirodhasamādheḥ paścādapyadarśanamityapravṛkto 'pi punaḥ saṃsaredityarthaḥ /
śaṅkāmutthāpya dūṣayati /
caritārthaceti /
nanu na śabdādyupabhogaṃ puruṣārthaṃ brūmo yena caritārthatā syāt /
api tu puruṣabhedadarśanaṃ taccādyāpi na bhavatītyārabhate śarīramiti deśayati /
puruṣārthena ca hetuneti /
co 'vadhāraṇe puruṣārthenaivetyarthaḥ /
pariharati /
tasya--cākaraṇāditi /
castvarthe /
deśyanivṛttau /
yadarthaṃ śarīrāṇyārabhate tanna kṛtamanyattu kṛtamitikiṃ kena saṃgatamityarthaḥ /
śaṅkate didṛkṣāviśeṣa iti /
darśanaṃ hi nañā paryudastamatastanmūlāṃ didṛkṣāṃ brūte sā cāpavarge nāsti tasmānnāpavṛktaḥ saṃsaratītyarthaḥ /
nirākaroti na prāgiti /
etaduktaṃ bhavati /
didṛkṣā hi buddhyāśrayā nāsatyāṃ buddhāvasti prakṛtipariṇāmaśca buddhistathā ca satyāṃ didṛkṣāyāṃ buddhiḥ buddhau satyāṃ didṛkṣeti parasparāśrayaprasaṅgaḥ /
na cānāditā parihāraḥ, sṛṣṭyādau dvayorabhāvāt /
asmākaṃ tu pralayasamaye dharmādharmasaṃskṛto 'styātmā manaśceti viśeṣaḥ /
satkāryamādāya śaṅkate /
sarvaśaktimattvāditi /
nirākaroti /
nāpavargābhāvaprasaṅgāditi /
(444/3) śliṣṭaṃ vibhajate didṛkṣāvannānātvadarśanamapyastīti /
na tadarthaṃ prakṛte pravṛttiḥ tathā ca na saṃsārastapradhvaṃsaścāpavargābhāvānnāstītyapavargābhāva
ityarthaḥ /
etadeva sphuṭayati /
vidyamāne ca nānātvadarśane tadarthaṃ pradhānasya prayuktirayuktā tataḥ saṃsārābhāvāttatpradhvaṃso 'pavargo na syāditi bhāvaḥ /
tamevāpavargābhāvaṃ tadvirodhisaṃsārasattve darśayati /
yadā ca nānātvadarśanamiti /
nidānānucchede nidānino noccheda ityarthaḥ /
punarvikalpaṃ darśayati /
ajñānamadarśanamiti ceti /
vivekajñānābhāvasya tulyatvādityarthaḥ /
śeṣamatirohitārthamiti /
apare tvārhatā adṛṣṭaṃ paramāṇuguṇaṃ varṇayanti /
pārthivānāmaṇūnāṃ manasaśca svaguṇaprayuktaṃ taccharīramāviśati /
tacca svakādevādṛṣṭātpudgalasya sukhaduḥkhopabhogaṃ sādhayati /

children.translated_text: But <s>adṛṣṭa</s> is not a <s>dharma</s> of the <s>pudgala</s> (soul).
For them too, as for the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, there is again the same consequence regarding liberation.
He establishes this:
"Of the quality of the atom." //68//

He raises a doubt:
"If that is caused by <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit)" — either the non-perception of the enjoyment of sound and the like, or the non-perception of the distinction between <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, is called <s>adṛṣṭa</s>.
"Caused by that" — this is the meaning.
He refutes: "in this" —
(443/4) Just as there was non-perception before [liberation], so too after the cessation-meditation (<s>nirodhasamādhi</s>) there would be non-perception — meaning: even one who has ceased [from worldly activity] would again undergo <s>saṃsāra</s>.
Having raised the doubt, he refutes:
"And because of having fulfilled its purpose" —
Objection: we do not say that the enjoyment of sound and the like is the purpose of the person (<s>puruṣārtha</s>), by which the fulfilment of purpose would be [attained].
Rather, the perception of the distinction of <s>Puruṣa</s> [from <s>Prakṛti</s>] — and that has not yet occurred — therefore [<s>Prakṛti</s>] commences the body — thus he teaches.
"And by the reason of the person's purpose" —
The word "and" is for emphasis — meaning: by the person's purpose alone.
He resolves:
"Because of not accomplishing that" —
The word "and" has the force of reason.
Regarding the cessation of what is being taught:
The meaning is: that for whose sake [<s>Prakṛti</s>] commences bodies — that has not been accomplished, while something else has been accomplished — what is this consistent with?
He raises a doubt: "the special desire to see" —
For "perception" (<s>darśana</s>) is negated by the particle "not"; therefore he speaks of the desire to see, which is its root — and that does not exist in liberation (<s>apavarga</s>); therefore one who is not liberated undergoes <s>saṃsāra</s> — this is the meaning.
He refutes: "not before" —
What is being said is this:
For the desire to see has <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) as its substrate and does not exist when <s>buddhi</s> does not exist; and <s>buddhi</s> is a transformation of <s>Prakṛti</s>. And thus, when the desire to see exists, <s>buddhi</s> [exists]; when <s>buddhi</s> exists, the desire to see [exists] — this leads to mutual dependence.
Nor is beginninglessness a resolution, because of the absence of both at the beginning of creation.
But for us, the distinction is that at the time of dissolution, the <s>ātman</s> endowed with impressions of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> exists, as does <s>manas</s>.
Accepting the <s>satkārya</s> (pre-existence of effect) [doctrine], he raises a doubt:
"Because of possessing all powers" —
He refutes:
"Not, because of the consequence of the absence of liberation (<s>apavarga</s>)" —
(444/3) He analyzes the compressed [argument]: "the perception of duality also exists in one who has the desire to see."
The activity of <s>Pradhāna</s> is not for the sake of that [duality-perception]; and thus there is no <s>saṃsāra</s>; and its cessation — liberation — does not exist because of the absence of <s>saṃsāra</s> — thus the absence of liberation — this is the meaning.
He makes this very point clear:
"And when the perception of duality exists, the impulsion of <s>Pradhāna</s> for its sake is inappropriate; therefore, because of the absence of <s>saṃsāra</s>, its cessation — liberation — would not exist" — this is the import.
He shows that very absence of liberation when <s>saṃsāra</s>, which contradicts it, exists:
"And when the perception of duality" —
The meaning is: when the root-cause is not destroyed, that which is rooted [in it] is not destroyed.
Again he shows an alternative:
"And ignorance is non-perception" —
The meaning is: because the absence of discriminative knowledge is equal [to non-perception].
The rest has a self-evident meaning.
But others — the <s>Ārhatas</s> (Jains) — describe <s>adṛṣṭa</s> as a quality of atoms.
The body enters into [the <s>pudgala</s> (soul)] through the qualities of earthen atoms and <s>manas</s> proper to them.
And that [body], through the <s>adṛṣṭa</s> belonging to its own [atoms], accomplishes the enjoyment of pleasure and pain for the <s>pudgala</s> (soul).
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 3.2.69: And because <s>manas</s>-<s>karma</s> is the cause, there is no severance of conjunction. //

children.text:
api cāsmin darśane prāyaṇaṃ na syādityāha /
manaḥ karmanimittattvāditi // 69 // asmaddarśane tūpapadyate prāyaṇamityāha /
vartamānaśarīrārambhakakarmāśayakṣaye tu bhaviṣyaddehāntarārambhakakarmāśayāntarādapasarpaṇaṃ manasa iti yuktaṃ prāyaṇam /
children.translated_text: Upon the exhaustion of the store of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmāśaya</s>) that commenced the present body, the departure of <s>manas</s> toward another store of <s>karma</s> that will commence a future body — that is death (<s>prāyaṇa</s>), and it is justified.
"Because of both reasons" —
The meaning is: [<s>manas</s> is] the cause of both approaching and departing. //69//

Moreover, in this [Jain] view, death (<s>prāyaṇa</s>) would not be possible — thus he says:
"Because <s>manas</s>-<s>karma</s> is the cause" — //69// But in our view, death is possible — thus he says:
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 3.2.70: And the consequence of eternality [of the body follows], because of the impossibility of death. //

children.text:
nanu bhavatu saṃyogānucchedaḥ kiṃ nobādhyataityata āha /
śarīrasya nityatvaprasaṅgaśca prāyaṇānupapatteḥ /
saṃyogāvyucchedādityarthaḥ /
nanu sadakāraṇaṃ nityamiti kathaṃ sakāraṇa śarīre nityaṃ bhavedityata āha /
nityatvaprasaṅga
iti prāyaṇānupattiṃ brūmaḥ /
vināśānupapattirityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: [If death were] accidental, without a cause,
there would be no difference in [the time of] death.

children.text: dṛṣṭaśca prāyaṇabhedaḥ kaścidgarbhasya eva praiti kaścijjātamātraḥ kaścitkumāraka ityādiriti akāraṇasya nityaṃ sattvamasattvaṃ vā syāt /
children.translated_text: But difference in death is observed: someone dies in the womb itself, someone immediately after birth, someone as a child, and so on — [therefore, if death were without a cause,] what is without a cause would either always exist or never exist,
like the sky and its flower — this is the meaning. //70//

Objection: let there be no severance of conjunction — what harm does that do to us? — to this he says:
"And the consequence of the eternality of the body, because of the impossibility of death."
The meaning is: because of the non-severance of conjunction.
Objection: what has no cause is eternal — but how would the body, which has a cause, be eternal? — to this he says:
We say the consequence of eternality — [meaning] the impossibility of death,
i.e., the impossibility of destruction — this is the meaning.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 3.2.71: This would be like the eternality of atoms and dark color (<s>śyāmatā</s>). //
He resists through the inconclusiveness of the reason "because of being without a cause":
"Like the eternality of atoms and dark color." //71//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 3.2.72: Not [so], because of the consequence of experiencing the fruits of unperformed actions (<s>akṛtābhyāgama</s>). //
He refutes:

children.text:
etacca neti (446/2) /
pramāṇenāviṣayīkṛtamakṛtam pratyuta pratyakṣāgamaviruddhamiti yāvat /
tasyābhyāgapro 'bhyupagamastatprasaṅgādityarthaḥ /
na ca paramāṇuśyāmatāpyakāraṇā pārthivarūpatvāt
lohitādirūpavadityanumānena tasyāpi pākajatvābhyupagamāditi bhāvaḥ/yathā śruti vā sūtrārthaḥ /
akṛtasya karmaṇaḥ phalopabhogaprasaṅgāditi /
yathā khalu paramāṇuguṇa eva nityaḥ śarīrādyārambhakastathā 'sau nityatvānna kena cit kriyate /
tasyākṛtasyaiva phalaṃ puruṣairupabhujyate tataścāyamāstikānāṃ vihitaniṣiddhapravṛttinivṛttinicayo 'narthakaḥ śāstrapraṇayanaṃ cāpyanarthakaṃ bhavediti bhāvaḥ /
etaccātivistṛtaṃ bhāṣye /
tasyārtho nigadavyākhyātaḥ
// 72 //
children.translated_text:
"And this — not" — (446/2)
What is not made the object of a <s>pramāṇa</s> is "unperformed" — rather, what is contradicted by perception and scripture — this is so much meant. Its acceptance (<s>abhyāgama</s>) is acknowledgment — because of the consequence of that — this is the meaning.
And the dark color of atoms is not without a cause either, because of being a color belonging to earth (<s>pārthiva</s>) —
like red and other colors — because of the acceptance, through inference, that it too is produced by heating (<s>pākaja</s>) — this is the import.
Or the meaning of the sūtra is according to the literal reading:
because of the consequence that the fruits of unperformed <s>karma</s> are experienced.
For just as the quality of atoms alone is eternal and is the commencer of bodies and the like, so too, being eternal, it is not performed by anyone.
Yet the fruit of that very unperformed [quality] is experienced by persons — and thus the determination of the orthodox (<s>āstika</s>) to engage in and refrain from what is enjoined and prohibited would be purposeless, and the composition of scripture too would be purposeless — this is the import.
And this is extensively [treated] in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>.
Its meaning is explained by mere recitation.
//72//
Thus, in the <s>Nyāyavārttikatātparyaṭīkā</s> composed by the venerable <s>Vācaspati Miśra</s>,
the third chapter is complete. //

children.text:
atra tṛtīye 'dhyāye prathame ānhike 75 sūtrāṇi, dvitīye ca 73 sūtrāṇi iti ādita ārabhya militavā 148 sūtrāṇi /
3 a0 1 ānhike 9 prakaraṇāni, 3 ānhike 9 prakaraṇāni /
militvā 16 prakaraṇāni /
āditaḥ 42 prakaraṇāni /
children.translated_text:
In this third chapter, the first section has 75 sūtras, and the second has 73 sūtras — thus from the beginning, combined, there are 148 sūtras.
In the third chapter, first section: 9 topics; third [sic, second] section: 9 topics.
Combined: 16 topics.
From the beginning: 42 topics.
The first section of the fourth chapter. //
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.1: Activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) is as stated. //

children.text:
atha manaḥ parīkṣānantaramuddeśalakṣaṇakramānurodhena pravṛttiḥ parīkṣituṃ yuktā, sā kasmānna parīkṣyata iti śaṅkānirākaraṇāya sūtramityāha /
manaso 'nantaramiti /
( 446/3 ) pravṛttiryathoktā (sū.1) //
children.translated_text:
Now, after the examination of <s>manas</s> (mind), activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) is appropriately to be examined in accordance with the order of listing and definition; [the question] why it is not examined — to remove this doubt, the sūtra is stated — thus he says:
"After <s>manas</s>" —
(446/3) "Activity is as stated" (sūtra 1) //

children.text:
asya śeṣastathā parīkṣitā yathā lakṣitā tathā parīkṣitetyarthaḥ /
pṛcchati kiṃ punariti /
prameyamātmādi manontaṃ parīkṣitaṃ, na punaḥ pravṛtteḥ svarūpaṃ vā kāryaṃ vā parīkṣitāmiti bhāvaḥ /
uttaram /
yāvaddharmādharmāśrayamiti /
ekadravyetyekasminnevātmani varttataityarthaḥ /
avasthitā na tu buddhyādivadāśutaravināśinītyarthaḥ /
ātmasamavāyāditi /
kāryatve satīti draṣṭavyaṃ viśeṣaṇam /
tena na sāmānyaviśeṣābhyāṃ vyabhicāraḥ /

children.translated_text: "Death and the like" — by the word "and the like," the destruction of pleasure and the like, and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>), are included.
The supplement is: "through the existence and non-existence of the <s>ātman</s>, which is the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> and liberation."
"Thus stated at the beginning" —
By the word "beginning" he shows that activity inheres in the <s>ātman</s>, not in earth and the like. //1//

The remainder of this: "it has been examined as it was defined" — meaning: it has been examined as it was characterized.
He asks: "what, then" —
The import is: the object of knowledge (<s>prameya</s>) — the <s>ātman</s> and the rest up to <s>manas</s> — has been examined; but neither the intrinsic nature nor the effect of activity has been examined.
The answer:
"As far as being the substrate of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>" —
"In a single substance" — meaning: existing in the <s>ātman</s> alone.
"Established" — meaning: not perishing as quickly as <s>buddhi</s> and the like.
"Because of inhering in the <s>ātman</s>" —
The qualifier should be understood as: "when being an effect."
Thereby, there is no deviation through the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) and the particular (<s>viśeṣa</s>).
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.2: Similarly, the defects (<s>doṣa</s>). //
If the defects are to be examined after activity, then let them be examined — to this he says:
"Similarly, the defects"
(sūtra 2) //

children.text:
uktā iti śeṣaḥ /
pravṛttitulyatayā pravṛtiparīkṣayaiva tāvaddoṣāṇāṃ sattvaṃ parīkṣitamityarthaḥ /
kāryarūpapravṛttitulyatāmāha buddhisamānāśrayatvāditi /
abhīṣṭaviṣayānucintanaprabhavāḥ khalvime doṣā nānucintanabuddhivyadhikaraṇā bhavitumarhanti, tathā sati caitrasyābhīṣṭaviṣayānucintane maitrasya rāgaḥ pravartteta /
tasmādbuddhisamānāśrayatvādātmaguṇāḥ
ātmaguṇatvācca kāryapravṛttitulyatayā pravṛttiparīkṣayaiva ttāvaddoṣāḥ parīkṣitā ityarthaḥ /
idaṃ ca pravṛttitulyatvamaparaṃ doṣāṇāmityāha /
saṃsārasyānāditvāditi /
etaccoktaṃ vītarāgajanmādarśanādityanena /
tathoddeśaparīkṣāpareṇa dvitīyasūtreṇa yatteṣāṃ doṣāṇāṃ parīkṣitaṃ tadāha /
samyagjñānā cceti /
syādetat /
guṇatvesatyātmaguṇā iti siddhyati tadeva tu kuta ityata āha /
kāryatvesatīti /
( 440/1 ) indriyāntaraṃ mana iti mānasapratyakṣaiścātmatvasukhatvādibhiranaikāntitvaṃ mā bhūdata uktaṃ kāryatve satīti viśeṣaṇam /

children.translated_text: In "because of being perceptible without the eye" too, the qualifier "when being an effect" should be appended. //2//

The remainder is: "have been stated." The meaning is: by their equality with activity, by the very examination of activity, the existence of the defects has been examined.
He states their equality with activity in the form of an effect: "because of having the same substrate as cognition (<s>buddhi</s>)."
For these defects, arising from the contemplation of a desired object, cannot have a different substrate from the contemplative cognition — for if so, from the contemplation of the desired object by <s>Caitra</s>, the attachment of <s>Maitra</s> would arise.
Therefore, because of having the same substrate as cognition, they are qualities of the <s>ātman</s>;
and because of being qualities of the <s>ātman</s>, by their equality with activity as effects, by the very examination of activity, the defects have been examined — this is the meaning.
And he states this other equality of defects with activity: "because of the beginninglessness of <s>saṃsāra</s>."
And this has been stated by [the sūtra] "because of the non-observation of the birth of one free from attachment."
Similarly, what has been examined of these defects by the second sūtra concerning both listing and examination, that he states:
"Because of correct knowledge" —
This might be [objected]: if they are qualities, [it follows that] they are qualities of the <s>ātman</s> — but how is that very [quality-status] established? — to this he says:
"When being an effect" —
(440/1) "<s>Manas</s> is another sense-organ" — and lest there be inconclusiveness through <s>ātmatva</s> (selfhood), <s>sukhatva</s> (pleasure-hood), and the like [apprehended] by mental perception — therefore the qualifier "when being an effect" is stated.

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.3: That [defects have a] threefold [classification], because of the existence of attachment (<s>rāga</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), and delusion (<s>moha</s>) as distinct entities. //
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.4: Not [so], because of not being the counterpart of a single [defect]. //

children.text:
tadevaṃ bahu parīkṣitaṃ doṣāṇāṃ,
yattu kiṃ ciddoṣāṇāmaparīkṣitamasti tatparīkṣitumupakramate /
prarvatanālakṣaṇā ityuktaṃ tathā ca mānādaya
iti /
rāgadveṣamohā eva doṣā na ca mānādayasteṣvantarbhavanti buddhivyapadeśabhedāt /
pravarttanālakṣaṇatvaṃ tu teṣāmapyasti tasmādativyāpakatvānna lakṣaṇametadyuktaṃ yuktatve vā lakṣaṇasūtre mānādayo 'pi doṣavatpaṭhanīyā iti pūrvapakṣaḥ /
siddhāntavādyāha nopasaṃkhyāyante saṃgṛhītatvāditi /
rāgadveṣamohānāṃ sāmānyatrayāṇāṃ kāmādayo viśeṣāstathā copapanno buddhivyapadeśabhedaḥ saṅgrahaśceti bhāvaḥ /
asvavastvādānecchā svāmidānapūrvikā spṛhā /
punarbhavaprārthanā tṛṣṇāhetubhūtā pravṛttidvāreṇa punarbhavapratisaṃdhānasyeti /
pramāṇaviruddheti/(449/1) anyāyenetyarthaḥ /
parasya jñātermamāpyetaditi buddhirabhiniveśaḥ
tatpratiṣedhābhiprāpayo jñānipiśācasyerṣyetyucyate /
amarṣalakṣaṇo dveṣa iti /
( 450/1 ) nanu kṛtāpakārasya yā asahiṣṇutā so 'marṣa iti dveṣasyaiva viśeṣa ityuktaṃ kathaṃ dveṣasāmānyamucyata

children.translated_text: — to this he says:
"Intolerance of pain and of the means of pain" —
"Delusion characterized as wrong apprehension" —

children.text: saṃśayopi hi yathābasthite padārthe ayathābhāvapratipatti bhavati, vyavasthitaṃ hi vastu avayavasthitatayā gṛhṇāti saṃśayaḥ evaṃ paṇḍitamānino mīmāṃsakadurdurūḍhasyābhimāna iti // 3-4 //
children.translated_text: For even doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>) involves a wrong apprehension of a thing that is in a certain state — for doubt grasps a determined thing as undetermined. Similarly, the conceit of one who fancies himself learned — like a <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> who has barely climbed [the ladder of learning] — is pride (<s>abhimāna</s>). //3-4//

Thus, much has been examined regarding the defects;
but what has not yet been examined regarding them — that he undertakes to examine.
"Characterized as impelling" — this was stated; and similarly, pride (<s>māna</s>) and the like —
attachment, aversion, and delusion alone are the defects, and pride and the like are not included in them, because of the difference in the designation of cognition.
But the character of impelling belongs to those [pride etc.] too; therefore, because of over-extension, this definition is inappropriate; or if the definition is appropriate, pride and the like should also be listed alongside the defects — this is the prima facie view.
The <s>siddhāntin</s> says: "they are not additionally listed, because of being [already] included."
Attachment, aversion, and delusion are three general [categories]; desire (<s>kāma</s>) and the like are their specific [forms]. And thus the difference in the designation of cognition and the inclusion are both justified — this is the import.
"Desire for what is not one's own property without the prior gift of the owner" is craving (<s>spṛhā</s>).
"The longing for re-existence" is thirst (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) — being the cause, through activity, of the re-linking to [a new] existence.
"Contradicted by <s>pramāṇa</s>" — (449/1) meaning: unjustly.
"The cognition 'this should be mine too,' directed toward another's possession" — this is acquisitiveness (<s>abhiniveśa</s>);
the resolve aimed at preventing that [other's possession] is called jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>) of the knowing demon (<s>jñānipiśāca</s>).
"Aversion characterized as intolerance" —
(450/1) Objection: the intolerance toward one who has caused offense is <s>amarṣa</s> (indignation) — and that is a specific [form] of aversion itself — so how is it stated as a general [form of] aversion?
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.5: [This threefold classification is] not a [valid] reason, because of deviation. //

children.text: ekiyonayo hi rūpādayo na caiṣāmekatvaṃ, yadi punastatra rūpādīnāṃ parasparabhedasiddhaye kaścitkāraṇabheda āsthīyate sa rāgādiṣvapi samāna iti bhāvaḥ /

children.translated_text: The <s>Bhāṣya</s> [reads]: "noble insight" (<s>āryaprajñā</s>).
"Noble" (<s>ārya</s>) — one who has reached [the truth] from afar.
"Noble" and "self-generated" (<s>asauprajñā</s>) — that is <s>āryaprajñā</s>.
Correct understanding (<s>samyagbodha</s>) is <s>sambodha</s> (awakening). //5//

For colors (<s>rūpa</s>) and the like that share a single origin are not one [in number]; and if, for establishing the mutual difference of colors and the like, some difference of cause is resorted to, the same applies to attachment and the like — this is the import.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.6: Among these, delusion (<s>moha</s>) is the worst, because the other [two] do not arise in one who is not deluded. //

children.text:
nāsati nidānocchede nidānināmuccheda iti--rāgadveṣayornidāninorucchedāya tannidānatvaṃ mohasya darśayati sati cārthāntaratva
iti /
teṣāṃ mohaḥ pāpīyān kutaḥ nāmūḍhasyetarotpatteḥ // 6 // amūḍhasyetarotpattirna bhavati yata ityatrārthe nāmūḍhasyetarotpatterityuktam /
mohādviṣayasya sukhasādhanatvānusmṛtiḥ
duḥkhasādhanatānusmṛtiśca saṅkalpaḥ /
rañjanīyāḥ kopanīyā iti kartari kṛtyo bhavyageyādipāṭhāt /
vārtikaṃ mūḍhomuhyatīti /
(451/3) mūḍha iti mohavāsanāvān /
bhavatu nidānocchedāducchedo nidāninaḥ nidānasya kuta uccheda ityata āha /
children.translated_text: Granted that by the eradication of the root cause there is eradication of what is rooted — but whence the eradication of the root cause? To this he says:
"from the knowledge of reality" —
from the practice of the antidote, there is eradication of the root cause
— this is the meaning. //6//

Without the eradication of the root cause, there is no eradication of what is rooted — to show that delusion (<s>moha</s>) is the root cause of attachment (<s>rāga</s>) and aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), which are rooted [in delusion], he says: "and there being a difference of subject-matter." "Of those, delusion is the worst" — from where? — "because the others do not arise for one who is not deluded." //6// The others do not arise for one who is not deluded — it is said "because the others do not arise for one who is not deluded" to express this meaning. From delusion, the recollection of the object as a means to pleasure and the recollection [of it] as a means to pain constitute volition (<s>saṃkalpa</s>). "Worthy of being delighted in, worthy of being angered by" — the potential-suffix (<s>kṛtya</s>) is in the agent-sense, from the reading of <s>bhavya</s>, <s>geya</s>, and the like. The <s>Vārttika</s> [reads:] "the deluded person is deluded" — (451/3) "deluded" means one who has the latent impression of delusion.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.7: Because of the relation of cause and effect, there is a different state from the faults (<s>doṣas</s>).
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.8 // He states the non-probativeness of the reason "because of [activity] being caused by faults":
"not because of being included in the definition of faults" —
"Such-ness" (<s>tathābhāva</s>) means belonging to the same class; "non-such-ness" (<s>atathābhāva</s>) means not belonging to that class. //7-8//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.9: And because of the tenability of the cause-effect relation, the non-denial of those of the same class.
He states the inconclusiveness:
"And because of the tenability of the cause-effect relation" //9//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.10: If the <s>ātman</s> is eternal, the existence after death (<s>pretyabhāva</s>) is established.

children.text:
utpādocchedau pretyabhāvo na cātmano nityasya tau staḥ tasmādasmin darśane na yuktaḥ pretyabhāvaḥ /
vaināśikānāṃ tu sattvotpādanirodhābhyāṃ yuktaḥ pretyabhāvaḥ /
pretyeti lyab mukhaṃ vyādāya svapitītivad draṣṭavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The [suffix in] <s>pretya</s> ("after dying") should be understood as the absolutive (<s>lyap</s>), like "sleeping with his mouth wide open" (<s>mukhaṃ vyādāya svapiti</s>).

children.text: tathā ca bhūtvā prāyaṇamiti bhavanaprāyaṇayoḥ samānakartṛkatvamapyupapannamiti pūrvapakṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus, "having existed, death" — the fact that existence (<s>bhavana</s>) and death (<s>prāyaṇa</s>) have the same agent is also justified — this is the prima facie view.

Because of the establishment of the eternality of the <s>ātman</s> in the previously discussed <s>sūtras</s>, and because of the fault of loss of what is done and acquisition of what is not done in the origination and cessation of the continuum, [there would be] non-engagement in [the pursuit of] prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>) and final liberation (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>),

children.text: ṛṣyupadeśānarthakyaprasaṅgaśca svadehendriyabuddhisaṃvedanāsambandhotpādavipanāśau nityasyātmano janmaprāyaṇe tathā copapannaḥ pretyabhāva iti siddhāntaḥ // 10 //
children.translated_text: and the consequence of the purposelessness of the teachings of the <s>ṛṣis</s> — [but in fact,] the origination and cessation of [the connection with] one's own body, sense-organs, intellect, and sensations are the birth and death of the eternal <s>ātman</s>, and thus <s>pretyabhāva</s> is established — this is the <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine). //10//

Origination and cessation constitute the existence after death (<s>pretyabhāva</s>); but for the eternal <s>ātman</s>, those two do not exist — therefore, in this system, <s>pretyabhāva</s> is not justified. But for the <s>Vaināśikas</s> (proponents of destruction), <s>pretyabhāva</s> is justified through the origination and cessation of the [psycho-physical] continuum (<s>sattva</s>).
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.11: Because of the perceptual validity of [the origination] of manifest [entities] from manifest [entities].
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.12: Not [so], because a pot is not produced from a pot.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.13: The production of a pot from a manifest [entity] is not denied.

children.text:
pretyabhāvavicāraprastāvenedamaparaṃ vicārayati /
yeyaṃ pretayotpattirnāma sā kathamiti cet /
atra hi prāvādukānāṃ nānāvidhā vipratipattayaḥ santi /
tatrābhimataṃ tāvatpakṣaṃ gṛhṇāti /
vyaktāditi /
agre vipratipattīrnivārayiṣyati /
śarīrendriyaviṣayopakaraṇādhāramiti ekavadbhāvena napuṃsakatvam /

children.translated_text: Inference that arises from a connection grasped by perception points to perception [as its basis], because of being rooted in perception.

children.text: nanu bhavatu śarīraṃ pṛthivyādi ca vyaktaṃ mahattvānekadravyavattvarūpaviśeṣebhyaḥ tanmūlakāraṇaṃ paramāṇavaḥ kathaṃ vyaktā ityata āha /
children.translated_text: Now, granted that the body, earth, and the like are manifest, [being known] from largeness, possession of many substances, and specific form — but how are atoms, which are their root cause, manifest? To this he says:
"because of the commonality with that" —
meaning: the body, such as a cow and the like, is preceded by a set of causal conditions including [entities] possessing form and the like. //11-13//

In the context of the investigation of <s>pretyabhāva</s> (afterlife), this further matter is investigated. If this so-called origination after death — how [does it occur]? For here, the debaters have various disagreements. Among those, he first takes up the accepted position: "from the manifest" — He will subsequently remove the disagreements. "Substratum of the body, sense-organs, objects, and instruments" — the neuter gender is due to treating them as a unity.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.14: The origination of existence from non-existence is [valid], because of the manifestation without [prior] destruction.

children.text:
ataḥ paraṃ prāvādukānāṃ tairthikānāṃ ca darśanānyupanyastāni kāni citpratiṣidhyante tatra kāni cidabhyanujñāyanta iti ( 454/3 ) tatra tāvadeke prāhurabhāvādbhāvotpattiḥ kutaḥ nānanupamṛdya prādurbhāvo yataḥ tasmādityarthaḥ /
viśyaṃ hi śūnyatāyā eva jāyate /
evaṃ kila śrūyate asadevedasagra āsīditi /
ata evādyāpyasata
eva janma dṛśyate na sataḥ tatkasya hetoḥ abhāvastasyā kāraṇamiti /

children.translated_text: And this [phrase] "because of the manifestation without [prior] destruction" is illustrative —
[the argument] should be seen as also [meaning:] because of the origination from the non-existent.
Therefore it is established that the world has the non-existent as its material cause. //14//

From this point on, certain views of debaters and sectarians are presented — some are refuted, some are approved. (454/3) Among these, first, some say: the origination of existence from non-existence — from where? — "because of the manifestation without [prior] destruction" — therefore — this is the meaning. For the world arises from <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) itself. Thus indeed the <s>śruti</s> is heard: "non-being (<s>asat</s>) alone was this in the beginning." For this very reason, even now, the birth of the non-existent alone is seen, not of the existent. For what reason? Non-existence is its cause — this [is the view].
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.15: Because of self-contradiction, [the argument is] inapplicable.

children.text: tatra siddhāntīpa gūḍhābhisandhirāha upamṛdyaprādurbhavatīti vyāghāta iti // 15 //
children.translated_text: Against this, the <s>siddhāntin</s>, with a hidden intention, says: "it manifests by destroying" — this is self-contradictory. //15//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.16: Not [so], because of the usage of the <s>kāraka</s> (case-relation) word with respect to the past and future.

children.text:
tadabhisandhimavidvān pūrvapakṣī dūṣayati /
na atītānāgatayoḥ kārakaśabdaprayogāditi /
upamṛdya prādurbhavatīti bhākta eṣa prayogo na mukhya ityarthaḥ /
bhinnasya kumbhasya kapālānīti tu yadyapi na sākṣātkārakaśabdastathāpi ṣaṣṭhyā sambandhābhidhānāt tasya kriyāmarbhatvātkriyāyāśca kārakanāntarīyakatvātpāramparyeṇa kārakaśabdatā draṣṭavyā /
pṛcchati kaḥ punaraṅkureṇa bījopamardārthaḥ /
(445/2) kā punarbhaktiḥ yayā yogādupasaṃgṛhṇāti bījamaṅkura iti bhavati prayoga ityarthaḥ /
uttaram /
anantarotpattyarthaḥ upamardyepamardayorapyānantaryamanayorapīti etatsāmānyamityarthaḥ /
punarapi gūḍhābhisandhireva siddhāntī uktaṃ smārayati /
atroktamiti /
abhiprāyamudghāṭayati /
yadapīdamucyata iti /
naupacārikaṃ prayogaṃ vyāsedhāmaḥ kārakaśabdānāṃ, kintu yathā bhaviṣyannaṅkuraḥ samprati asanna bījamupamṛdgāti evaṃ bījābhāvo 'sannāṅkuraṃ karotīti brūmaḥ /
tadidamāha api tvasataḥ kāraṇādutpattirna yukteti /
nanūktamupamṛdya prādurbhāvādityanenānantaryaṃ bījavināśāṅkurotpādayoḥ sūcitaṃ bījavināśānantaryāccāṅkurotpādasya bījavināśakāryatvamityata āha /
yatpunaretadānantaryasāmarthyāditi /
ananyaprayuktamānantaryaṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvasādhanam
idantu vyūhānantaryaprayuktamiti nābhāvasya kāraṇatvaṃ gamayitumarhatītyarthaḥ /
yadi vyūhāntarakāryo 'ṅkuro 'tha kasmādavinaṣṭe pūrvavyūhe na bhavatītyata āha /
na cāvinaṣṭe iti /
nanu yadi bījāvayavavyūhāntaramaṅkurotpādaheturna bījaṃ kasmādaṅkurārthinaḥ kṛṣīvalā bījamupādadataityata
children.translated_text: Now, if a different configuration of the seed's particles is the cause of the sprout's origination and not the seed [itself], why do farmers desiring sprouts take up the seed? To this
he says:
"and thus" —
In taking up the seed's particles, the seed inevitably comes along and cannot be rejected — this is the meaning. //16//

Not knowing that intention, the prima facie opponent objects: "not [self-contradictory], because of the usage of the <s>kāraka</s> word with respect to the past and future." "It manifests by destroying" — this usage is figurative (<s>bhākta</s>), not primary — this is the meaning. "The potsherds of a broken pot" — although this is not directly a <s>kāraka</s>-word, nevertheless, since the genitive case expresses a relation, and that [relation] involves the initiation of an action, and because action necessarily entails <s>kāraka</s>-status — this should be seen as <s>kāraka</s>-status by indirect succession. He asks: "what then is the purpose of the seed for the sprout by means of destruction?" (445/2) The meaning is: what is the figurative usage (<s>bhakti</s>) by the connection with which the seed is taken up by the sprout, giving rise to the usage ["the sprout from the seed"]? The answer: "for the purpose of immediate succession" — the succession of the destruction of the seed and the origination of the sprout is the commonality of these two — this is the meaning. Once again, the <s>siddhāntin</s> with his very hidden intention reminds [us of] what was said: "here it has been stated" — He discloses the intention: "and that which is said" — we do not prohibit the figurative usage of <s>kāraka</s>-words; but just as the sprout, being future and presently non-existent, does not destroy the seed, so too we say: the non-existence of the seed, being non-existent, does not produce the sprout. He states this: "but rather, the origination from a non-existent cause is not justified." Now, it was said that "because of the manifestation without destruction" indicates the succession of the destruction of the seed and the origination of the sprout; and because of the succession of the seed's destruction and the sprout's origination, the sprout has the seed's destruction as its effect — to this he says: "and as for this, through the power of succession" — succession not produced by something else is the proof of the cause-effect relation; but this [succession] is produced by a difference in configuration — therefore it cannot establish the causality of non-existence — this is the meaning. If the sprout is the effect of a different configuration [of seed-parts], then why does it not arise when the previous configuration is not destroyed? To this he says: "and not when [the previous configuration is] not destroyed" —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.17: Not [so], because [the sprout] is not produced from destroyed [seeds].
Having thus purified the meaning, he applies the <s>sūtra</s> to this very meaning:
"and of this meaning" —
The sprout is not produced from destroyed seeds.

children.text: bījavināśaścedaṅkurotpādaheturatha vinaṣṭe bīje tadavayaveṣu parasparavicchinneṣvasati teṣāṃ vyūhāntare kasmādaṅkuro na bhavati bhavati tu sati teṣāṃ vyūhe tasmādvinaṣṭebhyo 'ṅkurānutpatterasati vyūhe na bījanāśaḥ kāraṇamiti sūtrārthaḥ // 17 //
children.translated_text: If the destruction of the seed is the cause of the sprout's origination, then when the seed is destroyed and its particles are mutually separated, in the absence of their [re-]configuration, why does the sprout not arise? But it does arise when their configuration exists. Therefore, because the sprout is not produced from destroyed [seeds], when the configuration is absent, the destruction of the seed is not the cause — this is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>. //17//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.18: Because of the indication of sequence, [the argument is] not refuted.

children.text:
kramanirddeśādityasya hetorasmatpakṣe 'pyapratiṣedhaḥ /
tatrāpyānantaryasya tulyatvāt /
tathāpi vinigamanāyāṃ ko heturityata āha /
abhāvaścedaṅkurotpādakāraṇaṃ syāt /
anupākhyeya iti śeṣaḥ /
na hyananvayavinaṣṭayoḥ śāliyavabījayoḥ kaścidviśeṣo 'sti yenaikasmācchālyaṅkuro nānyasmāditi /
ko nu khalvabhāvānāmastyājānato bheda iti /
api ca kāraṇānāṃ śaktibhedātkāryāṇi bhinnaśaktiyuktāni /
yadā tu kāraṇānāmabhedastadā kutastacchektīnāṃ bhedaḥ tathā ca kāryāṇi bhinnaśaktīni na syurityāha /
ananvitaṃ ca kāryaṃ sarvābhiriti /
yadapyasata utpādādabhāvasyopādānatvaṃ tadapi kāryāṇāṃ bhinnatvena bhinnaśaktikatvena ca prayuktam /
tatprāgabhāvānāṃ svābhāvikabhedavirahāt /
api ca prāgabhāvānāmanāditvena kāryotpādasyāpyanāditvaprasaṅgaḥ
bhāvarūpakāraṇasahakāritvaṃ tvabhāvasya na niṣidhyate asmadabhimatasyopākhyeyasya /
ata
eva pākajādīnāṃrūpādīnāṃ pūrvarūpādidhvaṃsanimittatvamapyupeyate /
śrutistu pūrvapakṣābhiprāyā, tathā ca siddhāntaśrutyantaraṃ sadeva somyedamagra āsīditi kathamasataḥ sajjāyeteti /

children.translated_text: "The world-manifestation is a transformation of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>)"
— this view has been refuted by the refutation of the <s>asatkhyāti</s> (apprehension of the non-existent) and <s>anirvacanīyakhyāti</s> (apprehension of the indescribable).
Moreover, in [the case of] emptiness, because of the non-existence of the perceiver, [there would be] non-existence of the perceived too.

children.text: tasmānna śūnyatopādānastadvivarto vā viśvaprapañca iti siddham // 18 //
children.translated_text: Therefore it is established that the world-manifestation is not the material [product] of emptiness, nor is it a transformation of that. //18//

The non-refutation of this reason "because of the indication of sequence" obtains in our position too, because of the equality of succession even there. Still, what is the reason for determination? To this he says: "if non-existence were the cause of the sprout's origination" — "indescribable" is the remainder. For between the non-residually-destroyed rice and barley seeds, there is no difference whatsoever by which the rice-sprout would arise from one and not from the other. Who indeed knows the difference among non-existences? Moreover, because of the difference in the capacities of causes, the effects possess different capacities. But when there is no difference among the causes, whence the difference in their capacities? And thus the effects would not possess different capacities — he says: "and the effect, [being] unconnected, with all [causes]" — And as for the materiality of non-existence [established] from the origination from the non-existent, that too is motivated by the fact that effects are different and possess different capacities. Since prior-absences (<s>prāgabhāva</s>) lack any intrinsic difference [among themselves] — moreover, because of the beginninglessness of prior-absences, there follows the consequence that the origination of effects too is beginningless. But the co-operation of non-existence with a positive-entity cause is not denied — [speaking of] our accepted [non-existence] that is describable. For this very reason, even the causality of the destruction of the previous form and the like for [the new] form and the like produced by heating (<s>pākaja</s>) is accepted. But the <s>śruti</s> ["non-being alone was this in the beginning"] reflects the prima facie view; and thus, the <s>siddhānta</s>-<s>śruti</s> [states] otherwise: "being (<s>sat</s>) alone, dear one, was this in the beginning" — "how could being arise from non-being?"
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.19: <s>Īśvara</s> (God) is the cause — because of the observation that human action is fruitless [without divine grace].

children.text:
athāpara āha--- iśvaraḥ kāraṇaṃ puruṣakarmāphalyadarśanāt
(sū. 19) mā mūdayaṃ nāmarūpaprapañcaḥ śūnyatopādāno 'pi tu brahmopādānobhaviṣyati, brahmaivahi prapañcarūpeṇa pariṇamate mṛttikeva ghaṭaśarāvodañcanādibhāvena /
na caivaṃ nityatvavyāghātaḥ /
pariṇāme 'pi tattvāvighātāt tallakṣaṇatvācca nityatāyāḥ /
yadāha 'yasmiṃstattvaṃ na vihanyate tadapi nitya'mityekaṃ darśanam /
aparaṃ ca brahmaivānirvacanīyānādyavidyopadhānānnāmarūpaprapañcabhedena vivarttate sukhamivaikamanekamaṇikṛpāṇādibhedānnaikavidhapratibimbabhedeneti,
tadetaddarśanadvayamanena sūcitam /
īśvaro brahma īśanāyogāt /
cetanāśaktiḥ kriyāśaktiśceśanā /
sā cāsti brahmaṇīti brahmaśvaraḥ kāraṇaṃ jagataḥ /
śrūyate hi tadaikṣata bahusyāṃ prajāyeyetyādi /

children.translated_text: And this <s>śruti</s> declares the causality of a conscious [being] for the world.

children.text: na cābhāvo vā pradhānaṃ vā paramāṇavo vā cetayante /
children.translated_text: And neither non-existence, nor <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), nor atoms are conscious.

children.text: nanu jīvā eva cetanāstatkarmanimittonāmarūpaprapañco bhaviṣyati, kṛtamatra bhagavateśvareṇetyata uktaṃ puruṣakarmāphaldarśanāditi puruṣaścet
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) alone are conscious — and the world-manifestation of name and form will be caused by their <s>karma</s> (action) — what need is there for the blessed <s>Īśvara</s>? To this it is said: "because of the observation that human action is fruitless" — if a person

children.text: cetayenaivaṃ niṣphalaṃ karmārabheda, niṣphalaṃ vidvān pravarttamānaḥ kathaṃ cetano nāmadva tasmātpurūṣakarmāphalyadarśanādīśvaraḥ kāraṇamityarthaḥ // 19 //
children.translated_text: were conscious [enough to determine outcomes on his own], he would not undertake fruitless action. A wise person who engages [in action] yet [produces] fruitless [results] — how can he be called 'conscious'? Therefore, because of the observation that human action is fruitless, <s>Īśvara</s> is the cause — this is the meaning. //19//

Now another says: "<s>Īśvara</s> is the cause, because of the observation that human action is fruitless" (sū. 19). Let not this world-manifestation be foolishly [thought to be] the material product of emptiness; rather, it will have <s>Brahman</s> as its material cause. For <s>Brahman</s> itself transforms into the form of the world-manifestation, just as clay [transforms] into the form of a pot, saucer, water-vessel, and the like. Nor is there a contradiction with eternality in this way — because even in transformation, the essence (<s>tattva</s>) is not violated, and eternality is defined by that [non-violation of essence]. As it has been said: "that in which the essence is not violated is also eternal" — this is one view. And another [view:] <s>Brahman</s> itself, through the superimposition of beginningless, indescribable <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), appears as manifold in the form of the world-manifestation of name and form — just as a single [thing like] pleasure appears as many due to the different reflections in jewels, swords, and the like. This pair of views is indicated by this <s>sūtra</s>. <s>Īśvara</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, because of the connection with lordship (<s>īśanā</s>). The power of consciousness and the power of action constitute lordship. And that exists in <s>Brahman</s> — therefore <s>Brahman</s>-as-<s>Īśvara</s> is the cause of the world. For the <s>śruti</s> is heard: "that [<s>Brahman</s>] saw: 'let me become many, let me be born'" and the like.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.20: Not [so], because of the non-production of fruit in the absence of human action.
He refutes both these views:
"Not, in the absence of human action, because of the non-production of fruit" (sū. 20) //

children.text:
idamātrākūtam na tāvanmṛttikeva nāmarūpaprapañcarūpeṇa brahma pariṇamate /
taddhi sarvātmanā vā pariṇamate ekadeśena vā, tatra sarvātmanā pariṇāme tattvavighātādanityatvam /
ekedeśena pariṇāme sāvayavatvāttadevānityatvam /
atha tatvenānugatasya pariṇāmaḥ tacca brahma ? na tarhi brahmaṇaḥ pariṇāmaḥ /
na ca nirbhāgasyaikasya svasamvedanapratyakṣasya viparītajñānagocaratvasambhavaḥ /
sāmānyato grahe rūpaviśeṣāgrahe ca tadanyarūpāropeṇa vibhramo dṛṣṭaḥ śuktikādau, na tu jātu śuktirūpaṃ vidvāna rajatamiti viparyasyati /
na ca niraṃśe svasaṃvedanapratyakṣe brahmaṇi tatsvarūpāgrahaḥ sāmānyagraho vā bhavati /
tasmādīśvaro jagadbhedena vivartataityayuktam /
nimittaṃ tu syādīśvaro jagataḥ, sa cedanapekṣa eva jagatkāraṇamityucyate tatredamupatiṣṭhate /
napuruṣakarmābhāve phalāniṣpatteriti /
asya vyatirekamāha vārtikakāraḥ /
īśvaraścetkāraṇaṃ bhavediti /
( 456/11 ) ekarūrpaṃ kāryaṃ syādityāha īśvarasyeti /

children.translated_text: <s>Īśvara</s> would be non-sovereign (<s>anīśvara</s>) with respect to <s>karma</s>.

children.text: tathā ca tatkāraṇāni neśvareṇa prayujyantaityanekānto vakṣyamāṇo heturityarthaḥ // 20 //
children.translated_text: And accordingly, those causes of <s>karma</s> are not impelled by <s>Īśvara</s> — the forthcoming [argument] is an inconclusive reason (<s>anaikānta hetu</s>) — this is the meaning. //20//

This is the purport of the [objection]: First, <s>Brahman</s> does not transform (<s>pariṇāma</s>) in the form of the manifold of name-and-form, as clay [transforms into a pot]. For it either transforms in its entirety or in part. In the first case — transformation in its entirety — there would be non-eternality, because of the destruction of its real nature. In the second case — transformation in part — there would be the same non-eternality, because of having parts. Now, if [one says] the transformation is of that which is pervaded by the [unchanging] reality — and that is <s>Brahman</s>? — then there is no transformation of <s>Brahman</s> [at all]. And for a partless, unitary [entity] that is self-luminous through direct self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana-pratyakṣa</s>), there is no possibility of being the object of erroneous cognition. Error (<s>vibhrama</s>) has been observed in cases like mother-of-pearl and the like, through the superimposition of another form when there is a general apprehension but non-apprehension of the specific form — but no one who knows the form of mother-of-pearl ever erroneously cognizes it as silver. And in the case of <s>Brahman</s>, which is partless and self-luminous through direct self-awareness, there can be neither non-apprehension of its own nature nor a merely general apprehension. Therefore, [the claim] that <s>Īśvara</s> undergoes apparent transformation (<s>vivarta</s>) as the differentiated world is untenable. However, <s>Īśvara</s> could be the efficient cause (<s>nimitta</s>) of the world — but if it is said that he alone, without dependence [on anything else], is the cause of the world, then the following objection stands: without the <s>karma</s> (merit and demerit) of individual souls, there would be no production of results. The <s>Vārttikakāra</s> states the converse of this: 'If <s>Īśvara</s> were the [sole] cause.' (456/11) He says that the effect would be uniform — 'of <s>Īśvara</s>' —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 4.1.21: Because of being caused by that, [<s>Īśvara</s>] is not the [independent] cause. //

children.text: tadevamīśvaropādānattvaṃ ca brahmavivartatvaṃ ca nirapekṣeśvaranimittatvaṃ ca nirākṛtpayābhimataṃ pakṣaṃ gṛhṇāti /
children.translated_text: Thus, having refuted <s>Īśvara</s>'s being the material cause (<s>upādāna</s>), <s>Brahman</s>'s being an apparent transformation (<s>vivarta</s>), and <s>Īśvara</s>'s being the efficient cause without dependence [on <s>karma</s>], he accepts the desired position:
'Because of being caused by that, [<s>Īśvara</s>] is not the [independent] cause' (<s>sūtra</s> 21). //

āha /

mābhūdasya bhagavataḥ svārthaḥ parānugrahārthaṃ jagannirmāṇe pravartsyatītyarthaḥ /
atraiva dṛṣṭāntamāha /
ayaṃ yathā piturapatyānām /

dārṣṭāntike yojayati tathā pitṛbhūta īśvara iti /

avyāpakanivṛtteravyāpyasyānivṛtteriti /

kāryaṃ jñānaṃ svakāraṇaṃ śarīrādinātivarttate nityaṃ tu tadativarttamānamapi sāhityopalambhaṃ na viruṇaddhi, tasmādyathā 'nityaḥ śabdaḥ utpattimatvāt
ghaṭavaditi prayukte kaścitsādhyadṛṣṭāntayordharmavaicitryātpratyavatiṣṭheta,

na cedayaṃ ghaṭasādharmyeṇa rūpādimān evamanityo 'pi mābhūdityevaṃ ca pratyavatiṣṭhamāna utkarṣasamajātivādī parājīyate evamevevādyutkarṣasamajātivāditayā parājetavyaḥ sādharmyamātreṇāprayojakena pratyavasthānāt /
tasya ca sarvānumāneṣu sulabhatayā sarvānumānocchedāpādakatvāt /
syādetat /
utpattimattvamupādānādyabhijñakartṛpūrvakatvamātravyāptaṃ ghaṭādiṣu dṛṣṭaṃ tāvanmātrameva pṛthivyādīnāṃ gamayed nityasarvaviṣayajñānavatkartṛtvaṃ tu kutastyam /
na hi taddṛṣṭāntadharmiṇi dṛṣṭam /
atha rūpādyupalabdheḥ kriyātvena cakṣurādyanumānapi kathaṃ, na hi cchidādayaḥ kriyā indriyādisādhanāḥ
tāsāṃ kuṭhārādisādhanatvāt /
atha dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇyadṛṣṭamapīndriyasādhanatvaṃ pakṣadharmatābalātsidhyati /
rūpādyupalabdhigataṃ hi kriyātvaṃ tadeva karaṇaṃ gamayed yadupalabdhinirvartanasamarthaṃ,
na ca kuṭhārādayaḥ samarthā iti pakṣadharmatābalātkuṭhārādivilakṣaṇamadṛṣṭacaramapi cakṣurādyupasthāpayatīti ? taditaratrāpi samānam /
na hyayaribheyāniyatadigdeśaindriyakānaindriyakatrasasthāvarādilakṣaṇakāryotpādayaugapadyamasat i sarvaviṣayajñāne tannityatvevā sūddhumarhati,
no khalvīdṛśaṃ parameśvaravijñānaṃ kāryaśarīrādikāryaṃ sambhavati śarīrādyutpatteḥ prāgasyācaitanyena tatprākkālakāryāntarotpādāyeśvarāntarakalpanāprasaṅgāt /
evaṃ tatprāktatprāgityanekālaukikakalpanayā varaṃ buddhinityatvaṃ kalpitam /
etena śarīrendriyanityatvakalpanā 'pi pratyuktā /
