eva /
yaduddeśenābhicāraḥ śyenādinā kriyate tasyaiva pratyavāyo bhavati nānyasyeti niyamaḥ /
children.translated_text: The rule is: the adverse consequence (<s>pratyavāya</s>) occurs precisely to the person against whom the hostile rite (<s>abhicāra</s>) is performed by the <s>śyena</s> [sacrifice] and the like, not to another.
Here too, the causality with respect to the action is observed.
Just as on the ground called mud —
the rest is easy. //9//

The refutation: 'Because of the observation of the production of pots and the like' is the <s>sūtra</s>. He explains it: 'Of rods and the like that have attained the lump of clay, [there is] no non-distinction like that of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the ocean.' 'The parts of clay, by abandoning the previous arrangement' — (536/2) The provable is the action, and that [is provable]; the parts of clay are established — thus there is no deviation. But the pot is the result, not the provable — this is the import. 'What is the meaning of non-attainment?' — The import is: if what has not attained could prove, there would be over-extension. The answer: 'proving without mutual contact.' Otherwise, by [mere] intention, this [reason] has indeed attained [the provable].

children.text: NyS_5,1.9: dṛṣṭāntasya kāraṇānapadeśāt pratyavasthānācca pratidṛṣṭāntena prasaṅgapratidṛṣṭāntasamau //
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.9 [cont.]: Because of not stating the ground for the example, and because of the counter-argument with a counter-example, [these are] the comparable-by-extension and comparable-by-counter-example. //
'Because of not stating the ground for the example, and because of the counter-argument with a counter-example, the comparable-by-extension and comparable-by-counter-example' (<s>sūtra</s> 9). //

children.text:
dṛṣṭāntasya kāraṇaṃ pramāṇaṃ tasyānapadeśātprasaṅgapasamaḥ sādhyasamo hi dṛṣṭānte sādhyavaddhetvādyavayavaṃ prasañjayati /
pañcāvayavaprayogasādhyatāṃ dṛṣṭāntasya gatasyānityatvasya prasañjayatītyarthaḥ /
prasaṅgasamastu dṛṣṭāntagatasyānityatvasya pramāṇamātrasādhyatāmityapaunaruktyam /
bhāṣyaṃ sādhanasyāpi /
dṛṣṭāntagatasyānityatvaspaya sādhanaṃ pramāṇaṃ vācyamiti /
vārttikaṃ ghaṭa eva tāvadanitya ityatra ko heturiti /
atra kiṃ pramāṇamityarthaḥ /
bhāṣyaṃ pratidṛṣṭānta udāhniyate /
kiṃyāhetuguṇayuktamākāśamakriyaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ tasmādanena pratidṛṣṭāntena kasmāt /
kriyāhetuguṇayogo niṣkriyatvameva na sādhayatyātmana iti śeṣaḥ /
yadi punariyamanaikānitakadeśanā syāt kriyāhetuguṇayuktasyāpyakriyatvaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yathākāśasyeti tad etatsaduttaraṃ syāt /
na tvevametaditi jātiḥ /
śaṅkate /
vāyvākāśasaṃyogasyeti /
nirākaroti /
na tatsamānadharmopapatteḥ /
tatsamānadharmaṇo dharmiṇaḥ kriyāvattvopapatteḥ /
yadi tathābhūta evākāśe kasmānna karotītyata āha yastvasāviti /
(537/1) yastu manyate kāryotpādaikyavyaṅnyameva kāraṇaṃ na dṛṣṭakāryakāraṇasādharmyavyaṅnyamapīti,
tasya dūṣaṇānyāha yadi ceti /
children.translated_text: The ground (<s>kāraṇa</s>) of the example is the means of valid knowledge; because of not stating that, [this is] the comparable-by-extension (<s>prasaṅgasama</s>). For the comparable-by-provability occasions the provability of the example through [the requirement of] the members of the syllogism such as the reason and the like. (533/9) But the comparable-by-extension occasions the provability of the non-eternality established in the example through the means of valid knowledge alone — thus there is no repetition. The <s>Bhāṣya</s> [reads]: 'of the proof too' — the proof, i.e. the means of valid knowledge, of the non-eternality established in the example should be stated. The <s>Vārttika</s> [reads]: 'In "the pot indeed is non-eternal" — what is the reason here?' — meaning: what is the means of valid knowledge here? The <s>Bhāṣya</s> [reads]: 'a counter-example is cited' — 'Why? — An entity possessing the conjunction of a reason of inaction and a quality is observed [to be] without action, like <s>ākāśa</s>; therefore, by this counter-example, why [does it not prove non-eternality]?' — the conjunction of a reason of inaction and a quality, [namely] inactivity itself, does not prove [anything] regarding the self — this is the remainder. Now, if this teaching of inconclusiveness were [valid] — [namely,] 'even of something possessing the conjunction of a reason of inaction and a quality, inactivity is observed, as in the case of <s>ākāśa</s>' — then this would be a good answer. But this is not [a valid jāti] — therefore it is a [futile] rejoinder. He raises a doubt: 'of the conjunction of wind and <s>ākāśa</s>' — He refutes: 'Not, because of the tenability of the property common with that.' Because of the tenability of the property-bearer that has a property common with that [ākāśa] having activity. If in something of precisely such a nature — <s>ākāśa</s> — why does [the conjunction] not produce [activity]? — to this he says: 'but this one' — (537/1) But one who thinks that the indicator of a cause is only the unity of effect-production, and not also the similarity with an observed cause-effect [relation] — he states the criticisms of that [view]: 'and if' —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.10: Like the cessation of the extension regarding the material of a lamp, so is the cessation of that [extension]. //

children.text:
yadi prajñāpanārthamuttaraṃ nāprajñāto dṛṣṭāntaḥ /
tatra laukikaparīkṣakāṇāṃ buddhisāmyāditi śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: If the reply is for the purpose of making known [something], then an example that is not [already] known [is needed]. In that [context], because of the equality of understanding between worldly [people] and examiners — this is the remainder.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.11: And if the counter-example is taken as a reason, the example is not without a reason. //

children.text:
sa ca kathamahertuna syāditi (538/1) kathaṃ hetuḥ syāditi /
abhyupagamāditi /
madīyasya ca dṛṣṭāntasyābhyupagamānna tvadīyo dṛṣṭānta ityarthaḥ /
athaivaṃ prayuṅkte yathā madīyo na dṛṣṭāntastathā tvadīya iti tathāpi vyāghātānna dṛṣṭānto madīyasyādṛṣṭāntatve sādhye pratidṛṣṭāntena hi tena madīyasyā dṛṣṭāntatā sādhyā, sa cenna dṛṣṭāntaḥ madīpasyādṛṣṭāntatā sādhyeti vyāhatamityarthaḥ // 9 // 10 // 11 //
children.translated_text: 'And how would it be without a reason?' — (538/1) [means:] how would it be a reason? 'Because of [mutual] acceptance' — meaning: because of the acceptance of my example, [your] counter-example is not [valid] — this is the meaning. Now, if one argues thus: 'just as my [example] is not an example, so too yours' — even so, because of contradiction, [it is] not an example. For by his counter-example, the non-example-hood of my [example] is to be proved; and if that [counter-example] is not an example, then the non-example-hood of mine is [itself] to be proved — this is contradictory — this is the meaning. //9// 10// 11//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.12: Because of the absence of the cause before origination, [this is] the comparable-by-non-origination. //

children.text: udāharaṇapuraḥsaraṃ bhāṣyakāro vyācaṣṭe anityaḥ śabdaḥ prayatnānantarīyakatvād
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> explains with an illustration: 'Sound is non-eternal, because of being immediately subsequent to effort' —
'like a pot' — thus it is said.
Before hearing that [sound], because of the absence of the cause, [and] because of the absence of the non-eternal effect, eternality is obtained.
Because of the non-existence of a third category besides eternality and non-eternality — //12//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.13: Because of the tenability of a cause for what has originated in that manner, there is no negation of the cause. //
"Similarly, because of the tenability of cause for what has arisen as existent, there is no negation of cause" (sūtra 13). //
The refutation of that:

children.text:
nityatvena hi śabdasya dharmeṇānutpattyā pratyavastheyam /
na cānutpannaḥ śabda iti nitya iti cānutpattidharmaka
iti ca sambhavati /
utpannastṛtpattidharmā ca śabdaścāni tyaśceti nānutpattyā śakyaṃ pratyavasthātumityarthaḥ /
kāraṇopapatteriti prayatnānantarīyakatvasya pratiṣedha ityarthaḥ /
yaduktaṃ kāraṇābhāvādanityatvasya kāryasyābhāve nityatvaṃ prāptamiti tatrāha vārtikakāraḥ /
jñāpakaścāyaṃ heturna kāraka
iti /
kārako hi heturnivartamānaḥ svakāryaṃ nivartayati na tujñāpakastadabhāve 'pi bhūmau ciranikhātānāṃ nidhyādīnāmanivṛtteriti /
tataśca viśeṣaṇa manarthakaṃ prāgutpatterati /
(539/4) prāgasato hi sattāsambandha utpattiḥ prāgapi cedasāvabhyupagataḥ prāgiti viśeṣaṇamanarthakam /
utpatterabhāve sadaivānutpattidharmakatvādityarthaḥ /
apare tu prāgutpatteḥ kāraṇābhāvādityukte arthāpattisamaiveyaṃ jātiriti matvā 'syā uttaramāhuḥ yadaivaṃmucyeta prayatnānantarīyakatvādanityaḥ śabda iti tadarthādaprayatnānantarīyakatve nityatvamuktaṃ bhavatītyarthāpattitaḥ pratipakṣasiddherarthāpattisamaiveyaṃ jātirityabhimānaḥ /
evaṃ kṛte ta evāsyāṃ jātāvuttaraṃ bruvate nāyaṃ niyama iti /
tadetatpareṣāṃ mataṃ dūṣayati /
etattviti /
śaṅkate /
jātilakṣaṇābhāvānneyaṃ jātiriti cet /
sādharmyavaidharmyābhyāṃ pratyavasthānaṃ jātiḥ na cānutpattisamāyāḥ sādharmyaṃ vaidharmyaṃ vā 'sti kena cidityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: He refutes:
"Not [so], because of resemblance with unoriginated non-causes" —

children.text: yathā 'nutpannāstantavo na paṭasya kāraṇaṃ tathā śabdotpatteḥ prāganutpannaṃ prayatnānantarīyakatvaṃ nānityatvasya kāraṇamiti sādharmyeṇa pratyavasthānamityasti sāmānyalakṣaṇamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as unoriginated threads are not the cause of cloth, so too the property of being immediately subsequent to effort, being unoriginated prior to the origination of sound, is not the cause of non-eternality — this counter-argument through similarity exists — therefore the general defining characteristic [of <s>jāti</s>] is present — this is the meaning.

children.text: etāvatā cārthāpattisamāyā anutpattisamāto bhedo darśitaḥ ihānutpannairahetubhiḥ sāmyena kāryapratiṣedhāt arthāpattisamāyāṃ vākyārthaviparītāropeṇa pratiṣedhāditi // 13 //
children.translated_text: And by this much, the difference of the <s>arthāpattisama</s> from the <s>anutpattisama</s> has been shown: here, in the <s>anutpattisama</s>, the negation of the effect is through equivalence with unoriginated non-causes; in the <s>arthāpattisama</s>, the negation is through the attribution of the opposite of the sentence-meaning. //13//

One should counter [the opponent] by the property of non-origination, which is the characteristic of the eternality of <s>śabda</s> (sound).
But it is not possible for [the word] to be "unoriginated" and "eternal" and "having non-origination as its characteristic" simultaneously.
What is originated, has origination as its characteristic, and is <s>śabda</s> — is non-eternal; therefore one cannot counter [the opponent] through non-origination — this is the meaning.
"Because of the tenability of cause" means: the negation of the property of being immediately subsequent to effort — this is the meaning.
As for what was said — "in the absence of cause, since the effect which is non-eternality would be absent, eternality follows" — to that the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> says:
"And this reason is an indicator (jñāpaka), not a producer (kāraka)."
For a producing cause, when it ceases, causes its own effect to cease; but an indicating [cause does] not — because even in its absence, treasures and the like long buried in the ground do not cease to exist.
Therefore the qualifier "prior to origination" is meaningless.
(539/4) For origination is the connection with existence of what was previously non-existent; and if that [non-existence] too is accepted as prior, the qualifier "prior" is meaningless.
In the absence of origination, because [sound] would always have the characteristic of non-origination — this is the meaning.
But others, considering that when it is said "because of the absence of cause prior to origination," this <s>jāti</s> (futile rejoinder) is equivalent to <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), state the reply to it: when it is expressed thus — "sound is non-eternal because of being immediately subsequent to effort" — from the purport of that, the eternality [of sound] follows when there is absence of being immediately subsequent to effort — thus, because the counter-thesis is established through <s>arthāpatti</s>, this <s>jāti</s> is equivalent to <s>arthāpatti</s> — such is [their] opinion.
Having done so, those very [thinkers] state the reply to this <s>jāti</s>: "this is not a rule."
He criticizes this view of the others:
"But this" — etc.
He raises the doubt:
"If [one says] this is not a jāti because of the absence of the defining characteristic of jāti" —
<s>Jāti</s> is a counter-argument through similarity and dissimilarity; and the <s>anutpattisama</s> (non-origination-equivalence) has no similarity or dissimilarity with anything — this is the meaning.

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.14: Since the universal and the example are alike in being beyond the senses, because of the similarity of the eternal and the non-eternal, [this is] equivalent to doubt (<s>saṃśayasama</s>). //
The example for the reason "being immediately subsequent to effort" is a pot — etc.

children.text: yathā hi viśeṣadarśanaṃ niścayasya kāraṇamastīti niścayotpattireva sādharmyadarśanamātramasti saṃśayasya kāraṇamiti saṃśayenāpi bhavitavyamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the perception of a particular is the cause of certainty, and [since] certainty does arise, so too the mere perception of similarity is the cause of doubt, and therefore doubt too must arise — this is the meaning.
He clarifies the meaning and purpose of the <s>sūtra</s> through objection and resolution:
"The <s>saṃśayasama</s> [is equivalent to] the <s>sādharmyasama</s>" — //14//

children.text: NyS_5,1.15: sādharmyātsaṃśaye na saṃśayo vaidharmyād ubhayathā vā saṃśaye 'tyantasaṃśayaprasaṅgo nityatvānabhyupagamācca sāmānyasyāpratiṣedhaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.15: If there is doubt from similarity, there is no doubt from dissimilarity; or if there is doubt in both cases, there is the consequence of perpetual doubt; and because of the non-acceptance of eternality, the universal is not negated. //

children.text:
asya pratyākhyānasūtram /
sādharmyātsaṃśaye na saṃśayo vaidharmyāduśrayathā vā saṃśaye 'tyantasaṃśayaprasaṅgo nityatvānabhyupagamācca sāmānyasyāpratiṣedhaḥ (sū. 15) /
na sāmānyadarśanamātraṃ saṃśayasya kāraṇamapi tu viśeṣādarśanasahitaṃ viśeṣadarśane tu tadrahitaṃ na kāraṇamiti sūtrārthaḥ /
ubhayathā veti /
sādharmyaviśeṣadarśanābhyāmityarthaḥ /
nityatvānabhyupagamācca sāmānyasyeti /
nityaṃ saṃśayakāraṇatvānabhyupagamātsādharmyasyetyarthaḥ
// 15 //
children.translated_text:
The <s>sūtra</s> of refutation for this:
"If there is doubt from similarity, there is no doubt from dissimilarity; or if there is doubt in both cases, there is the consequence of perpetual doubt; and because of the non-acceptance of eternality, the universal is not negated" (sūtra 15).
Mere perception of similarity is not the cause of doubt, but rather [similarity] accompanied by non-perception of the particular; whereas the perception of the particular, when devoid of that [non-perception], is not a cause [of doubt] — this is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>.
"Or in both cases" means: through both similarity and perception of the particular — this is the meaning.
"And because of the non-acceptance of eternality of the universal" means: because of the non-acceptance of similarity as being an eternal cause of doubt — this is the meaning.
//15//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.16: Because of the similarity of both, [and] because of the establishment of the subject-matter, [this is] equivalent to the subject-matter (<s>prakaraṇasama</s>). //

children.text:
upalakṣaṇaṃ caitad ubhayasādharmyāditi /
ubhayavaidharmyādityapi draṣṭavyam /
etadvyācaṣṭe bhāṣyakāraḥ ubhayena nityena cānityena ceti /
dvitīyaśca nityasādharmyātpratipakṣaṃ pravartayati nityaḥ śabdaḥ śrāvaṇatvācchabdatvavaditi /
atha dvitīyasādhanapravṛttau prathamasya sādhanasya kiṃ bhavatītyata āha /
evaṃ ca sati prayatnāṃnantarīyakatvāditi heturanityasādharmyeṇocyamāno na prakaraṇamativartate /
mā 'tivarttiṣṭa prakaraṇaṃ ko doṣa ityata āha /
prakaraṇānativṛtternirṇayānativarttanam /
nirṇayāniṣpattirityarthaḥ /
evamānityasādhanavādinaṃ pratyuttaraṃ darśayitvā nityasādhanavādinaṃ pratyāha /
samānaṃ caitannityasādharmyeṇocyamāna
iti /
tadevaṃ sādharmyeṇa prakaraṇasamadvayamuktaṃ tathā vaidharmyeṇa prakaraṇasamadvayaṃ nityānityasādhanavādināveva pratyāha /
samānaṃ caitaditi /
ubhayavaidharmyāditi /
nityākāśavaidharmyātkṛtakatvādanityaghaṭavaidharmyāccāsparśavattvāditi /
tadevaṃ prakaraṇasamacatuṣṭayam /
pūrvapakṣavārttikaṃ saṃśayasamasādharmyasamābhyāmiti (540/13)pariharati /
nobhayapakṣasādharmyāttadbhedopapattiriti /
prakaraṇasame hi svapakṣaniścayena mayā vādipakṣasādhanaṃ dūṣaṇīyamiti buddhyā pravarttate /

children.translated_text: But in the <s>sādharmyasama</s> and <s>saṃśayasama</s>, the refutation of the [opponent's] proof is through merely establishing equivalence with the opponent's proof,
not through certainty about the counter-thesis — this is the distinction.

children.text: iha tu sāmyamātrāpādanaṃ na sādhanena, kiṃ tu dūṣaṇairityetāvatā samārthaḥ prayogaḥ sama iti boddhavyam // 16 //
children.translated_text: Here, however, the establishment of mere equivalence is not through the [opponent's] proof, but rather through refutations — and to that extent, the meaning of "equivalent" (sama) in the formulation should be understood. //16//

And this "because of the similarity of both" is merely illustrative.
"Because of the dissimilarity of both" should also be understood.
The <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> explains this: "with both — with what is eternal and with what is non-eternal."
And the second [disputant] introduces the counter-thesis through similarity with the eternal: "sound is eternal because of being auditory (śrāvaṇatva), like sound-hood (śabdatva)."
Now, when the second proof is introduced, what happens to the first proof? — to this he says:
"And in that case, the reason 'because of being immediately subsequent to effort,' when stated through similarity with the non-eternal, does not transcend the subject-matter (prakaraṇa)."
"Let it not transcend the subject-matter — what is the fault?" — to this he says:
"Because of not transcending the subject-matter, there is no transcending of determination; [that is,] no accomplishment of determination" — this is the meaning.
Having thus shown the reply against the proponent of the non-eternality proof, he speaks against the proponent of the eternality proof:
"And this is the same when stated through similarity with the eternal."
Thus, two <s>prakaraṇasamas</s> through similarity have been stated; similarly, he speaks of two <s>prakaraṇasamas</s> through dissimilarity, against both the proponents of the eternality and non-eternality proofs:
"And this is the same" — etc.
"Through dissimilarity of both" — etc.
"Through dissimilarity from eternal <s>ākāśa</s>, because of being produced; and through dissimilarity from non-eternal pots, because of being intangible."
Thus there is a tetrad of <s>prakaraṇasamas</s>.
The preliminary-objection <s>Vārttika</s> — "from the saṃśayasama and sādharmyasama" — he resolves (540/13):
"Not from the similarity of both theses, because of the tenability of the distinction between them."
For in the <s>prakaraṇasama</s>, [the respondent] proceeds with the conviction "I must refute the opponent's proof by [establishing] certainty about my own thesis."
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.17: Because of the establishment of the subject-matter from the counter-thesis, the negation is untenable, because of the tenability of the counter-thesis. //
"Because of the establishment of the subject-matter from the counter-thesis, the negation is untenable, because of the tenability of the counter-thesis" (sūtra 17). //
The refutation of this:

children.text:
dvayoḥ sādhanayostadānīmagṛhyamāṇaviśeṣayoḥ ko 'yamabhimānaḥ prativādino yanmayāsvapakṣasādhanenaiva vādinaḥ sādhanaṃ dūṣaṇīyamiti /
samānabalayoścedayamātmīyātsādhanātsvapakṣasiddhipamicchati ato 'nicchannapi vādināpi sādhanātsiddhimabhyupagamayitavyaḥ /
anyathā svasādhanātsādhyasiddhimupajīvya vyaktamiyaṃ rājaṅkulasthitiriti /
evaṃ vyavasthite sūtrabhāṣye yojayitavye /
pratipakṣātpratipakṣasādhanātprakaraṇasya prakriyamāṇasya sādhyasyeti yāvat /
siddheḥ samānāt svasādhanāt pratiṣedhasya prativādisādhanasya svasādhyasiddhidvāreṇa parakīyasādhanapratiṣedhasyānupapattiḥ /
kasmātpratiṣedhānupapattirityata uktaṃ pratipakṣopapatteḥ /
phalataḥ parakīyasādhanasya samānātsvasādhanātprakriyāsiddhiṃ svasādhyasiddhiṃ bruvatā pratipakṣātprakriyāsiddhiruktā bhavati prativādinā /
nanvevaṃ prakaraṇasamāvhayo hetvābhāso nodbhāvanīyaḥ prativādinā jātyuttaraprasaṅgādityata āha /
tattvānavadhāraṇācca prakriyāsiddhiḥ /
svasādhyanirṇayena parasādhyavighaṭanabuddhyā prativādinā sādhanaṃ prayujyamānaṃ prakaraṇasamajātyuttaraṃ bhavati /
satpratipakṣatayā vādinaḥ sādhanamaniścāyakaṃ karomīti buddhyā pratipakṣasādhanaṃ prayuñjāno na jātivādī saduttaravāditvāt /
satpratipakṣatāyā hetudoṣasyānaikāntikādivadupapāditatvāt /
tattvānavadhāraṇādityanena prakaraṇasamodāharaṇaṃ darśitam /
vārtikaṃ viruddhāvyabhicāryeṣa

children.translated_text: has been answered."
When both [disputants], of equal strength, each accept the establishment of their own provable from one of the two [reasons], the deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) of both is effectively established.
And the mutually contradictory non-deviating [reason] (<s>viruddhāvyabhicārin</s>) is not possible [here].

children.text: avyabhicāro hyavinābhāvaḥ sa ca pañcarūpasampattiścatūrūpasampattirvā na viruddhāvyabhicāriṇi sāstītyarthaḥ // 17 //
children.translated_text: For non-deviation means invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>), and that is either the five-fold or four-fold fulfillment [of the reason's conditions] — and that does not exist in the <s>viruddhāvyabhicārin</s> — this is the meaning. //17//

When the two proofs have, at that time, no apprehended distinction between them, what is this presumption of the respondent that "I must refute the proponent's proof by my own counter-thesis proof alone"?
If the two [proofs] are of equal strength, and he desires the establishment of his own thesis from his own proof, then even unwillingly, the proponent too must be made to acknowledge the establishment [of his thesis] from [his own] proof.
Otherwise, it would be like relying on the establishment of the provable from one's own proof and [then acting like] "clearly, this is the way of the royal court."
With things thus settled, the <s>sūtra</s> and <s>bhāṣya</s> should be construed:
"From the counter-thesis" means: from the counter-thesis proof; "of the subject-matter" means: of that which is being proved — so much is meant;
"the establishment" means: from one's own proof, which is equal [in strength]; "the negation" means: the negation of the opponent's proof through the avenue of establishing one's own provable — [this is] the untenability.
Why is the negation untenable? — to this it is said: "because of the tenability of the counter-thesis."
In effect, by the respondent who says that the subject-matter is established — [namely,] the establishment of one's own provable — from a proof that is equal [in strength] to the opponent's, the establishment of the subject-matter from the counter-thesis has been stated.
Now, should not the futile rejoinder called <s>prakaraṇasama</s> be put forward by the respondent, since [otherwise] there would be the consequence of a <s>jāti</s>-reply? — to this he says:
"And because of the non-ascertainment of the truth, the establishment of the subject-matter."
When the respondent employs proof with the conviction of refuting the opponent's provable through certainty about his own provable, his proof being employed becomes the <s>prakaraṇasama</s> futile rejoinder.
But one who employs counter-thesis proof with the conviction "I make the proponent's proof inconclusive by [showing] that it has a counter-thesis (satpratipakṣa)" is not a <s>jāti</s>-arguer, because he argues with valid replies.
Because <s>satpratipakṣatā</s> (having a counter-thesis) is established as a defect of the reason, like inconclusiveness and the like.
By "because of non-ascertainment of truth," the illustration of the <s>prakaraṇasama</s> is shown.
The <s>Vārttika</s> [reads]: "in the case of the mutually contradictory non-deviating [reasons], this
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.18: Because of the non-establishment of the reason in the three times, [this is] equivalent to non-reason (<s>ahetusama</s>). //
The <s>sūtra</s>, <s>bhāṣya</s>, and <s>vārttika</s> have been explained through the explanation of the general examination of the means of valid knowledge. //18//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.19: Because of the establishment of the provable from the reason, there is no non-establishment in the three times. //
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.20: And because of the untenability of the negation, [there is] non-negation of what is to be negated. //
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.21: Because of the establishment of the counter-thesis through presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>), [this is] equivalent to presumption (<s>arthāpattisama</s>). //
He construes the <s>sūtra</s> preceded by an illustration:
"Sound is non-eternal" — etc.

children.text: anityasādharmyādanityaṃ śabdaṃ bruvāṇo bhavānanakṣaraṃ nityasādharmyānnityatvaṃ śabdasya brūtaityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: You, who assert that sound is non-eternal through similarity with the non-eternal, are [implicitly] saying that sound is eternal through similarity with the eternal — this is the meaning from <s>arthāpatti</s>.
The distinction [from the <s>sādharmyasama</s>] is that in the <s>sādharmyasama</s> and the like, there is no description of the proponent's intention. //21//

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.22: Because of the presumption of what is unstated, [and] because of the tenability of the abandonment of the thesis — because of the unstatedness and because of the non-conclusiveness of the presumption. //
The <s>sūtra</s> of refutation for this:

"Because of the presumption of what is unstated, [and] because of the tenability of the abandonment of the thesis — because of the unstatedness and because of the non-conclusiveness of the presumption" (sūtra 22). //

children.translated_text: "Nor does this [presumption operate merely] from reversal" —
For not from every negation of eating does the reversed [conclusion of] non-eating hold universally.

children.text: dhanatvaṃ hi grāvṇaḥ patanānukūlagurutvātiśayasūcanārthaṃ na tvitareṣāṃ patanaṃ vārayati /
children.translated_text: For the heaviness of a stone, [which is] the excess of heaviness favorable to falling, [merely] indicates [heaviness]; but it does not prevent the falling of other things.
The <s>Vārttika</s> is easy to understand. //22//

He explains that: "without having demonstrated the capacity" —
Indeed, what is unstated is obtained from the statement [only] when, without presupposing it, the meaning of the statement cannot be coherent — as when it is said "fat <s>Devadatta</s> does not eat during the day," it is [presumed that] "he eats at night."
Or as when it is said "one should produce heaven through sacrifice," without an intervening <s>apūrva</s> (unseen potency), the meaning of the statement [requires] its capacity.
But when the provable is being established from an invariable similarity, it is not stated [by implication] that [one] should also establish [it] from a deviating similarity;
because of the incapacity of that [deviating similarity] for establishing the meaning of the statement,
[and] because the meaning of the statement is coherent without it.
But if what is unstated were cognized even without established capacity, then when you state the eternality [of sound], the non-eternality, which is unstated, should be cognized [by you].
And thus there would be the abandonment of your accepted eternality.
This he states: "when the non-eternal thesis, which is unstated, is established through its content (artha), the abandonment of the eternal thesis results."
Because the counter-argument is possible in reverse too,
he states the non-conclusiveness: "and this is equal to both theses."
And he states the non-conclusiveness from deviation: "nor does this [hold merely] from reversal" —

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.23: Because of the tenability of a single property, when there is no distinction — because of the consequence of total non-distinction from the existence [of similarity] — [this is] equivalent to non-distinction (<s>aviśeṣasama</s>). //

children.translated_text: The refutation-<s>Vārttika</s> [says]: 'it is not one <s>sama</s>' — //23//

If, because of similarity with a pot in being immediately subsequent to effort, there is a non-distinction called 'non-eternality' of sound — then, because of the similarity of everything with being (<s>sattva</s>), the consequence would be non-distinction of everything from everything. But it is not the case that, just as because of similarity in being immediately subsequent to effort, the non-eternality of sound and pot is a non-distinction — thus the refutation is the comparable-by-non-distinction (<s>aviśeṣasama</s>). 'Non-distinction' — the explanation of this is: 'non-eternality of both.' The <s>Vārttika</s> to be taught [says]: 'it does not differ from the comparable-by-similarity (<s>sādharmyasama</s>)' — (542/6).
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.24: Because of the untenability of a property in certain [cases] and the tenability [of it] in other [cases], there is no refutation. //
The <s>sūtra</s> of refutation for this:
'Because of the untenability of that property in certain [cases] and the tenability [of it] in other [cases], there is no refutation' (<s>sūtra</s> 24). //

children.translated_text: Now, [if it is said that] everything except sound is spoken of —
to that he says: 'Or the mention of "all entities" is purposeless.'

children.text: uktaśca viśeṣo 'nvayavyatirekasaṃpanno heturiti prayatnāntarīyakatvaṃ na tūttaraḥ sadbhāvopapatterityanvayavyatirekasampanna
children.translated_text: And it has been said that the specific [reason] endowed with positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>) is the [valid] reason — namely, being immediately subsequent to effort — but not the rejoinder [based on] 'because of the tenability of existence,' which is endowed with positive and negative concomitance —

The construction is: because of the tenability of that property — the property of the pot, namely non-eternality — when there is similarity such as being immediately subsequent to effort between sound and the like and the pot and the like, in certain [instances of] similarity; and because of the untenability of the property of mere being (<s>bhāvamātra</s>) when there is similarity such as existence (<s>sattva</s>) between sound and mere being, in certain [instances of] similarity — there is no refutation. What this means is: similarity that is endowed with invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>) is indicative [of the property to be proved], but not mere similarity. 'Existence is the ground for tenability' — meaning: it pervades existence. In the meanwhile, the annihilationist (<s>vaināśika</s>), thinking that non-eternality pervades existence (<s>sattā</s>), teaches: 'If it is held that non-eternality itself is another property' — He refutes: 'Indeed, when thus constructed' — the resolution of the prima facie and concluding positions has been elaborated in the third [chapter]. Moreover, some existents have their eternality ascertained by means of valid knowledge — such as <s>ākāśa</s> (space) and the like, <s>ātman</s>, and atoms; and some have their non-eternal nature determined by valid knowledge — such as pots and the like. Therefore, because existence (<s>sattva</s>) is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), it does not prove [non-eternality] — thus he says: 'And because of the eternal and non-eternal nature of what exists.' Moreover, the reductio that is adduced for the purpose of refutation itself establishes the very thing to be refuted, and does not negate [it] — thus he says: 'Because of the tenability of the existence of all entities.' The <s>Vārttika</s>: 'Similarity is observed in certain [cases]' — the remainder is: 'as pervaded [by the property].'
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.25: Because of the tenability of a reason for both, [this is] the comparable-by-tenability (<s>upapattisama</s>). //

children.text: yadyanityatvakāraṇaṃ prayatnānantarīyakatvamupapadyate tadasti śabdasyetyanityaḥ śabda iti /
children.translated_text: If the reason — being immediately subsequent to effort — for non-eternality is tenable, then sound possesses it; and [therefore] sound is non-eternal.

children.text: prakaraṇasamāyāṃ jātau pakṣapratipakṣasādhanayoḥ samānabalatve 'pi prativādi svāsādhanāsvapakṣasiddhpavayā vādisādhanadūṣaṇe pravarttate, upapattisamāyāṃ tu svasādhanenaiveti viśeṣaḥ // 25 //
children.translated_text: In the <s>jāti</s> of comparable-by-topic (<s>prakaraṇasama</s>), even when the proofs of the thesis and counter-thesis are of equal strength, the respondent engages in the refutation of the proponent's proof by [means of] the non-establishment of his own proof and the non-establishment of his own thesis. But in the comparable-by-tenability (<s>upapattisama</s>), [the respondent engages] by his own proof alone — this is the difference. //25//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.26: Because of the concession of the reason for tenability, there is no refutation. //
The <s>sūtra</s> of refutation for this:
'Because of the concession of the reason for tenability, there is no refutation' (<s>sūtra</s> 26). //

children.text: vādyabhimatasya sādhanasyopapattau yatkāraṇaṃ tasvaya prativādinā 'bhyanujñānāditi bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: The import is: because the reason for the tenability of the proof accepted by the proponent is itself conceded by the respondent.
The refutation of this [<s>jāti</s>] should be seen as similar to the refutation of the comparable-by-topic (<s>prakaraṇasama</s>).
The <s>Bhāṣya</s> and <s>Vārttika</s> are easy [to understand]. //26//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.27: Because of perception even when the stated cause is absent, [this is] the comparable-by-apprehension (<s>upalabdhisama</s>). //

children.translated_text: The capacity to produce another sound is the capacity to produce something of the same kind —
And thus, the non-eternality of sound is not a reason through exclusion-by-non-connection (<s>nāyogavyavaccheda</s>), because of the non-pervasiveness [of the reason].
Nor [is it a reason] through exclusion-by-other-connection (<s>anyayogavyavaccheda</s>), because another reason is available — this is the intent of the <s>jāti</s>-proponent. //27//

'Of the cause of non-eternality' — meaning: of the indicator (<s>jñāpaka</s>). Now, the object of the precedence of occurrence and connection is the property of the proof, not the property of what is to be proved; for that [property to be proved] is the object of [another] occurrence-and-connection. Thus [the argument] is employed: 'Whatever is immediately subsequent to effort, all that is non-eternal' — for by this, being immediately subsequent to effort is excluded from [entities] other than the non-eternal. But non-eternality is unrestricted — if it were [found] in sound that is not immediately subsequent to effort, or elsewhere, what contradiction would there be of being immediately subsequent to effort with the restriction of non-eternality? For that [contradiction] would exist if something eternal were also observed as immediately subsequent to effort — but this is not so. Therefore, there is no occasion at all for the arising of the comparable-by-apprehension — because of the absence of the seed [i.e., the basis for the objection]. To this, the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> says: 'The meaning of the comparable-by-apprehension is the superimposition of non-pervasiveness on the proof through the superimposition of all provable [properties].' (543/7) Although the sound intended as having verbal nature is intended as provable through non-eternality, from the context 'sound is non-eternal, because of being immediately subsequent to effort, like a pot' — nevertheless, superimposing that [the argument intends] mere sound, [the objector] superimposes the defect of partial non-establishment (<s>bhāgāsiddhatva</s>) on the proof — this is the meaning of the comparable-by-apprehension. He shows this very superimposition through another example: 'Everything is non-eternal.' Even though the thesis is 'sound is non-eternal,' [the objector] superimposes 'everything is non-eternal' — this is the construction. The <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>'s [earlier] example was deficient, and therefore the seed for presenting another example [was planted]. But one who is not satisfied, [arguing] that in the thesis 'sound is non-eternal,' the superimposition of the non-eternality of everything is baseless — to him he says: 'That which is heard' — although 'sound is non-eternal' is heard, nevertheless, because of the capacity [of the argument], 'everything [is non-eternal]' is intended.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.28: Because of the tenability of that property from another cause as well, there is no refutation. //

children.translated_text: 'But when [there is] being immediately subsequent to effort' —
he teaches.
'[This is a] <s>jāti</s>' —
he refutes: 'No' — //28//

The <s>sūtra</s> of refutation for this: 'Because of the tenability of that property from another cause as well, there is no refutation' (<s>sūtra</s> 28). He explains that: 'by one who says "because of being immediately subsequent to effort"' — from the cause, i.e., from effort, a restriction on the origination of sound is being prescribed, in order to prove the non-eternality of phonemes — but a restriction of the effect to [one] cause [is not being made]; it is not being said that every sound is produced only from effort and not from the conjunction of wind, the breaking of a tree, and the like — such that there would be non-pervasiveness of the reason. But the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is: because of the tenability of that property — of the property of what is to be proved — from another cause as well, i.e., from another indicator as well, there is no refutation. The <s>Vārttikakāra</s> explains this very [point]: 'By one who says "sound is non-eternal"' — the remainder is: 'through being immediately subsequent to effort.' Another cause — another indicator of non-eternality — for the sounds produced from the breaking of branches and the like is not being denied. If even the non-eternality of those not included in the thesis [follows] from another cause — let it be so, no matter — this is the meaning. Nor is another cause, such as being the basis of cognition-distinctions and the like, being denied for the non-eternality of the sound that is the thesis-subject. He states the view of one school: 'Others, however, state the solution: that which is immediately subsequent to effort' — he criticizes that: 'But this is not [beyond] dispute.' This is the intent: being immediately subsequent to effort belongs to the thoracic wind's action, for that [action] arises from the conjunction of <s>ātman</s> possessing effort. But the conjunctions, separations, and the like [occurring] in the wind at the chest and other locations are not immediately subsequent to effort — much less is sound [so]. And when this is the understanding of the initial sound, what can be said about being immediately subsequent to effort of the final [sound] that is heard, which inheres in the auditory cavity? Therefore, one who accepts the being-immediately-subsequent-to-effort of sound without a means of valid knowledge — nothing can be proved to him by a means of valid knowledge. For one whose establishment of the provable is [achieved] merely by appearance, independent of means of valid knowledge, [this] is easily available everywhere. Thus, the seed of dissatisfaction has been stated by this. Having conceded the being immediately subsequent to effort of sound, he says:

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.29: Because of the non-apprehension of the non-apprehension of that, [and] because of the establishment of non-existence upon the establishment of non-existence, [and] because of the tenability of the opposite of that, [this is] the comparable-by-non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhisama</s>). //

children.text: anupalabdhisamapratiṣedhasya lakṣaṇaṃ darśayituṃ tatpratiṣedhyaṃ tāvadāha bhāṣyakāraḥ /
children.translated_text: In order to show the definition of the refutation of the comparable-by-non-apprehension, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> first states what is to be refuted:
'And this — the cause of its non-apprehension — would be grasped' —
Having stated what is to be refuted,
he states the definition of the refutation, [i.e.,] the <s>jāti</s>:

'Because of the non-apprehension of the non-apprehension of that, because of the establishment of non-existence upon the establishment of non-existence, and because of the tenability of the opposite of that — [this is] the comparable-by-non-apprehension' (<s>sūtra</s> 29). //

'There is no non-apprehension of what existed prior to utterance.' Therefore, [the objector argues that] some obstruction and the like, as in the case of water and the like, is the cause of its non-apprehension — to this he says:

children.text:
vyācaṣṭe teṣāmāvaraṇādīnāmanupalabdhirnopapadyate /
upalabhyamānatve upalabdhirūpatayā anupalabdhitvānupapatteḥ /
tathā cānupalabdheranupalambhādanupalabdhirnāstītyāvaraṇādyupalabdhisiddhiriti /
āvaraṇa ivāvaraṇānupalabdhirapyanupalabdhisametyarthaḥ
// 29 //
children.translated_text: He explains: 'The non-apprehension of those — of the obstruction and the like — is untenable.' Because, if they were being apprehended, then because of having the nature of apprehension, the untenability of their non-apprehension [follows]. And thus, because of the non-apprehension of the non-apprehension, non-apprehension does not exist — and therefore the establishment of the apprehension of the obstruction and the like [follows]. The meaning is: the non-apprehension of the obstruction too, like [the non-apprehension of] the obstruction [itself], is a comparable-by-non-apprehension. //29//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.30: Because of the nature of non-apprehension consisting in non-perception, [the reason in the comparable-by-non-apprehension] is not a [valid] reason. //
The <s>sūtra</s> of refutation for this: 'Because of the nature of non-apprehension consisting in non-perception, [it is] not a [valid] reason' (<s>sūtra</s> 30). //

children.translated_text: From non-apprehension — the valid means of knowledge that negates apprehension — the non-apprehension of obstruction is established.
Why? — to this he says:
The non-apprehension is the object of that valid means of knowledge that negates apprehension — and from that, the absence of obstructions and the like —
this should be understood. //30//

The non-apprehension of obstructions and the like indicates the absence of the obstructions and the like — but not the absence of the self (<s>ātman</s>). The apprehension of obstructions and the like [has as its] form [the apprehension of something perceptible] — for indeed, that non-apprehension is not [a non-apprehension] of the self, such that it could indicate the absence of the self. Even apprehension has as its object what is apprehensible (<s>upalabhya</s>), not the self — how much less non-apprehension! Therefore, non-apprehension is a reason for the absence of the apprehensible — not a reason for the absence of the self; for in that case, that [non-apprehension] itself would not exist, and then even the absence of the apprehensible would not [be established] — and there would be [the existence of] obstruction and its apprehension too. This is what the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> says: 'because of non-apprehension' — this is a non-reason. Why? Because non-apprehension has the nature of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhātmakatva</s>). He explains this: 'because of being merely the absence of apprehension.' By the word 'merely' (<s>mātra</s>), he excludes the nature of 'absence of the self' that is attributed [to non-apprehension] by the <s>jāti</s>-proponent. Now, let this non-apprehension be [merely] the absence of apprehension — and let it not be [anything about] the apprehensible — what is the consequence regarding the absence of obstructions and the like? — to this he says: 'What exists is the object of apprehension; by apprehension, its existence is known.' But from non-apprehension — which has the nature of non-apprehension — that [existence] cannot be asserted — this is the import. He states what is to be known from non-apprehension: 'What does not exist — that is [the object] of non-apprehension.' Now, let this be known — what [follows] even from this much? — to this he says: 'This non-apprehension of obstructions and the like is [itself] the non-apprehension [that indicates absence].' For you, the <s>jāti</s>-proponent, by occasioning — through the non-apprehension of the non-apprehension of obstructions and the like — the apprehension of obstruction and the [existence of] obstruction, must counter-argue at the cost of annulling the domain of non-apprehension itself. This being so, it is better that its domain be the obstruction and its apprehension — thus, by this [non-apprehension], the transactions of cognition of existence and non-existence, [verbal] designation, and conventional behavior that sustain the entire course of the world are accommodated. This is what is stated — 'This non-apprehension of obstructions and the like is the non-apprehension' — [meaning:] the valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) that has non-apprehension as its domain; operating in [the domain of] non-apprehension, which is its own domain, when apprehension is absent, it does not negate non-apprehension — its own domain — but rather [negates] apprehension alone. But for the <s>jāti</s>-proponent, [even non-apprehension] would be negated, and thus the entire worldly convention would be destroyed — this is the import. And non-apprehension, being unrefuted, is fit to serve as a reason for the absence of obstructions and the like. Now, mere non-apprehension is not a reason for apprehending absence — let there be no doubt regarding the existence or non-existence of the rabbit-mark on the far side of the moon — to this he says: 'but obstructions and the like' — the apprehensible, or apprehension, is not established as non-existent from mere non-apprehension; rather, [only] what is [of such a nature that it] should be perceived if it existed — therefore there is no over-extension — this is the meaning. Now, because apprehension, which would indicate the existence of its own object, is absent, let the obstructions and the like not be apprehended — but whence the absence of those? — to this he says: 'from non-apprehension, the valid means of knowledge that negates apprehension, the object of non-apprehension — namely the absence of the apprehensible — is known.' [That is:] 'the obstructions and the like, which are causes of the non-apprehension of sound, do not exist.' Then does the valid means of knowledge that negates apprehension directly indicate the absence of the apprehensible? — to this he says: 'Not' —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.31: And because of the internal awareness of the existence and non-existence of varieties of cognition, [this is known] within the self. //
Not only is the tenability of non-apprehension to be understood through the valid means of knowledge whose domain is negation,
but [it is] also knowable to every person through inner self-awareness — thus says the <s>sūtrakāra</s>:
'And because of the internal awareness of the existence and non-existence of varieties of cognition, within the self' (<s>sūtra</s> 31). //

vyācaṣṭe aheturiti vartate /
śarīra iti /
prāguccāraṇāc śabdasyānupalabdherasattve sādhyamāne 'naikāntikatvaṃ syād yadi tu paścādviśiṣyeta āvaraṇādyasaṃbhave satīti tato hetvantaraṃ nāma nigrahasthānaṃ syādityāśaṅkya vārtikakāra āha /

ayamarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: But when 'when existence is conceded' is [added] —

children.text: viṣayaviparyayassūcyate tadāvaraṇādyasabhave satyanupalabdherasattvamityasya viparyaya evaṃ prayoktavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: the contrapositive of the object is indicated: in the absence of obstructions and the like, because of non-apprehension — the non-existence [follows]; and the contrapositive of this should be formulated thus:

children.text: sattvopagame cāvaraṇādyasaṃbhave satyupalabhyeteti asya viparyayasyāvyabhicārād nārthāpattisama
children.translated_text: 'When existence is conceded, in the absence of obstructions and the like, [the entity] would be apprehended' — because of the non-deviation of this contrapositive, [it is] not a comparable-by-presumption —
this is the meaning. //31//

He explains: 'it is a non-reason' — this carries over. 'In the body' — Before the utterance [of the sound], when the non-existence [of sound] is being proved through its non-apprehension, there would be inconclusiveness — [namely,] if [one says that non-apprehension proves absence even] afterwards [but not before, there is no distinction]. But if [the argument] is later qualified as 'in the absence of obstructions and the like' — then it would be [the ground of defeat called] 'shifting to another reason' (<s>hetvantara</s>) — anticipating this, the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> says: 'The formulation is: [the non-apprehension holds] in the absence of obstructions and the like, when existence is conceded.' (544/8) He states the purpose of adding 'when existence is conceded': 'In the absence of obstructions and the like, when existence is conceded, because of the non-deviation of the contrapositive, it is not a comparable-by-presumption (<s>arthāpattisama</s>).' The meaning is: if, when 'in the absence of obstructions and the like, because of non-apprehension' is stated, someone counter-argues with the <s>jāti</s> of comparable-by-presumption: 'when it is said "in the absence of obstructions and the like, because of non-apprehension," what is implicitly arrived at is: in the presence of obstructions and the like, there would be apprehension' —

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.32: Because of the similarity [of all things with a non-eternal entity], and because of the tenability of having equal properties, [there would be] the consequence that everything is non-eternal — [this is] the comparable-by-impermanence (<s>anityasama</s>). //
All entities have the similarity of existence (<s>sattva</s>) with a non-eternal pot — //32//

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.33: Because of the non-establishment [of the thesis] through [mere] similarity, [there is] the non-establishment of the refutation — because of the similarity of what is to be refuted. //

This is the <s>sūtra</s> of refutation: 'Because of the non-establishment [of the thesis] through similarity, the non-establishment of the refutation — and because of the similarity of what is to be refuted' (<s>sūtra</s> 33).

children.text: NyS_5,1.34: dṛṣṭānte ca sādhyasādhanabhāvena prajñātasya dharmasya hetutvāttasya cobhayathā bhāvānnāviśeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.34: And because in the example, a property recognized through the relation of provable and proof serves as the reason, and because that [property] exists in both ways, there is no non-distinction. //
Having thus brought the <s>jāti</s>-proponent to a position of equality [in apparent difficulty], he states the ultimate refutation:

children.text: dṛṣṭānte ca sādhyasādhanabhāvena prajñātasya dharmasya hetutvāttasya cobhayathābhāvānnāviśeṣaḥ (sū. 34) //
children.translated_text: 'And because in the example, a property recognized through the relation of provable and proof serves as the reason, and because that exists in both ways, there is no non-distinction' (<s>sūtra</s> 34). //

children.text:
sādharmyāmātraṃ cāśrityasādhyā vinābhāvarahitamiti /
deśyavārttikamaviśeṣasamāta
iti /
pariharati bhidyata iti /
yaccāviśeṣasamauttaramiti /
(545/7) sarvānityatvaṃ hi prasañjayatā na śabdānityatvaṃ niṣiddhaṃ bhavatīti tatroktamityarthaḥ /
atra śaṅkate nāsādhanāditi /
pariharati /
na viśeṣahetūpapatteriti /

// 34 //
children.translated_text: 'Relying merely on similarity, [the thesis] is devoid of invariable concomitance' — the <s>Vārttika</s> instructed on the comparable-by-non-distinction (<s>aviśeṣasama</s>). He refutes: 'it is different.' 'And what was the reply of the comparable-by-non-distinction' — (545/7) the meaning is: it was stated there that by occasioning the non-eternality of everything, the non-eternality of sound is not negated. Here he raises a doubt: 'not, because of non-proof' — He refutes: 'not, because of the tenability of a distinguishing reason.' The rest is easy. //34//

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.35: Because the eternal property exists in the non-eternal, and because of the tenability of eternality in the non-eternal — [this is] the comparable-by-permanence (<s>nityasama</s>). //

children.text: na hyasti saṃbhavaḥ sāmānyasamavāyātiriktadharmā nityā dharmī cānitya iti // 35 //
children.translated_text: for there is no possibility that a property is eternal through the inherence of a universal while the property-bearer is non-eternal — apart from [the inherence of that universal]. //35//
Because of the constant existence of the property, there is the constant existence of the property-bearer too —

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.36: Because in what is to be refuted, the eternal property exists in the non-eternal, and because of the tenability of non-eternality in the non-eternal, there is no refutation. //

śaṅkate pratiṣedhyeti /
evamabhyupagacchato 'yaṃ doṣa ityetatparametad na tu svapakṣopavarṇanaparametaditi śaṅkārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The doubt-raising [means:] this defect [arises] for one who accepts thus — this is directed at the other party, not at describing one's own position — this is the meaning of the doubt.
He refutes: 'Not, because of the untenability of the alternative' —
'And because the answer to the contradiction has [already] been stated' —
The meaning is: the answer to the [objection from] contradiction was given [as] the untenability of the question. //36//

This is the <s>sūtra</s> of rejection: 'Because in what is to be refuted, the eternal property exists in the non-eternal, and because of the tenability of non-eternality in the non-eternal, there is no refutation' (<s>sūtra</s> 36). The meaning is: there is a defect both in accepting and in not accepting the reason 'the eternal-and-non-eternal existence of the property.' The non-eternality of sound is the absence of existence terminated at a later [point] — i.e., the inherence of existence. And in that case, the question is untenable. For if the absence is [caused by] a destroyer — the non-eternality is [still] that — even so, the question is untenable. Or, even on our view [where non-eternality is] inherence — even so, that [untenability holds]. For the non-eternality of sound is the inherence of existence terminated at a later point. And that [inherence] is not something superimposed upon sound, because of its own independence — this is the meaning. The <s>Vārttika</s>: 'Because non-eternality is not accepted as a separate property' — (546/8) For non-eternality is the inherence of non-everlasting existence, and that [inherence] is not a property separate from inherence, nor is inherence a property either, because of not being dependent [on the property-bearer as an independent quality]; but because of being described in dependence [on the property-bearer], it is in some sense called a 'property-bearer' — this [is the point]. Moreover, when it is said that 'non-eternality is the conjunction with non-everlasting existence,' the question is not appropriate. For one who is sent to 'bring a pot' does not turn around and ask 'should a pot be brought or a cloth?' — it is of this kind — this is the meaning. Moreover, the alternative 'is non-eternality eternal or non-eternal?' does not arise, because of contradiction — to this he says: 'And the conjunction with everlasting and non-everlasting existence is of a single [entity].' He raises a doubt: 'regarding what is to be refuted' —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.37: Because of the multiplicity of effects produced by effort, [this is] the comparable-by-effect (<s>kāryasama</s>). //

yena tu kāryasamā jātiranyathaivoktā tadyathā 'nityaḥ śabdaḥ kṛtakatvād ghaṭavadityukte anyad mṛtpiṇḍādikāryatvaṃ ghaṭasya anyacca vivakṣāprayatnavāyupreraṇābhighātakāryatvaṃ śabdasya tasmācchabdakṛtakatvasya ghaṭādikṛtakatvādbhedānna sādhanaṃ kṛtakattvamanityatvasyeti /
seyaṃ kāryānyatvena pratyavasthānātkāryasameti /

children.translated_text: Therefore he says: 'What shows the non-establishment of the provable [property] by means of a slight difference in effecthood — that is the comparable-by-effect' — thus says the venerable [<s>Uddyotakara</s>].
<s>Kīrti</s> also says:
'When, because of the co-presence of the property-to-be-proved with effecthood in general, proof is [established],
the assertion of difference due to the difference in the relata — that fault is considered comparable-by-effect.'

He explains its meaning with an illustration: 'Sound is non-eternal, because of being immediately subsequent to effort.' And that effecthood and non-eternality are mutually unmixed was shown in the very first chapter. Having cited the illustration, he introduces the <s>jāti</s>: 'This being so, the objection is stated: "because of the multiplicity of effects produced by effort."' Being-immediately-subsequent-to-effort is either origination immediately after effort, or apprehension immediately after effort. The first alternative [is rejected] because of non-establishment. Therefore, apprehension-immediately-after-effort is to be maintained. In that regard, he states the comparable-by-effect objection: 'Things apprehended immediately after effort are observed to both originate immediately after effort — like pots and the like — and to be manifested (<s>abhivyakti</s>) when obstruction is removed — like root-pegs and the like that are covered. So, is the origination of sound immediately after effort, or [is it] manifestation?' — there is no distinction. Thus, the counter-argument through [the claim of] non-distinction regarding the effect is the comparable-by-effect (<s>kāryasama</s>). But the [version of] comparable-by-effect stated by another is as follows: 'When it is said "sound is non-eternal, because of being produced, like a pot" — the effecthood of the pot [involves] being the effect of clay and the like, while the effecthood of sound [involves] being the effect of the intended effort, wind-propulsion, and impact — therefore, because of the difference of the effecthood of sound from the effecthood of pots and the like, being-produced is not a proof of non-eternality.' This comparable-by-effect [arises] from the counter-argument through [the claim of] difference-in-effecthood.

children.text:
tadanena yadīśvarasādhananirālaraṇāyoktam---tanugirisāgarādīnāmanyatkāryatvam
anyacca prāsādāṭṭālagopurādīnā miti tadapi jātyuttaramenetyuktaṃ bhavati /
na ca pratyakṣadṛśyamānaṃ buddhimadanvayavyatirekānuvidhānaṃ saudhādīnāmiva tanubhuvanādīnāṃ tāstītyetāvatā bhedena kāryabhede śabdamātrābheda iti sāprantam /
abhūtvā bhāvalakṣaṇasya kṛtakatvasya saṃsthānavattvasya vā vastuna evābhedāt tasmādetadapyayuktam /
'vastubhede pravṛttepi śabdasāmyādabhedinaḥ /
na yuktā 'numitiḥ pāṇḍudravyādiva hutāśane' /
na ceyaṃ jātirutkarṣāpakarṣasamābhyāṃ bhidyate sādhyadṛṣṭāntayordharmavikalpena pravartamānatvāttasmātsūtrakārokta
eva kāryasamosaṃkīrṇa iti yuktamutpaśyāmaḥ
// 37 //
children.translated_text: By this, what was said in order to refute the proof of <s>Īśvara</s> — that the effecthood of bodies, mountains, oceans, and the like is one thing, and the effecthood of mansions, towers, gate-houses, and the like is another — that too is said to be a <s>jāti</s>-reply. And the positive and negative concomitance with an intelligent [agent] that is directly observed for palaces and the like also exists for bodies, worlds, and the like — so merely by this much difference, [to argue] 'because of the difference in the effect, there is [only] a verbal [similarity] without [real] identity' is not fitting. Because of the real identity of the property of being-produced — characterized as coming-into-being-after-having-not-been — or of possessing configuration — with the [same] real entity. Therefore this too is unjustified: 'even when [the word] operates in different [kinds of] real things, an inference [treating them as] identical because of verbal sameness is not justified — like [inferring] fire from a pale substance.' And this <s>jāti</s> is not different from the comparable-by-excellence and comparable-by-deficiency, because it operates through the difference in properties between the thesis-subject and the example — therefore we rightly see that the comparable-by-effect stated by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> is indeed the unmixed [one]. //37//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.38: If effecthood is different, then effort is not a cause — because of the tenability of [another] cause of non-apprehension. //
This is the <s>sūtra</s> of rejection —
If the effect is different [from manifestation], effort is not the cause, because of the tenability of the cause of non-apprehension (<s>sūtra</s> 38). //

children.text:
kāryasyotpattirna lakṣaṇasyānyatve 'bhivyaktilakṣaṇātkāryātprayatnasyābhivyaktiṃ pratyahetutvaṃ na bhavatītyata āha /
anupalabdhikāraṇasyāvaraṇāderupapatterabhivyaktihetutvaṃ syād evaṃ tu nāstīti vyatirekaparaṃ draṣṭavyam /
sati kāryānyatva iti bhāṣyaṃ sūtravadyojanīyam /
yatra prayatnānantaramityatra yatratatrayorvyatyāsaḥ
tatra prayatnānantaramabhivyaktiryatrānupalabdhikāraṇaṃ vyavadhānamupapadyata iti /
kasmādanupalabdhikāraṇopapatteḥ prayatnābhivyaṅgyatvamityata āha /
vyavadhānāyogācceti /
(505/1) co hetvarthe /
prayatnānantarabhāvina iti /
viṣayeṇa viṣayiṇamupalakṣayati prayatnānantarabhāvina
ityarthaḥ /
anupalabdhikāraṇopapatterityasya vyatirekapradhānatāmāha /
na tu śabdasyānupalabdhīti /
deśyavārtikaṃ saṃśayasamāta iti /
(547/7) pariharati ubhayasādharmyāditi /
viśeṣānupalabdhau satyāmubhayasādharmyātsaṃśayasamaḥ /
idaṃ tu viśeṣopalabdhimavivakṣitveti viśeṣaḥ /
tadidamuktamayaṃ tu na tatheti /
deśayati sādharmyasamāta
iti /
nirākaroti na hettvadhyāropaṇāditi /

children.translated_text: 'Because of being immediately subsequent to effort' — this [reason] is refuted by being superimposed [with the claim that it amounts to] 'perception immediately after effort.'
But in the comparable-by-similarity (<s>sādharmyasama</s>), there is no superimposition — this is the meaning.

children.text: tadevaṃ jātyuttaravādinaṃ prati sādhanavādinā sarvatraiva samyak samādhānaṃ svasādhanasya vaktavyam /
children.translated_text: Thus, against the <s>jāti</s>-rejoinder-proponent, the proof-proponent should state in every case the correct resolution of his own proof.
When this is so, the debate concludes with the determination of truth. //38//

The origination of the effect — not of the definition — when [the effect] is different from the effect defined as manifestation, [the claim that] effort is not a cause of manifestation does not hold — therefore he says:
'Because of the tenability of the cause of non-apprehension, such as obstruction and the like, there would be causality for manifestation; but this is not the case' — this should be seen as primarily [an argument from] negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>).
'Given that the effect is different' — the <s>Bhāṣya</s> should be construed like the <s>sūtra</s>.
'Where, immediately after effort' — here the pair of 'where' [clauses] are transposed:
'Where, immediately after effort, there is manifestation — there the cause of non-apprehension, [namely] obstruction, is tenable.'
Why is manifestability by effort [established] because of the tenability of the cause of non-apprehension? — therefore he says:
'Because of the impossibility of obstruction' —
(505/1) The word 'ca' is in the sense of a reason.
'That which exists immediately after effort' —
By the object, he indicates the possessor of the object: 'that which exists immediately after effort' — this is the meaning.
He states the primarily negative-concomitance character of 'because of the tenability of the cause of non-apprehension':
'But not the non-apprehension of sound' —
The indicated <s>Vārttika</s> [reads]: 'from the comparable-by-doubt' —
(547/7) He resolves: 'because of the similarity with both' —
When no specific [distinguishing feature] is apprehended, it is comparable-by-doubt due to the similarity with both.
But here the distinguishing feature is that [the speaker] did not intend [to claim] the apprehension of a specific [feature] — this is the difference.
This is what was said: 'But this one is not so.'
He teaches: 'from the comparable-by-similarity' —
He refutes: 'Not, because of the superimposition of reason-hood.'
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.39: In refutation too, there is an equal fault. //

children.text: yadi punarvādyapi jātivādinaṃ prati sādhanābhāsena pratayavatiṣṭhate tataḥ ṣaṭpakṣyāṃ satyāṃ na tattvanirṇayāvasānā kathā bhavediti śiṣyahitaḥ sūtrakāraḥ samādhānābhāsavādinaṃ prati ṣaṭpakṣīmavatārayati /
children.translated_text: If, however, the proponent too responds to the <s>jāti</s>-proponent with a proof-semblance, then, given the six-fold [positions], the debate would not conclude with the determination of truth — therefore the <s>sūtrakāra</s>, acting in the interest of the students, introduces the six-fold [scheme] against the proponent of semblance-resolutions.
'In refutation too, there is an equal fault' (<s>sūtra</s> 39). //

children.text:
tadetatsūnatrāvatāraparaṃ bhāṣyaṃ hetoścedanaikāntikatvamupapādyate prativādine 'naikāntikatvādasādhakaḥ syāditi /
yadi cānaikāntikatvādasādhakaṃ vādino vacanaṃ pratiṣedhe 'pi samāno doṣaḥ /
yo 'yaṃ prayatnakāryānekatvāditi pratiṣedho jātivādinanaḥ so 'pyanaikāntikaḥ /
evaṃ hyaikāntikaḥ syādyadi sarvameva pratiṣedhed
yatastu kiṃ citpratiṣedhati kiṃ cicca na, tasmādayamanaikāntikaḥ
ato 'sādhaka ityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: He states another interpretation:
'Or, of sound' —
The eternality position [holds that sound exists as] manifestation, not origination.

children.text: evamanityapakṣe utpādo nābhivyaktirityayaṃ viśeṣo na sidhyatyayaṃ pratiṣedhe 'pi samāno doṣa ityarthaḥ // 39 //
children.translated_text: Thus, in the non-eternality position, [the view that it is] origination and not manifestation — this specific distinction — is not established; in refutation too, there is an equal fault — this is the meaning. //39//

This <s>Bhāṣya</s> is for the purpose of introducing the <s>sūtra</s>: 'If the inconclusiveness of the reason is demonstrated, the opponent would be non-probative due to inconclusiveness.'
And if, due to inconclusiveness, the proponent's statement is non-probative, then in refutation too, there is an equal fault.
This refutation by the <s>jāti</s>-proponent — 'because of the multiplicity of the effects of effort' — is also inconclusive.
For it would be conclusive only if it refuted everything;
but since it refutes some things and does not refute others, therefore it is inconclusive,
hence non-probative — this is the meaning.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.40: [It is] the same everywhere. //

children.text:
na kevalamasyāṃ jātāvayaṃ samādhānābhāso vādino 'pi tu sarvatraiva jātāviti śiṣyān śikṣayati sūtrakāraḥ /
sarvatraivam (sū. 40) // asminsamādhāne prayukte vādinā punarjātivādī pratyavatiṣṭhate /
children.translated_text:
Not only in this [particular] <s>jāti</s> is this a semblance-resolution of the proponent, but everywhere in [all types of] <s>jāti</s> — thus the <s>sūtrakāra</s> instructs the students.
'The same everywhere' (<s>sūtra</s> 40). // When this resolution is employed by the proponent, the <s>jāti</s>-proponent again counter-argues.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.41: In the counter-refutation of the refutation, the fault is like the fault of the refutation. //
this is the counter-argument of the <s>jāti</s>-proponent — this is the meaning. //41//
The refutation belongs to the <s>jāti</s>-proponent; the counter-refutation of that belongs to the original proof-proponent; in that [counter-refutation], there is an equal fault —

children.text: NyS_5,1.42: pratiṣedhaṃ sadoṣamabhyupetya pratiṣedhavipratiṣedhe samāno doṣaprasaṅgo matānujñā //
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.42: Having accepted the refutation as faulty, in the counter-refutation of the refutation, the consequence of an equal fault is the acceptance of the [opponent's] position (<s>matānujñā</s>). //

children.text: atha pañcamaṃ pakṣaṃ sādhanavādinaścaturthapakṣavādinaṃ prati matānujñāpāpādanamāha /
children.translated_text: Now, he states the fifth position — the imputation of acceptance-of-the-opponent's-position (<s>matānujñā</s>) by the proof-proponent against the fourth-position proponent:

children.text: pratiṣedhaṃ sadoṣamabhyupetya pratiṣedhavipratiṣedhe samāno doṣaprasaṅgo matānujñā (sū. 42) //
children.translated_text: 'Having accepted the refutation as faulty, in the counter-refutation of the refutation, the consequence of an equal fault is the acceptance of the [opponent's] position' (<s>sūtra</s> 42). //

children.text: NyS_5,1.43: svapakṣalakṣaṇāpekṣopapattyupasaṃhāre hetunirdeśe parapakṣadoṣābhyupagamāt samāno doṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.1.43: In the statement of the reason for the subsumption of the tenability expected from the own-position definition, because of the acceptance of the fault of the opponent's position, there is an equal fault. //

children.text:
seyaṃ matānujñā tṛtīye pakṣe pañcamapakṣavādino 'pi sādhana vādina
iti jātivādī ṣaṣṭhapakṣasthita āha /
children.translated_text: This very acceptance-of-the-opponent's-position, [applicable] in the third position, [applies] also to the fifth-position proponent, the proof-proponent — thus the <s>jāti</s>-proponent, standing in the sixth position, says:

'In the statement of the reason for the subsumption of the tenability expected from the own-position definition, because of the acceptance of the fault of the opponent's position, there is an equal fault' (<s>sūtra</s> 43). //

children.text:
svapakṣaṇe lakṣyate tadutthānatvājjātiḥ svapakṣalakṣaṇā anaikāntikatvodbhāvanalakṣaṇā tāmabhyupetya
anuddhūtya pratiṣedhe 'pi jātilakṣaṇe samāno 'naikāntikatvadoṣa ityupapadyamānaṃ svapakṣe 'pi doṣaṃ parapakṣe jātivādipakṣe sādhanavādyupasaṃharati /
tatra cānaikāntikaṃ hetuṃ brūte tadevaṃ svapakṣalakṣaṇāpekṣopapattyupasaṃhāre hetunirddeśe parapakṣe yatsvayaṃ dūṣaṇaṃ dattaṃ tasyābhyupagamādvādino 'pi samānova doṣa
iti /
jātivādino vacanaṃ ṣaṣṭhe pakṣe sthitasya tadevaṃ vistīrya saṃkalayyāha /
tatra khalu sthāpanāhetuvādina iti /
seyaṃ ṣaṭpakṣī samānadoṣāpādanenānirṇāyakatvātpaunaruktyācca na tattvanirṇayāya paryāptā, tasmātsamādhānābhāsena jātivādinaṃ prati na pratyavastheyaṃ, kiṃ tu samyak sādhanena, tathā ca ṣaṭrapakṣī upahatānāvatarati /
tattvanirṇayaparyavasānā ca kathā bhavati /
yadi tvasya kadā citsamyaksādhanavādino 'pi pratibhākṣayātsamādhānaṃ na sphurati tato 'tyantaparājayādvaraṃ saṃśayo 'pīti nyāyena samādhānābhāsenāpi pratyavastheyamevetyāśayavānāha /
children.translated_text: But if sometimes even for a proponent of correct proof, the resolution does not become clear due to the decline of insight, then — [thinking] 'by the principle that even doubt is better than utter defeat' — one should counter-argue even with a semblance-resolution — with this intent he says:
'Regarding their good or bad [quality]' —
By the commentary on the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, the <s>Vārttika</s> too has been explained.

children.text: etāstu jātayo na tattvavivekamupakurvanti prayujyamānatayā nirākaraṇīyatayā tvāsāmapyupakāra iti // 41 //
children.translated_text: But these <s>jātis</s> do not contribute to the discernment of truth by being employed; however, by being refuted, they too contribute [to the discernment of truth]. //41//

That which is characterized by one's own position — the <s>jāti</s> is characterized by one's own position because it arises therefrom — characterized by the attribution of inconclusiveness — having accepted that [fault of one's own position],
without dispelling it, in the refutation too, which has the character of a <s>jāti</s>, 'there is an equal fault of inconclusiveness' — [the proof-proponent], subsumes under the opponent's position — the <s>jāti</s>-proponent's position — the fault that is tenable in his own position.
And therein he states an inconclusive reason. Thus, 'in the statement of the reason for the subsumption of the tenability expected from the own-position definition, because of the acceptance of the fault that was itself given as a criticism to the opponent's position — the proponent too has an equal fault.'
The statement of the <s>jāti</s>-proponent, standing in the sixth position — he states this expanded [account] and then summarizes:
'Therein indeed, the proof-proponent's thesis-reason' —
This six-fold [scheme], because of imputing an equal fault, is non-determinative, and because of repetitiveness, is not sufficient for the determination of truth. Therefore, one should not counter-argue against the <s>jāti</s>-proponent with a semblance-resolution, but rather with a correct proof. And thus the six-fold [scheme], being refuted, does not descend [into debate].
And the debate concludes with the determination of truth.
Thus, in the <s>Nyāyavārttikatātparyaṭīkā</s> composed by the venerable <s>Vācaspati Miśra</s>,
the first section of the fifth chapter [is concluded]. //
In the <s>Nyāyavārttikatātparyaṭīkā</s> composed by the venerable <s>Vācaspati Miśra</s>,
the fifth chapter.

children.text: NyS_5,2.1: pratijñāhāniḥ pratijñāntaraṃ pratijñāvirodhaḥ pratijñāsaṃnyāso hetvantaramarthāntaraṃ nirarthakam avijñātārtham apārthakam aprāptakālaṃ nyūnamadhikaṃ punaruktam ananubhāṣaṇam ajñānam apratibhā vikṣepo matānujñā paryanuyojyopekṣaṇaṃ niranuyojyānuyogopasiddhānto hetvābhāsāśca nigrahasthānāni //
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 5.2.1: Abandonment of the thesis, shifting to another thesis, contradiction of the thesis, renunciation of the thesis, shifting to another reason, shifting to another topic, the meaningless, the unintelligible, the incoherent, the untimely, the deficient, the redundant, the repetitious, silence, ignorance, inability to respond, evasion, acceptance of the opponent's position, overlooking what should be questioned, questioning what should not be questioned, the thesis-already-proved, and semblances of reasons — these are the grounds of defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>). //
